title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
services: Amazon SageMaker;AWS Lake Formation;AWS Step Functions
speakers: Romi Patel (AWS); Mohammed Ali Syed (Experian); Rohit Kumar Singh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.

title: Unifying fragmented data: A lakehouse for the agentic AI era
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Glue
speakers: Prasad Shetty (AWS); Himanshu Sahni (AWS)
abstract: Financial services organizations face growing data volumes, strict regulations, and architectures where siloed warehouses and separate data lakes fragment data, drive up costs, and slow insights. In this chalk talk, we walk through a modern Lakehouse architecture on AWS that combines the cost benefits of data lakes with the governance and performance of data warehouses. We explain how Amazon S3 Tables with managed Apache Iceberg and AWS Glue Catalog semantic search deliver a single governed data foundation supporting agentic AI, traditional AI/ML, and analytics workloads. Learn practical patterns for a scalable Lakehouse you can apply immediately.

title: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
speakers: Jose Romero (AWS); Kalyan Kumar Neelampudi (AWS)
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Data mesh on AWS: governance, identity, and end‑user attribution
speakers: Mert Hocanin (Amazon Web Services); Zach Mitchell (AWS)
abstract: Data mesh promises domain‑owned data as a product — but the hard part is governance: who can access what, and how you prove it after the fact. In this interactive chalk talk, we whiteboard two patterns for building a data mesh on AWS and debate when each one fits. The first is a centrally governed mesh using attribute‑based, fine‑grained access controls across separate producer, consumer, and governance accounts. The second is a peer‑to‑peer mesh where the producer directly approves each consumer's subscription. We'll follow a single data product through the AWS Glue Data Catalog from publication to subscription, wire enterprise identity (federated from your existing identity provider, such as Okta or Entra) all the way through to the query, and show how trusted identity propagation and end‑user attribution give you per‑user accountability you can audit end to end.

title: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance
speakers: Parul Saxena (Amazon Web Services); Sreeji Gopal (Amazon)
abstract: Apache Iceberg V3 is now production-ready, and adopting deletion vectors, row lineage, and new data types across your lakehouse requires careful planning. In this session, explore implementation patterns using Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon S3 Tables. Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write, how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3 incremental processing cuts batch costs. Leave with a practical migration strategy for your Iceberg upgrade.

title: Design an open, cost-effective and high-performant lakehouse with Apache Iceberg on
speakers: Radhika Jakkula (Amazon Web Services); Saman Irfan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What does it take to build a lakehouse that's open, fast, and cost-effective? In this chalk talk, we unpack real architectural decisions behind Apache Iceberg on AWS—from Amazon S3 Tables (delivering up to 3x faster queries and 10x higher TPS) to unified metadata management with the AWS Glue Data Catalog across Athena, EMR, and Glue ETL. Bring your questions as we whiteboard trade-offs around schema evolution, ACID transactions, time-travel queries, and avoiding vendor lock-in. Leave with actionable patterns tailored to your workload.

title: Best practices for operating an Apache Iceberg lakehouse at scale
speakers: Aditya Challa (AWS); Priyanka Chaudhary (AWS)
abstract: Operating an Iceberg lakehouse at scale means taming the operational overhead that grows with your data. In this chalk talk, we dive into table maintenance strategies—compaction, snapshot expiration, and orphan file cleanup—and discuss how Amazon S3 Tables automates these tasks. We'll whiteboard patterns for metadata management with AWS Glue Data Catalog, storage cost optimization through lifecycle-aware file pruning, and partition evolution without rewriting data. You will leave with battle-tested operational patterns for production Iceberg workloads.

title: Building a semantic layer with AWS Glue Data Catalog and AWS Context
speakers: Syed Humair (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Varshni Muralidharan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this chalk talk, we dive into how AWS Context assembles semantic data from multiple semantic stores to create a semantic layer, which is then turned into a unified context layer through a knowledge graph. This enables AI agents and analytics engines to understand business meaning, relationships, and intent — not just schema and location. We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.

title: Cost-effective serverless data integrations and workflows for AI-ready data
speakers: Raghuveer Reddy (Goldman Sachs); Sakti Mishra (Amazon.com Services, Inc.); Shrey Malpani (AWS)
abstract: AI is only as good as the data beneath it and building high-quality, well-integrated data products shouldn't break your budget. In this session, learn how to build cost-effective AI-ready datasets using AWS Glue, Amazon MWAA and Apache Iceberg. We'll show how Glue Data Quality and Glue serverless ETL, now with generative AI-assisted development, lets you ingest, transform, and prepare high-quality data at scale. We’ll demonstrate how Amazon MWAA serverless empowers a single DAG to coordinate workloads across AWS Glue, and other engines - all of this while paying only for what you use. Pairing this setup with Apache Iceberg further enhances your AI workloads with query-ready production data pipelines that move the needle without breaking the bank.

title: Automating data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
speakers: Sudipta Bagchi (Amazon Web Services); Asif Abbasi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join this session to experience the power of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive in to an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline - governed end-to-end through AWS Glue Data Catalog - where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines, with Glue Data Catalog as the metadata backbone tying governance, lineage, and discovery together across the pipeline.

title: Build a governed semantic layer with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP
speakers: Ignacio Fernandez Gonzalez (amazon web services); Itziar Molina Fernandez (AWS); Paula Iglesias Ahualli (Amazon Web Services); Andrea Perez Isla (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Angel Emmanuel Hernandez Cebrian (AWS)
abstract: Financial services organizations struggle with inconsistent metric definitions, AI hallucination risks, and analyst bottlenecks. In this session, you’ll build a governed semantic layer with three key pillars (accuracy, consistency, and explainability) essential for agents to operate securely at scale. You’ll then connect to AI agents powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that query, interpret, and act on financial data via MCP, enabling natural language access to complex financial metrics. Your agents reason rather than guess, with full auditability for financial regulators. Leave with a production-ready architecture pattern that goes beyond "chat with your data" demos.

title: What's new in AWS Glue Data Catalog for data and AI governance
abstract: Data spread across lakes, warehouses, and third-party platforms is hard to find, govern, and use. In this session, explore how AWS Glue Data Catalog embraces open standards and open table formats so your data stays portable and accessible across the tools and engines your teams already use. Learn how to discover and register data from a range of sources, govern and manage access from one place, and connect your catalog to Apache Iceberg-compatible engines, so you can avoid lock-in and keep the freedom to choose the right tool for each job. Ideal for data engineers, platform teams, and data architects building open, governed analytics across their data estate.

title: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
speakers: David H Gardner (AWS); Jason Dalba (AWS)
abstract: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

title: Architect AI-powered analytics with Amazon Quick across your data platforms
speakers: Jackson Dowden (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect BI and conversational AI experiences to their existing data platforms. In this session we'll diagram architectural patterns for connecting Amazon Quick to structured data sources and integrating with third-party catalogs and semantic layers. We'll compare the available connectivity approaches, including data sources and MCP-based action connectors, and discuss when to use each. Considerations will span production use cases like BI dashboards, embedded analytics, text-to-SQL Q&A, and agentic workflows. Together we'll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.

title: From prompt to pipeline: Agentic data engineering
services: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA);AWS Glue
speakers: Kamen Sharlandjiev (AWS); Matt Sampson (AWS)
abstract: Data engineers spend weeks building pipelines describable in a single sentence. AI agents change this by autonomously discovering data, building transformations, and orchestrating workflows via natural language. Explore how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) gives agents standardized access to AWS analytics services. See a live demo of an agent composing across AWS Glue, Amazon Redshift, and MWAA Serverless to build a pipeline from a single prompt. Leave with patterns and tools to start building.

title: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
speakers: SOUMIL SHAH (Zeta Global); Shivam Patel (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but multi-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.

title: Simplify identity and security management in an open data architecture on AWS
speakers: Aarthi Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services); Amir Bar-Or (Amazon)
abstract: As organizations unify data across Amazon S3 data lakes, S3 Tables, and Amazon Redshift using the open data lakehouse architecture, securing access at scale becomes critical. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into simplifying trusted identity propagation so end-user identities — not shared service roles — reach the data plane, designing multi-dimensional tag-based access control taxonomies that scale automatically through inheritance, enforcing column-level and cell-level security across federated catalogs, and auditing every access event to individual users.

title: Accelerating data analytics on Apache Iceberg with Amazon S3 Tables
speakers: Satesh Sonti (Amazon Web Services); David Zhang (Amazon)
abstract: Every analytics query starts with how your data is stored. In this session, learn how Amazon S3 Tables deliver purpose-built Iceberg table storage that accelerates query performance, reduces storage costs, and eliminates table maintenance overhead. See how to pair S3 Tables with Athena, Redshift, and EMR to get faster results at lower cost, automate compaction and snapshot management, and simplify your lakehouse without changing your query engine or workflow.

title: Accelerate lakehouse analytics with Apache Iceberg materialized views
speakers: Saunak Chandra (Amazon); Santiago Abarca (AWS); Sharad Pai (Amazon Web Services India Private Limited)
abstract: Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS store pre-computed query results as Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 or Amazon S3 Tables. These views are not only open, as in compute once and consume from any Iceberg-compatible engine – they accelerate your lakehouse analytics while reducing costs. Join this hands-on session to experience how Apache Iceberg Materialized Views on AWS simplify medallion architectures, lakehouse migrations, accelerate BI query transactions and complex joins.

title: Build a fully managed data lake with Amazon S3 Tables
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Amazon Web Services); Sumaja Kapa (Amazon)
abstract: Data lakes have evolved from raw Parquet files with Hive-style partitioning to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables. In this hands-on workshop, you'll understand that evolution, then build a working analytics data lake with Amazon S3 Tables in under two hours. You'll create an S3 table bucket, ingest real-world data, migrate data into the bucket, and query it with Amazon Athena. You'll also learn how to connect third-party tools like DuckDB for interactive exploration. Along the way we’ll cover the benefits of fully managed Iceberg tables and when to use Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation for open data architectures.

title: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
speakers: Lee Kear (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.

title: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
speakers: Shubham Purwar (AWS); Nidhi Nayak (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

title: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
speakers: Majisha Namath Parambath (Amazon Web Services); Harsha Battapady (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.

title: Advanced Optimization & Cost-Saving Strategies for Amazon Athena
speakers: Sundeep kumar (Amazon Web Services); Scott Rigney (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Dive deep into Amazon Athena's most powerful capabilities in this interactive chalk talk for experienced practitioners. We'll explore cost-saving techniques—CTAS for materializing expensive query results, partition projection to eliminate metadata lookups, and EXPLAIN-based tuning to minimize bytes scanned. Discuss workgroup budgets, provisioned capacity for predictable pricing, and query result reuse to avoid redundant scans. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

title: From SAP to Agentic AI: Building a unified data strategy on AWS
speakers: Abhijeet Jangam (AWS); Diego Lombardini (AWS)
abstract: This chalk talk presents a unified architecture spanning SAP Business Data Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services. Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. We introduce the AWS for SAP MCP Server, accessing OData services as AI-ready tools via Model Context Protocol. Live demos showcase AI agents resolving supply chain exceptions, generating Customer 360 insights, and accelerating BW modernization.

title: Governed ModelOps: From customization to deployment with SageMaker AI
speakers: Siamak Nariman (Amazon Web Services); Bobby Lindsey (AWS); Sunita Koppar (Amazon Web Services); Naresh Nagpal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
speakers: Erika Nagamine (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Poulomi Dasgupta (Amazon)
abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Redshift Graviton instances deliver up to 35% better price-performance, accelerating workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

title: Build agentic AI applications with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS
speakers: David Greenshtein (AWS); Nathan Yee (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

title: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
speakers: Omer Dawelbeit (Amazon Web Services); Sudhir Kalidindi (AWS)
abstract: Organized fraud rings exploit the gaps between siloed detection systems, making them invisible to traditional rules-based approaches. In this workshop, you’ll construct a fraud detection optimization system that tackles them at scale. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, and train an ensemble combining transaction foundation model embeddings with graph embeddings for measurable score improvement. Then deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, and creates validated detection rules. Leave with an end-to-end working system you can replicate in your own environment.

title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Neptune;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: James Wu (AWS); Amit Kalawat (AWS)
abstract: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.

title: Build conversational AI agents for query federation with Amazon Athena
speakers: Arturo Bayo (Amazon Web Services); Steve Phillips (Amazon Web Services); Shoukat Ghouse (Amazon Web Services); Pathik Shah (Amazon Web Services); Sandeep Mishra (Amazon Web Services, Inc)
abstract: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for faster conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and multi-cloud data stores – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

title: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
services: Amazon Athena;Amazon Redshift;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Behram Irani (AWS); Rohit Vashishtha (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Open data lakehouses and data lakes can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, graviton efficiencies, intelligent-tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples of real-world workloads on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower you analytics costs.

title: Data mesh to agentic AI: Building an AI-ready enterprise on AWS
speakers: Prasanna Ramaswamy (Canadian Pension Plan Investment Board); Rishi Gera (AWS)
abstract: How do you build an AI-ready data foundation in a global investment organization without compromising trust, governance, or speed? CPP Investments—manager of one of the world’s largest pension funds—is evolving from fragmented data toward a governed enterprise data platform on AWS, using data mesh principles, federated ownership, and platform engineering to scale with guardrails. Join their CTO for a look inside the architecture, operating model, and critical trade-offs shaping this evolution, and how it brings trusted data closer to investment decisions while laying the foundation for conversational data experiences and agentic AI.

title: Don't ban it, broker it: Govern AI coding agents with Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Karthik Mokashi (AWS); Jayanth Ranjan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI coding agents are becoming embedded in development workflows. In regulated environments (e.g.,financial services), that raises concerns around data residency, code exfiltration, auditability, and runaway costs. But banning the tools creates shadow AI. In this session, we'll whiteboard a better path by pointing AI coding agents at Amazon Bedrock through a gateway in your VPC. One control point for identity, data residency, prompt inspection, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, cost controls, and immutable audit. We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

title: Gaining insights with S3 Metadata and annotations
speakers: Lee Kear (AWS); Bimal Gajjar (Amazon); Fabio Lattanzi (Amazon Web Services); Sumaja Kapa (Amazon)
abstract: Learn how S3 annotations let you attach rich, structured context (JSON, XML, YAML, or plain text) directly to your objects without re-uploading them. In this session, you will configure annotations on a live dataset, build an enrichment pipeline that attaches AI-generated summaries on ingest, query annotation payloads at scale through S3 Metadata's Apache Iceberg table in Athena, and wire an AI agent that discovers and retrieves objects using annotation-based search. You leave with patterns for zero-read agentic discovery and metadata architectures that scale to billions of objects.

title: Getting Started with Apache Iceberg: The AI-Ready open lakehouse advantage
speakers: Hugo Mineiro (AWS); Diego Ortiz (AWS); Rahul Sharma (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In the agentic AI era, the same modern lakehouse is also your AI-ready foundation: the quality, openness, and organization of your data is what separates successful AI outcomes. Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 Tables gives you that true portability and engine interoperability to build your AI-ready data foundation. Welcome to this hands-on workshop, where you will build an open lakehouse on AWS to serve analysts and agents both, while tackling real-world data challenges including a medallion architecture, table maintenance, change data capture and GDPR compliance.

title: Govern data and AI agents with lineage and context in AWS Glue Data Catalog
speakers: Navneet Srivastava (Amazon); Jorge A Lopez (AWS)
abstract: AI agents generate SQL, surface insights, and take action on your data. Without governance guardrails, they hallucinate column meanings, query stale tables, and return wrong answers with high confidence. In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. Walk away with practical patterns for governing AI-assisted analytics the same way you govern human analysts

title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
speakers: Rishabh Bhatia (Amazon Web Services); Shawn Chang (AWS)
abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
speakers: Mihika Naik (AWS); Vidit Ochani (Amazon)
abstract: Your data is scattered across warehouses, lakes, databases, and streams. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all of your data, enforces consistent governance across it, and makes it discoverable across engines and teams. See how to enrich, curate, and share metadata at scale, and give AI agents the context they need to get work done accurately and efficiently. Ideal for data engineers, architects, and platform teams.

title: Compete to build an AI agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Xavier Loup (Amazon Web Services); Laurent Guizard (AWS)
abstract: Organizations are ready to move beyond rule-based workflows to agents that reason, adapt, and act. In this gamified workshop, you'll use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to assemble a realistic conversational banking agent end-to-end: orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness; secure tool integration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway; and guardrails with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy. Prebuilt modules accelerate development so you can focus on agent logic. Compete in real time as your agent's accuracy and efficiency are scored on a live leaderboard. Leave with a working agent pattern you can adapt to your own use cases and bragging rights on the leaderboard.

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
speakers: David H Gardner (AWS); Don Simpson (AWS)
abstract: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications.

title: Core banking agent-ready: From composable to agentic financial services on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon EventBridge
speakers: Neha Daudani (AWS); Michelle Mei-Li Pfister (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The shift from composable to agentic banking is a re-architecture. Discover the reference architecture for turning a core banking platform into an intelligent core with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration, Amazon ECS for the control plane, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for domain context, and Amazon EventBridge for event-driven ingestion. We explore two consumption patterns ISVs can offer bank customers: exposing core banking APIs to customer-owned agents, and shipping a managed agentic layer for conversational AI and autonomous lending, deposit, and payment operations, eliminating up to 70% of repetitive manual work. Learn the hard-won lessons on infrastructure, governance, and product differentiation.

title: Designing performant and cost-effective data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
speakers: Ankit Kalyani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

title: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Specifications
speakers: Shankar Ramachandran (AWS); Clark Richey (Amazon)
abstract: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization — but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. In this chalk talk, we start from the foundational layers of compute, storage, and networking and build outward through data, security, observability, and AI. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability — and in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most. Along the way, we challenge common myths: that managed services equal lock-in, that Kubernetes equals portable, and that open source alone guarantees freedom. Through interactive whiteboarding, we'll design portable architecture patterns together — examining real trade-offs, open specifications like Apache Iceberg, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and MCP, and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.

title: Don't rewrite your APIs: Make them agent-ready for agentic AI
speakers: Piyali Kamra (Amazon Web Services); Amit Maindola (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations want agentic AI, but valuable capabilities sit behind legacy APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and internal services. In this chalk talk, we explore practical, low-lift patterns for making existing endpoints agent-ready without replacing systems of record. Using a financial services scenario, we walk through how OpenAPI specs, AWS Lambda facades, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway expose existing endpoints as composable agent tools. We show how existing RBAC and OAuth scopes map into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Cedar policies so you reuse your governance posture. Walk away with a 5-level maturity model you can apply to your own API estate.

title: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda
speakers: Jorge Castans Garcia (Amazon Web Services); Jannis Kambach (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.

title: From CSV to Iceberg: Understanding open data formats on Amazon S3
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Amazon Web Services); Danny Jones (AWS)
abstract: Building a data lake on Amazon S3 and need to decide between Parquet, Hive, and Iceberg – or understand how your team already did? In this session we develop the mental model for storing structured data on Amazon S3 and trace how it evolved. Understand formats from CSV to Parquet that accelerate analytic queries, walk through the evolution of table and partition schemas that organize data at scale, and learn how open table formats like Apache Iceberg bring database-like capabilities to your data lake. Leave with a clear picture of each and how Amazon S3 Tables bring it all together as a fully managed experience.

title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
speakers: Monica Vyavahare (Amazon Web Services); Harsha Battapady (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.

title: Make streaming data AI-ready before it goes stale (sponsored by Confluent)
abstract: Real-time data loses value when it gets stuck in pipelines. In this session, learn how Confluent, IBM and AWS are helping make streaming data immediately usable for analytics and AI. See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. Discover how this integration enables data engineers to reduce ingestion complexity, strengthen governance and put real-time data to work for analytics and AI with Amazon Athena. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.

title: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS (sponsored by Qlik)
speakers: Jason Hall (QlikTech, Inc.)
abstract: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams;Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK);Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
speakers: Sarang Bapat (United Airlines); John Morkel (Amazon Web Services); Subham Rakshit (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations are accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking

title: Trace Lineage From AI Endpoints and Models to Data
speakers: Nishchai JM (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every number in a dashboard and every answer from an AI agent rests on a chain of data you may not be able to see. Can you prove where it came from? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard one lineage graph connecting endpoints, models, jobs, and tables across your pipelines on Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena, anchored on the AWS Glue Data Catalog. We trace a production number back to the tables that fed it, work out what breaks before a schema change ships, and have an AI agent show the provenance of its own answer.

title: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
speakers: Melissa Kwok (AWS); Kelvin Lawrence (AWS)
abstract: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: What's new in Amazon SageMaker platform
speakers: Shikha Verma (AWS); Derek Chau (Cathay Pacific Airways); Brian Ross (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance, and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team needs.

title: Zero-Shot Demand Forecasting with Chronos 2, SMUS, and Quick Suite
speakers: saadari Adari (Amazon Web Services); Prakash Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Stockouts and overstocks quietly erode margin for retail and CPG brands, driving lost sales, markdowns, and working capital tied up in the wrong inventory. Traditional forecasting models take months to train and tune, and struggle with the cold-start problem for new products and locations. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to architect zero-shot demand forecasting pipelines using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with the Chronos 2 time-series foundation model, developed by the Amazon Science team and proven on Amazon's own retail and CPG demand at scale, requiring no historical model training. We walk through the end-to-end design: SMUS notebooks for rapid experimentation, Chronos 2 for multi-variate time series prediction, and Amazon Quick Suite for conversational analytics that let planners explore forecasts in natural language..

title: 10 tips for querying Apache Iceberg data with Amazon Redshift
speakers: Srishti Mittal (Amazon Web Services); Nita Shah (AWS)
abstract: Learn practical strategies for working with Apache Iceberg on Amazon Redshift — from schema design and file sizing to partition pruning, compaction, sort order optimization, predicate pushdown, materialized views, and metadata management. Walk away with an actionable checklist to improve your Iceberg workloads.

title: Agents can delete your data lake. Can you recover it? (sponsored by Rubrik)
speakers: Adam Rusho (Rubrik); Jérôme Cousin (TGS)
abstract: AI is multiplying the identities and agents that can change your AWS data. One over-scoped role or runaway agent can delete or overwrite the data your models depend on, in an S3 lake or Iceberg lakehouse. Replication copies a bad write, versioning is often off. How do you recover without a valid backup? Learn where recovery breaks across S3, Glue Data Catalog, S3 Tables, and databases and pipelines around them, then how Rubrik recovers petabytes in hours, restoring only what changed, critical data first, within your RTO. Resilience spans your estate. Hear how TGS built a ransomware-resilient platform with Rubrik. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

title: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Tim Stoakes (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.

title: Boost Apache Spark performance and reduce costs with AWS Analytics
speakers: Kalyan chakravarthi Janaki (Amazon Web Services); Suthan Dhas Phillips (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore best practices for building high-performing, cost-efficient Spark applications using AWS analytics data processing services. We'll discuss the AWS performance-optimized runtime for Apache Spark—delivering up to 4.5x faster execution across Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue—meaning faster jobs and lower compute spend. Explore flexible deployment models—long-running clusters, on-demand elasticity with EMR Serverless, Kubernetes integration with EMR on EKS, and Graviton instances for up to 30% cost reduction. We'll also highlight how Glue's auto scaling, Flex execution class, and Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines while optimizing costs.

title: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
speakers: Islam Elhamaky (AWS); Sachin Kulkarni (AWS)
abstract: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.

title: Build at scale real-time ingestion pipelines for Apache Iceberg tables
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
speakers: Pratik Patel (Amazon); Umesh Chaudhari (AWS)
abstract: Landing streaming data into Apache Iceberg at scale is a complex undertaking. In this chalk talk, we dissect practical reference architectures for real-time ingestion into Iceberg tables, covering Kafka to Flink, Kinesis to Firehose, and managed pipelines through Amazon S3 Tables. Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.

title: Building high-quality data products for AI agents
speakers: David Victoria (Amazon); Lakshmi Ramchandran Nair (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are only as effective as the data they rely on. This chalk talk focuses on how to build and manage high-quality data products and contextual information for use by AI agents. You'll learn how to deliver accurate, up-to-date, and well-governed data for AI systems, including context engineering, RAG strategies, fine-tuning dataset curation, and automated quality checks. We'll cover how to manage AI context, handle data drift, and perform classical data management activities in the Agentic AI world.

title: Building ontologies with Amazon Neptune
speakers: Jayaraman Sampath (AWS); Taylor Riggan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Build stablecoin infrastructure from key management to agentic payments
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: Nikolay Vlasov (Amazon Web Services Australia Pte. Ltd.); Munkyu Seong (AWS); Jinsung Huh (Amazon Web Service); Hun KIM (AWS); Sudhir Kalidindi (AWS)
abstract: Stablecoins are redefining payments and settlement infrastructure in financial services. In this session, build a production-ready stablecoin infrastructure on AWS spanning secure key management with AWS Key Management Service and and AWS Nitro Enclaves, multi-signature governance workflows, token minting/burning/swapping operations, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments for autonomous agent-to-agent transactions. Get hands-on experience building wallet infrastructure and executing USDC stablecoin operations end-to-end. Walk away with a working architecture that bridges traditional key management with the emerging agentic commerce paradigm.

title: Give your AI agent an expert-level playbook with the Agent Toolkit for AWS
speakers: Avichay Marciano (Amazon); Brandon Schur (AWS)
abstract: What if your AI agent could explore schemas, generate correct SQL, load data, and run migrations — all through the Agent Toolkit for AWS with expert-level context? In this chalk talk, we explore how the AWS MCP Server paired with packaged AWS Analytics skills give agents like Claude Code, Kiro, and Cursor deep AWS service expertise — from SQL syntax and metadata discovery to migration planning and performance tuning. Bring your toughest questions — we'll cover setup, agent workflows, and best practices for your environments.

title: Govern your context layer for AI agents with AWS Context
speakers: Leonardo Gomez Virahonda (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to carry your existing data permissions into a governed context layer your AI agents need to work accurately across structured and unstructured data. AWS Context assembles semantic data from your catalogs, glossaries, query logs, and access patterns into one governed context layer, honoring the governance contract placed on your data assets. Each user's identity flows through the agent so every answer is scoped to what they are authorized to see. We will whiteboard and interact on how identity propagates, how retrieval is filtered, and where permissions break.

title: Patterns for mitigating AI-powered security threats in financial services
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Culture of Security
speakers: Russell Lewis (AWS); Parth Pandit (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI-driven vulnerability identification creates elevated risks for financial services organizations as attackers find and exploit software and configuration flaws at machine speed. Patching alone is no longer sufficient. In this chalk talk, we explore mitigation patterns that help financial institutions reduce exposure and strengthen their defensive posture. Walk through how Amazon Inspector, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS Continuum, Kiro, and network isolation work together to detect, contain, and respond to AI-accelerated threats. Attendees will gain mitigation strategies and actionable next steps they can take back to their security teams.

title: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
speakers: David Zhang (Amazon); Mohit Saxena (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.

title: What's new with Amazon S3... and now files!
speakers: Shakhi Hali (AWS); Ben Grubin (AWS)
abstract: Twenty years of redefining storage, and Amazon S3 continues to evolve beyond objects to serve you wherever you are and however you work with data. This session highlights that evolution, led by the convergence of object and file storage with the launch of S3 Files, delivering full file system access to your S3 data without sacrificing scalability or economics you expect from S3. We also explore S3 Vectors for AI workloads, S3 Metadata for richer data discovery, and S3 Tables for managed Apache Iceberg data lakes. Come see what’s launched, what’s next, and how to put it all to work.

title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
speakers: Bhuvaneswari Subramani (Intuitive.ai); Ayyanar Jeyakrishnan (WellsFargo); Vivek Raja P S (Aivar Innovations)
abstract: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

title: Accelerating Apache Spark 4.1 workloads with AWS Analytics
speakers: Sekar Srinivasan (Amazon); Giovanni Matteo Fumarola (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Apache Spark 4.1 is the latest engine upgrade, and AWS is the best place to run it. Learn best practices for building high-performing Spark 4.1 applications using Amazon EMR. Explore what's new, from the ANSI-compliant type system and Variant data type to Spark Connect and Python-first APIs, and how the AWS performance-optimized runtime amplifies these improvements at scale. See how the Spark Troubleshooting and Upgrade agent accelerates migration by automatically identifying deprecated APIs and recommending code fixes, and how AWS Glue and Apache Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines with open table formats.

title: Agentic AI for manufacturing: Build a cross-domain digital thread
speakers: Scott Robertson (Amazon Web Services); Brian Anderson (AWS)
abstract: Manufacturing data lives in silos — from engineering systems through production lines. In this workshop, build an agentic digital thread: a knowledge-graph-powered AI system that unifies OT and IT data across the product lifecycle and answers cross-domain questions in real time. Using Amazon Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS IoT SiteWise, deploy agents that autonomously traverse connections from product design through production operations — linking engineering changes to equipment assets to quality events — without point-to-point integrations. Leave with a deployable reference architecture adaptable to any manufacturing environment.

title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Lambda
speakers: Stav Ochakovski (Eon); Ran Isenberg (Palo Alto Networks)
abstract: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

title: A practical guide to Apache Iceberg migration on AWS
speakers: Stefano Sandonà (Amazon Web Services); Salim Tutuncu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Lambda;Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL
speakers: Aditya Samant (Amazon); Vlad Vlasceanu (AWS)
abstract: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

title: Build AI-Powered Analytics with Conversational BI on Amazon Quick
speakers: Neeraj Kumar (AWS); salim khan (AWS)
abstract: Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline, from data ingestion to conversational consumption. Use Amazon Quick's Data Catalog to discover data, query it live without moving it into SPICE, then enrich and import metadata with semantics inherited to build natural-language Q&A. In this hands-on workshop, you start with seven raw banking tables: no catalog, no definitions. An agent inspects the data and builds the catalog for you. You ask questions in plain English and get answers. An agent generates a dashboard showing which top customers are slipping. Another agent, aware of the bank's compliance rules, checks every offer before it ships. Then you automate the full response as a Quick Flow and wrap it in a custom app your team can use. You leave with a working banking command center that agents built, and that you can rebuild in your own account using conversational analytics.

title: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift
speakers: Andre Hass (Amazon Web Services); Vinayaka Gangadhar (AWS (Amazon Web Services)); Ivan Fernandez Perea (Amazon Web Services); Ajay Kumar Govindaram (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language, but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions on preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

title: Building a Zero Trust for Agentic AI Practice: A Partner Framework
speakers: Krishna Prasad Prasad (Amazon Web Services Inc.); YaduKishore Tatavarthi (AWS); Henry Axelrod (AWS); Shashi Raina (AWS); Reet Takkar (AWS)
abstract: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

title: Building Managed Security Practices with AWS Security Hub Extended and Partners
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Patrick McDowell (Amazon Web Services); Yaton Bowens (AWS)
abstract: Your customers don't want more tools—they want outcomes. In this session, learn how AWS Security Hub Extended, AWS Artifact, and other tools combine to create a powerful foundation for partners delivering managed security and compliance services at scale. Security Hub Extended gives MSSPs a single pane of glass and OCSF-normalized findings that eliminate integration headaches. Pair this with our extended security portfolio to create the foundation for audit-ready compliance frameworks across financial services, healthcare, and public sector, and you have a differentiated "detect, respond, and prove compliance" offering your customers can't get elsewhere. Whether you're an MSSP building SOC-as-a-Service, an ISV integrating into the Security Hub ecosystem, or a consulting partner delivering compliance transformations, this session shows you the better together story of working with AWS.

title: Build orchestration agents for AWS Glue ETL
speakers: Raghu Prabhu (Amazon Web Services); Sushovan Basak (AWS); Vivek Shrivastava (AWS); John Oshodi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What happens when you give an AI agent the keys to your ETL infrastructure? In this builder session, you'll build an agentic workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that accepts natural language instructions and autonomously orchestrates ETL jobs on AWS Glue. Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

title: Closing the loop: using frontier agents for continuous governance
speakers: Emir Ayar (AWS); Peter Grainger (AWS); Charles Roberts (Amazon Web Services); Cameron Smith (AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE)); Ryan Dsouza (AMAZON)
abstract: Wire two AWS frontier agents into an automated find-and-fix security loop aligned to the Well-Architected Framework. AWS Security Agent pen-tests a web application and flags a privilege-escalation vulnerability. You author a DevOps Agent skill that queries findings through AWS Continuum MCP Server on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, correlating the operational symptom to the vulnerability in your codebase and generating a GitLab merge request, with human approval at every gate. Trigger the exploit, approve the fix, watch AWS Continuum revalidate it closed, and update your pipeline to block similar vulnerabilities before they reach customers. Automated detection, investigation, remediation, verification, and ongoing prevention closes the loop and provides continuous governance.

title: Danske Bank's AI City: Scaling AI agents across an enterprise
speakers: Kasper Tjørntved Davidsen (Danske Bank A/S); John Bustamante Madsen (Danske Bank); Anantharaman Seshadri (AWS)
abstract: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. Danske Bank started with a handful of generative AI experiments and now runs more than 40 use cases in production. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.

title: End-to-End ModelOps on SageMaker AI: Experiment to Production
speakers: Paolo Di Francesco (Amazon Web Services); Nisha Gambhir (AWS Proserve)
abstract: Hands-on workshop where practitioners experiment with SageMaker AI end-to-end ModelOps capabilities: onboard, build, govern, deploy, monitor. Attendees track experiments with managed MLflow, orchestrate repeatable training workflows with SageMaker Pipelines and built-in lineage tracking, register and version models in Model Registry with model cards and approval gates, deploy through CI/CD promotion pipelines, and monitor for drift and quality with Model Monitor. Governance such as access control, validation, approvals, and Responsible AI guardrails is embedded into every step. Attendees leave with a repeatable, governed path from experiment to production they can stand up within a week

title: Full-stack data agents using Box MCP and AWS
speakers: Oscar Carrasquero (AWS); Padmaraj Anand (AWS); Gopal Surapaneni (Amazon Web Services); Janardhan Molumuri (AWS); Chidambaram Muthappan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations struggle to assess contract compliance as terms live in unstructured documents while structured financial and risk data sit in operational databases across the enterprise. In this session, build an AI agent that performs real-time contract compliance analysis, bridging unstructured content stored in Box with operational structured data on AWS. Using Box MCP in AWS Marketplace, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Aurora, you implement a multi-MCP architecture, routing to Box for contract extraction and to AWS databases for operational data, producing auditable compliance determinations citing both unstructured content and structured data. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Give your AI agents business context with AWS Glue Data Catalog
speakers: Prasad Nadig (AWS); Luis Campos (AWS); Aritra Ghosh (Amazon); Joel Farvault (Amazon Web Services); Kunal Ghosh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. In this builders' session, learn how to turn the AWS Glue Data Catalog into a trust layer for AI agents. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Ground your agents with AWS Context and Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Hari Thatavarthy (Amazon); sandeep Adwankar (Amazon)
abstract: Agents are only as good as the context they're given. In this session, see how AWS Context makes the agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker more accurate and useful by grounding agents in business metadata. We'll show how context-aware agents like SageMaker Data Agent break complex requests into structured, multi-step plans, generate validated SQL, Python, and PySpark against your real data, and keep humans in the loop with built-in checkpoints. You'll learn practical techniques to feed the right context to your agents, connect additional sources, and turn a capable assistant into one that truly understands your environment.

title: Innovate faster, stay compliant: Innovation Sandbox for financial services
speakers: Peter DeVries (AWS); Gonzalo Escarrá (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Financial services organizations need to experiment fast while meeting regulatory and governance requirements. In this chalk talk, explore how organizations deploy Innovation Sandbox on AWS to give teams safe, ephemeral environments without compromising security posture. We’ll discuss real-world patterns for network isolation, automated guardrails via SCPs, and time-bound account lifecycles that satisfy risk committees and regulators. We’ll walk through how organizations balance developer autonomy with controls mapped to frameworks like SR 26-2 and OCC heightened standards, and you’ll leave with practical approaches for rolling out Innovation Sandbox on AWS while keeping compliance teams confident.

title: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
speakers: Steve Ash (Amazon AWS); Aditya Krishnan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.

title: Ontology-Powered AI Agents: Verifiable Decisions Across Manufacturing
speakers: Raja GT (Amazon Web Services); Vedanth Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Manufacturing stakeholders make dozens of high-velocity decisions daily. Each must be traceable, defensible, and grounded in enterprise knowledge and lifecycle data. Yet the systems informing these decisions remain siloed, and AI agents reasoning over this fragmented data cannot produce verifiable results. Ontologies solve this by structuring manufacturing knowledge so agents can trace decisions back to their source data. In this chalk talk, we show how ontology-grounded agents, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, make verifiable decisions across the lifecycle with a live demo. Attendees leave with a reference architecture, best practices, and a clear path to building verifiable AI agents for manufacturing.

title: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
speakers: Ayush Kanyal (AWS); Bappaditya Dutta (AWS)
abstract: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

title: Turn autonomous agents into accountable ones
speakers: Vijay Shekhar Rao (AWS); Michael Tschannen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."

title: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
speakers: Ram Vittal (Amazon); Anastasia Tzeveleka (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.

title: Your data, your engine: How open source and open standards power analytics on AWS
speakers: Ram Nottath (Amazon Web Services); Arun Shanmugam (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Open table formats and open-source engines like DuckDB give organizations the freedom to choose the right tool for each workload, from interactive dashboards and exploratory analytics to large-scale data processing, with no lock-in. In this session, learn how to capitalize these open tools to build on AWS and turn it into a competitive advantage for your business. We deep dive into the application of each engine, how they complement one another across the analytics lifecycle, and how data governance capabilities like catalog access, fine-grained governance, and consistent table management on AWS further simplify multi-engine architectures in production.

title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Yaniv Cadosh (Amazon Web Services); Brendan Paul (Amazon Web Services); Shimi Rokah (AWS)
abstract: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.

title: Accelerate analytics and AI with an open lakehouse architecture on Apache Iceberg
speakers: Brian Mitchell (AWS); Shruti Worlikar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Stop choosing between your data lake and data warehouse. Join this session to explore how to build a unified, open, and secure data lakehouse architecture, on Apache Iceberg. Learn how the lakehouse breaks down data silos and opens your data estate offering flexibility to use your preferred query engines and tools that accelerate time to insights. Learn about recent launches that improve data interoperability and performance, and enable large language models (LLMs) and AI agents to interact with your data. Discover robust security features, including consistent fine-grained access controls, attribute-based access control, and tag-based access control that help democratize data without compromises.

title: Accelerate Your FDE Journey: The Harness & FDE Delivery Kit
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK);Kiro
speakers: Dhana Vadivelan (AWS); Phani Kumar Lingamallu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The AWS FDE Delivery Kit replaces linear agent pipelines with delivery loops: each program's output enriches shared state and feeds the next. Live-coding: from plain-English intention to production CDK infrastructure, Bedrock agents with guardrails, and AgentCore via re-resolve cycles.

title: Amazon S3 Tables: A deep dive into storage built for Apache Iceberg
speakers: Amy Yu (Amazon Web Services); Yuri Zarubin (AWS)
abstract: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.
