title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Meric Degirmenci (AWS); Rickard Löfström (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

title: Autonomous Multi-Agent system for Manufacturing: Live Demo with Kiro
speakers: Christophe Renard (AWS); Mourad Alia (AWS)
abstract: To achieve the operational agility markets require, manufacturers are turning to AI agents that can reason and act autonomously across the product lifecycle. This session demonstrates how to rapidly build autonomous multi-agent systems using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Kiro that connect CMMS, MES, and ERP systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Watch a live demo where we use Kiro to develop specialized manufacturing agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root causes, and orchestrate corrective actions autonomously. Discover how Kiro's spec-driven development workflow compresses multi-agent system development from months to days. Leave with proven architecture patterns that you can apply to transform your production planning, supply chain optimization, and anomaly management processes.

title: Build a brand knowledge graph for retail and CPG AI
speakers: Martin Sakowski (AWS); John Mousa (Amazon Web Services); Matt Barbieri (Amazon Web Services); Liam Strye (Amazon Web Services); Imran Dawood (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Retail and CPG brands invest years building product expertise, from visual styling rules to ingredient pairing and formulation knowledge, that generic AI simply cannot replicate. In this builder session, you'll construct a Graph RAG solution that encodes brand-specific curatorial knowledge into an Amazon Neptune Analytics knowledge graph with multimodal vector embeddings. Using a CPG product catalog, you'll build graph schemas capturing formulation relationships, brand hierarchies, and cross-category pairing rules. Then see how vector similarity search combined with graph traversal enriches retrieval context before grounding Amazon Bedrock LLM responses. Leave with a working deployed architecture adaptable across retail and CPG.

title: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
speakers: Jayaraman Sampath (AWS); Hal Cooper (AWS); Kelvin Lawrence (AWS); Melissa Kwok (AWS); Dustin Brown (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
speakers: Pragnesh Shah (AWS); Mahesh Jadhav (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every organisation's modernization journey is unique — we whiteboard how to build, deploy, and share custom transformation agents using the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit — from orchestrator architectures and MCP patterns to one-command Bedrock AgentCore deployment. Bring your challenges.

title: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
speakers: Kelvin Lawrence (AWS); Taylor Riggan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.

title: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: George Agiasoglou (Amazon Web Services); Hisyam Jukifli (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

title: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL
speakers: Shayon Sanyal (AWS); Aditya Samant (Amazon)
abstract: How do you take an AI agent from a local prototype to a governed application that recovers from failure? In this session, follow a reference application through five phases: querying business data with SQL, connecting agents to Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, adding hybrid retrieval, deploying to production, and enabling durable workflows. See how Aurora PostgreSQL unifies relational data, pgvector embeddings, full-text search, and workflow state. Explore Strands Agents on Bedrock AgentCore, verify identity and enforce row-level security for data access, and govern tool calls with AgentCore Policy. Code walkthroughs show recovery from saved steps, idempotency to prevent duplicate actions, and audit records that make outcomes traceable.

title: Closing the academic advising gap with AI agents
speakers: Nityanand Singh (Amazon Web Services); Maria John (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Universities lose students to inadequate academic advising: advisors are overwhelmed, and students wait days for answers. In this chalk talk, we explore the end-to-end architecture of an AI student advising agent: specifying and building the agents with Kiro on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, connecting it to student record systems via MCP, adding guardrails for sensitive student welfare queries, and surfacing the agents to students through AWS Quick embedded in their existing LMS. We'll whiteboard real-world advising scenarios, turn them into agents you can evaluate, and discuss the trade-offs between automation and human escalation.

title: Constrain AI agents with permissions boundaries and Cedar in AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS IAM Access Analyzer
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: David Sokolik (Amazon Web Services); Ravid Glam (AWS)
abstract: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, and unconstrained permissions lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you build defense-in-depth governance for agentic workloads. You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.

title: Design a governed ontology in Neptune that any agent can query
speakers: Brad Bebee (AWS); Meet Bhagdev (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into a governed ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query. See how AI-assisted authoring cuts modeling from months to hours, where one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. The graph stays in your account.

title: Enterprise-Ready: How NetEase Governs AI at Scale
speakers: Dan He (NetEase, Inc.); Zhuobin Huang (AWS)
abstract: Learn how NetEase, one of the world's largest gaming companies, is building enterprise AI governance as AI adoption scales across the organization. Discover how Amazon Bedrock enables multi-model routing, cost controls, and team-level budget management to optimize AI usage. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. Learn why a platform-first approach to cost, access, and safety is critical for enabling AI innovation at enterprise scale.

title: Evaluate, Disclose, Safeguard: A Production-Readiness Framework for AI Agents
speakers: Gulcin Batmaz (Amazon Web Services); Nawaz Varda (AWS)
abstract: Every organization is building AI agents, but few have made it to production. You can't prove it works, you can't prove it's responsible, and compliance won't sign off. In this chalk talk, we walk through a production-readiness framework for AI agents on Amazon Connect. First, evaluation: measuring resolution with the Connect Simulation API to score AI agents on the same bar as human agents. Second, responsible AI: disclosure patterns that build trust, escalation triggers for sensitive journeys, and harm avoidance for regulated industries. Third, safeguards: defense-in-depth governance for agents that process refunds and access sensitive data, including asymmetric PII, MCP tool authorization for human confirmation, and automated escalation when confidence drops. Leave with a checklist: what to measure, what to disclose, what to block, and when to ship.

title: Event-driven AI agents for security triage with AWS Continuum
speakers: Lavanya Bandari (Amazon); Ashish Kumar (Amazon Web Services); Nikita Jaggi (AWS)
abstract: Security teams need to detect, correlate, and respond to threats faster than manual processes allow. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Continuum orchestrates event-driven AI agents that triage, investigate, and escalate security incidents in real time. We walk through how alerts from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub flow through Amazon EventBridge, triggering AWS Lambda functions that invoke agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with human-in-the-loop controls for high-severity events. Discover best practices for reducing alert fatigue, accelerating MTTR, and scaling security operations for financial services and other regulated industries where every response must be explainable and audit ready.

title: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Vishnu Vettrivel (Qualtrics); Saurabh Bhutyani (AWS); Varsha Velagapudi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.

title: How to decompose Oracle and SQL Server into purpose-built databases
speakers: Anand Bilgaiyan (AWS); Yogi Barot (AWS)
abstract: A monolithic traditional RDBMS databases serves transactions, reporting, and search, but serves none of them well. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard how to decompose a proprietary database into purpose-built layers on AWS, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional workloads, Aurora pgvector for semantic search and GenAI (RAG), and Amazon Redshift via zero-ETL for real-time analytics, for a smarter modernization approach. We'll walk through how this pattern eliminates licensing costs, removes ETL pipelines, and turns your operational data into an AI-ready platform. Come ready to whiteboard your decomposition use case.

title: How Workday built multicloud data interoperability foundation for Agentic AI
speakers: Avijit Goswami (Amazon Web Services); Shankar Ramachandran (AWS); Mehreen Ali (Workday)
abstract: As enterprises scale agentic AI, the hardest problem is often giving agents secure, governed access to data spread across multiple clouds. Physically copying the data between clouds introduces cost, latency, and governance risk. In this session, you will learn how Workday leverages Apache Iceberg catalog federation to build bidirectional, zero-copy integration that enables cross-cloud data access without duplicating or moving data. You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.

title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Prasanth Ponnoth (AWS); Milan Bavadiya (AWS)
abstract: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

title: Inside DuckDB and how AWS Analytics puts it to work
speakers: Eric Jones (AWS)
abstract: DuckDB has become one of the most talked-about innovations in analytics, and now the team behind it, DuckLabs, is part of AWS. In this session, dive deep into the architecture of DuckDB, the in-process analytical database that brings fast OLAP performance to laptops, serverless functions, and data pipelines. Learn how its vectorized execution engine, columnar storage, and zero-dependency design make it well suited for embedded analytics, local development, and edge processing. Explore real-world use cases, performance characteristics, and how DuckDB complements AWS analytics services, including Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon Redshift. Whether you're a data engineer, data scientist, or architect, gain the technical depth to put DuckDB to work.

title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
speakers: John Cherian (AWS); Anurag Singh (AWS)
abstract: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

title: NatWest: Embedding AI agents into the software delivery lifecycle
speakers: Rafael Mosca (AWS); Diana Kennedy (NatWest Group); Raj Dasoar (NatWest)
abstract: AI is moving beyond code completion to reshape how software is built. In this session, learn how NatWest, one of the UK's largest banks, uses Kiro and agentic AI to accelerate design, development, and delivery across its engineering organization. NatWest will share how it embeds AI into everyday engineering while meeting the demands of a highly regulated environment, from security and compliance guardrails to identity and access integration and governance. Explore how the team measures developer productivity and reinvents its delivery workflows. You’ll learn how to bring agentic development to your own engineering teams.

title: OAuth delegation patterns for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Fei Yuan (Amazon Web Services); Jeff Lombardo (AWS)
abstract: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, and delegating the right access without over-permissioning is hard. In this chalk talk, we use code examples to work through authorization delegation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. We cover the OAuth grant flows that matter for agents, including authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine calls, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. For each flow, you see which agent scenario it fits and when to choose it over the others.

title: Optimize performance and cost for archival data with Amazon S3
speakers: Howard Kang (AWS); Amita Marconda (Amazon)
abstract: Not all data needs frequent access, but it still needs the right retrieval strategy when called upon. In this chalk talk, learn how to design a cost-effective archival storage strategy using Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes. We cover how to analyze access patterns to identify archival candidates, automate data movement with S3 Lifecycle policies and S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and design restore workflows using S3 Batch Operations and S3 Event Notifications. Whether you're retaining compliance data for years or staging cold datasets for periodic analytics, leave with a practical framework for balancing retrieval performance against long-term storage costs.

title: Orchestrating AI agents for continuous code security hardening
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Owen Hawkins (AWS)
abstract: Agentic AI is increasing the rate at which organizations discover and fix security vulnerabilities — and the rate at which findings arrive faster than anyone can act on them. In this workshop, you'll build an agentic security hardening pipeline using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore: deterministic scanners fan out across code, dependencies, secrets, and infrastructure; reviewer and triage agents correlate and rank what comes back; and policy-as-code gates decide on demonstrated evidence rather than on agents agreeing. You'll learn how to decompose a security audit into parallelizable agent tasks, and how to keep a human holding every consequential decision before changes reach production.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
speakers: Kandha Sankarapandian (AWS); Roland Barcia (AWS)
abstract: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

title: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
speakers: Manjit Chakraborty (Amazon Web Services); Neeraj Roy (AWS)
abstract: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

title: Ship faster with AWS CloudFormation
speakers: Idriss laouali (Amazon Web Services); Diwakar Chakravarthy (Amazon.com)
abstract: AWS CloudFormation lets you manage infrastructure as code with increasing confidence and speed, whether you're deploying directly or through AI agents. In this chalk talk, we dive into the capabilities that shorten your dev-test cycle and keep deployments safe: deploy in seconds with Express mode, catch errors before deployment with pre-deployment validation, author templates faster using the CloudFormation Language Server in your IDE, connect AI agents to CloudFormation with the Agent Skill and MCP Server, reorganize stacks without disruption using Stack Refactoring, and prevent accidental overwrites with drift-aware change sets. Bring your templates and your toughest questions, we'll workshop solutions live.

title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Lambda
speakers: Jacky Chan (Beever AI Limited)
abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI
speakers: Richard Fan (ExpressVPN); Shaoyi Li (Pax Technology)
abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

title: Train and deploy large-scale models with governance at every step
speakers: Paulo Pontes Vieira de Aragao (Amazon Web Services); Amin Dashti (AWS)
abstract: Training a large-scale model is the easy part. Getting it into production with the right data flowing in, governance enforced, and multiple deployment paths ready is where most teams stall. This chalk talk works through how to build one training pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, bring in enterprise data that amplifies model value while respecting data protection policies, and deploy the same model into Amazon Bedrock for inference or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agent orchestration. Governance follows the model at every step. No bolted-on compliance. You leave with an architecture you can build against immediately.

title: What's new in Amazon Redshift
speakers: Naresh Chainani (AWS); Milind Oke (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Cut costs, query faster, and unify your warehouse and data lake without trade-offs. In this session, learn how new Graviton-powered RG instances deliver better price-performance, a built-in data lake engine lets you read and write Apache Iceberg tables in place, multi-warehouse architecture gives teams independent scale with shared data, and Redshift Serverless improvements let you get insights on your data without managing infrastructure. Whether you're consolidating on open table formats or building the analytics backbone for AI agents, walk away knowing exactly how to put these capabilities to work.

title: What's new in AWS Data Processing
services: Amazon Athena;Amazon EMR;Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA)
speakers: Kinshuk Pahare (Amazon); Anurag Singh (Netflix, Inc.); Bryan Liles (Amazon)
abstract: Explore the latest advancements in AWS Analytics designed to transform your data processing landscape. This session unveils powerful new capabilities across key services, including Amazon EMR for scalable big data processing, AWS Glue for seamless data integration, Amazon Athena for optimized querying, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) for complex workflow orchestration. Discover how these innovations can supercharge performance, optimize costs, and streamline your entire data ecosystem. Whether you're looking to enhance scalability, improve data integration, accelerate queries, or refine workflow management, join us to gain actionable insights that will position your organization at the forefront of data processing innovation.

title: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
speakers: Sophie Bacon (AWS); Sabrina Petruzzo (AWS)
abstract: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

title: Accelerate platform engineering on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Q Developer;Kiro
speakers: Sebastien Allamand (AWS); Shani Adadi Kazaz (Amazon)
abstract: Platform teams struggle to balance developer velocity with operational efficiency. Self-service platforms promise faster delivery, but require orchestrating multiple tools, managing infrastructure complexity, and maintaining governance. In this workshop, you'll build an Internal Developer Platform using Amazon EKS Capabilities, which provides fully managed Argo CD for continuous deployment, ACK for AWS resource management, and kro for Kubernetes resource orchestration. You'll deploy polyglot applications, implement progressive delivery strategies, and automate infrastructure management while leveraging AI to boost productivity. Leave with practical experience in platform engineering patterns to ship faster without sacrificing control. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Accelerate service onboarding with composable AI plugins
speakers: Aryan Desai (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Aditi Pendharkar (AWS)
abstract: Service onboarding workflows consume hours across security, risk, and governance teams through manual approvals, evidence gathering, and threat modeling. These tasks are auditable, repetitive, and ripe for agentic decomposition. In this chalk talk, we walk through a composable AI plugin pattern that decomposes service onboarding into lightweight modules any agentic client can consume. We discuss how each plugin integrates with any agentic client to execute governance checks end-to-end. We share architecture patterns, working code examples, and show you how to reduce security review time. You’ll leave with a decomposition pattern and an open-source repo to get started.

title: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
speakers: Abhishek Pandey (Amazon Web Services); Ankur Taunk (AWS)
abstract: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We walk through three memory patterns: episodic (past interactions), semantic (customer knowledge graphs), and procedural (learned resolution paths). We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. Bring your memory challenge and we'll design the persistence layer on the whiteboard.

title: Agents under oath: HIPAA-compliant agentic AI on AWS
speakers: Vignesh Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services); Ray Chang (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents in government healthcare don't just query databases. They reason, remember, and act. Each of those capabilities opens a new surface where protected health information (PHI) can leak model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. Traditional RBAC and encryption were not built for this. In this chalk talk, we will walk through a real prior authorization determination scenario together, map where PHI bleeds through an ungoverned agent and then redesign the architecture as a group — four trust zones, sixteen controls, all mapped to HIPAA Security Rule safeguards. Come ready to draw and debate.

title: Automate savings with AWS Billing and Cost Management services
services: AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS Compute Optimizer;AWS Savings Plans
speakers: Haritha Chitalia (AWS); Savanna Jensen (AWS)
abstract: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. Bring your questions and challenges.

title: Best practices for production agents on AgentCore, with Nasdaq
speakers: Isaac Privitera (Amazon Web Services); Mike O'Rourke (Nasdaq Omx Group, Inc.)
abstract: Learn best practices for the full agent lifecycle on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Ship agents to production with microVM isolation, persistent memory, and any framework. Use gateway to connect agents to MCP servers, knowledge bases, and APIs with automatic authentication. Trace model calls with OpenTelemetry-compatible observability and run continuous evaluations. Nasdaq joins to share how its GenAI platform empowers 10,000 employees build agents for research, coding, and workflow automation. Hear how Nasdaq scales agent runtime infrastructure and handles multi-account isolation and agent identity, and the operational patterns required to run agentic AI reliably in a regulated financial services environment.

title: Bring Your Own Ontology: Ground Amazon Quick in Enterprise Context
speakers: Tom Ron (Amazon Web Services); Fatima Khakwani (AWS)
abstract: Enterprise questions rarely have answers in a single document. Your business runs on connections — customers to products, teams to processes, risks to regulations — but vector search doesn't see any of that. In this chalk talk, we show how to ground Amazon Quick in your enterprise context by integrating it with a knowledge graph built from your domain knowledge. We'll walk through how we built this pattern using GraphRAG for real customers and the results they achieved. Then we'll open the whiteboard — bring your toughest use case and we'll sketch your ontology live, showing how Quick would traverse it to deliver dramatically better answers.

title: Build an AI-powered AWS Backup analyst and remediate with AgentCore
speakers: Aram Koukia (Amazom Development Center Canada); Azat Penjiyev (AWS); Siddhesh Chavan (Amazon Web services); Daimon Songer (Amazon); Soumyajit Das (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Few teams have the capacity to continuously audit their backup posture across accounts and regions. AI agents can do that work and recommend fixes while keeping you in control. In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and run a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval on AWS Bedrock AgentCore Harness. The system runs in your own environment after the session.

title: Build a payment-enabled agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments
speakers: Jay Galvin (Amazon Web Services); Khozaima Motiwala (AWS); Anil Nadiminti (Amazon Web Services); Deepika Prabhakara (AWS); Karim Akacem (AWS)
abstract: AI agents that can autonomously transact open new possibilities in financial services—from purchasing market data to paying for risk scores in real time. In this builders' session, you'll configure an AI agent using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments with the open source x402 protocol. You'll set up payment managers, connect to data providers, define budget controls with IAM policies, and monitor transactions with Amazon CloudWatch. Leave with a working agent that autonomously transacts, reasons about costs, and delivers results end to end.

title: Build better, review faster: AI-Powered Well-Architected reviews
abstract: Periodic reviews can't keep pace with infrastructure that changes daily. In this hands-on workshop, stand up the AWS Well-Architected Agent for continuous, goal-driven reviews across a multi-account environment. Configure agent profiles, cross-account role chaining, and business goals that prioritize across Cost Optimization, Security, Resilience, and Performance pillars. See how the agent enriches Trusted Advisor, Compute Optimizer, and Resilience Hub signals with cross-pillar trade-off analysis. Run pre-deployment reviews against CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform, then remediate through AI-generated SOPs. Wire recommendations into CI/CD via the Well-Architected API. For architects, platform engineers, and operations leads who want always-on architectural governance in their delivery lifecycle.

title: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
speakers: Adam Richter (AWS); Jason Wu (Amazon)
abstract: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. In this chalk talk, we'll map an AI workload from architecture to bill, then apply a practical framework to measure, attribute, optimize, and govern its cost and value. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

title: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
speakers: Arne Knoeller (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. In this chalk talk, learn how to architect and manage cross-enterprise agentic orchestration using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer

title: Building enterprise agent platform on AgentCore
speakers: Chaitra Mathur (AWS); Anubhav Mangal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.

title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
speakers: Jordi Macià Ferrer (Amazon Web Services); David Christian (AWS)
abstract: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

title: Build Multi-Agent Workflows with Amazon Quick, MCP & AgentCore
speakers: Josh Anderson (AWS); Vishnu Elangovan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Design and build a multi-agent system inside Amazon Quick where specialized agents collaborate to automate complex business processes. Connect to enterprise systems through MCP servers on Bedrock AgentCore, implement inter-agent communication, configure OAuth 2.0 authentication, and deploy autonomous workflows using Quick Flows. Modeled after production deployments running 12+ coordinated agents across ERP, finance, and procurement, you'll leave with a working multi-agent solution you can replicate in your own environment.

title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Oscar Diaz Cordovez (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.

title: Configure Security & Governance Controls for Amazon Quick
speakers: Marshall Bunch (Amazon Web Services); Leo Mentis Raj Selvaraj (AWS)
abstract: Implement comprehensive security and administrative controls for Amazon Quick. Practice configuring identity integration, access policies, and data governance frameworks. Learn to establish monitoring, auditing, and compliance controls that meet enterprise requirements. Work through scenarios covering user management, content governance, and security best practices for Quick Suite environments in production.

title: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
speakers: Melody Yang (AWS); Narendra Gupta (Amazon)
abstract: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

title: Drive AI and ML ROI with cost-efficient data analytics on AWS
speakers: Imtiaz (Taz) Sayed (Amazon); Aneesh Chandra PN (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Delivering ROI for AI and ML at enterprise scale demands more than just great models — it requires a data and analytics foundation engineered for cost efficiency from day one. This session examines different cost efficiency levers that pair AWS data and analytics services with AI/ML workloads to maximize price-performance. We explore patterns including right-sizing your data infrastructure for training, inference, feature extraction, ETL pipelines and selecting optimal storage formats to minimize costs. You'll learn how to instrument cost observability across your analytics stack, apply tagging strategies for AI workload attribution, and implement governance guardrails that prevent runaway spend — turning your data foundation into a competitive advantage for ML and AI delivery.

title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
speakers: Madhu Bussa (Amazon); Mike George (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

title: From rules to reasoning: Build an intelligent tagging compliance agent with AgentCore
speakers: Avi Harari (AWS); Gautam Bhaghavatula (Amazon Web Services); Francesco Provino (AWS); Nour Shlian (Amazon); Ibrahim Cesar (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: AWS Config rules detect missing tags, but what about resources where the correct tag value isn't obvious? In this builder session, you'll create an AI agent using AgentCore that goes beyond detection to intelligent remediation. Your agent analyzes resource context, account ownership, VPC placement, creator identity, naming patterns to infer correct tag values, and handles ambiguous cases by requesting human input. Start where Config rules end: not just "is it tagged?" but "what should the tag be?"

title: How Mercedes-Benz accelerates engineering and production with AI
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Neptune
speakers: Daniel Schleicher (AWS); Jan-Peter Krämer (Mercedes-Benz Group AG)
abstract: Mercedes-Benz is using agentic AI on AWS to transform how vehicles are brought to life, from engineering to production. Hear how Mercedes-Benz is using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to accelerate engineering for 14,000 engineers—building specialized AI agents that reason over millions of interconnected artifacts, compressing specification generation by 90%, from 35 weeks to 3.5. On the factory floor, discover how Mercedes used AWS to build a fully cloud-native manufacturing execution system orchestrating 1M+ vehicles annually, with AI-powered quality intelligence providing rapid root-cause analysis and digital twins helping optimize throughput. Walk away with real-world lessons for deploying industrial AI at scale.

title: How RBC built a regulated multicloud platform
speakers: Chris Brandon (Amazon Web Services); Vinh Tran (RBC); Ernani Cecon (Royal Bank of Canada)
abstract: Enterprises running regulated workloads across multiple clouds face a compounding challenge: every platform decision — databases, message buses, orchestration — deepens lock-in and complicates compliance. The Royal Bank of Canada chose a different path. Over seven years, RBC built a multicloud Kubernetes platform spanning AWS, Azure, and on-premises, purpose-built for financial services under multi-jurisdictional oversight. RBC shares how they eliminated vendor lock-in by migrating to open-source databases and messaging, established a "golden path" that lets teams deploy to any cloud without rearchitecting, and extended that foundation into agentic AI operations for automated root-cause analysis and remediation. Walk away with a practical playbook for building a compliant, portable multicloud platform that strengthens your security posture at every layer.

title: Implementing agentic AI solutions on-premises and at the edge
speakers: Fernando Galves (Amazon Web Services); Kyle Palasti (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-premises data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera)
speakers: Dipankar Mazumdar (Cloudera, Inc.)
abstract: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow. Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: Leverage the power of MCP servers for resource inventory and compliance
speakers: Pal Patel (Amazon); Francisco (Chico) Ferreira (AWS)
abstract: AI agents can now interact with AWS services through the Model Context Protocol. In this code talk, we live-build a governance agent that uses MCP to query AWS Config for resource configurations. You'll see how to construct compliance checks, detect configuration drift, and trigger automated remediation using natural language all powered by Config's recording and advanced query capabilities. We explain the architecture decisions and trade-offs so you can adapt this pattern to your own governance workflows.

title: Modernize SAP business processes with agentic AI on AWS
speakers: Shirli Cohen (Amazon); Stephan Kremer (AWS)
abstract: Enterprise processes span SAP for ERP, Salesforce for CRM, and ServiceNow for ITSM, connected by aging, brittle integrations that are slow to change. Agentic AI offers a better path: replacing point-to-point integrations with agents that reason across applications. In this workshop, you modernize an SAP-centric business process by orchestrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents over Model Context Protocol, including the AWS for SAP MCP Server. You implement cross-application use cases spanning finance, supply chain, and operations then leave with a deployable reference architecture for moving from custom integrations to agent-orchestrated workflows.

title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Hoseong Seo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.

title: One Context Layer, Every Surface: Enterprise Knowledge for Agents That Work Anywhere
speakers: Suren Raju (Amazon); Josh DeMuth (AWS)
abstract: Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.

title: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
speakers: David Petrocelli (Caylent); Pablo Inchausti (Caylent)
abstract: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.

title: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
speakers: Swapna Bandla (Amazon); Austin Groeneveld (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to build a modern, streaming analytics solution for real-time data processing and power it with agentic AI capabilities to analyze events and extract patterns for actionable responses. This session will provide a hands-on experience on building a streaming solution using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for complex event processing, and Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock Agent Core to take immediate action. Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

title: Processing PII without exposing it using AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computin
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EMR;AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: Sathish Kumar Prabakaran (Amazon Webservices India Pvt. Ltd); Abhishek Jawali (Amazon Web Services India Private Limited)
abstract: How do you process PII data at scale without giving your data pipeline access to the plaintext? In this workshop, you combine AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing with Amazon EMR on EKS to build a high-assurance screening system. AWS Nitro Enclaves provides isolated compute environments within EC2 instances to protect highly sensitive data. Encrypted records are sent to an enclave, where data is decrypted only after AWS KMS verifies the enclave's cryptographic attestation. Screening rules are applied and only the decision is returned. Plaintext never leaves the enclave boundary. The pattern generalizes to any workload processing highly sensitive data at scale.

title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Siamak Ziraknejad (Amazon); Dani Mitchell (Amazon Web Services); Aakash Upadhyay (Amazon Web Services); Nabil Ezzarhouni (AWS); Sunita Koppar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.

title: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
speakers: Francisco Fagas (AWS); Vimala Pydi (AWS); Oren Waldman (Amazon Web Services); Aditya Chaphekar (Amazon Web Services); Vineedh George (AWS)
abstract: Enterprise data teams maintain ETL pipelines built on legacy tools like stored procedures, custom bash scripts, IBM DataStage and others, that resist migration due to undocumented dependencies. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.

title: Red team CTF: when auth and guardrails aren't enough
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: JaQuan Thompson (AWS); Mac Stevens (AWS)
abstract: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
speakers: Sreekumar Nair (Amazon Web Services Singapore Private Limited); Anand Bilgaiyan (AWS)
abstract: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.

title: Teaching Quick to Remember and Connect with Memory and Knowledge Graphs
speakers: Thomas Delteil (Amazon Web Service)
abstract: Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn't remember what worked yesterday, can't tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how Amazon Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We'll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up — bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.

title: The AgentCore Governance Loop: Policy, Guardrails, Observability
speakers: Harpreet Singh Siddhu (Penn Mutual Life Insurance)
abstract: Building an agent takes an afternoon. Operating it safely across a team takes architecture. In this session learn how to build a multi-agent reference platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and walk the full governance loop including cataloging agents for discovery, enforcing what they can do with Cedar policy at the gateway, filtering what they can say with Guardrails, and tracing behavior through observability. You will learn where the pieces integrate cleanly and where the seams break. You leave with a governance reference architecture you can adapt to any agentic workload, plus the lessons the documentation leaves out.

title: Trust but verify: Building the audit loop for AI agents in production
speakers: Justin Ossai (Amazon Web Services); Bhavini Bhatia (Amazon Web Services); Farzin Bagheri (AWS); Simone Pomata (Amazon Web Services); Vinodkumar Mandalapu (AWS)
abstract: An AI agent can answer every request successfully and still make the wrong decision. In this builders’ session, you will build an end-to-end audit loop on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using Amazon CloudWatch for traces, AgentCore Evaluations to apply an LLM-as-a-judge against business rules, and AWS DevOps Agent to investigate alarms. Then watch a customer service agent refund a customer without required human approval, while traces show zero errors. Reconstruct the decision, and see the loop automatically surface what error monitoring misses.

title: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
speakers: Abhimanyu Siwach (Amazon); Eashank Kaushik (AWS)
abstract: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.

title: Unlocking SAP Data with AI: From Zero-ETL to Agentic Automation
speakers: Ramkrishna Borhade (Amazon); Pavol Masarovic (AWS)
abstract: Critical business data remains locked inside SAP ERP and BW systems, limiting real-time insights and AI-driven automation. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to break down data silos using a modern, cost-effective architecture without expensive ETL pipelines. Explore a unified analytics strategy spanning Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services that enables end-to-end SAP data modernization. Then, build with the AWS for SAP MCP Server, enabling agentic AI to orchestrate across SAP, Salesforce, and AWS without writing code.

title: A deep dive on IAM policy evaluation
aoi: Well-Architected Framework;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Matt Luttrell (Amazon); Khaled Sinno (AWS)
abstract: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising. We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.

title: Agentic commerce: shopping assistants to agent-ready infrastructure
speakers: Aditya Pendyala (Amazon Web Services); Adler Oliveira (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents are reshaping how consumers discover and purchase products, and retail and CPG brands have a massive opportunity to meet them where they are. This chalk talk covers both sides of the agentic commerce stack. First, we walk through how retailers can launch conversational shopping customized to their catalog and brand voice in weeks with the Agentic Shopping Assistant on AWS, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and inspired by Amazon's own AI shopping experience. Then we explore how to make your platform discoverable by external AI agents through structured product feeds, headless APIs, and payment orchestration for machine-initiated transactions.

title: Agentic fairness: Practical methods to detect bias in AI-driven decisions
speakers: Bharathi Srinivasan (AWS); Denis V Batalov (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents are increasingly making real-world decisions — approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts — yet most fairness testing still focuses on whether chatbots use offensive language. This gap creates real business and regulatory risk. Join this session to explore how to assess whether your agentic AI systems apply equitable treatment across chosen demographic attributes using defined fairness criteria. Through hands-on examples spanning financial services, customer support, and commerce, discover how to move from language-level toxicity checks to decision-level fairness audits. Learn to identify disparate treatment, choose appropriate fairness metrics for your use case, and implement testing frameworks that catch bias where it matters most: in the outcomes that affect people's lives.

title: Agents at the Gate: Governing AI in EC2 Image Builder
speakers: Rielah De Jesus (Amazon Web Services); Smriti Ohri (Amazon Web Services); Maksim Poletaev (AWS); Malini Chatterjee (AWS); Sabha Parameswaran (Amazon)
abstract: EC2 Image Builder pipelines sprawl fast, and frontier agents that run for hours unattended need guardrails. In this builders' session, decompose Image Builder operations into reusable agent skills run via Kiro, Claude Code. Author AWSTOE components and orchestrate workflows, then harden images and scan for CVEs. Mid-build, a WaitForAction step pauses the pipeline and hands the image to AWS Security Agent to pentest; what it finds decides whether the build ships, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval. Leave with a reusable skill library and governance pattern.

title: AI discipline: UCLA's data foundation and framework for saying no
speakers: Mary Strain (Amazon Web Services); Aditya Singh (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invested in their data foundation first. Their large-scale data modernization—Bruin Cloud and the campus Data Hub—created a unified, governed data environment across a sprawling research university, but it wasn't enough. As AI demand surged, Deputy CIO Veronica Garcia and her team built a disciplined product management approach to evaluate, prioritize, and scale AI use cases against UCLA's mission. Learn how UCLA’s technical architecture accelerated data modernization, the framework used to determine AI priorities, and the governance model that keeps it all aligned that launched high-impact use cases from increasing fundraising, advancing research, and supporting student safety and success.

title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
speakers: Kobe Xu (Deloitte)
abstract: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.

title: Architecting firewalls on AWS: a layered defense strategy
speakers: Patrick Duffy (Amazon Web Services); Jonathan Woods (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: With automated traffic now more than half of the web, a single firewall layer can't separate good bots from L7 attacks. This chalk talk covers how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including firewall patterns attached to AWS Transit Gateway. Then we dig into the tradeoffs, including centralized versus distributed inspection, cost versus latency, and when one service can carry the load and when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we whiteboard a design for your environment.

title: Architecting for digital sovereignty with AWS Hybrid Cloud solutions
speakers: Sherry Lin (Amazon); Lakshmi VP (AWS)
abstract: This session uses real-world case studies to understand how AWS hybrid cloud architectures such as AWS Local Zones, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS Outposts help customers meet their digital sovereignty needs. It examines data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and security guardrail options available in hybrid cloud solutions. It then shows how to configure governance controls, including Service Control Policies (SCPs), to help customers comply with regulatory requirements. Finally, it covers how to detect and prevent unauthorized data flows between hybrid infrastructure and the parent Region.

title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
speakers: Piyush Mattoo (AWS); Abhishek Nanda (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
speakers: Rachna Rachna (AWS); Isha Dalal (Amazon)
abstract: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

title: Authenticating workloads to the outside world
speakers: Fei Yuan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your workloads and agents authenticate to external systems today mostly via individual OAuth implementations, secrets in config files, and custom refresh logic owned by separate teams. In this chalk talk, we'll explore patterns for centralizing how workloads obtain, manage, and govern credentials for non-native services. We'll diagram a reference architecture covering control, data, and governance planes, walk through real-world authentication flows and discuss how to design policies that control which workloads can access which external credentials.

title: Automated compliance evidence from day one
speakers: Nicole Klatt (AWS); Pal Patel (Amazon); Marc Luescher (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Bill Ohlson (AWS); Desiree Brunner (AWS)
abstract: Your compliance team spends weeks collecting evidence manually before every audit. Automated evidence collection eliminates that burden from day one. In this builders' session, you'll learn how to leverage AWS GRC services, including AWS Config, AWS Organizations, AWS CloudTrail, and Control Catalog, to configure automated evidence collection, map controls to your target framework, use the AI compliance agent to validate both technical controls and procedural policies, and build continuous drift detection that alerts you before your next audit finds the gap.

title: Automate your landing zone and network migration with AWS Transform
services: AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK);AWS Control Tower;AWS Transform
speakers: Suhail Fouzan (Amazon Web Services); Todd Gruet (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Designing landing zones and translating on-premises networks into cloud-native architectures is complex and time-consuming. AWS Transform automates both. In this workshop, you'll see the landing zone agent analyze your requirements and deploy AWS Control Tower, organizational units, service control policies, and workload accounts as infrastructure as code. Then the network agent translates VMware networking components or firewall configurations into VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateways with hub-and-spoke or isolated topologies, ready for deployment in CDK or Terraform modules. Laptop required.

title: AWS Serverless developer experience
speakers: Stephen Liedig (Amazon Web Services); Paul Nobuo Okada (Amazon Web Services Japan)
abstract: The AWS Serverless Developer Experience (SDE) workshop is a hands-on workshop that immerses developers in building serverless solutions. It covers composing serverless applications, event-driven architecture principles, serverless observability, open-source tools, and deployment automation, and is available in Python, Typescript, Java, or .NET runtime. The workshop aims to accelerate your serverless maturity through a real-world use case, challenging you to understand the “why” behind the design decisions, and their implementation, as you complete the solution and apply Serverless best practices.

title: Breathing Life into Game Worlds with Amazon Neptune & GraphRAG
speakers: JP Velasco (AWS); Heungsu Ha (AWS); matthew nimmo (AWS); Yeonho Lee (AWS)
abstract: Static NPC dialogue can't unlock rich game worlds. This session shares a production pattern using Amazon Neptune, Bedrock GraphRAG, and the "Entity as Agent" approach. We will live-demo natural-language character relationship search, in-character AI dialogue, and in-game party composition recommendations.

title: Build agentic automations for business processes with Amazon Quick Automate
speakers: Reagan Rosario (AWS); Zuhayr Raghib (AWS)
abstract: In this session, learn how to build an enterprise-grade automation using Amazon Quick Automate. Through a financial services example, explore how specialized AI agents work together to handle complex interactions across web pages and business applications. You'll create a production-ready automation featuring custom agents that leverage knowledge and tools to transform a merchant onboarding process. Using Quick Automate's chat based authoring and visual studio, you'll configure a workflow with multiple agents, integrate with multiple tools, test and debug the workflow, and then deploy it using robust enterprise controls. Walk away knowing how to develop agentic automations for real-world use cases.

title: Build Agentic Video Streaming Observability Using Kiro and Bedrock
speakers: Osmar Bento Junior (Amazon Web Services); Dirk Boekee (AWS Elemental); Adrian Ramos (Amazon Web Services); Devendra Sharma (Amazon Web Services); Abhimanyu Varshney (UOM, Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Media operations teams struggle to correlate issues across complex live streaming pipelines. In this hands-on session, build an agentic video observability and analytics application using Kiro and Amazon Bedrock that monitors the entire live streaming chain using AWS Elemental MediaConnect, MediaLive, MediaPackage, MediaTailor and Amazon CloudFront. Deploy AI agents using Strands Agents SDK and MCP servers to ingest, visualize, and investigate end-to-end QoE/QoS analytics across three layers: origin health, CDN performance, and client-side CMCD telemetry. Learn how to create a unified dashboard and natural language interface for streaming quality investigation across every pipeline stage.

title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
speakers: Melissa Kwok (AWS); Varma Gottumukkala (Amazon Web Services); Taylor Riggan (Amazon Web Services); Don Simpson (AWS); Chun Schiros (AMAZON)
abstract: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
speakers: Mikhail Vaynshteyn (Amazon Web Services); Muthu Pitchaimani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
speakers: David H Gardner (AWS); Varma Gottumukkala (Amazon Web Services); Kevin Willis (Amazon); Don Simpson (AWS); Chun Schiros (AMAZON)
abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
speakers: André Stoll (Amazon Web Services); Uri Segev (AWS)
abstract: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

title: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
speakers: Kahu Tawhai (Amazon Web Services); Nelson Martinez (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework.
