We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

title: Building serverless applications with Terraform
speakers: Lavanya Tangutur (Amazon); Debasis Rath (Amazon Web Servcies)
abstract: Master the integration of serverless technology with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform on AWS. In this hands-on workshop, learn to efficiently define, deploy, and maintain serverless architectures—from Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints to DynamoDB tables and EventBridge rules. Whether you're new to Terraform or looking to apply it to serverless workloads, you'll gain practical experience writing reusable modules, managing state, and automating deployments across environments. Walk away with patterns you can immediately apply to your own serverless projects. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build Provable Zero-Trust Agents with Automated Reasoning checks
speakers: Nafi Colette Diallo (Amazon); Wale Akinfaderin (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

title: Build your iOS CI/CD pipeline with AI agents on EC2 Mac
speakers: Markus Weyerhaeuser (Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL); Scott Malkie (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build iOS CI/CD pipelines on Amazon EC2 Mac using AI-powered workflows with Kiro CLI and AWS MCP Server. Define infrastructure as declarative specs while AI agents guide deployment, explain concepts, and validate configurations. This hands-on workshop covers EC2 Mac architecture, dedicated hosts, Xcode automation, GitLab setup, and CloudWatch monitoring through interactive AI modules. Learn to collaborate with agents and balance automation with understanding. Gain practical experience in both EC2 Mac operations and modern spec-driven, AI-assisted development workflows for Apple platforms.

title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
speakers: Ryan Tan (Amazon Web Services); Megan Sattler (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: CEO Keynote
speakers: Barbara Karuth-Zelle (Allianz SE); Matt Garman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join AWS CEO Matt Garman for the re:Invent 2026 CEO Keynote as he shares the latest innovations powering the agentic era. From AI infrastructure and inference to data, agent platforms, and the software agents AWS is building, see how AWS gives you the depth, breadth, and integration to build what's next with new announcements and stories from customers already doing it.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
speakers: John Mallory (Amazon Web Services); Mike Houle (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

title: Citizens Bank: Building AI-Native CX from Vision to Production
abstract: Financial services customers expect fast, personalized service, but compliance, security, and regulatory requirements make automation a high-stakes challenge. Discover how Amazon Connect Customer enables financial institutions to design agentic customer experiences, where AI self-service blends autonomous reasoning with deterministic guardrails for identity verification, fraud checks, and regulatory disclosures. Learn how business teams, not only engineers, build and refine these experiences, automating complex interactions like account servicing, disputes, and payments while maintaining full compliance and governance. See how Citizens Bank lifted containment by 30 points, elevated CSAT, and transformed their contact center without compromising trust.

title: Closing the compliance loop when agents change your infrastructure
speakers: David Sokolik (Amazon Web Services); JaQuan Thompson (AWS)
abstract: AI agents and automated pipelines now change your infrastructure faster than any review can keep up, and not every change comes through CloudFormation. In this workshop, you'll close the compliance loop end to end: author a CloudFormation Hook that enforces encryption and tagging before deployment, then extend the same logic into an AWS Config custom rule with CloudFormation Guard so out-of-band changes get caught continuously. You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.

title: Cocktails to Code Building AI Bartenders with Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Jimmy Dahlqvist (Sambla Group)
abstract: Plain-language AI orders fail if models hallucinate items that are out of stock. I built a reliable AI bartender grounded strictly in live inventory data. This session covers how an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock uses Strands Agents, AgentCore, and MCP tools to fetch real-time menus. We will dive into the serverless architecture, see what breaks during live text streaming, and evaluate the cost versus performance tradeoffs of production grounding. You will leave with a reusable pattern and the repository to build reliable, data-driven agents.

title: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
speakers: Jacob Cravinho (AWS); Matt Boland (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. Implement an MCP server with versioned tools, wire it to AgentCore Gateway for discovery and invocation, then expose an entire Step Functions workflow, human-in-the-loop gates and all, as a single callable tool. Add scoped agent identity, watch an unauthorized call get blocked, then an authorized one go through. Walk away with a repeatable playbook for turning existing APIs into agent-ready tools.

title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
aoi: Application Security;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Cryptography and Post-Quantum
speakers: Jonathan Herzog (Amazon Web Services); Ruben Merz (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What if you need to process sensitive data without exposing it to the system performing the computation? In this hands-on workshop, use fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to evaluate selected ML models while inputs remain encrypted and only the data owner decrypts the results. Work through encrypted inference for medical images, spam messages, and financial transactions in Amazon SageMaker Studio, then deploy a validated FHE model bundle to an AWS Lambda serving path. Examine the architecture, trust boundaries, performance constraints, and operational trade-offs that determine where FHE is practical today. Leave with concrete AWS patterns for privacy-sensitive and regulated workloads.

title: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Michael Davis (AWS); Nicholas Hans Jaeger (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

title: Data & AI Keynote
speakers: Andy Warfield (Amazon Web Services); Swami Sivasubramanian (AWS); Francessca Vasquez (AWS)
abstract: The future is already here...it's just not evenly distributed in production. Most teams have agents that shine in a demo and stall before they do real work. The ones who get to production changed three things: how agents reach their data, how they measure what agents are worth, and the limits they set. Join Swami Sivasubramanian and Andy Warfield to learn how to make these same shifts in your organization.

title: DDI Architecture Patterns: DNS, DHCP, and IPAM at AWS
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Zero Trust;Identity & Access Management
abstract: Join us to explore architecture patterns for DDI - DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (IPAM). This session covers approaches for resolving DNS across hybrid and multicloud environments, managing private and public domains, and unifying address management for consistent governance and visibility. Walk away with best practices that simplify DDI operations at scale.

title: Democratizing precision time on EC2: make clocks work for you
speakers: Shamik Chakraborty (Amazon); Josh Levinson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Distributed systems builders have avoided relying on wall clock time for anything critical. Times are changing. Amazon Time Sync now delivers microsecond accuracy on EC2, making clock precision a feature, not a bug, in your system design. We whiteboard how customers in databases, AI, financial services, and media approach design in new ways, and share our open source ClockBound work on the clock error bound as a standard interface for your applications.

title: Deploy without drama: Safe, automated releases on AWS
speakers: Michael Michael (AWS); Anastasia Giannoulas (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Releasing software shouldn't mean holding your breath. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and AppConfig help you automate safe, hands-off deployments to Amazon EC2, ECS, and Lambda across accounts and Regions. Learn to apply canary and linear traffic-shifting strategies, wire CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback, and use stage-level conditions to gate promotions on integration tests. Whether you're deploying a single service or orchestrating hundreds, leave with patterns for zero-downtime releases you can trust.

title: Designing security governance for your AWS multi-account foundation
services: AWS Control Tower;AWS Organizations;AWS Security Hub
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Culture of Security;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Avik Mukherjee (Amazon Web Services); Ishai Shvartz (Amazon)
abstract: AWS gives you flexibility to design your multi-account environment, but customer needs guidance choosing the right security services to deploy, where, and how to validate the deployment against AWS best practices. This session shows how the AWS Security Reference Architecture provides a prescriptive security blueprint you layer on top of your account governance foundation. Using whiteboarding, you cover OU design, service prioritization, centralized vs. distributed placement, design considerations, validation with SRA Verify, and deployment acceleration. You leave with a tailored governance model ready for implementation.

title: Designing the AWS Secure Research Environment: Architecture deep dive
services: AWS Control Tower;AWS Organizations;AWS Security Hub
speakers: Devin Hicks (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Chris Riddle (AWS)
abstract: Discover how the AWS Secure Research Environment (SRE) helps research institutions stand up NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 infrastructure. Explore the architecture: Landing Zone Accelerator (LZA) customization, multi-account strategy with Control Tower Account Factory, preventive SCPs versus detective controls, Network Firewall egress, and automated evidence collection feeding Security Hub. No setup is required. Using a simulated pipeline, you work through and gain a deep understanding of the LZA configuration customizations an SRE needs, customize them for your organization, and leave with your own SRE config files. We provide next-step instructions for deploying those configs in a real, customer-owned AWS environment later.

title: Developer Keynote
speakers: Clare Liguori (Amazon Web Services); Marc Brooker (Amazon Web Services); Eric Johnson (Amazon)
abstract: Building software has never moved faster, and it has never asked more of developers. In this keynote, AWS Engineers and Heroes from the community tackle what's still hard: going from idea to a live app in minutes, building agents that actually work, and trusting code you didn't write yourself. Expect live demos, hard-won lessons from the AWS team that built a new service with an AI software factory, and an honest look at how the developer's job is changing. Come see how AWS is making it easier to build anything you can imagine, then go build it.

title: Duke Energy: Human-Led, Agent-Driven Enterprise App Innovation on AWS
speakers: Mrunal Daftari (AWS); Archy Peesapati (Duke Energy Corporation); Daniel D Morris (Duke Energy)
abstract: Duke Energy is pioneering a new frontier in software creation by combining human leadership with agent-driven execution using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AppGen, its enterprise AI platform. Specialized agents enable both developers and business users to rapidly build production-ready, full-stack applications with speed and precision, driving millions in cost savings while accelerating innovation. This strategic, multi-year collaboration is transforming manual workflows into intelligent, automated processes across business units. The approach supports scalable adoption of agentic AI while ensuring strong governance, reliability, and operational excellence—empowering teams to innovate faster, reduce complexity, and modernize systems consistently across the enterprise.

title: Embed FinOps into your CI/CD pipelines
services: AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS CloudFormation;AWS CodePipeline
speakers: Travis James (AWS); Fredrik Tunvall (AWS); Jenny Shen (AWS); Hicham Lahlali (AWS); Shubho Laga (Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL)
abstract: Cost overruns from infrastructure changes often go undetected until after deployment, making shift-left cost governance a critical capability for platform and DevOps engineers. This builders' session guides attendees through constructing a working cost estimation gate integrated directly into a CI/CD pipeline. Using AWS CodePipeline, the AWS Pricing Calculator, and CloudFormation change sets, attendees build a pipeline stage that evaluates infrastructure cost impact at pull request time and enforces configurable spend thresholds before deployment proceeds. Bring a laptop to complete hands-on exercises with expert guidance in a small-group setting.

title: Enforce AI guardrails across your organization without the friction
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Organizations
speakers: Michael Ingoldby (Amazon Web Services); Rob Whitelocks (AWS)
abstract: Your security team defines the controls, and your product teams build and deploy AI applications across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts. This chalk talk shows how to enforce AI guardrails centrally without making your security team the bottleneck. We walk through an architecture for applying Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through controls at the AWS Organizations, account, and AI infrastructure layers. You see how controls inherit across those layers, which limitations to plan for, and how tiered governance lets teams tailor controls to their applications while the organizational baseline stays enforced.

title: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Glue
speakers: Colin Leek (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Learn proven patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

title: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
aoi: Well-Architected Framework;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Matt Luttrell (Amazon); Matthew Heck (Amazon)
abstract: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon QuickSight;AWS Billing and Cost Management
speakers: Brenno Passanha (Amazon Web Services); Judith Lehner (AWS); Ariel Fu (AWS); Yuriy Prykhodko (AWS); Eric Scott Christensen (Amazon)
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: Fix a Security Hub finding once with four layers of controls
speakers: Todd Kudlicki (Amazon Web Services); Maitreya Ranganath (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: You remediate a finding today and see the same class of finding next week. This chalk talk shows how to break that cycle. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and work through four control layers. An SCP stops the misconfiguration, an AWS CloudFormation Guard rule catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation corrects drift. Each finding you remediate this way becomes a rule that keeps it from coming back.

title: Fix Data Gaps Fast: Agentic Onboarding with Amazon Connect Decisions
speakers: Colby Ward (AWS); Ali Zagros (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: 81% of enterprises report AI initiatives delayed or abandoned due to data and governance gaps — and 80–90% of new enterprise data is unstructured. The bottleneck isn't the model; it's the data. In this session, see how Amazon Connect Decisions uses agentic AI teammates to eliminate that gap. Watch a supply chain planner go from zero to a running demand forecast — connecting raw CSVs with no pre-cleaning, letting AI intelligently map and type-convert data, catching and fixing quality issues conversationally, and encoding tribal knowledge from a Word doc into live decision rules. No ETL code, no JIRA tickets, no months-long implementation. Onboarding in weeks, not months.

title: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Joe Rudd (AWS); Abdu Mahmoudi (Amazon Web Services); Desiree Brunner (AWS); Markus Rollwagen (AWS)
abstract: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.

title: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
speakers: Ramanathan Muralidhar (AWS); Jason Rodriguez (AWS)
abstract: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
speakers: Priyatam Mudivarti (Amazon Web Services); Simon Guo (Amazon)
abstract: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you own the loop or let AWS handle it? We build one on-call responder three ways: an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a managed loop with built-in memory and tool routing, AgentCore Runtime for full control, and AWS DevOps Agent as a batteries-included DevOps harness. Then we build the shape most teams land in: your own orchestrator, DevOps Agent composed in headless over remote MCP and A2A. Bring your challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
speakers: Amit Arora (AWS); Sabeena Shafaq (Expedia Group)
abstract: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.

title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
speakers: Arko Dutta (AWS); Prema iyer (AWS)
abstract: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

title: Governing hundreds of accounts in seconds: agentic AI meets Landing Zone operations
speakers: Randy Domingo (AWS); Bo Lechangeur (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI that lets operators use natural language to apply organizational changes in minutes, if not seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption through a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. An AI agent generates each change plan, and before anything is applied, an org-wide preview catches conflicts and policy violations. Issues are surfaced up front instead of discovered after a break. Attendees learn how we built LZA 2.0 with Kiro spec-driven development and Rust, and how to design pre-deployment previews that keep multi-account operations safe.

title: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
speakers: Raza Hafeez (Amazon Web Services); Divya Ananthanarayanan (Amazon); Manikandan Paramasivan (KOHO Financial)
abstract: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.

title: How GE Vernova scaled self-service AI Agents to 75,000+ workers on AWS
speakers: Abhishek Naik (Amazon Web Services); Tony Miles (GE Vernova)
abstract: GE Vernova set out to put AI directly into the hands of every employee; from the C-suite to field engineers through its Amp 2.0 platform. In this session, learn how GE Vernova integrated Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and AgentCore to deliver self-service agentic capabilities enabling employees across all roles to interact with enterprise data, automate workflows, and surface insights via natural language. Learn and discover how the team designed agents serving diverse personas, the governance and guardrails for enterprise-wide deployment, and how AgentCore's managed infrastructure enabled rapid scaling without custom orchestration. Walk away with a blueprint for democratizing AI across a global industrial workforce.

title: How LSEG Built a Multicloud Internal Developer Platform with Kubernetes and AI
speakers: Richard Chester (AWS); Dean Bryen (LSEG PLC)
abstract: At London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), deploying enterprise workloads traditionally took weeks or months of onboarding, governance, networking, and operational setup. In this session, we’ll share how a small AI-augmented engineering team built RouteOne: LSEG’s fully managed multicloud application platform, enabling developers to deploy compliant workloads across multiple cloud providers in minutes by committing their code and a single YAML definition. We’ll explore the Kubernetes-based control plane, enterprise guardrails, and AI-native developer experience powered by APIs, MCP and agent skills. We’ll also share lessons learned from using AI-assisted engineering practices to rapidly deliver a lean, enterprise-grade platform in a regulated environment.

title: How Santander governs hundreds of AI agents in production on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Javier Ros (Banco Santander HQ); Juan Antonio Albarrán Fernández (Amazon Web Services); Hector Rodes (Banco Santander)
abstract: Financial institutions need a consistent way for independent teams to build, deploy, and govern AI agents without creating silos or losing visibility. In this session, learn how Banco Santander built Santander Cortex—a self-service platform where business teams configure, deploy, and monitor their own AI agents with tools, knowledge bases, memory, guardrails, and authorization using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We'll cover identity integration, agent-to-agent (A2A) interoperability across independently owned teams, and the governance model that made self-service possible without losing control. The platform runs hundreds of agents, including customer-facing chatbots serving millions of users across more than 10 countries.

title: How to Govern an agent fleet: auto-approve the routine, escalate the ambiguous
speakers: Matej Macek (Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL); Ganesh sedhai (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your teams are building agents faster than anyone can review them by hand, and that creates operational and security risk along with the visibility problem. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet. You enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. Then you connect these into an operating model that approves routine actions automatically and sends only the ambiguous ones to a person, so you can deploy more agents than your team could review individually.

title: How Uber brought AWS into its agentic AI stack across clouds
speakers: Ellie Tamari (AWS); Ganapathi Krishnamoorthi (Amazon); Varsha Mahadevan (Uber)
abstract: Uber runs 100+ LLM-powered use cases such as rider support, fraud detection, developer tools, on a cloud-native AI platform built outside AWS. As it scales toward agentic workloads, Uber is bringing AWS in for Bedrock and AgentCore, creating a deliberately multicloud architecture, with agents that reason, retrieve, and act across data and services on more than one cloud. That transition surfaces challenges no single-cloud team hits. Federating identity across providers, orchestrating agents whose tools and data span clouds, and enforcing one governance and observability layer over all model traffic. In this session, Uber shares how the team weighed build-vs-buy for agent orchestration, memory, and observability, and the cloud-agnostic patterns they used to add a cloud without re-platforming. Walk away with a blueprint for extending an AI platform across clouds for agentic workloads.

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
speakers: Andy Hayes (AWS); DJ Rahming (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. Discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences industries—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.

title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
speakers: alexis Henry (Amazon); Ankur Shanbhag (AWS)
abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

title: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Avinash Dalvi (Quantiphi); S Logesh (ShellKode); Poobalan P (Factset)
abstract: Opening a bank account should take seconds, not days. This session shows how AI agents can speed up KYC while keeping the final decision under control, specialized agents that run on Agentcore Harness investigate identity, documents, fraud signals, and screening results, with checks running in parallel. AgentCore Gateway routes tool requests through Cedar policies before tools run, while deterministic rules decide whether a case moves forward or needs human review. The session follows a clean case, an ambiguous case, and a new risk event after onboarding. Attendees leave with a pattern for regulated agentic systems.

title: Land migrated workloads with controls already in place
services: AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Organizations;AWS Transform
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Jakob Altevolmer (AWS); David Piet (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most migrations add governance controls after workloads land on AWS, and that creates rework. This chalk talk shows how to build guardrails into your AWS Transform migration workflow with AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls in place. Bring your migration challenges, and we design a secure-by-default landing together that carries governance through each phase of the migration.

title: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
speakers: Kevin Donohue (aws); Brian Stucker (Amazon)
abstract: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.

title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
speakers: Luca Guida (AWS); Rohith Vijayasankar (Amazon Web Services); Gaurav Acharya (AWS); Alexander Pogorielov (Amazon Web Services); Frederic Schoenberger (AWS)
abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.

title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Mario Kiessling (amazon.com); Roshan Thekkekunnel (AWS)
abstract: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

title: Multi-Agent Operations for Broadcast & Streaming
speakers: Osmar Bento Junior (Amazon Web Services); Bryan Samis (AWS)
abstract: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.

title: Multi-tenant agentic AI with Aurora and DynamoDB
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: David H Gardner (AWS); Arjan Schaaf (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Multi-tenant compute modernization with Amazon EMR on EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EMR
speakers: Ifetayo Stewart (Amazon Web Services); Akshara Shah (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What does it take to run millions of diverse jobs a day across many tenants without costs spiraling or one bad workload taking down the fleet? In this chalk talk, we explore how organizations modernize a multi-tenant compute layer on EMR on EKS to serve batch analytics, streaming, ML, and agentic AI from one platform. We whiteboard the choices that make it possible: custom bin packing to mix heterogeneous tenant workloads efficiently, EKS provisioned control planes to sustain high job throughput per cluster, and Graviton to drive down cost per job. Bring your scaling challenges and we'll design solutions together.

title: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
services: AWS Control Tower;AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Organizations
speakers: Nivedita Tripathi (Amazon); Alex Torres (AWS) (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprises go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS Organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You dive into the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned engagements with customers like you.

title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Ikenna Izugbokwe (Amazon); Lukonde Mwila (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

title: Northwestern Mutual: Reinventing policy servicing with agentic AI
speakers: Andy Hall (Amazon Web Services); Brett Truelove (The Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company); Kristopher Pfeiffer (The Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company)
abstract: Financial representatives at Northwestern Mutual traditionally logged service requests and waited for back-office resolution. In this session, we'll walk through the production architecture behind this transformation: Amazon Bedrock Agents connected to core insurance systems through the Model Context Protocol, with orchestration and governance controls designed for a regulated environment. We'll cover authorization patterns, auditability, human oversight, and lessons learned moving from proof of concept to production. Representatives now resolve significantly more requests directly—reducing resolution times, improving good-order processing, and driving higher satisfaction, with participants reporting better outcomes for their clients.

title: Operating Serverless at scale: What changes at 1000+ functions
speakers: Biswanath Mukherjee (AWS India Pvt. Ltd.); Ben Freiberg (AWS)
abstract: What works at 10 Lambda functions may not work at 1,000. Deployments that took seconds now take hours. A single misconfigured function triggers account-level throttling. Observability drowns in noise. In this chalk talk, we discuss what changes at scale: deployment strategies that roll out code safely across hundreds of functions, account structure and concurrency management to prevent blast radius problems, observability approaches that surface signal without drowning in cardinality, and platform engineering patterns that let application teams ship independently. We share what large-scale Serverless operators do differently and where the common pitfalls are.

title: Operational resilience in regulated environments with AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Ronny Rodriguez (AWS); Prashanth Ramanathan (AWS)
abstract: As software delivery accelerates, financial services organizations struggle to manage incidents across fragmented toolchains. In this chalk talk, learn how AWS DevOps Agent acts as an always-on operations teammate for regulated environments—resolving incidents autonomously, strengthening systems proactively, and validating releases before they reach production. We'll whiteboard four patterns: how the agent investigates and resolves incidents in minutes; how the agent learns from past incidents to recommend improvements; how on-demand SRE tasks give your team instant operational intelligence; and how release readiness reviews catch compliance and dependency risks before code ships. Bring your operational challenges and leave with best practices.

title: Optimize analytics workloads on Amazon EKS for performance and cost
services: Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Sundar Shanmugam (Amazon Web Services); Ramesh Mathikumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The analytics landscape is undergoing a shift as global data volumes grow at unprecedented rates. This rapid growth, combined with rising demand for real-time analytics, is driving organizations to modernize and optimize their data processing pipelines and analytics workloads. EKS’s cost-performance and scalability make it the best place to run these workloads. In this workshop, you will learn hands-on how to optimize EKS for Spark & Kafka workloads using different Karpenter configurations, Spot and Graviton instances, and NVMe volumes. You will also explore observability best practices and granular cost visualization per job. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Optimize smarter: EKS performance with APerf and AI-powered analysis
speakers: Congkai Tan (Annapurna Labs (U.S.) Inc.); Allan Henrique Homenhuck (AWS Brazil)
abstract: Your EKS workload is running, but is it actually efficient? Profile a live application with APerf to see what's consuming CPU cycles: syscall overhead, worker imbalances, inefficient library calls. Issues invisible in dashboards but obvious in a flame graph. APerf Analyzer MCP generates prescriptive guidance, configuration adjustments, and instance recommendations grounded in actual workload behavior. Implement fixes, redeploy, validate. Tasks escalate: fix a worker imbalance, eliminate a blocking call, resolve a writeback burst. Choose Python, Java, or Node.js. A live leaderboard tracks progress—who will finish first?

title: Orchestrate GuardDuty and Network Firewall to prevent exfiltration
aoi: Data Protection;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Maxim Raya (AWS); Meriem SMACHE (AWS)
abstract: Compromised workloads and AI agents share a common path: outbound channels that most teams barely monitor. From CVE-driven RCE on EC2 to prompt injection on agentic systems, both threats end with unauthorized data leaving your environment. In this session, dive deep into a layered egress architecture combining AWS Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall, VPC endpoint policies, SCPs, RCPs, GuardDuty, and IAM Access Analyzer. We'll trace concrete attack scenarios through each control and show how to orchestrate them to prevent data exfiltration.

title: Orchestrate multi-layer disaster recovery for critical workloads
services: AWS Fault Injection Service;AWS Resilience Hub;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Darshan Patel (AWS); Joe Chapman (AWS)
abstract: Your AZ recovery plan and your Region failover plan were probably built by different teams, tested at different times, and have never run together. The result: untested failover paths that turn outages into incidents. Explore how to build a unified recovery framework with Amazon Application Recovery Controller. From zonal autoshift for rapid single-AZ mitigation, to Region switch for cross-Region failover, learn how ARC unifies both layers into a single orchestrated approach. Then discover how to run automated resilience tests that continuously validate your recovery posture before a real event forces the question.

title: Partner Keynote
speakers: Bob Cagnazzi (Presidio Global Public Sector); Ruba Borno (AWS); Matt Yanchyshyn (AWS); Matt Garman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS Partners, this one's for you. You're powering today's biggest transformations, and AWS is building alongside you to make co-selling and going to market simpler. This is your biggest moment of re:Invent, where you'll leave knowing where to invest and how to win in the agentic era. Join Dr. Ruba Borno and guests including AWS CEO Matt Garman for a game plan built on agent-run migrations with your data plugged in, your expertise embedded in customer tools, and more profitable business models, plus a Marketplace and Partner Central demo on reaching more buyers faster. Don't miss it.

title: Patterns for embedding FinOps into cloud architectural decisions
services: AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS CloudFormation;AWS Organizations
speakers: Nataliya Godunok (AWS); Steph Gooch (AWS)
abstract: Every architectural decision carries a cost implication, yet cost is typically discovered in monthly bills rather than design reviews. In this code talk, we demonstrate how to shift FinOps left, optimising before you deploy rather than reacting after. Through two personas, a FinOps engineer and a builder, you will see live how to embed cost governance into infrastructure-as-code, tackle real architectural trade-offs then show how AI coding assistants accelerate this at scale. You will leave with deployable CloudFormation examples and a decision framework for choosing the right cost governance level for your organisation.

title: Performance tuning for streaming ingestion with Apache Iceberg
speakers: Shana Schipers (Amazon Web Services); Francisco Morillo (Amazon Web Services); Diego Garcia (AWS); Angel Conde Manjon (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Unlock real-time streaming into Apache Iceberg with advanced performance tuning. Learn how to optimize ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink for fraud detection, IoT monitoring, and real-time analytics. This session covers throughput optimization through partitioning, parallelism, write distribution, batching, and checkpoint tuning. Discover techniques to reduce small file issues with compaction, minimize write amplification with deduplication, and maintain low-latency ingestion at scale, turning raw streaming data into actionable insights with efficiency and reliability.

title: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
speakers: Rucha Kiwlekar (Amazon Web Services); Allyn Henderson (AWS)
abstract: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

title: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
speakers: Alyson Keenan (AWS); Vipin Gupta (AWS)
abstract: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.

title: Running larger, higher-fidelity quantum experiments on Amazon Braket
abstract: Amazon Braket offers access to the latest trapped-ion quantum hardware alongside advanced error mitigation techniques, unlocking the largest, highest-fidelity quantum workloads on the platform. In this chalk talk, we demonstrate how error mitigation combines noise-aware transpilation and error suppression to expand usable circuit volume, and how trapped-ion connectivity enables deeper, more complex circuits. We will whiteboard a real workload to estimate cost, runtime, and expected fidelity gains.

title: Safer, simpler, faster upgrades with managed blue/green deployments
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)
speakers: Paola Lorusso (AWS); Ryan Shevchik (AWS)
abstract: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. In this chalk talk, you will architect a blue/green database upgrade solution to support major or minor engine version upgrades and perform schema changes with minimal and predictable downtime. Active participation is encouraged as you architect a solution to meet your requirements. In open discussion, learn the trade-offs involved in database management when using blue/green deployments and how to design the most effective upgrade solution to meet your needs.

title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
speakers: Aravind Subramanian (Amazon Web Services); Sanghwa Na (AWS)
abstract: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

title: Scaling Pharma Transformation Through Data-Driven Agentic AI (sponsored by Tech Mahindra)
abstract: Hear from a leading U.S. pharmaceutical company on its journey to transforming enterprise AI from isolated experiments into a scalable business capability. Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. This session will explore the architectural principles, governance strategies, and leadership decisions required to scale compliant, trusted, and value-driven AI. Join Tech Mahindra and a pharma industry leader to learn how data-driven Agentic AI is reshaping the future of the intelligent pharma enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by Tech Mahindra, an AWS Partner.

title: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
speakers: J.D. Bean (Amazon)
abstract: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Amazon Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. Apply the security patterns your organization already trusts to AI workloads on Bedrock.

title: Secure and Scalable Multi-Tenant Deployment Patterns for Amazon Quick
speakers: Vineet Kachhawaha (AWS); Chin Rane (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: As organizations scale their adoption of Amazon Quick across business units, subsidiaries, and partner ecosystems, deploying a secure multi-tenant architecture becomes critical. This chalk talk explores proven deployment patterns that balance tenant isolation, governance, and operational efficiency when rolling out Amazon Quick at enterprise scale. We will walk through two primary isolation strategies: multi-account separation using AWS Organizations for environment-level boundaries (dev/staging/prod), and namespace-based logical isolation within a single account for user-cohort segmentation.

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
speakers: Mac Stevens (AWS); Alex Waddell (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code and PRs faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defense-in-depth framework spanning five pillars - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defense at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, CodePipeline and more. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

title: Six Ways AI Fails Who Your Nonprofit Serves — And How to Stop Each One
speakers: Sam Grace (Amazon Web Services); Annie Cimack (AWS)
abstract: Every AI application touching real people can fail in ways that cause harm. In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.

title: Snowflake: Build a Multi-Engine Architecture on A single AI Ready Governed Data Copy (sponsored by Snowflake)
speakers: Matt Sidley (Snowflake Computing Inc); David Mitchell (Cox Automotive)
abstract: Delivering enterprise analytics and AI requires an architecture designed for operational flexibility not forcing complex data movement. Snowflake's interoperable lakehouse gives teams total agency to query and write to data where it lives using the right engine for every job. This session explores how organizations establish universal open metadata governance powered by Apache Polaris while preserving rich semantic business context across tools. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud simplifies data management, lowers total cost of ownership, and accelerates time to insight for every team, and agent, across your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

title: Technical Innovations Keynote
speakers: Colm MacCarthaigh (AWS); Matt Wood (AWS)
abstract: Agents don't follow a script. They change plans mid-task, reach for tools they didn't know they'd need, and create demand you can't predict. For two decades, the hardest workloads builders brought to AWS have pushed us to rethink everything from Graviton and Trainium to the shape of the data center network, to the way storage scales, and how we prove systems behave as intended. Join AWS's top engineers and scientists for an under-the-hood look at the technology that came out of that pressure, the kind of story you won't hear anywhere else. See how AWS infrastructure adapts as your work changes, freeing you to stop engineering around constraints and build anything you can imagine.

title: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
speakers: Mrudhula Balasubramanyan (Amazon); Praveen Nerellapalli (AWS)
abstract: Advisors across mission-driven organizations—financial advisors, benefits navigators, program coordinators—juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and delayed plan delivery while clients go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See how to collapse this fragmentation into configuration using the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. Learn to securely plug domain-specific skills and disparate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly into the harness to generate tailored action plans in real time. Then, deploy the agent to isolated microVM sessions utilizing native memory strategies and Bedrock Guardrails. Leave with sample configurations, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building production advisors that scale.

title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
services: Amazon API Gateway;Amazon CloudFront;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Anton Babenko (Compliance.tf)
abstract: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.

title: Tokenomics of attacks: how AWS defends you from AI-powered threats
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
aoi: Data Protection;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Paul Bodmer (AWS); Alexandra Lee (AWS)
abstract: AI isn't just transforming how we build, it's transforming how attackers exploit. In this session, AWS threat researchers share the intelligence they observe in real time: the prompts adversaries feed into AI systems, the tokenomics that make AI-powered attacks devastatingly scalable, and the shrinking window between vulnerability disclosure and weaponized exploitation. We'll share first-hand threat intel from MadPot, AWS's globally distributed honeypot network, and show how AWS protects AI-based workloads. You'll learn how AWS Active Threat Defense capabilities proactively block malicious infrastructure before it reaches your workloads, so you can innovate with AI confidently while staying ahead of emerging threats.

title: Turn your cloud migration into a security transformation
services: AWS Config;AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Security Hub
speakers: Rochak Karki (Amazon Web Services); Shivam Patel (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: Forward-looking organizations aren't just migrating to AWS — they're using migration to transform their entire security posture. In this workshop, your workloads have just landed on AWS and you'll immediately secure them using sandbox accounts. You'll use Amazon GuardDuty to detect runtime-level threats and malware, Amazon Inspector to prioritize software vulnerabilities, and AWS Security Hub to correlate findings into actionable exposures. You'll finish by building an automated remediation pipeline that isolates compromised resources without human intervention. Leave with a repeatable Day 1 security playbook for any migrated workload. Laptop required.

title: Unified Commerce Intelligence for Amazon Brands on Amazon Quick
speakers: Duncan Watson (AWS); Manikanta Gona Grafsgaard (AWS)
abstract: Brands selling on Amazon generate rich signals across commerce and advertising — order trends, catalog performance, competitive pricing, campaign metrics, and customer engagement. The opportunity lies in connecting these signals into a unified view that drives faster, smarter decisions. In this chalk talk, we design an architecture that composes two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — the SP-API MCP Server for Selling Partner operations and the Amazon Ads MCP Server for campaigns and reporting — behind Amazon Quick as a conversational layer. We'll whiteboard how brands can build cross-domain queries, like correlating ad spend with order velocity or surfacing catalog insights that inform campaign strategy. Leave with production-grade patterns for building agentic commerce workflows tailored to your brand's data

title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
speakers: Colin Marden (Amazon Web Services); Kenta Sato (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.); Marco Masciola (Amazon Web Services); Jun Zhang (Amazon Web Services); Ana Suja Lucia (AWS)
abstract: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

title: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Outposts;AWS Transform
speakers: Aditya Lolla (Amazon Web Services); Gokul Chandra Purnachandra Reddy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, you use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. You work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. See how Trianz's Concierto platform also integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance.

title: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
speakers: Aaron Castellanos (Amazon); Swapnil Singh (Amazon Web Services); Kevin Hakanson (Amazon Web Services); Murithi Gitonga (Amazon Web Services); Ibrahim Cesar (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: What's new with the Amazon SageMaker Data Agent
speakers: Ramesh Harisaran Singh (AWS)
abstract: The Amazon SageMaker Data Agent helps data teams move from a plain-language request to results faster. In this session, learn how it helps you discover and understand your data, generate and run analysis, build and operationalize data workflows, and connect analytics work through to model development. See how it can take on the repetitive, time-consuming steps of data work so your team can focus on the questions that matter and the decisions that follow. Whether you're exploring a new dataset or building an end-to-end workflow, learn how the Data Agent brings governed, agentic development to every step of your data work.

title: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
speakers: Storm Alexander Manterola Guijt (AWS); Asal Shams (AWS)
abstract: When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
speakers: Preetam Rebello (Amazon Web Services); Simran Singh (AWS Canada)
abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: leveraging native OIDC providers from Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries, and using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
speakers: Haresh Nandwani (AWS); Richard Ainley (AWS)
abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
speakers: Rian Brooks-Kane (Idea 11); Ian Mckay (Kablamo)
abstract: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

title: Agentic AI Governance for Regulated Industries
speakers: Jayanthi Rajaraman (AWS); Ranjan Banerji (Amazon)
abstract: As agentic AI expands into regulated industries, autonomous decisions must meet compliance before production. This session gives partners a governance framework spanning technical and non-technical requirements — not just architecture. We demo a working multi-agent system and share the code.

title: Agentic AI in Production: Natera Saves Lives, Cuts Costs, Grows Revenue
speakers: Mirko Buholzer (Natera, Inc.); Tamara Gagliardi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Natera, a global leader in cell-free DNA testing for oncology, women's health, and organ health, built reusable agentic infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to power multiple internal platforms from a single framework. Natera's VP of Engineering will share the technical decisions behind this infrastructure and provides a blueprint for building once and scaling across your organization. See a live demo of one platform built on this foundation for revenue cycle management, cutting prior-authorization denial rates 6x, reducing touchpoints by 5x, and enabling new use cases to go live in less than a week.

title: Agentic developer experience with Amazon EKS
speakers: Majid Shokrolahi (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Sumanth Nidamanuri (Amazon Web Services); Dariush Azimi (Amazon); Hasnain Raza (AWS); Niall Thomson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Transform your Kubernetes development workflow using generative AI. In this workshop, use Kiro CLI and the EKS MCP Server to automate complex operations, troubleshoot applications through natural language, and deploy micro services on Amazon EKS — all with AI-powered assistance. Work through hands-on labs: explore clusters using natural language, fix connectivity and ingress issues by orchestrating EKS MCP with Terraform MCP, and deploy new application components using AI-guided analysis. Leave with practical skills to integrate AI-powered automation into your existing Kubernetes workflows and dramatically improve developer productivity.

title: A leader's guide to moving from AI investment gridlock to acceleration
speakers: Chris Hennesey (AWS); Paul Krebs (AWS)
abstract: Fund the platform or the use case? Demand proof before investing, or invest to generate the proof? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and can't wait for the annual budget cycle. To move at the pace of AI, the CIO and CFO must be in lockstep. Two former operators share how the best pairs manage AI like a venture portfolio: bets in the face of uncertainty, recycling of wins into the next ones, and governance that scales across the portfolio rather than project by project — plus the key questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
speakers: Zac Burns (Amazon Web Services); Ronan Prenty (AWS)
abstract: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
speakers: Eric Jones (AWS); Mark Twomey (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
speakers: Sulaman Khan (AWS); Deric Martinez (Amazon Web Services); Fiona McCann (AWS); Ben Turnbull (AWS); Sofia Kendall (Amazon AWS)
abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.

title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
speakers: Brent Rabowsky (AWS); Hazim Qudah (AWS)
abstract: Organizations deploying AI workloads face a critical decision at every step: which AI service handles which job, and will it hold up at scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to use them together. We'll ground it in a real example: an agentic coding system pairing a Bedrock frontier model for complex coding with a fine-tuned open weight model on SageMaker AI for high-volume automated PR reviews. It runs on AgentCore, which supports any model or provider mix, including Bedrock and SageMaker AI, for cost- and performance-optimized architectures.

title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
speakers: Ayushi Goyal (Amazon Web Services); Aran Singh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

title: Automate disaster recovery with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Chiara Marzano (AWS); Arnav Khare (AWS)
abstract: Financial institutions face stringent regulatory requirements for operational resilience, demanding reliable disaster recovery with tight RTO/RPO targets across complex application portfolios. Yet failover procedures often remain manual and prone to error under pressure. In this chalk talk, we explore how to design a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates end-to-end disaster recovery automation for regulated workloads. We’ll walk through how a coordination agent delegates to specialized sub-agents for readiness verification, infrastructure operations, Terraform code generation, Git operations, and deployment validation—each with human-in-the-loop approval gates.

title: Automate patching and compliance with AI-powered visibility
speakers: Ganesh Sambandan (Amazon Web Services); Justin Thomas (Amazon Web Services); Ravindra Kori (Amazon); Yukitaka Ohmura (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.); Jim Grabinski (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Tracking patch compliance across hundreds of accounts is manual, slow, and hard to prove to auditors. In this hands-on builders' session, you automate patching and continuous compliance in your environment, then let AI do the heavy lifting: generate a multi-account compliance dashboard with Apps in Amazon Quick and answer compliance questions with natural language instead of hand-building reports. By the end, you'll know how to turn raw patch data into audit-ready answers on demand.

title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
speakers: Praneeta Prakash (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.

title: AWS fundamentals for the accidental SQL Server database administrator
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS Transform
speakers: Baris Furtinalar (AWS); Andy Ward (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You became a DBA, and now someone's asking you to be a cloud architect too. With over 240 AWS services, knowing where to start is half the battle. In this chalk talk, we'll map your core DBA tasks to AWS equivalents, covering networking, security, high availability, and disaster recovery for SQL Server.
