We'll also explore how AI-powered tools like Kiro and AWS Transform can accelerate your ramp-up, from intelligent code generation to modernizing .NET and SQL Server workloads. You'll leave with a clear path to choosing, securing, and cost-optimizing the right services. Come with questions.

title: AWS Partner: Govern AI agents by hacking one first
speakers: Parvesh Chopra (AWS)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. Exploit a live AI agent with a prompt injection attack that approves a fraudulent transaction, then defend it. Fix it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to block prompt attacks and PII leaks. Verify it: prove your controls are in place with AWS Config conformance packs and find ungoverned AI resources with Resource Explorer. Observe it: trace agent decisions and guardrail interventions in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave ready to assess a customer's AI agents for governance gaps, protect them, and prove the controls work. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS Transfer Family: From SFTP to Agentic AI Workflows
speakers: Prabir Sekhri (AWS); Matt Boyd (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how to build enterprise-grade file transfer solutions using AWS Transfer Family and extend them into agentic AI workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through building secure SFTP servers, integrating with enterprise identity providers like Okta and Azure AD, and automating file processing using Terraform. We'll explore how event-driven architectures handle malware scanning with GuardDuty, and how AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore take over downstream tasks like data extraction and fraud detection. Bring your questions. You'll walk away with practical patterns for evolving traditional managed file transfer into intelligent, agentic processing pipelines.

title: Beyond RSA: Post-quantum data encryption using ML-KEM in AWS KMS
speakers: Vipul Gupta (AWS)
abstract: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography secure nearly every application today, and both are vulnerable to future cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Data captured now can be decrypted later, so applications needing long-term confidentiality should adopt post-quantum encryption well before those computers arrive. AWS KMS now offers ML-KEM, the NIST-standardized replacement for RSA and ECDH key establishment and ultimately encryption under asymmetric keys. It protects the private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. In this session, learn about ML-KEM and how to use it as a building block for quantum-safe encryption using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE).

title: Breaking down batch inference with Ray Data on Amazon EKS
speakers: Andy Palmer (AWS); Vara Bonthu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.

title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
speakers: Leo Simberg (Amazon Web Services - AWS); Efren Mercado (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, you build a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances — the best of both worlds. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, you deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. You profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, and implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. By the end, you have a hybrid deployment with a live cost dashboard showing 30–45% savings vs. GPU-only baselines.

title: Build a digital asset tokenization issuance solution
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Everton Fraga (AWS); David-Paul Dornseifer (AWS); Simon Goldberg (Amazon Web Services); Joshua Smith (Amazon Web Services); Arvind Raghu (AWS)
abstract: The emergence of digital assets and stablecoins requires bridging traditional message-based finance protocols such as SWIFT and ISO 20022 to programmable settlement rails while preserving institutional security, auditability, and governance. In this session, learn how to build a production-ready end-to-end hybrid settlement architecture on AWS that ingests financial messages, normalizes them into canonical settlement instructions, and executes tokenized asset transfers on-chain. Explore hardware-backed signing with AWS KMS, on-chain signer governance, and three settlement patterns: issuance, redemption, and transfer, with full audit trails, idempotent transaction handling, and EIP-712 typed signing. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL
speakers: Shayon Sanyal (AWS); Radwan Deeb (AWS); Rinisha Marar (Amazon Web Services); Sudhir Amin (Amazon Web Services); Kanishka Chaturvedi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What if your agent's most convincing answer rests on the wrong evidence? Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Aurora PostgreSQL across more than 500,000 product listings in three connected hands-on labs. Debug SQL combining full-text search, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and pgvector semantic search under shared filters. Repair reciprocal rank fusion, inspect Amazon Bedrock reranking, and compare retrieval settings against judged queries. Then build a Strands agent, connect its retrieval tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime. Trace its searches to cited specifications and reviews, and test what happens when requirements change. Leave with reusable retrieval SQL and working agent code.

title: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Arun Lakshmanan (AWS); Gene Alpert (AWS)
abstract: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.

title: Build AI agents to operate desktop and mainframe apps on WorkSpaces
speakers: Stephen Stetler (Amazon Web Services); Dave Jaskie (Amazon)
abstract: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

title: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Christian Melendez (AWS); Oussama Kandakji (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
speakers: Jeff Bascle (Lockheed Martin Corporation); Taylor Riggan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

title: Build an AI-powered student services with Connect Customer
speakers: Varun Pole (AWS); Ekta Vasa (AWS)
abstract: Education institutions field thousands of student inquiries each semester across enrollment, financial aid, and academic support. In this chalk talk, we architect agentic AI-powered student services using Amazon Connect Customer. You’ll configure a knowledge base with university content and connect it to Connect Customer for real-time AI-generated recommendations during live calls, then deploy a self-service experience that resolves common inquiries over voice and chat. We'll cover when to use deterministic intent handling vs. agentic reasoning, MCP tool integration with student systems, and guardrails for FERPA compliance. By the end, you'll have a working prototype that boosts advisor productivity and reduces student wait times.

title: Build and deploy agents to Lambda and EKS with Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Addy Upreti (AWS); Santosh Kulkarni (AWS)
abstract: Bring an agent idea and leave with it deployed. In this workshop you use the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock to build an agent from scratch, give it tools and memory, and add guardrails, permissions, and observability. There are multiple ways to deploy agents in production including Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Lambda MicroVMs, and Amazon EKS. In this lab you deploy to Lambda and EKS. Leave with a reference architecture for agents you can actually ship. Laptop required.

title: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic
speakers: Reilly Manton (Amazon Web Services); Hector Lopez (Amazon Web Services); Nitin Eusebius (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build and deploy a voice agent with Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic. Learn how to build and deploy a voice agent using Nova 2.5 Sonic, Strands BidiAgent, AgentCore, and customized Skills. The session covers both bidirectional streaming architecture (Nova 2.5 Sonic) and cascading architectures using Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Polly. Attendees will learn reference architectures, implementation patterns, deployment steps, and best practices for building scalable, production-ready voice agents using AI coding tools.

title: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
speakers: Zelle Steyn (Amazon Web Services); Negin Rouhanizadeh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream, using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. You'll construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions to the ARTF specification, then orchestrate a multi-agent pipeline that simulates adversarial auction scenarios and scores your bidding strategy against the outcomes. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and plug in your own bidding model to see how it performs. You'll leave with a working ARTF container and auction-simulation harness you can point at your own models.

title: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL;AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Shayon Sanyal (AWS); Maxym Kharchenko (AWS)
abstract: Turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into agent skills and test whether they improve an agent's advice. Work through three incidents on a live cluster: RDS Proxy session pinning that starves checkout connections, a payout job whose open transaction blocks checkouts, and stalled order delivery alongside a long-running transaction that holds back vacuum cleanup. Complete and refine skills that cover pre-flight checks, execution, validation and rollback. Freeze a grading rubric, then compare the same agent, hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, without and with your skill. Write Python recovery checks that reject incomplete fixes, perform the repairs yourself, and verify customer recovery using independent database and business records.

title: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)
speakers: Shayon Sanyal (AWS); Aditya Samant (Amazon)
abstract: Build an agentic retail assistant that answers from business facts under explicit controls. Across four connected labs, combine Aurora PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector with reciprocal rank fusion and Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock. Connect search and inventory tools to specialists built with the Strands Agents SDK, then deploy them to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy. Protect customer records with identity binding and PostgreSQL row-level security, and enforce Cedar policies on Gateway tool calls. Approve a store credit, query the audit records, and verify denied calls don't execute and retries don't duplicate credits. Patterns are reusable across Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL.

title: Build governed remediation workflows for Aurora database operations
speakers: Chirag Dave (AWS); Anum Jang Sher (Amazon); Nazneen Jafri (Amazon Web Services); Maxym Kharchenko (AWS); Sudhir Amin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for Aurora performance issues, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting from a performance investigation, review recommendations and apply remediation through human-in-the-loop approval gates backed by scoped IAM permissions and API guardrails. The session covers capturing an auditable trail from insight to action, and planning for post-change verification and rollback actions when needed. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Aaresh Sharma (Amazon Web Services); Sai Charan Teja Gopaluni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

title: Building & Governing Apps on Quick
speakers: Shane Thompson (Amazon Web Services); Art Chan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Anyone can generate apps from a sentence - the hard part is governing them and getting them in front of the right users. This chalk talk whiteboards the full lifecycle of Amazon Quick Apps: building them from natural language with no separate hosting, wiring in data and actions through MCP, and the three sharing paths - private, public URLs, and enterprise sharing gated behind admin approval workflows.

title: Building Serverless applications at AI speed
speakers: Josh Rodgers (AWS); Archana Venkitaramanan (Amazon Web Services); Charleston Telles (AWS); Sahil Malhotra (AWS); David Lamb (AWS)
abstract: Manually wiring up Lambda functions, API Gateway routes, and IaC templates for every new service is repetitive work that AI handles well. In this builders' session, use Kiro to go from natural language specifications to a deployed serverless application. You'll configure MCP tool servers to give the AI agent access to AWS APIs, author steering documents that produce consistent output, and iterate on generated infrastructure until it passes validation. Walk away with techniques for getting reliable, production-ready code from AI-assisted workflows. Bring your laptop.

title: Building the data architecture that survives agentic analytics (sponsored by Edelbyte)
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon EC2 - Graviton
abstract: Human queries are bounded, repeatable, and predictable, so techniques like caching, sampling, and precomputation keep them fast and affordable. AI agents are none of those. One prompt becomes dozens of novel, complex queries at machine speed, so caching an agent's curiosity is nearly impossible. At a leading automotive R&D group, 1,400 engineers and their agents query 200 petabytes of vehicle telemetry, with 600 terabytes ingested daily, to engineer higher-quality, more reliable vehicles and reach production faster. This session shows the AWS architecture behind it and how it delivers real-time analytics with full retention at the scale agents have made standard. This presentation is brought to you by Edelbyte, an AWS Partner.

title: Building Wealth Advisor Agents with Full Stack Architecture
speakers: Mar Cánovas (AWS); Bruno Marcondes (AWS)
abstract: In this SimuLearn session, you leverage the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform ito build production-grade wealth management advisor. You create Memory resources for client personalization, configure a Gateway with MCP tool targets for account and market data, deploy specialist agents and a supervisor to Runtime, and authenticate users through Cognito. The result is a multi-agent advisor that recognizes each client, remembers their goals, and produces auditable financial guidance through governed tools.

title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
speakers: Reetesh Surjani (AWS); Anshu Bathla (AWS)
abstract: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
speakers: Prasanna Venkatesh Sridharan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

title: Build multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence for automotive
speakers: Amit Kumar (AWS); Venkat Devarajan (AWS); Ajit Kumar KP (Amazon Web Services); Vijai Thoppae (AWS); Gopi Krishnamurthy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Warranty and repair workflows span claim history, technical service bulletins, supplier quality records, and regulatory thresholds — a high-cost, fragmented data challenge for automotive OEMs. In this builders session, construct a multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence system using Strands SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build a triage agent that classifies incoming cases, a research agent that queries Bedrock Knowledge Bases across TSBs and repair records, and a resolution agent that synthesizes findings into a structured decision with cited evidence routed for technician approval via human-in-the-loop controls.

title: Build multi-agent workflows with Strands Agents SDK on AWS
speakers: Arun Kumar Selvaraj (Amazon Web Services); Daniel Lorch (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build a multi-agent system using the Strands Agents open source SDK. You will create specialized agents with distinct roles, connect them via MCP for tool access, implement agent-to-agent delegation patterns, and add memory for stateful conversations. Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.

title: Build production AI assistant with Hugging Face Libraries and models
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Louise Ping (Annapurna Labs (AWS)); Jeff Boudier (Hugging Face)
abstract: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant, but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this chalk talk, we architect a production solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. You will leave able to run native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium and own your AI stack end to end.

title: Build scalable streaming and messaging applications with Amazon Kinesis and AmazonMSK
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams;Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
speakers: Ali Alemi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Messaging and streaming should be simple, elastic, and cost-efficient, no matter how your workloads change. In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is making it easier and more affordable to build messaging and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3 and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less, and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.

title: Build secure APIs faster with Amazon API Gateway and Kiro CLI
speakers: Jacob Cravinho (AWS); Josh Rodgers (AWS); Archana Venkitaramanan (Amazon Web Services); Raphael Lima (Amazon Web Services); David Lamb (AWS)
abstract: Secure your APIs with confidence and build them faster. In this builders' session, dive into Amazon API Gateway authorization strategies including Amazon Cognito user pools, Amazon Verified Permissions, Lambda custom authorizers, IAM authorizers, and machine-to-machine scenarios. Through hands-on exercises, implement each strategy and understand their trade-offs. Once secured, ship faster—use Kiro CLI, OpenAPI, and MCP servers to go from spec to deployed API in minutes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
speakers: Rajesh Kumar Ravi (Amazon Web Services); Abhinav Krishna (AWS)
abstract: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. This workshop walks you through the full optimization loop on AgentCore: instrument with OpenTelemetry traces, score with built-in and custom evaluators, generate data-backed recommendations that rewrite your system prompt or tool descriptions, validate offline with batch evaluation, then split live traffic with A/B testing through AgentCore Gateway until you have statistical confidence to promote. You will run every step hands-on, ship a measurably better agent configuration, and leave with a repeatable process that replaces guess-and-check prompt iteration with evidence.

title: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
speakers: Anil Kumar (Amazon); Stan Fan (AWS); Augusto Dias (AWS); Haofei Feng (AWS); Joe Guo (Amazon)
abstract: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.

title: Connect agents across frameworks live using the A2A open protocol
speakers: Saurav Mohanty (Amazon); Madhukiran J (Amazon Web Services India)
abstract: Agents built on different frameworks need to talk to each other. In this session we will build two agents on Strands and LangGraph, then wire them together using the A2A protocol hosted at the Linux Foundation. You will see the full handshake: AgentCard publication for discovery, task negotiation, streaming artifact exchange, and multi-turn collaboration between agents that share nothing except the protocol. We will deploy both sides on AgentCore Runtime and demonstrate cross-framework interoperability working live. You will leave with the patterns to make any framework's agents collaborate over a standard wire.

title: Context engineering for production agents on AgentCore
speakers: Akarsha Sehwag (Amazon Web Services); Noor Randhawa (Amazon)
abstract: An agent is only as good as what fills its context window. System prompts, skills, tool definitions, conversation history, retrieved documents, long-term memory, they all compete for limited space. Get the mix wrong and you waste tokens, degrade reasoning, or lose critical instructions mid-conversation. This chalk talk breaks down every layer of context that shapes agent behavior on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover how to structure system prompts, define skills effectively, manage tool context through gateway, retain the right conversation history, and use Memory strategies to persist what matters across sessions. Bring your agents, we optimize them live.

title: Custom SRE agents: From prompt to proactive ops with DevOps agent
speakers: Harish Goud Mandhadi (AWS); osamamu Munir (AWS); Bhavani Kanneganti (AWS); Rohit Sharma (Amazon Web Services); Garrett Pollard (AWS)
abstract: In this builder session, learn how to create custom SRE agents that turn a simple prompt into automated, environment-specific operational workflows. Using pre-configured tools and integrations, you'll define agents tailored to your priorities, whether that's anomaly detection, performance optimization, cost analysis, or resiliency recommendations. See how agents combine real-time observability data with structured reasoning to surface actionable improvements without manual investigation. Walk away with hands-on experience designing an agent that monitors your operational patterns and proactively recommends next steps, so your team spends less time diagnosing and more time shipping.

title: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
speakers: Ganesh Prabhu Jayachandran (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Mansoor Ali Khan (Amazon)
abstract: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation at regulatory scale. In this chalk talk, we walk through the decision framework for choosing first-party tools versus AWS Lambda versus MCP integrations based on latency, complexity, and compliance requirements. Explore deterministic state-machine patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents. We discuss automated evaluation pipelines using Amazon Connect Customer Conversational Analytics and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. Debate trade-offs and leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center environment.

title: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
speakers: Christina Defoor (Amazon Web Services); Anand Iyer (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

title: Demystifying AWS KMS authorization: building key policies that scale
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
aoi: Data Protection;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Kevin Kevin (AWS); Patrick Palmer (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Authorization to your key involves a mix of key policies, IAM policies, grants, SCPs, and VPC endpoint policies — each playing a distinct role in access decisions. This talk demystifies how these policies are evaluated in the context of AWS KMS, then applies that understanding to create a scalable policy design. You'll learn about ABAC, using grants for dynamic delegation, and AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) which offers a simpler yet scalable way to share keys in your organization. You'll leave with the mental model to predict outcomes and reusable patterns that grow with your organization.

title: Deploy and manage blockchain nodes on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Kiro;AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Yinal Ozkan (Amazon Web Services); Everton Fraga (AWS)
abstract: Self-managing blockchain nodes at scale requires expertise in infrastructure sizing, storage optimization, chain synchronization, snapshot management, and patching, amid rapidly evolving protocols. In this session, explore a reference architecture for deploying self-managed nodes on AWS using Amazon EC2 and AWS Blockchain Node Runners, an open source initiative. The session includes a whiteboard walkthrough of a sample solution, diving deep into each component, addressing key challenges, and exploring AI-driven node deployment with Kiro and how to leverage AWS DevOps Agent for management.

title: Deploying Governed AI Agents in Clinical AI
speakers: Dan Eakin (AWS); Bret Borota (Amazon)
abstract: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. Radiology Partners is tackling this with MosaicOS, a full imaging lifecycle system powered by agentic AI that spans order placement through billing. In this lightning talk, learn how MosaicOS uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate multiple AI models across the radiology workflow while maintaining governance and observability required in regulated clinical environments. See how agentic orchestration moves radiology from tool-level automation to coordinated, clinician-directed intelligence at scale.

title: Develop with natural language and agentic AI in Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Juan Luis Polo Garzon (AWS); Shreya Jain (AWS)
abstract: Dive into modern approaches to data engineering and machine learning using natural language and agentic AI assistance. We'll walk through practical examples that show how conversational AI and agents can streamline the development of data and ML workflows within Amazon SageMaker. You'll leave with the technical know-how you need to automate data engineering tasks and streamline ML development without writing code.

title: Emerging multi-agent patterns for complex financial workflows
speakers: Evandro Franco (AWS); Alfredo Castillo (AWS)
abstract: Multi-agent systems are rapidly evolving beyond static orchestration patterns. In this chalk talk, we explore the newest collaboration paradigms gaining momentum, including ephemeral agent patterns and self-improving agents, alongside established approaches like hierarchical, sequential, and peer-to-peer coordination. Walk through how to apply these patterns to claims adjudication, underwriting, and financial portfolio advisory using Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness engineering best practices. We'll discuss when to select each pattern, how to combine them for complex workflows, and how AgentCore harness capabilities enable scalable, governed multi-agent architectures. Gain practical guidance for designing the next generation of agentic applications.

title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
speakers: Krutika Khinvasara (Amazon Web Services Inc.); Omar Tabbakha (AWS)
abstract: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

title: Firewall policy management for mixed regulated and legacy workloads
services: AWS Network Firewall;AWS WAF;AWS Network Security Manager
speakers: Dario Goldfarb (Amazon Web Services); Ian Olson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your firewall policy now has to cover new workloads on modern tech stacks alongside legacy systems still running Windows. Some of them fall under financial regulations, and others under privacy controls. In this code talk, we show how new firewall management features help you write policy elements your team can understand and maintain, avoid policy sprawl, and spend less time preparing for audits.

title: From documents to decisions: Agentic AI for federal operations
speakers: Harsha Tadiparthi (Amazon Web Services); Raghavarao Sodabathina (AWS)
abstract: Accelerate mission-critical federal operations with agentic AI—from public-information analysis to sensitive document workflows. This expert chalk talk explores patterns for document review, supply chain optimization and classified medical health records backed by real-world implementations. Whiteboard multi-agent orchestration with Amazon Bedrock, including least-privilege tool access, human approval, auditability, and failure recovery. Compare Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for eligible workloads such as regulatory review, grants, and benefits processing with FEDRAMP (Class C and D). Further explore container-based agent architectures for IL4/IL5 environments using authorized AWS services and models.

title: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
services: Amazon API Gateway;Amazon Bedrock;AWS Step Functions
speakers: Sid Singh (AWS); Philip Klose (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores live agent behavior across multiple quality dimensions and how the optimization capability discovers better system prompts and tool configurations from production traces. Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. We'll demonstrate the full observe-evaluate-improve cycle with an underwriting agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents Framework, then discuss how the pattern applies to claims, fraud, and customer service agents.

title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Local Zones;AWS Outposts
speakers: Ina Rademacher (AWS); Joshua Smith (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves traders with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs adjacent to the matching engine with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency to the matching engine through Amazon VPC peering: bringing compute into New York Local Zone cuts round-trip latency by roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the AWS Region offers a fully managed API that also serves agentic trading systems via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever for your location-sensitive workloads.

title: Getting Started with AgentCore: ship an agent to production in 2 hours
speakers: Madhu Samhitha Vangara (Amazon); Robert Belson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. Not because the AI is hard, but because the infrastructure around it is: memory, tool access, identity, policy, observability, evaluation. This workshop closes that gap in three hours. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add each production capability using the AgentCore CLI: runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy, observability, and evaluation. AgentCore is framework and model agnostic, so everything applies whether you use LangGraph, CrewAI, Strands, or your own stack. Leave ready to ship.

title: Getting the capacity you need: EC2 Launch APIs and Intelligent Auto Scaling deep dive
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon SageMaker;Amazon WorkSpaces
speakers: Justin Kwong (Amazon); Samruddhi Kochkar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Getting the right compute at the right time is a two-part challenge: launching instances effectively and scaling them intelligently. This deep dive covers both. First, we explore RunInstances—EC2's oldest and most important API—sharing launch best practices, how flexibility helps you get the capacity you need, and how EC2 Fleet incorporates advanced strategies into your calls. Then we go under the hood of EC2 Auto Scaling, and the intelligence that also scales DynamoDB, WorkSpaces, EMR, SageMaker AI, and Aurora. Learn how to use target tracking, predictive scaling, and auto-tuning to automatically and intelligently scale your workloads.

title: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
speakers: David Victoria (Caylent)
abstract: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

title: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
speakers: Vince Palazzo (AWS); Guillaume Marchand (AWS France); Florian Clanet (AWS); Alen Zograbyan (Amazon Web Services); Iryna Oliinykova (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts (true, misleading, or false), with source citing at broadcast-compatible latency. Learn how to build it yourself using a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Leave with a mapped path to create a reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you such as: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.

title: Guardrails for AI-generated Serverless infrastructure
speakers: Tomas Mihalyi (AWS); Stan Fan (AWS)
abstract: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

title: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
speakers: Dan Malloy (AWS); Shyam Sunder Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Then extend it — encode your team's expertise as skills, connect custom MCP tools, automate investigations from alarms, and approve agent-executed fixes. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

title: How AWS Continuum validates security findings across the SDLC
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Security Agent;Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Jeremy Schiefer (AWS)
abstract: AWS Continuum embeds security expertise at every stage of the software development lifecycle: AWS Continuum reviews architecture documents, AWS Continuum scans pull requests and full repositories, and AWS Continuum can pentest deployed applications. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into how AWS Continuum coordinates multiple analysis passes with built-in safety guardrails and multi-step validation to deliver high-confidence findings. Bring your questions about integrating security into CI/CD pipelines and scaling AppSec across multiple teams.

title: How Blue Origin built a centralized enterprise knowledge graph on AWS
speakers: Jay Naves (AWS); Prabhuram Mohan (Blueorigin); Clark Stevens (Blue Origin)
abstract: Building enterprise AI applications shouldn't require every team to reinvent the wheel — standing up data pipelines, managing security, and keeping knowledge bases current. Blue Origin faced this at scale: dozens of teams, hundreds of data sources, and growing demand for AI apps that could reason across all of it. The answer was RAGNet — a centralized enterprise knowledge graph platform built on Amazon Neptune and Amazon Bedrock that aggregates structured and unstructured data into a secure, always-current graph any developer or AI agent can query in plain natural language.

title: How Bristol Myers Squibb Scales AI from Experiments to Enterprise with AWS
speakers: Ethan Sena (Bristol Myers Squibb); Brian Loyal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Bristol Myers Squibb is scaling AI from targeted experiments to enterprise transformation through its AI Accelerator program. In this session, hear how BMS pairs business-led innovation with AWS to move AI use cases from idea into production. See how this approach is applied across Product Development and Supply, where AI helps improve decision velocity, strengthen supply resilience, optimize operations, and speed the delivery of medicines to patients. Learn how BMS and AWS built the foundation, operating model, and reusable capabilities to scale AI responsibly, turning isolated wins into a repeatable enterprise capability that other organizations can follow.

title: How FINRA Brings Governed Agentic AI to Its Member Firms on AWS
speakers: Noah Egorin (FINRA); Eric Weller (FINRA - Financial Industry Regulatory Authority); Brandon Webb (Amazon)
abstract: FINRA protects investors and enforces regulation for 3,400+ broker-dealer firms and 1.2 million financial professionals, so regulation must evolve as fast as the markets it oversees. FINRA is exploring the role agentic AI services like Amazon Quick can play on FINRA’s Gateway, its primary external platform serving firms. This session covers the how: the design patterns and guardrails for responsible AI in a regulated environment, including draft-and-attest human accountability, data grounding with hallucination detection, tenant isolation, and a pragmatic governance model. Behind that experience, FINRA keeps models and frameworks interchangeable, so capabilities evolve without rebuilding. Leave with a practical framework for governing agentic AI at scale.

title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
speakers: Trevor Mack (Rapid7); Navyata Bawa (AWS); David Killmon (AWS)
abstract: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.

title: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
speakers: Yuriy Prykhodko (AWS); Alessandro Bellini (Max Mara Fashion Group)
abstract: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.

title: How Ramp tracks and governs AI spend down to the team, model, and API key
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Jigna Gandhi (Amazon); Alexander Chau (Ramp); Richard Wang (Ramp); Siddhi Surana (Ramp)
abstract: When AI token spend spans multiple providers and dozens of teams, knowing who spent what, on which model, and whether it's COGS or OpEx requires its own pipeline. We'll cover ingesting usage data from third-party AI APIs, processing with Temporal workers, persisting on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, running on Amazon ECS Fargate, and surfacing anomalies before they hit your invoice. See how Ramp attributes spend by provider, model, team, and API key, and attributes cost down to the request-level when teams connect their router, gateway, or internal data. Learn how Ramp separates COGS from OpEx for accurate unit economics, then closes the loop with governance.

title: How to Build Autonomous Enterprise Agents with SOPs using Kiro and Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Eduardo Bratz (AWS); Harshavardhan Padaval (Amazon Web Services); Ferry Mulyadi (Amazon Web Services); Sagar Tallapragada (Amazon Web Services); Venkat Tatavarthy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprise operations hit a limitation when humans can't keep up with the volume of exceptions in ERP systems like SAP which is solved by autonomous AI agents. In this session, learn how to build production agents by writing SOPs in natural language. We'll cover how to write SOPs that let agents exercise judgment while embedding guardrails. A single SOP becomes a deployable agent, and this pattern scales across different business processes. Using Kiro's spec-driven development and Strands agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, partners own the full agent lifecycle and differentiate by layering domain expertise and industry-specific IP into SOPs. Walk away with hands-on experience building the agentic architecture that enables autonomous enterprise operations for your customers.

title: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
speakers: Pujah Goviel (AWS)
abstract: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.

title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
speakers: Dmtiri Pavlichin (AWS); Bryan Wilkinson (Amazon)
abstract: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

title: Integrate Agents with MCP Servers and Tools using AgentCore Gateway
speakers: Marco Tamassia (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your agent may handle basic conversations well, but to take real-world actions it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this hands-on lab, use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tools with JWT authorization. Register tool targets, connect to a pre-deployed nutrition coach agent, and validate how it dynamically discovers and invokes new capabilities at runtime without redeployment.

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
speakers: Tolga Orhon (Amazon Web services); Marco Jahn (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
speakers: Hahnara Hyun (Amazon Web Services); Jake Wolf (AWS)
abstract: Three tools belong in your toolbelt for moving Java from x86 to AWS Graviton. AWS Transform custom runs across hundreds of repos and integrates with CI/CD. The open-source Java skill runs locally in your coding agent, no AWS credentials needed, with final validation on Graviton hardware. The APerf MCP server measures x86 vs. Graviton performance before and after you migrate so you can rightsize. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and timeline. Watch all three run live on one codebase, see where each succeeds and hands off, and leave with a decision framework for when to use each.

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
speakers: Vikram Mehto (Amazon Web Services); Anuj Dewangan (Amazon)
abstract: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

title: MCP is Just An MVP. Knowledge Lakes Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio)
services: Amazon Redshift;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)
speakers: Pete Griffiths (Atolio)
abstract: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a knowledge lake built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.

title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
speakers: Rahul Gupta (Amazon)
abstract: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
speakers: Kevin Willis (Amazon); Keren Tseytlin (AWS)
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

title: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Billing and Cost Management
speakers: Adam Richter (AWS)
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: Multicloud Operating Models for ISVs
speakers: Dave Smith (SAP Global Cloud Operations); Joachim Aumann (AWS); Olga Calvo (AWS)
abstract: ISVs adopting multiple clouds face the same trade-offs. This breakout distills cloud-agnostic operating-model patterns from production multi-cloud estates -- workload placement, abstraction layers, resiliency, and FinOps (optimization, tokenization), and unified observability -- illustrated by SAP running at 25,000+ accounts across AWS, Azure, and GCP. SAP's team walks through what stayed cloud-specific, what they unified, and what they had to invent. Leave with operating-model patterns you can apply across clouds.

title: Multi-Tenant Agentic Platforms: A Scalable Reference Architecture
speakers: Ujwal Bukka (Amazon Web Services); Ranjith Raman (AWS)
abstract: SaaS is going AI-native. ISVs must orchestrate third-party agents at scale. This session presents a multi-tenant architecture covering MCP, A2A, and AgentCore for orchestration, entitlement-based monetization, secure token exchange, agent lifecycle via Agent Registry, and cross-tenant observability.

title: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Network Firewall;AWS Transit Gateway
speakers: Preetkumar Shah (Amazon Web Services); Pål-Magnus Slåtto (Amazon Web Services); David Fowler (Amazon Web Services); Lawton Pittenger (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. Starting with a realistic multi-VPC setup with AWS Transit Gateway, you will deploy Network Firewall and configure routing, inspection, and logging in minutes using reusable modules. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

title: Now serverless has servers. What now?
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Evandro Pires da Silva (evandropires.com.br)
abstract: I spent years advocating for serverless, but as a CTO, I could not always see a viable path to bring it into certain business scenarios. In this talk, I share what has changed with the new AWS capabilities, why this can change the game for larger companies, and, along the way, I explore the concepts and how these services work in more depth to help us think about architecture with more clarity.

title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
speakers: Smruti Tripathy (Amazon Web Services); Kien Tran (Amazon)
abstract: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

title: Optimize agentic AI costs with EC2 Capacity Blocks and Spot Instances
speakers: Sherif AbdElGawad (Amazon)
abstract: Agentic AI turns ML infrastructure into a dynamic scheduling problem, where the goal is cost per accepted outcome. In this lightning talk, watch a self-managed agentic workflow run financial services portfolio stress testing on Amazon EC2, with telecom and media content generation as bonus patterns. EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML reserve capacity for deadline-critical stages, while EC2 Spot Instances add elastic, checkpointable capacity for parallel work. A bounded agentic planner proposes placement across NVIDIA GPUs and AWS silicon while deterministic controls enforce budget and deadline limits, keeping cost per accepted outcome low as workloads shift.

title: Optimize AI inference costs: Compare token economics on AWS silicon
speakers: Simon Coope (Amazon Web Services); Melchi Salins (AWS)
abstract: Most enterprises run their entire AI pipeline on GPU and can overpay. AWS's silicon portfolio (Trainium & Graviton) along with NVIDIA GPU, Intel, and AMD all offer radically different cost-per-token economics for different workloads. This session delivers a decision framework for matching silicon to workload: training and inference on Trainium, RAG pipelines on Graviton, real-time agents on GPU, batch on Intel/AMD. Includes Bedrock vs. self-host crossover analysis, volume thresholds, and the architecture patterns to put the savings into practice.

title: Orchestrating agentic applications with Lambda durable functions
speakers: Abbi Gorelik (AWS); Rohan Mehta (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents are powerful, but production workloads need more than an LLM and a prompt. They require deterministic routing, audit trails, compensation logic, and human oversight. In this workshop, build agentic orchestration using AWS Lambda durable functions and MCP tools. Learn to design workflows that checkpoint progress, recover from failures automatically, and pause for human-in-the-loop approval—all without managing additional infrastructure. You'll implement tool-calling patterns, handle multi-step reasoning with retries, and deploy agents that are observable, testable, and production-ready. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Policy to Proof: govern deployments at machine speed
speakers: Welly Siauw (AWS); Jerry Peter (Amazon); Jean Velez Torres (Amazon Web Services); Vinicius Elias (AWS); Pujah Goviel (AWS)
abstract: When agents and automated pipelines deploy at machine speed, manual sign-off can't keep up, so the proof has to be built into the pipeline itself. Developers want to ship fast, governance teams want controls enforced, and compliance teams want evidence. In this builder session, you'll build a CI/CD pipeline that satisfies all three: cfn-guard validation against policy rules, CloudFormation deployment, Config evaluation after deployment, and a compliance report generated as a pipeline artifact. The full policy-to-proof loop in one pipeline. You leave with a working pipeline where every deployment validates governance rules and produces audit evidence on its own.

title: Preventing unintended access: a practical guide to data perimeter controls
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Nitin Kulkarni (AWS); Sowjanya Rajavaram (AWS); Manas Chhabra (AWS); Vaibhav Chowla (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Are you looking to prevent unintended access to your data and mitigate data exposure risks? This hands-on session demonstrates how data perimeter controls implemented through service control policies (SCPs), resource control policies (RCPs), and VPC endpoint policies help keep corporate data within organizational boundaries. You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.

title: Production Agentic Trading: Build the pipeline Moeve runs on AgentCore
speakers: Loreto Albinana (Moeve); Aristides Fernandez (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: This session details the implementation of an agentic workforce managing the trade lifecycle in production energy trading operations. In this workshop, you'll build the pipeline Moeve runs in production: a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that extracts deal data from unstructured emails, resolves ambiguity deterministically against master data, and carries evidence per field. You'll harden it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on input and output, then score it for accuracy and run-to-run consistency, including the fields that measured badly, and why. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for production deployment of mission-critical trading workflows with strict latency and reliability requirements.

title: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Muhammad Wasiq (AWS) (Amazon (AWS)); Bryan Van Hook (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.

title: Provision Desktops for Builders Faster with WorkSpaces
abstract: Builders lose days configuring environments. IT teams struggle to govern the growing sprawl of AI tools and extensions across their organization. In this session, we explore these challenges and share how Amazon WorkSpaces is approaching the builder desktop experience. We'll discuss what enterprises need to provision environments faster, maintain governance across multiple surfaces, and keep pace as AI-assisted development becomes the norm. Bring your questions.

title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
speakers: Kiran Patel (AWS); Phil Harrison (AWS Elemental); Vipul Patel (Comcast)
abstract: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Building an AI-Ready Data Foundation
speakers: Anurag Singh (AWS); Jigna Gandhi (Amazon)
abstract: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: Scale production agents reliably with AgentCore
speakers: Shishir Bharathi (AWS); Satveer Khurpa (AWS)
abstract: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios and we architect solutions together.

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
speakers: Max Hausner (AWS); Eitav Arditti (AWS)
abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

title: Scaling operations with MCP, ACP, and A2A
speakers: Babu Samayapuram Suthanthira Raju (AWS Singapore Pte. Ltd); Jyothi Madanlal (AWS)
abstract: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

title: Securing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with AWS WAF and a self-healing security agent
speakers: Piotrek Witkowski (Amazon Web Services); Alex Moening (AWS)
abstract: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll build an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, and autonomously remediates threats and generating a plain-English incident summary.

title: Self-Tuning Demand Forecasts: How Agentic AI Puts Business Users in the Driver's Seat
speakers: Ali Zagros (Amazon Web Services); Colby Ward (AWS)
abstract: Amazon Connect Decisions is redefining how organizations approach demand forecast tuning. Traditionally, improving forecast accuracy meant navigating complex data engineering pipelines and hyperparameter optimization — work that was time-intensive, technically demanding, and largely inaccessible to business users. In this chalk talk, we unpack how Amazon Connect Decisions takes an agentic approach to solve this: intelligent agents continuously self-tune demand forecast models by incorporating business user feedback directly into the refinement loop, removing the undifferentiated heavy lifting. Walk through a live demonstration of self-tuning in action, learn how this business-first approach shifts forecast ownership to the people who understand the demand signals best, and discuss how Amazon Connect Decisions is shaping the future of agentic supply chain solutions.

title: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
speakers: Nima Kaviani (AWS); Vipin Mohan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

title: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
speakers: Mona Mona (AWS); Willie Lee (AWS)
abstract: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

title: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
speakers: Mohamed Othman (Amazon Web Services); Nisha Notani (AWS)
abstract: Inconsistent tags make it hard to see what runs where. In this code talk, we build automation that keeps tagging clean at scale: a tagging schema that defines the keys and values that matter, an AWS Config rule that flags non-compliant resources, and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that remediates them automatically or with approval. We also query untagged resources across thousands of resources and multi accounts. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root-cause analysis.

title: Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
speakers: Aravind Rajendran (AWS); Wei Teh (Amazon Web Services); Maheshwaran G (AWS India); Devendra Sharma (Amazon Web Services); Sanjay Singh (AWS)
abstract: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. In this hands-on session, we walk through practical techniques for building cost-optimized video understanding pipelines on AWS. You'll learn how to reduce inference costs, right-size your architecture, and accelerate time to value without sacrificing accuracy. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable.

title: Tekion: Reinventing automotive retail with agentic AI on AWS
speakers: Vibhu Pareek (AWS India)
abstract: Automotive retail runs on complex, menu-driven workflows — scheduling service, ordering parts, structuring deals, closing books. Tekion, whose cloud-native platform powers thousands of dealerships, reimagined it as conversational AI, the industry's first AI-native automotive DMS. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Tekion's production agents — spanning sales, service, parts, F&I, and accounting — execute actions rather than suggesting them, serving every role from service advisor to dealer principal. Learn how Tekion architected a reusable agent platform, applied guardrails for safe autonomy, and turned industry operations AI-native.

title: Telecom Contact Centers: Design Patterns for integrated AI Agents
speakers: Shalima Bhalla (AWS); Robin Harwani (Amazon)
abstract: Telecom customers demand fast, accurate service, yet IVR systems frustrate them, and when calls reach a human agent, context from the automated interaction is lost. Based on real-world implementations, this chalk talk explores alternatives to IVR using AI powered agents. We will walk through architectural options for customer facing agents built on Amazon Connect, how to pass conversation context to human agents when they step in, and options for integrating with OSS/BSS services using MCP and prebuilt integrations in Amazon Connect. We will examine the trade-offs that come with each design choice, so bring your questions!

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Nihilson Gnanadason (AWS); Daniel Wirjo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

title: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen
speakers: Pranjit Biswas (AMAZON WEB SERVICES); David Bounds (AWS)
abstract: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production.
