Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. We design a supervisor agent coordinating specialists across drive-thru, kitchen prep, inventory, and labor scheduling. Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI
speakers: Nima Fotouhi (Amazon); Mike Saintcross (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

title: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Dhammika Sriyananda (Amazon Web Services); Karthik Annamalaisamy (AWS India)
abstract: Your multi-tenant SaaS application runs on Amazon ECS. Now your customers expect AI-powered features but adding agents to an existing platform introduces new challenges. Including tenant isolation for model access, per-tenant memory and conversation state, cost attribution across shared infrastructure, and agent orchestration at scale. In this workshop, you start with a working SaaS application on Amazon ECS and progressively add agentic capabilities using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement tenant-aware agent routing, configure isolated tool execution with ECS task-level security boundaries, add persistent memory per tenant, and instrument with end-to-end observability. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
speakers: Jonathan Jenkyn (AWS Security Assurance Services); Angela Morrison (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations planning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. In this chalk talk we whiteboard the PQC Readiness Maturity Model: five levels from discovery to quantum-ready, each with measurable milestones. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, modernize how you protect data, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

title: Turn raw telemetry into answers with OpenTelemetry
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon CloudWatch Logs;AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: SUDHEER Sangunni (Amazon Web Services); Snehal Nahar (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Kiran Prakash (Amazon Web Services); Mateus Prado (AWS); Jose Augusto Ferronato (AWS)
abstract: Raw telemetry arrives noisy, unlabeled, and hard to query, so teams waste time cleaning data before they can act. In this hands-on builders session, you set up OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and traces from a live sample application, then use Amazon CloudWatch pipeline processors to enrich and normalize the data in flight. You build the enrichment rules, explore results with natural language query, and leave with a reusable pattern for turning raw signals into analysis-ready telemetry.

title: Turn security logs into actionable intelligence
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS CloudTrail
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Rafael Pereyra (Amazon Web Services); Erik Weber (AWS); Thomas Sceifers (AWS); Dan Girard (AWS); Yohan Ponniah (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Security teams drown in logs but struggle to investigate fast. In this hands-on session, turn raw security telemetry from CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and VPC flow logs into actionable intelligence with Amazon CloudWatch. We'll centralize logs in the CloudWatch Unified Data Store, then query across sources to investigate real scenarios: after-hours data access, credential misuse, and exfiltration patterns. You'll build a security dashboard that surfaces who did what, from where, and when. Walk away with reusable queries and dashboards you can deploy in your own accounts, moving from reactive log search to proactive security visibility.

title: What's new with Amazon API Gateway
speakers: Giedrius Praspaliauskas (AWS); Eric Johnson (Amazon)
abstract: Your next API consumer might not be a person. AI agents, MCP servers, and coding assistants are calling APIs programmatically, and they need machine-readable schemas, predictable error contracts, and discoverable endpoints. In this session, we cover what's new with Amazon API Gateway: recent launches, direct service integrations that eliminate Lambda glue code, declarative event wiring, and patterns from real customer deployments. We also discuss how to design APIs that serve both human developers and autonomous agents without maintaining separate interfaces.

title: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
speakers: Dotan Horovits (Amazon Web Services); Andrew Ross (AWS)
abstract: "The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with autonomous relevance tuning and persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today. OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents."

title: Accelerate database protection and testing with EBS Snapshots and clones
speakers: Shibin Michaelraj (Amazon Web Services); Santhosh Arunuri (AWS)
abstract: Teams that rely on backups alone risk slow dev cycles, compliance gaps, and prolonged recovery times. Learn how Amazon EBS Snapshots and Volume Clones solve these challenges together. See how Snapshots deliver incremental, cross-region data protection with automated lifecycle policies for compliance, while Volume Clones create instant local copies for development and testing. We'll compare cost, performance, and architectural tradeoffs. You'll leave with a decision framework for when to snapshot, when to clone, and how to combine both in production architectures.

title: Accelerating AWS Graviton migrations at scale with AI
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
speakers: Jackson Wagstaff (Amazon Web Services); Jake Wolf (AWS)
abstract: In this session, we explore how agents accelerate AWS Graviton migrations, improving price/performance for workloads across every phase from migration planning, compatibility validation, to performance testing and optimization. We’ll examine various agentic tools where attendees will learn how to choose the right solution and practical steps to implement the tools in their environments. Participants will leave with actionable strategies to reduce manual overhead and harness AI to unlock Graviton’s benefits at scale.

title: Agentic advertising with privacy-enhanced data collaboration
speakers: Ryan Malecky (Amazon Web Services); Zelle Steyn (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Programmatic advertising is shifting from rule-based heuristics to autonomous agents that plan, orchestrate, and bid inside the millisecond bidstream. This Lightning Talk shows three AWS building blocks combining into one agentic ad tech stack: multi-agent collaboration on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for media planning and inventory optimization; ARTF-compliant containers running deep-learning models on NVIDIA Triton and Amazon EKS for real-time bid shading, audience activation, and deal management; and AWS Clean Rooms ML as the trust layer, training lookalike models on collective data without exposing underlying records. Leave with a reference architecture for where inference, orchestration, and privacy all work together.

title: Agentic AI for software-defined vehicles: Compress the V-Cycle with Kiro
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Kiro
speakers: Steven Miller (Amazon Web Services); John Vangelov (AWS)
abstract: Automotive embedded software teams face complex V-Cycle workflows, safety standards, and competitive pressure to ship faster. In this workshop, experience how agentic AI transforms the embedded software V-Cycle — compressing timelines from weeks to hours without sacrificing quality or traceability. Attendees build a remote start/stop feature for an autonomous mower platform, using Kiro to orchestrate agents across requirements engineering, code generation, virtual-target testing, and test automation.

title: Agentic Integration: How AI Agents Replace Static CRM Connectors
speakers: Chintan Gandhi (Aamzon Web Services); Ritesh Choudhary (AWS)
abstract: Every enterprise has dozens of integrations connecting their CRM, ticketing, and backend systems to their customer experience platform, and every one of them is static, brittle, and expensive to maintain. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon Connect Customer, powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP), shifts integration from point-to-point connectors to intelligent, agentic orchestration. The AI agent reasons across multiple systems in real time, assembling unified customer context that no single system holds alone. We whiteboard the architecture: how MCP connections work, how each new system compounds the intelligence available to every interaction, and how to evaluate which integrations to migrate first. Bring your integration pain (Salesforce, ServiceNow, homegrown systems) and we'll design the agentic alternative on the whiteboard.

title: Agents that train themselves: autonomous reinforcement learning on AWS
speakers: Rachit Mehta (Amazon); Arron Bailiss (Amazon Web Services); Patrick Gray (Amazon); Gautam Sirdeshmukh (AWS Agentic AI); Bryan Lu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Can an AI agent teach itself to land a spacecraft? In this hands-on Builders' session you hand a Strands agent one goal: land the lunar lander gently. Then you watch it write its own reward, run reinforcement learning, and grade the result, looping until it sticks the landing. You'll catch it cheating, then watch it diagnose and fix its reward. When a run stalls, you fan out parallel agents and let a sealed judge crown the winner before shipping it to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Give an agent a goal and a judge it can't game, and it trains itself.

title: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
speakers: Ioannis Moustakis (AWS); Aritra Nag (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most teams start with one or two Amazon EKS clusters and grow into a fleet. AWS manages the control plane, but on standard EKS your team still owns version upgrades, add-ons, node lifecycle, and operational efforts. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling inventories your EKS clusters, translates node and add-on configuration, and flags what must change before you cut over. Learn patterns for enabling EKS Auto Mode with minimal disruption, then scaling the migration across your fleet in a fraction of the time manual work takes.

title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
speakers: RISHU GUPTA (Amazon Web Services); Philon Terving (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

title: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
speakers: Mike Ellis (AWS); Giedrius Praspaliauskas (AWS)
abstract: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AI-Enabled SRE: Empowering Incident Commanders at Riot Games
speakers: Randy James (AWS); Cory Ramirez (Riot Games)
abstract: Learn how Riot Games built an AI-powered post-incident review workflow within its LiveOps Process & Analytics (P&A) team using AWS AgentCore. Integrated with Datadog, Slack, Jira, and version-control sources, the platform orchestrates modular AI agents that gather evidence, validate incident impact, and generate structured reviews and RCA drafts. With humans in the loop to review and approve outputs, it accelerates analysis, reduces toil, and improves consistency—helping teams identify root causes and prevent recurrence. Beyond post-incident response, this work establishes a reusable foundation for standardizing and scaling AI-assisted operational workflows across LiveOps, enabling teams to adopt intelligent automation while maintaining human oversight.

title: AI-Powered FinOps: Cloud Cost Optimization in Practice
services: AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS Compute Optimizer;AWS Savings Plans
speakers: Rupesh Lunia (Amazon); Enrico Bonaccorsi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Embed FinOps as an operational discipline using AI-powered cost optimization. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how to shift left on cloud financial management by integrating cost discipline throughout development. Explore AWS services for automated optimizations, rightsizing, and savings plans. Gain experience with AI/ML and container workload cost allocation, multi-cloud reporting, and AI-powered spend analysis. Implement automated strategies using real workload data. Laptop required

title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
speakers: ラフール Pathak (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
speakers: Ryan Seaman (Amazon); Dr. Bernadette Han (American Psychological Association)
abstract: AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Leaving governance models built for deterministic software no longer sufficient. AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result. Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.

title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
aoi: Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS;Training & Certification
speakers: Daniel Slater (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Erin Kraemer (AWS)
abstract: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Culture of Security;Agentic AI
speakers: Sarah Davenport (Amazon); Rush Carskadden (Amazon)
abstract: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
speakers: Taimur Rashid (Amazon Web Services); Mario Thomas (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

title: Allocate shared AWS infrastructure costs to your business units
speakers: Erik Nestorovic (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Shared Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon EKS clusters, and network resources improve efficiency but can obscure which applications and business units drive spend. In this session, learn how to attribute shared costs based on actual usage. Follow a practical example using AWS Split Cost Allocation Data for S3 and EKS and Flexible Cost Allocation for networking. Then use AWS Cost Categories and Data Exports to combine each business unit’s share of storage, compute, and networking spend into a unified view. Walk away with a repeatable approach to showback and chargeback across your shared AWS environment.

title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
speakers: Sam Parmett (Amazon); Will Cavin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.

title: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
speakers: Dan Kiuna (AWS); Alok Dhamanaskar (AWS)
abstract: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
speakers: Matt Carter (AWS); Christer Christer (AWS)
abstract: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios, such as credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse. We'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

title: Architecting video search at trillion scale with Amazon S3 Vectors
speakers: Ran Pergamin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Storing and querying 1.5 trillion vectors demands rethinking traditional vector database architecture. Join this talk to learn how Bright Data built its video search retrieval layer on Amazon S3 Vectors, covering index partitioning across massive collections, embedding storage layout for sub-second nearest-neighbor queries, and cost/latency trade-offs versus dedicated vector databases at this scale. Bright Data walks through its approach to sharding, metadata filtering, and query routing, with benchmarks comparing throughput and cost per million queries. You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns for evaluating S3 Vectors in large-scale search, RAG, or embedding retrieval systems.

title: Architect resilient, multi-region workforce access on AWS
services: AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Prashob Krishnan (Amazon Web Services); Laura Reith (Amazon Web Services); Alex Milanovic (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most AWS workforce access hinges on a single Region and a single identity provider. When either one goes down, everyone who signs in is affected—developers can't ship, DevOps engineers can't deploy, and administrators may be locked out just when they need access most. This session applies defense in depth across four layers: IAM Identity Center multi-Region replication, direct IAM federation through AD FS, Regional AWS STS endpoints, and break-glass IAM users. You learn how to decide which layers your environment needs, the order to fail over in, and how to test the full path without disrupting production.

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
speakers: Amila Weerasinghe (Amazon); Olcay Boz (Amazon)
abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

title: A Unified AWS Data and AI Strategy for SAP Customers
abstract: Explore how AWS and SAP customers can unlock value through converging data and AI strategies. From zero-copy integration with SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon S3, to enterprise AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, learn practical approaches to automate SAP processes and accelerate innovation at scale.

title: Automate AI governance and risk management with John Deere
speakers: segolene Dessertine-Panhard (Amazon Web Services); Carl Kubalsky (John Deere)
abstract: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. Walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how John Deere applied these principles through AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) to automate risk management. Learn how static checks verify controls at code and documentation level while dynamic checks analyze APIs and traces in real time, achieving over 30% reduction in assessment time and continuous visibility into AI risk posture. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.

title: Automate dispute resolution with Amazon Connect and Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Kayla Jing (AWS); Kalindi Vijesh Parekh (Amazon Web Services); Ajay Desai (AWS); Arnab Chakraborty (Amazon Web Services); Madhavi Evana (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.

title: Autonomous SRE: AWS DevOps Agent in Financial Services
speakers: Prem Dhayalan (Capitalone Bank); Saurabh Saxena (Amazon)
abstract: In this session, learn how a large financial institution deploys AWS DevOps Agent as an autonomous SRE teammate to reduce incident investigation time from hours to minutes and free engineering teams from reactive firefighting. Explore the architecture spanning CloudWatch, Splunk, GitHub, and Slack integrations, and see how the agent correlates telemetry across data sources to identify root causes and generate mitigation plans. Walk away with practical patterns for deploying agentic operations in regulated, compliance-sensitive environments.

title: Auto Scaling meets Capacity Reservations: Patterns that work
speakers: Jon Burns (AWS); Harsh Bhimjyani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Capacity Reservations hold your instances. Auto Scaling right-sizes your fleet. Together, they give you both availability and cost efficiency. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to make them work seamlessly. We'll walk through strategies that keep reservation utilization high during scale-in, mixed-instance policies that balance cost and availability, and fallback patterns for Capacity Blocks transitions. Bring your scaling architecture and we'll work through it on the board.

title: AWS and Nu: Building scalable architecture using IAM Account access manager
services: AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Laura Reith (Amazon Web Services); Hugo Feijó (Nubank); Tim Kosanke (AWS)
abstract: As organizations grow across teams, AWS accounts, and countries, workforce access often becomes a bottleneck. This is especially true when you depend on existing IAM roles you don't want to re-engineer. Learn how IAM account access manager helps you assign your existing IAM roles to users and groups in IAM Identity Center, give native AWS CLI access to your workforce, and carry each user's identity into every role session, all on a resilient architecture. Then see how Nu, the largest digital bank in Latin America, modernized a decade-old authorization model across 11 organizations and hundreds of AWS accounts to securely scale for more than 140 million customers.

title: AWS Backup: Architecture deep dive
abstract: Dive into AWS Backup architecture with AWS experts, including how new capabilities fit into your design. We work through deployment strategies, backup storage options, restore scenarios, and security posture. Bring your questions, leave with a plan.

title: AWS Marketplace checkout, your website, your brand
speakers: Hussein Khazaal (AWS); Eddie Lee (AWS)
abstract: When a buyer on your website is ready to purchase, AWS Marketplace gives them a procurement path their company has already approved. AWS Marketplace Storefront brings that path onto your own domain, so you keep your brand, your journey, and your sales team's visibility. In this chalk talk we'll build one live: catalog selection, buyer routing, embedding on your domain, and wiring requests into your CRM.

title: Behind the Scenes: Building the Telecom Concierge
speakers: Aymen Saidi (Amazon Web Services); Rahul Shira (AWS)
abstract: Whether you caught the demo on the expo floor, or you are enhancing your customer service systems with AI, this chalk talk dives into the architectural decisions powering a hyper-personalized customer experience. Explore the intelligent routing and retrieval trade-offs, and understand the business model implications when operators can shrink their physical footprint without degrading experience. Leave with a reference framework for designing context-aware systems at scale, a decision matrix for your retail strategy, and clarity on the ROI drivers so you can architect similar solutions in your network.

title: Best practices for agentic-driven operations
speakers: Dave Schnorr (Best Buy); Bill Fine (Amazon); Metanat Hooshsadat (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are moving from assistants to operators, but how do they actually work within your operational workflows? Understand the architecture of agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root cause across distributed systems, and execute remediation like rollbacks, scaling, and traffic shifts. Learn how agents reason over telemetry, sequence actions, and determine when to escalate. Explore best practices for shaping agent behavior through guardrails, approval gates, and feedback loops as core design elements. Leave with a framework for evaluating where agents should act autonomously versus where human judgment remains essential.

title: Best practices for cost optimization with AWS Backup
speakers: Samreen Taj K P (Amazon Web Services); Lakshmi Nair (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS Backup protects workloads across more than 20 AWS services, and each resource type brings its own cost profile. In this chalk talk, learn practical approaches to managing your data protection TCO by tailoring your AWS Backup strategy to each workload. We'll dig into full versus incremental backups, lifecycle policies, cold storage tiering for S3 and other resource types, and backing up direclty to logically-air-gapped-vault to protect data from ransomware without maintaining multiple copies. Then we'll cover how to build cost observability using AWS Backup reporting and monitoring to track and optimize spend.

title: Best practices for making coding agent orchestration more deterministic
speakers: Arundeep Nagaraj (Amazon Web Services); Romain Dura (AWS)
abstract: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this chalk talk, we will walk through best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale multi-agent workloads. Bring questions, challenges, or edge cases you ran into and we'll walk you through how to approach them to improve reliability.

title: Best Practices for .NET modernization with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform;Kiro
speakers: Renuka Krishnan (AWS); Neeraj Handa (Amazon Web Services); David Pallmann (Amazon Web Services); Runeet Vashisht (AWS); Chan Zaw (AWS)
abstract: As organizations look to reduce tech debt for their .NET applications, builders are looking to accelerate modernization with AI tools. In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
speakers: Shreya Manjunath (Not applicable); Avi Mittal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. In this chalk talk, learn how to match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Explore the decision framework covering instance types, DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration with Research and Engineering Studio (RES). Whether supporting a VFX render farm's artist desktops, an oil company's subsurface workstations, or an automotive design studio, leave with guidance balancing performance, cost, and simplicity.

title: Beyond the IDE: autonomous development with Kiro web and mobile
speakers: Artur Rodrigues (AWS); Massimo "Max" Becker (AWS - Kiro)
abstract: Kiro web and mobile bring agentic development to your browser—every session in an isolated cloud sandbox, no local setup, accessible anywhere you have an internet connection. In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Beyond the pilot: How customers scaled Kiro and proved the value
speakers: Diana Kennedy (NatWest Group); Rory Richardson (AWS) (AWS); Kym Weiland (FINRA - Financial Industry Regulatory Authority); Michael Erdman (Southwest Airlines Co.)
abstract: Adopting a coding agent is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one. In this panel, engineering leaders from companies that deployed Kiro at scale share what worked: rollout strategies that drove adoption, training approaches that met developers where they were, governance guardrails that satisfied security teams, and the metrics they use to measure productivity impact. Bring your questions—this is an open conversation about the patterns, pitfalls, and payoffs of making AI-assisted development the default across an engineering organization.

title: Break free from Oracle licensing and modernize to Aurora PostgreSQL
speakers: Harpreet Virk (AWS); Tejpreet Reen (AWS)
abstract: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. You'll work through PL/SQL translation, dependency resolution, and validation using AWS agentic AI.

title: Build agents on OSS models with blazing fast inference on SageMaker AI
speakers: Dan Ferguson (AWS); Piyush Daftary (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Stop paying frontier-model prices for agentic workloads. In this hands-on session, build production-ready AI agents powered by open-source models like Qwen3 and Gemma4 running entirely on Amazon SageMaker AI. You'll deploy models with optimized serving, connect them to multi-turn tool-use workflows through OpenAI-compatible APIs, and enable real-time bi-directional streaming for responsive agent interactions. Leave with a working cost-optimized agent stack you fully control — fast inference, zero vendor lock-in, and patterns for scaling agentic workloads on your own terms.

title: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
speakers: RK Vyas (AWS); Bimal Gajjar (Amazon); Saket Jangle (Amazon Web Services); Arik Porat (AWS); Krutarth Doshi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.

title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
speakers: Paul Mietz Egli (AWS); vtbloise Bloise (Amazon); Vanitha Sugumaran (Amazon); Tim Ness (Amazon); Krishna Kadiyala (AWS)
abstract: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

title: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
speakers: Peter Giuliano (Amazon Web Services); Jean-Francois Landreau (AWS)
abstract: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

title: Build and Ship an AI-Powered App with Amazon Quick
speakers: Roy Yung (AWS); Mei Liu (AWS); Douglas Bergquist (Amazon); Oyin Oguntoye (AWS); Vaidy Janardhanam (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this hands-on builder session, you'll use Amazon Quick to design, iterate on, and publish a fully functional application through natural-language conversation. You'll connect to a live data source (pre-provisioned via MCP), shape your app interactively with generative AI, persist state across users, and publish something your team or customers can use immediately. Whether you're accelerating decision-making, automating operational workflows, or putting insights directly in the hands of end users, this session shows how Quick Apps collapses the gap between having an idea and shipping a solution. Bring your laptop and be ready to build.

title: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
speakers: Nicholas Clegg (Amazon); Elizabeth Fuentes Leone (AWS); Jonathan Segev (AWS); Albert Zhao (Amazon); Joy Chakraborty (AWS)
abstract: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
speakers: Leonardo Azize (AWS); PRAVEEN HOSUR NARAYANA GUPTA (AWS India); Pedro Rosinholi (AWS); Alin Scurtu (AWS); Prabhu G (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Teams deploying AI agents inherit two exposures. Any client reaching the endpoint can invoke the agent, and it can reach any destination its tools name. In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.

title: Building an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
speakers: Jimmy Silva (AWS); Bruno Marcondes (AWS)
abstract: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.

title: Building and scaling inference workloads on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Managed Grafana;Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
speakers: Shivam Dubey (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Eric Anderson (AWS)
abstract: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building an interconnectivity fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);Amazon VPC Lattice;AWS PrivateLink
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Zero Trust;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Jamie Wenzel (Amazon Web Services); Yécine Allouache (Aws)
abstract: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts - whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities - creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don’t cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. In this session, build a private interconnectivity fabric: a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

title: Building a partner business on Amazon Lightsail
speakers: Murat Guven (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon Lightsail is a simple, low-cost cloud platform designed for small and medium business workloads. In this chalk talk, we start with an overview of what Lightsail offers and common use cases partners are delivering today. We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

title: Building Context-Aware Agents with AgentCore Memory
speakers: JP Schramek (AWS); Sri Kola (Amazon)
abstract: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.

title: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
speakers: Sudhir Kumar (Amazon Web Services); Raviteja Sunkavalli (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.

title: Building event-driven architectures
services: Amazon EventBridge;Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Katherine Vishnevskaya (Amazon)
abstract: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building multi-tenant RAG: Isolation, cost, and scale
speakers: Aakash Upadhyay (Amazon Web Services); Hans Nesbitt (AWS)
abstract: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.

title: Building production AI agents on AWS: compute, security, state, and cost
speakers: Uma Ramadoss (AWS); Heeki Park (AWS)
abstract: Agents are moving from demos to production, and the compute you pick shapes security, state, and cost downstream. This session follows a real agent running on AWS and the decisions behind it. Explore serverless compute choices for agents: Lambda durable functions for orchestration and long-running workflows, and Lambda MicroVMs for running untrusted agent-generated code in isolation. Learn how to secure agents with IAM, AgentCore Identity, gateways, and secrets management, making agents stateful with RAG knowledge bases and AgentCore Memory. Control cost through token visibility, caching, pause-snapshot-resume, and right-sizing. Bring your agent architecture and the tradeoffs you're weighing.

title: Build low latency real-time bidding workloads with AWS RTB Fabric
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS RTB Fabric
speakers: Sergio Serra (AWS); Gerry Louw (AWS)
abstract: With the growth of digital media, including streaming video and retail media, customers that operate advertising platforms need to buy, sell, deliver, and measure millions of ad transactions per second while meeting stringent latency requirements. In this chalk talk, you will learn how to run real-time bidding workloads with your AdTech partners on a dedicated network in the cloud using AWS RTB Fabric. You will learn how to setup, onboard, and integrate AWS RTB Fabric with your supply and demand-side-platforms. Additionally, you will learn about key features including the core network, modules, and pricing model of the service.

title: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
speakers: Anil Maktala (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.

title: Build Your Agentic Transformation Roadmap with AWS Transform
speakers: Apoorva Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services, In.c); kevin shin (AWS)
abstract: You want to adopt agentic AI, but with hundreds of applications at different maturity levels, knowing where to start is the real challenge. In this chalk talk, we'll work through a practical framework for turning AWS Transform's automated agentic readiness and modernization analyses into a phased transformation plan. You'll see how to interpret portfolio-level scores, prioritize applications by business value and technical debt, sequence work into actionable phases, and connect readiness gaps to concrete next steps. Bring your portfolio challenges — you'll leave with a prioritization approach you can apply immediately

title: Capital One's WorkSpaces Journey: 320 to 20,000 Desktops in 72hrs
speakers: Rafael Blanco (Capital One); Joshua Schlumpberger (Capital One); Valeria Pascucci (Amazon)
abstract: Learn how to achieve enterprise-scale cloud desktop deployment from Capital One, who went from 320 manual provisions per day to 20,000 compliant desktops in 72 hours. Gain production-tested architectural patterns for meeting compliance requirements without slowing delivery. You'll also get a first look at the latest WorkSpaces innovations and our vision for the future of cloud desktops, including how we're expanding what's possible for IT teams managing modern workloads at scale. This session is for those migrating from VDI, scaling an existing fleet, or planning for what's next.

title: Centralized governance for multicloud environments
services: Amazon CloudWatch;AWS Security Hub;AWS Systems Manager
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Culture of Security
speakers: Craig Edwards (AWS); Simone Pomata (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with disparate security findings along with mis-aligned operational metrics, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model across AWS and Azure, leveraging Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability and AWS Security Hub for aggregated findings into a single surface.You'll walk through a deployable architecture that gives one analyst a unified view across clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.

title: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon EC2 - Graviton;Amazon EC2 Linux
speakers: Jake Wolf (AWS); Santiago Cardenas (AWS)
abstract: Most game studios pick server instances by vibes. This chalk talk replaces that with a number you measure on your game: cost per player at your tick rate. At the whiteboard we answer three questions: what does one tick cost, how many players fit, and what does a player cost? You’ll see how to time the whole tick in Unreal Engine and Unity, load a server with bots or thin clients against a failure rule set up front, and repeat across instances. Then we share what we measured on modern Amazon EC2 instances across AWS Graviton, AMD, and Intel: where clock speed pays, and where price decides.

title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Kiro
speakers: Matt Houghton (CDL)
abstract: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.

title: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: John Terhune (Amazon Web Services); Lee Hannigan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
speakers: Wale Akinfaderin (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Sapeksha Vemulapati (Amazon); Gowtham Shankar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EC2 - Graviton
speakers: Borja Pérez Guasch (AWS); Jon Loinaz Anton (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
speakers: Liz Radway (AWS Velocity Labs); Thomas Oosterhuis (AWS)
abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

title: DDI Architecture Patterns: DNS, DHCP, and IPAM at AWS
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Zero Trust;Identity & Access Management
abstract: Join us to explore architecture patterns for DDI - DNS, DHCP, and IP Address Management (IPAM). This session covers approaches for resolving DNS across hybrid and multicloud environments, managing private and public domains, and unifying address management for consistent governance and visibility. Walk away with best practices that simplify DDI operations at scale.

title: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
speakers: Angus Tong (Amazon Web Services); Saurabh Sharma (Amazon AWS)
abstract: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.

title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
speakers: Trevor Schiavone (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Abdu Mahmoudi (Amazon Web Services); Nadhya Polanco (AWS); Matt Eglin (AWS); Emre Alptekin (AWS)
abstract: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

title: Deploy accelerated workloads with Amazon ECS Managed Instances
speakers: pradip kumar Pandey (Amazon web services); Sai Kumar Samala (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon ECS Managed Instances let you run workloads on specialized EC2 hardware without managing the infrastructure underneath. In this workshop, deploy accelerated workloads across ML accelerators on fully managed compute. Dive deep into ECS capacity providers, learn how to optimize costs and horizontally scale accelerated workloads. Finally, we’ll monitor accelerators through CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working configuration you can adapt for your own accelerated workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Deploying a Fitness App from Specs with Kiro and AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Kiro
speakers: dima Farer (AWS); Sri Kola (Amazon)
abstract: In a simulated scenario, Fitness trainers waste 30 minutes daily on manual data entry and cannot spot trends across clients. In this SimuLearn session, you build FitTrack AI using Kiro's spec-driven workflows and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You design flexible schemas, create agent tools for client management and natural language analytics, deploy the agent on ECS Fargate, configure Bedrock Guardrails for health safety, and implement anomaly detection using database change streams.

title: Deploy, scale, and tune AI model serving with self-managed agents
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Aniruddha Deodhar (AWS); Alex Iankoulski (AWS)
abstract: Setting up AI infrastructure, tuning model performance, and benchmarking throughput could mean navigating brittle tooling, context rot in long sessions, irrelevant retrieval, missing guardrails for irreversible actions, bursty GPU and CPU demands, and observability gaps. In this chalk talk, explore how to set up, manage, and scale self-managed autonomous agents on AWS to address these challenges with built-in memory, safety boundaries, and audit trails. We will walk through how to quickly deploy a reference architecture on Amazon EKS, tune a 550B-parameter model for inference using disaggregated serving with NVIDIA Dynamo and vLLM, and scale with Elastic Fabric Adapter for cross-node KV cache transfer.

title: Designing  AI Agents with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Voice AI
speakers: Anuj Jauhari (Amazon Web Services); Nitin Eusebius (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multimodal AI agents need to understand more than text and interact through more than a screen. In this interactive chalk talk, we’ll explore how Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings connects knowledge across text, documents, images, video, and audio, including semantic search over spoken content and sound, while voice AI enables natural conversational interaction. We’ll examine cross-modal retrieval, audio and video segmentation, multimodal context, conversational orchestration, latency, and grounding tradeoffs for building responsive agents that can listen, understand, retrieve, and converse across modalities.

title: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
speakers: Kevin Hakanson (Amazon Web Services); Julian Lovelock (Amazon)
abstract: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers, including Amazon Cognito, with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns locally or in Amazon Verified Permissions, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema and policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.

title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
speakers: John Tristan (Amazon)
abstract: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

title: DTCC: Rethinking mainframe modernization with spec-driven development
speakers: Baps Patil (DTCC); Elie El khoury (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Services like Kiro, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Continuum, and AWS DevOps Agent have enabled DTCC to rethink its software delivery lifecycle. Now, the company is harnessing agents to modernize its legacy mainframe infrastructure. DTCC has adopted a spec-driven approach to COBOL refactoring, front-loading the process with a focus on principles, target architecture, and anti-pattern avoidance. In this session, you’ll see how a small team of engineers produced a fully functional microservice-based trade data ingestion platform in a few weeks, cutting the development timeline by 60% while laying the foundation to scale to peaks of 300+ million trades per day and beyond.

title: EC2 at 20: Rebuilding the control plane while it is running
speakers: Don McGarry (AWS)
abstract: Amazon EC2 launched in 2006 as four services backed by a single MySQL database. Twenty years later, it is one of the largest distributed systems ever built — and most of that original architecture had to be replaced while serving production traffic, with no maintenance window and no change to the API contract customers depend on. In this session, EC2 engineers dive deep on two of the hardest migrations: making the control plane Availability Zone independent so a single-AZ event cannot escalate into a regional one, and moving EC2 metadata off MySQL. We walk through the failure modes that forced each decision, how correctness was verified before every cutover, how we proved a single-AZ failure stays in a single AZ, and the things we got wrong along the way. You will leave with migration and isolation patterns you can apply to your own systems at any scale.

title: EC2 Flex and T instances: Get modern performance at lower cost
speakers: Saurabh Modh (Amazon Web Services); Mykhailo Karataiev (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Many workloads do not fully use all of the compute resources of a given instance, and we offer Flex and T instances to help cost-optimize for such workloads while getting the latest generation performance. In this session, we will dive deep into both Flex and T instances, which workloads are most suitable for these instances, high-level design, and ways customers can monitor the performance experience with these instances.

title: EC2 Spot: Capacity patterns and strategies from the team that runs it
speakers: Hyangelo Hao (Amazon Web Services); Chad Schmutzer (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this chalk talk, two engineers from the EC2 Spot team share what they see from the inside: how capacity behaves across regions, instance families, and time of day, including why Graviton-based Spot is consistently available and how seasonal patterns create predictable opportunities. Bring your Spot architecture questions. We'll whiteboard real diversification strategies, walk through anonymized examples from our most successful customers, and discuss what separates workloads that scale effortlessly on Spot from those that struggle.

title: End-to-end agentic modernization with United Airlines & Bank Hapoalim
speakers: Lior Kenzin (BANK HAPOALIM LTD.); Boris Alexandrov (Amazon); Margarita Rubio (United Airlines)
abstract: Legacy applications across mainframe, midrange, and distributed platforms have long resisted modernization efforts. A new approach that combines deterministic methods with agentic AI is changing that by delivering speed and accuracy. Learn how United Airlines modernized crew operations while maintaining FAR compliance, and how Bank Hapoalim analyzed a 3.2-million-line mortgage application and delivered an insurance module to production under a board-mandated deadline while reducing operational risk. Follow the end-to-end journey, from automated discovery and business rule extraction with AWS Transform through microservices engineering with Kiro to production deployment. Leave with a playbook for modernizing the applications everyone said were untouchable.

title: Event-driven agents at scale: building agentic AI on Amazon MSK
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
speakers: Luca Perrozzi (AWS); Masudur Rahaman Sayem (AWS)
abstract: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. In this session, we present reusable patterns for building multi-tenant, event-driven agentic systems on Amazon MSK: dispatch-and-resume for long-running tool calls, topic and partition design keyed to tenant and conversation, decoupling the agent loop from channels and analytics, and durability and replay so in-flight work survives deploys and retries. Learn a practical approach for designing agentic SaaS that stays reliable as load, tools, and channels grow.

title: Everything you've wanted to know about performance on EC2 instances
speakers: Arthur Petitpierre (Amazon Web Services); Seth Fox (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
speakers: Ramesh Mathikumar (Amazon Web Services); Kumudhan Cherarajan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
speakers: Vishal Lakhotia (AWS); Paul Kelsey (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with AWS Security Agent to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

title: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
speakers: Ruchi Bhatia (AWS); Sandeep Raveesh (AWS)
abstract: AI agents that do real work, such as financial advising, coding, and customer operations, reason across turns, call tools, and recover when steps fail mid-conversation. Prompting won't get you there, and building multi turn RL from scratch takes weeks. We'll whiteboard how SageMaker AI's managed MTRL connects your Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent under 10 lines of code, handling rollouts, trajectories, and checkpointing, auto cataloged in SageMaker AI catalog. We'll cover reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute keeping GPUs from idling, and smaller specialized models outperforming larger ones at lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case and we'll sketch how to train it.

title: Foundational architecture excellence: the operability trade-off
speakers: Saurabh Saxena (Amazon); Farzin Bagheri (AWS)
abstract: Elegant architectures that ignore operational reality become expensive liabilities. From hundreds of enterprise engagements, we expose the architectural decisions that silently create operational debt — decomposition without observability boundaries, blast-radius assumptions that fail under correlated load, and abstraction layers hiding the signals operators need. We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.

title: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform;Kiro
speakers: Khurram Khawaja (AWS); Mangesh Budkule (Amazon)
abstract: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.

title: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
speakers: Ben van der Merwe (AWS); Caroline Frost (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

title: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents
speakers: Nathan Jones (Amazon Web Services); Aris Tsakpinis (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every layer of an agent, from context and harness to planning loops, places additional demand on the inference engine. Each model turn created by planning, tool use, retrieval, reflection, or retry shapes cost, latency, and reliability. This chalk talk traces that evolution on Amazon Bedrock and shows the inference impact of each layer, with best practices to get them right: versioning prompts, grounding context, engineering a reliable harness, setting verifiable goal conditions, and designing loops that know when to stop. Leave knowing how each layer shapes cost, latency, and reliability.

title: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK);Amazon MQ
speakers: Mazrim Mehrtens (AWS); Vignesh Selvam (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk, we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60 minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.

title: Future-proof your keys: HSMs to AWS KMS in the post-quantum era
services: AWS CloudHSM;AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: Kevin Kevin (AWS); Derek Tumulak (AWS)
abstract: Cryptography is changing fast. The dedicated HSM you rely on today, whether AWS CloudHSM or an on-premises appliance, carries operational overhead that will only grow as the industry moves toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and stricter digital sovereignty requirements. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now covers most workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, with the same FIPS 140-3 Level 3 security, lower cost, and zero infrastructure management, while giving you a clear on-ramp to PQC and the sovereignty controls to keep your keys and data under your control. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through it together: we'll assess your workload, map signature and encryption migration paths, and show how moving to KMS puts you on the fastest path to post-quantum readiness. Meet the AWS Cryptography team and leave with a plan and concrete next steps.

title: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium;Amazon EC2 - Graviton
speakers: Barak Nissim (AWS); Kumar Shubham (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each?
