In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

title: Good fences make good neighbors: a network perimeter approach to data perimeters
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Swara Gandhi (Amazon Web Services); Jesse Lepich (AWS)
abstract: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architectural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.

title: Gotta detect 'em all: finding rogue devices with Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Jenifer Wang (Amazon Web Services); Reshad Habibzai (AWS); Anthony Castaneda (Amazon); Insoo Jang (Amazon Web Services); Collin Chew (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Participants build and command autonomous drone fleets to identify rogue devices using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS IoT Greengrass, and Strands Agents. This gamified scenario showcases a Human-Machine Teaming architecture in which AI operates autonomously within defined trust boundaries, with human-in-the-loop escalation at configurable confidence thresholds.

title: Governance foundations for AI workloads that grow into autonomous agents
speakers: Rodolfo Brenes (Amazon Web Services); Nivas Durairaj (AWS)
abstract: Agentic workloads are reaching production, and governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. This session shows how to build a governance foundation for AI with AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to autonomous agents. You apply preventive and detective controls to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence, and map controls to frameworks such as ISO 42001. The same controls hold whether the workload is a single model call or a fleet of agents acting on their own.

title: Grow Adoption Where Customers Work with AWS Bedrock and Quick
speakers: Morris Singer (Amazon Web Services); Abhishek Maligehalli Shivalingaiah (AWS); Stanley Chukwuemeke (AWS); Abhinav Sarin (Amazon Web Services); Martin Ristov (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your customers increasingly live inside an AI work surface, and your product needs to be there too. In this hands-on session, you'll take a SaaS product—its API and a simple agentic capability—and bring it into Amazon Quick using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll adapt it for AgentCore, wire up secure identity, then build Chat Agents, Research, Flows, and Apps that put your product's intelligence in front of users. Customers get your whole product in Quick, as-is. Walk out with a working reference pattern and the ability to spin up POCs for product leadership.

title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
speakers: Samir Araujo (AWS)
abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium, covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization, all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. You will leave able to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: Sudhir Reddy Maddulapally (AWS); Arvind Raghu (AWS)
abstract: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.

title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
speakers: Ariella Sasson (AWS); Necibe Ahat (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent, progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll create a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

title: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk (sponsored by Senzing)
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Gurpinder Dhillon (Senzing Inc); Gurshish Dang (Verisk Analytics)
abstract: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project. This presentation is brought to you by Senzing, an AWS Partner.

title: How Adobe unified multicloud observability with open source
speakers: Vikram Mehto (Amazon Web Services); Chris Featherstone (Adobe)
abstract: Adobe operates production services across AWS and Azure, but 20+ monitoring tools and per-cloud dashboards turned every cross-cloud incident into a translation problem before debugging could begin. In this session, hear how Adobe standardized on OpenTelemetry and consolidated to four open-source technologies (Cortex, Grafana Tempo, FluentBit, and Grafana) with AWS as the operational hub processing 1M+ trace samples per second. The result was a single pane of glass for every engineer regardless of where workloads run, and multi-million dollar savings through telemetry compression. Walk away with a proven, vendor-independent playbook for multicloud observability built on open source and open standards.

title: How Citizens Bank reimagined CX with Amazon Connect Customer & GenAI
speakers: James Kraeutler (AWS); Deepak Nair (Citizens Bank)
abstract: Citizens Financial Group is transforming its customer service ecosystem using Amazon Connect Customer, Amazon Lex, and generative AI. In this session, learn how Citizens migrated legacy IVR and contact center infrastructure to Amazon Connect Customer, deployed conversational AI across voice and digital channels, and integrated generative AI-powered agent assist and real-time conversation intelligence. We cover the solution architecture spanning Amazon Connect Customer, Amazon Lex, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge, along with measurable outcomes in containment rates, handle time, and routing accuracy. Attendees will gain a practical blueprint for enterprise-scale customer experience transformation in financial services.

title: How Moeve turned natural language into enforced governance controls
speakers: Luis Rodriguez Montilla (AWS); Rayco Martínez Hernández (MOEVE); Nicole Klatt (AWS)
abstract: Translating compliance requirements such as GDPR or NIS2 into enforceable controls usually means writing policy by hand. Moeve built a Governance Control AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock to change that. You see how engineers ask questions in natural language and the system turns their intent into SCPs, hooks, and AWS Config rules assigned at OU and account scope, validated through CI/CD and GitOps. Moeve shares the architecture and what it learned running the assistant in production.

title: How SCHUFA strengthened security operations with AWS Security Hub
speakers: Scott Ward (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Across complex cloud environments, security teams must sift through a growing volume of signals to prioritize the risks that matter most. AWS Security Hub correlates these signals across AWS and multicloud environments to surface critical attack paths and help you respond at scale. Hear firsthand from SCHUFA, Germany's main credit scoring agency, on how they adopted Security Hub to streamline security operations under strict regulatory requirements. We'll also dive into the latest capabilities, including multicloud visibility, enhanced risk correlation, AI-powered detections, and visibility into AI workloads.

title: How to build an autonomous compliance environment auditors trust
speakers: Kristine Lynn Harper (AWS Security Assurance Services, LLC); Suchita Verma (Amazon)
abstract: Auditors require evidence of compliance on demand. Learn how to keep your AWS environment audit-ready at all times, continuously producing the proof auditors need, without manual intervention. Across services such as AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Security Hub and more, we walk through an architecture that automatically collects evidence, maps it to your control frameworks, checks whether the collected evidence meets control requirements, identifies gaps and delivers prescriptive guidance to close each gap. We finish with how AI agents now investigate findings, draft remediations, and defend evidence to auditors, moving compliance from continuous monitoring to continuous resolution.

title: How to solve for multicloud identity lifecycle management
speakers: Phillip Spies (aws); Rodney Underkoffler (Amazon Web Services); Joshua Stultz (National Institutes of Health)
abstract: Organizations operating in multiple clouds face a compounding multi-cloud identity lifecycle governance challenge. How do you provision, manage, audit, and decommission identities when each cloud provider enforces different authorization models, attribute schemas, and lifecycle hooks? In this session, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), a federal research organization, describes how it uses a centralized identity governance platform to provision identities and entitlements across AWS and Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to avoid governance divergence and design identity lifecycles where access reviews, birthright provisioning, and decommissioning work consistently, regardless of which cloud the identity lands in.

title: Improving operations with agentic AI
speakers: Greg Eppel (Amazon Web Services); Elliot Markowitz (Verisk Analytics); Igor Sedukhin (AWS)
abstract: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.

title: In-Country HPC: How TGS Processes Seismic Data on AWS Brazil
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Kun Jiao (AWS); Faisal Asif (TGS)
abstract: TGS -- one of the world's largest multi-client geoscience data providers -- faced a significant cost challenge running its business-critical Rackmon EFWI GPU workload at scale. By strategically deploying this workload on AWS infrastructure in Brazil, TGS leveraged Brazil's ReData Special Tax Regime to dramatically reduce the tax burden on GPU-intensive seismic processing. The result: material cost savings on one of the most computationally demanding workloads in the energy industry -- and a reusable in-country processing architecture that can serve future customers with data residency requirements in other geographies.

title: Investigating Threats to AI: Incident Response to Compromised AI Workloads
speakers: Kyle Shields (AWS); Steve de Vera (AWS)
abstract: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
speakers: Joe Guo (AWS); Bolin Chen (Amazon)
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
speakers: Nihar Sheth (AWS); Pushparaju Thangavel (AWS)
abstract: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

title: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
speakers: Joe Losinski (AWS); Matt Diamond (AWS)
abstract: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

title: Latest trends: Network/EBS intensive workloads on Amazon EC2 instances
speakers: Anti Gyori (Amazon); Aaron Chen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: EC2 network 'n' and EBS-optimized 'b' instances deliver the highest, most consistent network and EBS performance in the cloud. Join us for a tour of the latest Graviton and Intel instance types in these families, plus the networking and EBS technologies that unlock peak performance for your workloads. Learn how customers leverage these instances for new workloads associated with AI/ML training and inference, and traditional network-intensive workloads such as security & network virtual appliances, and EBS-intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and in-memory databases.

title: Learn how to build a Genomics PCS pipeline on AWS
services: Amazon FSx for Lustre;AWS Parallel Computing Service
speakers: Shubhendu Dubey (AWS); Kumar Shubham (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build and run a real genomics variant-calling Slurm pipeline on AWS PCS using a mixed Graviton + GPU fleet. This session will cover PCS queue design, Slurm partition strategy, FSx for Lustre, EFA networking, and result aggregation to Amazon S3. By the end, you’ll create a reproducible, production-grade HPC workflow for life-sciences workloads.

title: Make the agent code while you sleep
speakers: Keerthi Sreenivas Konjety (Amazon); Govindhi Venkatachalapathy (AWS)
abstract: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
speakers: Hajer Bouafif (AWS); prasadnu Mohan Prasad (AWS)
abstract: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.

title: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
speakers: Yaniv Ehrlich (Eon.io); Gonen Stein (Eon)
abstract: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. This presentation is brought to you by Eon, an AWS Partner.

title: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
speakers: Hillel Antonov (Bridgewater Associates); Kyle Seaman (AWS); Aaron Longwell (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.

title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
speakers: Bowen Wang (Amazon Web Services); Matt Berk (AWS); Jordi Espasa Clofent (Aviv Group GmbH)
abstract: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
speakers: Pavitra Krishnan (AWS); Derek Chiles (AWS)
abstract: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

title: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
speakers: Vikas Babu Gali (Amazon); Koushik Rajagopal (Amazon)
abstract: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

title: Migrating petabytes of data: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
speakers: Ameen Khan S (AWS); Wali Akbari (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes. Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.

title: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
speakers: Satya Vandrangi (AWS); John Jamail (AWS)
abstract: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.

title: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
speakers: Varun Kulkarni (AWS); Moshe Barlev (AWS)
abstract: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

title: Need for Speed: The journey to high EBS performance on EC2 instances
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Shyam Rajagopal (Amazon); Kirill Davydychev (AWS)
abstract: Achieving consistent, low-latency block storage at cloud scale requires rethinking every layer of the IO stack. In this session, we walk you through the architectural evolution of Amazon EBS, and show how a series of innovations reduced hypervisor overhead, slashed network latency, and enabled higher block storage IOPS and throughput on your EC2 instances. We will also discuss how Nitro enabled specific EBS features such as Instance bandwidth Configuration, Torn Write Protection, and detailed performance statistics via NVMe logs. Bring your questions and leave with an understanding of how EBS delivers high performing block storage for your mission-critical applications.

title: Network policy across hundreds of accounts with AWS Network Security Manager
speakers: Ian Olson (Amazon Web Services); Robert Albach (AWS)
abstract: Once an organization grows to hundreds of accounts, managing network security policies by hand becomes a liability. AWS Network Security Manager deploys AWS WAF, AWS Shield, and soon to come AWS Network Firewall across a multi-account environment from a single policy definition. This session covers how to build defense in depth with Network Security Manager, and how to keep centralized network security manageable as you add accounts.

title: Observability-driven scaling: Teaching EKS clusters to right-size themselves
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Tiago Reichert (AWS); HC Lo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Scaling container workloads reactively by waiting for CPU to spike or pods to crash leaves money on the table and risks user-facing latency. This chalk talk explores observability-driven scaling: using CloudWatch Container Insights, KEDA, and custom metrics pipelines to make Amazon EKS clusters anticipate demand before it arrives. We walk through real architectures where teams replaced reactive HPA with predictive scaling informed by business metrics, reduced over-provisioning by 40%, and cut P99 latency during traffic ramps. Bring your scaling headaches and we'll whiteboard solutions together.

title: One agent to thousands: Building for scale with Newforma
speakers: Benjamin Bazso (Newforma, Inc.); Mahesh Biradar (Amazon); Vikrant Dhir (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same ungovernable sprawl that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms. Agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance, and this tension drives every platform decision, from dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, to policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, to defense layers that compose without coupling. We walk through how Newforma operationalized this architecture on AWS, and attendees leave understanding how to layer orchestration, policy, and defense into an enterprise agent platform that scales safely.

title: Operating Lambda at scale: Choosing the right execution model
speakers: Nati Goldberg (AWS); Uri Segev (AWS)
abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

title: Optimize cost & performance in Amazon RDS for SQL Server
speakers: Eric Felice (AWS); Sudhir Amin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Cost and performance are top of mind for customers, and these topics go hand in hand. In this chalk talk, learn how to deploy a performant and cost-effective Amazon RDS for SQL Server solution that fits your needs. Explore RDS monitoring tools and native SQL Server features that can be leveraged to pinpoint query inefficiencies, optimize workloads, and right-size your database instances for both cost and peak performance.

title: Optimize your Amazon Aurora resources to reduce costs
speakers: Chirag Dave (AWS); Aditya Samant (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native managed relational database that lets you create, manage, and scale your database resources with ease. In this session, dive deep into Aurora cost components and see how you can use cost-focused features and tooling to optimize costs for your workload without sacrificing performance or scale. Learn how the Aurora I/O-Optimized configuration can help you achieve cost savings for I/O-intensive workloads, and discover how Database Savings Plans can provide additional cost reductions through flexible commitment-based pricing.

title: Optimize your Amazon EC2 instances: Profile, diagnose, decide
speakers: Toby Buckley (AWS); Julio Arnedo (AWS)
abstract: Which EC2 instance performs best? It depends on the workload. In this hands-on workshop, learn a repeatable methodology: observe with APerf, find breaking points, diagnose pipeline bottlenecks, and decide by price-performance across AWS Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. Then fix code guided by profiling data.

title: Optimizing model performance with agentic loops on AWS Trainium
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Esha Lakhotia (Annapurna Labs); Adam Stanley (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Extracting peak performance from AI accelerators requires optimization at every level, from framework configuration down to individual kernels, and the complexity grows with every new workload. Agentic loops replace this manual work with autonomous profiling, diagnosis, and code generation, iterating toward performance targets without human intervention. In this session, we demonstrate this workflow on AWS Trainium, purpose-built to deliver better price-performance for AI workloads. Explore how these loops identify bottlenecks, how persistent memory prevents repeated failures, and how long-running campaigns uncover optimizations for different inference shapes. You will leave able to run agentic optimization loops yourself on AWS Trainium.

title: Orchestrating Physical AI workloads on AWS: Compute and pipeline patterns
speakers: Vincent Wang (Amazon); Carlos Manzanedo Rueda (AWS)
abstract: Physical AI projects — robotics, autonomous systems, digital twins — require complex multi-stage pipelines spanning simulation, training, evaluation, and edge deployment. Each stage demands different compute and orchestration. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architecture patterns combining AWS Batch for parallel simulation, Amazon EKS with Karpenter for heterogeneous GPU/Trainium training, and SageMaker Hyperpod showcasing managed resiliency. We'll compare when to use EKS vs. Batch vs. ParallelCluster, discuss cost optimization with Capacity Blocks and Spot, and solve attendee architectures live on the whiteboard.

title: Outrun technical debt in the age of autonomous development
speakers: Ritik Khatwani (Amazon Web Services); Ali Maaz (Amazon); Alessandro Lori (Verizon Connect)
abstract: The legacy estate has not gone away. Aging applications with undocumented business logic, outdated frameworks, and platforms nobody wants to touch remain a priority. Agentic tools have increased development velocity, but speed does not eliminate technical debt — it changes its shape. This compounding debt erodes productivity, weakens security posture, and inflates operational cost. Learn how AWS Transform custom and continuous modernization help organizations assess and remediate technical debt at scale — from framework migrations like Angular to React to language translations like C to Rust.

title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
speakers: Mansi Suratwala (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Fabio Braga de Oliveira ()
abstract: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

title: Practical applications of edge compute in Amazon CloudFront
speakers: Nick McCord (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Edge compute is a practical way to build faster, smarter applications. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into how Amazon CloudFront empowers developers to run custom logic at the edge using CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge, and the Key Value Store. We'll explore real-world use cases, architectural patterns, and recent feature launches that unlock powerful personalization, performance optimization, and cost efficiency. Come ready to whiteboard, ask questions, and discover how to push intelligence closer to your users.

title: Prime Video Financial Systems on the Road to 10x Velocity with Kiro
aoi: Innovation & Transformation;Automation;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Tulip Gupta (AWS); Robert Cicero (Amazon); Kannan Ekanath (Amazon)
abstract: This chalk talk will deep-dive into Prime Video Financial Systems' journey toward 10x engineering velocity with Kiro. Starting at 3x through AI-assisted sprints, the team evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery, where agents pick up tasks, implement code, raise code requests, address feedback, and merge 24/7 without human intervention. Each step compounds, enabling parallel execution, zero idle time, and freeing engineers to focus on design and review. This is an honest, in-progress story that demonstrates the concrete methodology, structured specs, persistent Kiro sessions, and architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.

title: Private AI agent egress: VPC Lattice meets AgentCore Gateway
speakers: Shubham Singh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your AI agents need to call private MCP servers, internal REST APIs, and OAuth providers, but those backends must never touch the public internet. In this lightning talk, we demo how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway uses managed Amazon VPC Lattice endpoints to route agent traffic privately into your VPC. We'll configure a private MCP server target, show traffic staying on the AWS backbone, and cover key patterns including intermediate domain routing, private certificate workarounds with ALB, and cross-account connectivity. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for secure, zero-public-internet agentic workloads.

title: Race to migrate and modernize with agentic AI at the EBA cloud party
speakers: Rajesh Kumar (Amazon); Maria Armstrong (AWS)
abstract: Imagine compressing months of cloud migration and modernization into days, tackling legacy code, tight timelines, and cross-team coordination head-on. That's exactly what the Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) method delivers. In this hands-on, gamified EBA workshop, cross-functional squads split into workstreams and race to migrate and modernize a legacy app and its databases, apply cloud best practices, and deploy the transformed architecture, all in the cloud. Experience firsthand how EBA shatters silos and compresses migration and modernization from months into days with AWS Transform and Kiro. You'll get repeatable playbook your team can run on Monday. Ready to play?

title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
services: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams;Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
speakers: Chinmayi Narasimhadevara (Amazon Web Services); Ankita Mishra (Amazon)
abstract: Batch jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive agentic AI on AWS.

title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
speakers: Aoife Egan (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Sanket Nasre (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
speakers: Kevin McGehee (Amazon); Jeff Duffy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

title: Reimagining Patient Engagement with AI and Cloud (sponsored by Incedo Inc.)
services: Amazon Redshift;Amazon SageMaker AI;Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speakers: Nitin Seth (Incedo Inc - SI Partner)
abstract: Life sciences organizations are exploring how AI and cloud can transform engagement across the patient journey. This executive discussion will examine how connected data, generative AI and intelligent automation can enable more personalized, timely and responsive patient experiences. The conversation will explore opportunities to reduce friction, improve engagement, drive adherence, and deliver more connected omnichannel experiences aligned with business priorities. It will also address the challenges of data fragmentation, governance, trust and adoption. Attendees will gain practical executive perspectives on moving beyond AI experimentation to scalable, responsible solutions that deliver meaningful value for patients and life sciences organizations.

title: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
speakers: Ash Naik (Amazon/AWS); Elizabeth Davis (AWS)
abstract: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.

title: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
speakers: Kunj Thacker (Amazon Web Services); Mevlit Mustafa (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers, and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.

title: Right-size and scale Amazon ECS with effective autoscaling patterns
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Fargate
speakers: Debojit Bhadra (AWS); Shalabh Srivastava ()
abstract: Autoscaling containerized workloads means scaling both tasks and the infrastructure underneath them. This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

title: Right workload on the right cloud - multicloud workload placement
abstract: You operate a multicloud organization, and every new workload raises the same challenge: which cloud should this workload run on? Too often the answer comes down to habit, existing vendor relationships, or whoever argues loudest, and workloads end up somewhere that adds complexity, risk, or complicates compliance. In this session you will learn how to approach multicloud workload placement so that the decisions you make are explainable, repeatable and auditable.

title: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
speakers: Erez Zarum (AWS); Dmitry Nutels (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.

title: Scale AI-powered software development securely with Bedrock
speakers: Sriharsha M S (Amazon Web Services Inc.); Pedro Javier Paez (AWS); Jose Navarro (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Your dev teams are adopting AI coding agents fast: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, open-source agents, and more. Without a shared platform, every team rolls its own auth, its own cost tracking, its own rules. In this builders session, build one platform on Amazon Bedrock that manages all of them. Package your security policies, coding standards, and delivery practices as reusable plugins, agent skills, and MCP servers, then apply consistent identity, sandboxing, observability, and cost controls across every agent. Use the platform to turn an issue into a tested change, then adapt the architecture across your organization.

title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
speakers: Erez Zarum (AWS); Sheetal Joshi (AWS)
abstract: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

title: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
speakers: Samyak Kathane (Amazon Web Services); Venkata Sistla (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.

title: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Pinak Panigrahi (Annapurna ML, AWS); Achintya Pinninti (Amazon Web Services); Andre Gomes (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. See how purpose-built chips change the inference economics equation as you deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and connect the Neuron software stack to familiar open-source frameworks without rewrites to achieve superior tokenomics. You will leave able to run performant, cost-effective frontier model inference in production on AWS Trainium yourself.

title: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Billing and Cost Management
speakers: Sagar Utekar (CrowdStrike)
abstract: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.

title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
speakers: Maxim Raya (AWS); Itay Meller (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

title: Select and launch the right EC2 instance for your workload and budget
speakers: Tirtho Deb (AWS); Ian Bablewski (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: With hundreds of EC2 instance types spanning compute, memory, storage, and accelerator families, choosing the right one can be overwhelming. In this session, learn a practical framework for matching your workload characteristics—CPU, memory, network, and storage requirements—to the optimal instance type and size. We cover cost-performance tradeoffs across On-Demand, Spot, and Savings Plans, share real-world selection patterns for common workloads, and demo tools that simplify decision-making. Leave with a repeatable process to right-size from day one.

title: Serverless observability: OpenTelemetry and vended logs
speakers: Franklin Aguinaldo (Amazon Web Services); Maxime David (AWS)
abstract: Debugging distributed serverless applications used to mean stitching together X-Ray traces, CloudWatch logs, and custom metrics from multiple extensions. In this chalk talk, we cover setup and configuration, end-to-end tracing with API Gateway vended logs, and distributed tracing across Step Functions, EventBridge, and SQS. We also discuss observability for agentic workloads: tracking token consumption, tool call success rates, and workflow checkpoint state. Bring your observability questions, especially around cost at scale: sampling, filtering, and cardinality management.

title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
speakers: Guillermo Ojeda (Caylent)
abstract: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

title: Simplifying how you use AWS: automating common patterns on your behalf
speakers: Steve Rice (AWS)
abstract: Getting the most out of AWS often means manually setting up the same optimizations, integrations, and best-practice patterns across your applications. What if AWS could handle more of that for you - automatically and securely - so you benefit from AWS capabilities without the setup overhead? In this chalk talk, we explore emerging approaches for running AWS-authored logic in isolated, secure-by-default environments alongside your applications, implementing common patterns on your behalf and simplifying how you consume AWS services. We'll whiteboard how this model works, where it fits in your architecture, and how it changes the effort required to adopt AWS best practices.

title: State Street: AI agents that write, deploy, and govern at scale
speakers: Ata Turk (State Street); Vignesh Ashok kumar (State Street Corp); Manjit Chakraborty (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Landing zones, drift detection, and migration backlogs pile up faster than platform teams can manage. In this lightning talk, State Street will share how they built AI agents that embed directly in application teams, taking infrastructure requirements as input, generating compliant Terraform, and handling provisioning without a ticket queue. Every resource stays within policy guardrails before it reaches production. Learn how integrating AI agents into the DevOps lifecycle accelerates delivery while maintaining governance and security across the enterprise.

title: Stop fighting fires: operations that prevent incidents
speakers: Isaiah Salinas (AWS); Ania Develter (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The best incident is the one that never happens, yet most teams stay stuck firefighting. Learn to collect the right operational signals beyond just observability and use AI to spot problems before they page anyone. We'll cover auto-healing and remediation with traditional techniques and AI agents that catch misconfiguration before production. You'll discover how early-warning systems spot issues before customers do, and how agentic investigation turns past incidents into ranked recommendations that prevent future ones. Walk away with actionable steps to start building proactive operations.

title: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
speakers: Saurabh Saxena (Amazon); Ramesh Seshadri (Amazon.com)
abstract: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.

title: Strategies for optimizing enterprise licenses on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS License Manager
speakers: Christine Megit (Amazon Web Services); Valerie Rosenfield (AWS); Parker Caputo (Exxon Mobil Corporation)
abstract: Migrating to the cloud and running efficiently once you're there are two different disciplines. In this session, hear ExxonMobil's firsthand journey from a large-scale lift-and-shift migration to a disciplined, data-driven optimization practice, and the role the AWS Optimization and Licensing Assessment (OLA) played both before the move and after, for ongoing optimization. Parker Caputo (ExxonMobil) shares how his team used real utilization data to right-size 800+ EC2 instances and realize over $2M in annualized savings without sacrificing performance. We'll then explore the tools and programs that make optimization an informed decision at any stage, and close on the layer most native tools can't see on their own: Microsoft licensing. Learn why licensing can represent 30–50% of Windows and SQL Server workload TCO, and how to optimize it as part of your cloud cost strategy.

title: Streamlining Claims Processing with Amazon Quick
speakers: Ryan Forger (Amazon Web Services); Ryan Leavitt (Amazon)
abstract: Claims adjusters spend hours retrieving policy data, applying business rules, and drafting decision letters manually. In this SimuLearn session, you use Amazon Quick Automate to orchestrate the entire claims process. You configure REST API and MCP connectors, build a multi-step workflow with Custom Agent steps, and chain together policy retrieval, rules validation, and AI-powered letter generation. The workflow handles missing data gracefully and stores audit-ready decision letters in S3.

title: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
speakers: Sanchith Kandaka (AWS); Fenil Patel (Amazon); David MacDonald (Amazon); Harith Gaddamanugu (AWS); Kartik Bheemisetty (AMAZON WEB SERVICES)
abstract: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds. Origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
speakers: Håkon Eriksen Drange (Sopra Steria)
abstract: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."

title: The Art of the Impossible: How Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Tulip Gupta (AWS); Naresh Narayanan (Amazon)
abstract: Discover how two Amazon teams tackled seemingly impossible problems with agentic AI running on AWS. Prime Video enabled content discovery at a scale where personalized curation was never feasible, building an AI discovery assistant powered by agentic search on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, vector-powered retrieval, and frontier and custom LLMs on SageMaker. Launched to millions of Fire TV customers, it replaced endless scrolling with conversation starters like "hidden gems from the '80s" and natural voice exploration. Amazon Pharmacy now autonomously resolves most of its hundreds of thousands of monthly customer contacts while staying HIPAA compliant. Specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock Agents and Amazon Connect handle billing, fulfillment, and pharmacist workflows, hand off to humans, increasing satisfaction. Learn to apply their approaches to your own seemingly impossible problems.

title: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
speakers: AMAN Raj (Amazon Web Services); Nitin Kumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. Over-decomposed architectures create distributed monoliths, event spaghetti, and operational nightmares that cost more and move slower than the monolith they replaced. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.

title: The Trade Desk's Cloud Journey: AI-Assisted Optimization to AI Agents
speakers: Shreyas Shah (The TradeDesk); Sharik Pahwa (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The Trade Desk operates a real-time advertising platform on AWS, where infrastructure must handle massive scale while making bidding decisions in milliseconds. At that volume, cloud cost optimization is a continuous discipline, not a one-time audit. In this breakout, The Trade Desk shares how it moved from manual cost audits to an AI-assisted approach: an internal MCP server that lets AI agents investigate cost and usage data, surface savings across services like S3, NAT Gateway, EBS, and Graviton, and apply a repeatable method for optimizing workloads over time. You'll see how the team structured the agents, what they found, and where the approach is headed.

title: Threat technique catalog for AWS: practical controls for real TTPs
speakers: Shannon Brazil (AWS); Cydney Stude (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Threat actors are evolving faster than ever, leveraging AI-generated exploits and automated attack tooling to move at machine speed. AWS CIRT sees these techniques firsthand across customer incidents of all sizes. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn observed attacker patterns into an advantage: build actionable detections and mitigations into your security operations before the next incident hits.

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
speakers: David Yanacek (AWS); Priyatam Mudivarti (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

title: Transform Episodic Content into High-Converting Microdramas
speakers: Chris Swan (AWS); Saurav Bhattacharya (AWS)
abstract: Turn your episodic content into binge-worthy microdramas. In this session, you'll learn how to build both single- and multi-episode formats, multiply one source into a library of platform-ready content assets, and monetize a story in multiple ways including advertising, subscription, and social distribution. We'll walk through scroll-stopping production techniques optimized for vertical, mobile-first viewing, and the pacing and cliffhanger patterns that drive completion and re-watch rates. Leave with a repeatable workflow for producing microdrama series at scale and a clear playbook for turning your existing catalog into high-converting, platform-ready short-form videos.

title: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Mikhail Shapirov (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Vikram Venkataraman (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.

title: Turn a Bee wearable into your re:Invent notetaking companion
speakers: Kourtney Meiss (Amazon); Emerson Sklar (Amazon Alexa)
abstract: re:Invent keynotes don't slow down for note-taking. Last year's CEO keynote announced roughly 28 launches in two hours. Careful notes still leave you with names, not links. So build an agent that does the finding. Participants in this workshop will get a Bee Pioneer wearable: it transcribes while you listen, and a double-press bookmarks anything worth a deep dive. Your agent (Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock) reads the transcript and researches each announcement through the AWS MCP Server, producing one markdown file linking every launch to its docs. Then make it yours: benchmark cheaper models, post to Slack, or run it in the cloud.

title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
speakers: kirankumar chandrashekar (Amazon Web Services); Ryan Yanchuleff (AWS)
abstract: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

title: Unlock your AWS Graviton potential using Graviton Savings Dashboard and AI skills
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Billing and Cost Management;Amazon Quick Suite
speakers: Rosa Corley (AWS); Jake Wolf (AWS); Rajani Guptan (AWS); Julio Chaves (AWS); Bhavik Gandhi (AWS)
abstract: How much can you save by migrating to Graviton? In this builder session, explore two complementary ways to answer it, hands-on. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an AWS Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent runs against your cost and usage data to produce a prioritized migration plan. Use both tools against a sample fleet, identify migration candidates, and see how quickly cost data becomes a migration strategy. Walk away with actionable insights and a deployment kit for your own accounts.

title: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
speakers: Marc Brooker (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.

title: Watch AWS Transform convert SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL live
speakers: Prasad Rao (AWS); Alexander Dragunov (AWS)
abstract: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.

title: What's new with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
abstract: Organizations increasingly need to work with the same real-time data in different ways depending on the workload, and today that often means integrating services and building custom workarounds to make it fit. In this chalk talk, we head to the whiteboard to explore how Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is evolving to handle more of these patterns natively, so you can consolidate more of your real-time architecture onto one service. We work through how to design for the way your workload actually behaves, how scaling can adapt automatically as traffic rises and falls, and where teams can remove complexity and cost rather than adding another pipeline.

title: When AI Moves Money: Secure the Agentic Future of Financial Services (sponsored by TrendAI™)
abstract: Organizations are racing to adopt AI, but many struggle to balance innovation, governance, and security. In this session, learn how Discover how technology leaders are enabling AI innovation while reducing operational risk and complexity. enterprises are using TrendAI Vision One on AWS to accelerate AI initiatives, gain visibility across complex cloud environments, and reduce operational risk without slowing the business. Discover real-world deployment patterns, lessons learned, and the architectural principles that help security teams move from reactive defense to proactive risk management while enabling AI at scale. Built on AWS-native services and integrated across the cloud ecosystem, this approach helps organizations simplify operations, improve threat detection, and confidently embrace the next wave of transformation. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
speakers: Shubhankar Sumar (AWS); Damian Niezgoda (AWS)
abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
speakers: Mukund Rao (Amazon Web Services); Sushanth Mangalore (AWS)
abstract: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Amee Shah (Amazon Web Services); Harshil A Shah (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
speakers: Lydia Eichelberg (MongoDB); Nina Lopatina (MongoDB)
abstract: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Your next Quantum developer might be an AI agent
services: Amazon Braket;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Kiro
speakers: Nick White (Amazon Web Services); Ishaan Pakrasi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI is changing who can build quantum applications. See how AI assistants including Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Jupyter AI, and Classiq help developers move from natural-language prompts to optimized quantum workloads on Amazon Braket. Learn how AI generates code, synthesizes hardware-aware circuits, benchmarks on simulators and QPUs, and integrates with HPC resources. Through real examples, you'll see how AI-native workflows reduce complexity, accelerate experimentation, and make quantum development accessible to more builders.

title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
aoi: Digital Sovereignty;Disaster Response & Recovery;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Hossam Ebrahim (AWS); Paul Armstrong (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.

title: Accelerate Apache Spark data processing with GPUs at lower cost
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EMR
speakers: Karthik Prabhakar (Amazon Web Services); Vidish Mehta (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Data-intensive workloads like feature engineering, large-scale ETL, and real-time analytics push CPU-based clusters to their limits. In this session, learn how Amazon EMR with NVIDIA RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark runs Spark workloads up to 3.7x faster on Amazon EC2 G7 instances—with no code changes. We share benchmarking results, walk through architecture and tuning patterns, and show how finishing jobs faster lowers the cost per run, even at a higher hourly rate.

title: Accelerate database protection, recovery, and testing with Amazon EBS
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: James Kuhlke (Amazon); Juha Sarimaa (Amazon Web Services); Tom Edward Bailey (AWS); Sara Kilbride (AWS); Kathy Huffstetler (Amazom)
abstract: Protecting your data and troubleshooting issues are essential for running production self-managed databases on AWS. This builders’ session tackles both. Get hands-on with EBS Snapshot Lock for immutable backups, Recycle Bin for accidental deletion recovery, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for automated, application-consistent snapshots. Learn Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization for predictable restore throughput and use EBS Volume Clones to create virtually instant point-in-time copies without impacting production. You will leave with a practical playbook to improve your database resilience. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Accelerate declarative resource management with Amazon EKS Capabilities
speakers: Petro Kashlikov (AWS); Tzahi Mizrahi (AWS); Javier Garcia Garcia (AWS); Amine Hilaly (AWS); Navya Srivastava (AWS)
abstract: Platform teams struggle to deliver self-service infrastructure that is both fast and governed. Developers want Kubernetes-native provisioning, but adopting new tools while managing existing IaC investments creates friction. In this builders session, explore the latest Amazon EKS Capabilities features including kro Collections, Graph Revisions, and reactive watches for advanced declarative resource management. Then use Kiro to build an agentic workflow that accelerates migration from legacy IaC to Kubernetes-native resource definitions. Leave with working implementations you can bring back to your platform.

title: A day in the life of a SPIFFE SVID
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Brendan Paul (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Workloads across AWS, on premises, and other clouds need verifiable identity without long-lived secrets, and SPIFFE provides it. In this lightning talk, we show how to issue SPIFFE SVIDs and how they flow into AWS. You follow one SVID through SPIRE attestation, cross-cloud federation, exchange for STS credentials through IAM Roles Anywhere or AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and presentation to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity for AI agent tool access.

title: Adding agentic AI to your legacy app without a rewrite
speakers: Franz Stefan (Amazon Web Services); Robert Hanuschke (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Full legacy application rewrites take years. Agentic AI lets you deliver value now. In this code talk, we build an AI agent that wraps an existing legacy application without changing the core system. You'll see how the agent understands user intent, calls existing application functions, and helps users complete business tasks through a modern conversational experience. Ask questions as we go from legacy to AI-assisted workflow in real time. You'll leave ready to put agentic AI in front of your legacy application today.

title: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
speakers: Matias Kreder (Ryz Labs); Ricardo Ceci (VN Studios)
abstract: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.

title: Agentic commerce: Use AI agents with AWS Marketplace
speakers: Arun Saksena (AWS)
