abstract: Managing software procurement across dozens of tools, teams, and accounts is slow and error-prone. In this lightning talk, we use AI agents to automate the buyer journey on AWS Marketplace to discover and evaluate products, accept discounted offers instantly, enforce governance, achieve operational excellence, request refunds and cancellations, and gain unified visibility into spend and cost management. Compress procurement from weeks to minutes while maintaining governance and financial controls.

title: AI Assistant for Public Sector: Governance Without Compromise with Amazon Quick
speakers: Rima Olinger (AWS); Mike Westwood (University of Exeter); Sonali Sahu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Public sector organizations serve diverse populations with strict boundaries: students and administrators, citizens and case workers, patients and providers. They need AI that works across these groups without compromising data isolation, compliance, or governance. Multi-tenant environments demand security frameworks most AI assistants were not built to meet. Hear from a higher education customer who faced these constraints and displaced their incumbent tool in favor of Amazon Quick's governance-first architecture: tenant-level data isolation, role-based access controls across distinct user populations, and compliance frameworks built for regulated environments. Learn why existing solutions fell short, how Quick's native governance model met their requirements without custom engineering, and what the transition looked like from decision to deployment.

title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
aoi: Business Intelligence;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Tom Godden (AWS); Karolis Urbonas (AWS)
abstract: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

title: Allianz: Building domain AI agents that scale across the enterprise
speakers: Lars Nettemann (Allianz); Patrik Nagel (AWS); Lennard Ufer (Allianz)
abstract: Delivering one coherent agent experience across a large enterprise means connecting agents to core business systems, each with its own identity, compliance, and security requirements. Learn how Allianz moved a reusable agentic framework into regulated production, with one entry point routing every request to specialist domain agents through open standards like MCP. The session covers the trust model, with scoped authorization at every boundary, and how shared services for identity, data protection, and consent let business teams focus on their domain. Finally, discover go-live lessons and who owns a shared agent service across legal entities.

title: Aperf: An all-in-one tool for performance data collection and analysis
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon EC2 Linux
speakers: Congkai Tan (Annapurna Labs (U.S.) Inc.); Arthur Petitpierre (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. Finally, we'll open the conversation to collect feedback and feature requests from the audience.

title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
speakers: Daniela Kinsella (The New York Times); Will Matos (Amazon Web Services); Heeki Park (AWS)
abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.

title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
speakers: Everton Queiroz (Banco Bmg); Matheus Arrais (AWS)
abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.

title: AWS migration agents fast-tracking SAP modernization
speakers: Erik Kamman (AWS)
abstract: AI agents built on AWS are fast-tracking SAP migration and modernization from months to days. Learn from our marquee customers how they are deploying agentic fleets on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore spanning SAP landscape, auto-resolving complex workflows same-day that previously took days across multiple teams, saving thousands of hours and millions in operational costs. A reusable framework means each new agent inherits production-grade infrastructure from day one. In this session, learn how AI-powered migration agents de-risk ECC-to-S/4HANA transitions, accelerate RISE with SAP adoption, and modernize ABAP and BW workloads.

title: AWSome Automation: From Project Brief Prompt to Landing Page (sponsored by Storyblok)
speakers: Daniel Mendoza (Storyblok)
abstract: Building a product-launch agent means solving several problems at once: assembling content from approved components, enforcing brand guidelines, localizing across markets, and ensuring a human has final say before anything reaches production. This session examines how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Storyblok handle each of those concerns without requiring a separate governance layer. Explore why a custom Strands agent made more sense than the no-code harness, how Cedar policies, Storyblok's component whitelist, brand guidelines, and publishing workflows form complementary guardrail layers, and how the architecture takes a brief to a reviewed, localized landing page in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Storyblok, an AWS Partner.

title: AWS Partner: Build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption
speakers: Gaby Chaib (AWS)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI workflows fail in ways that don't show up until production: a human misses the deadline, an external system says no, a sub-workflow loses state mid-flight. Fix it. Combine Step Functions, Lambda durable functions, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore into a three-layer stack that routes decisions, checkpoints execution, and reasons through uncertainty. Run real scenarios through the Simulator Panel and trace every layer live. Leave ready to build AI workflows that laugh in the face of disruption. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS Partner: Ship an AI agent without crossing your fingers
speakers: Emiliano Espinoza (AWS)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. AI agents work great in demos but break in production. Replace luck with observability. Prototype a role-based agent with the Strands SDK. Evaluate it with custom evaluators for quality and compliance. Deploy it to production on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Observe it with OpenTelemetry tracing and CloudWatch dashboards. Detect drift by evaluating production traffic at scale. Leave ready to take a customer's AI agent from prototype to production-grade. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Balancing trust and agility: payment cryptography in the cloud with Capital One
speakers: Balaji Palanisamy (Amazon); Kevin Osborn (Capital One)
abstract: How can we trust AWS with our payment keys? Join AWS payment security specialists and Capital One as they break down the controls and compliance behind cloud-based payment cryptography. Learn how AWS built trust through transparency, openly sharing its security architecture in public documentation and validating compliance through rigorous third-party assessments. As a result Capital One offloads infrastructure security to AWS and channels its energy into application-level protection and payment innovation that moves the business forward.

title: Beyond AIOps: Operating safely in the age of agent sprawl
speakers: Tarran Benson-West (HMRC); Ash Thankey (Amazon Web Services); Paul Moran (AWS); Samuel Walls (HM Revenue & Customs)
abstract: As organisations move from a small number of AI assistants to a distributed ecosystem of agents that can discover tools, make decisions, and act, operational excellence must evolve. Drawing on HMRC’s work to develop a governed platform model for agentic systems, this session explores a practical maturity model spanning inventory, ownership, identity, delegated authority, observability, blast-radius controls, evaluation, and human accountability. Learn how existing platform engineering, SRE, security and service-management practices can be extended across cloud and SaaS ecosystems without creating a separate governance regime for every agent or vendor. Designed for platform leaders, SREs and architects preparing to scale agents safely in complex, regulated environments.

title: Bringing better Amazon EC2 price performance to your pipeline with AWS Graviton
speakers: Diego Nieto Marin (AWS); Allan Henrique Homenhuck (AWS Brazil)
abstract: Which workload should move to AWS Graviton first? And what actually changes in your pipeline? In this code talk, we answer both live. We profile an application portfolio to find strong Arm64 candidates, check dependency and library compatibility, and update a working CI/CD pipeline to build multi-architecture container images for x86 and Arm64, so you see exactly what changes and why. Then we deploy the workload and run a side-by-side load test to compare price performance. You'll leave with a repeatable workload-selection checklist and pipeline patterns you can apply to your own AWS Graviton adoption with minimal disruption.

title: Build a cost optimization playbook for your AI workload
speakers: Eitan Sela (Amazon); Shreeya Sharma (Amazon Web Services); Shivi Shivi (Amazon Web Services Inc.); Yaakov Tayeb (Amazon); Jamie Brearton (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to cut the cost of your AI workloads without sacrificing quality. In this builders session, you work through a curated set of representative prompts and apply three high-impact levers: prompt caching, Intelligent Prompt Routing, and right-sizing model choice. You measure token cost before and after each change, so you see exactly which levers move the needle and which do not. You're welcome to bring a prompt from your own workload to test alongside the guided examples. Leave with a repeatable cost optimization playbook and the evidence to support each decision.

title: Build a data-driven migration plan with AWS Transform
speakers: Kiran Kuppa (AWS); Rodney Bozo (Amazon Web Services); Hrushikesh Shah (AWS); Mike Kuznetsov (AWS); Sassan Hajrasooliha (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: You're planning a data center exit and need leadership to say yes. That means persuasive data, realistic cost estimates, and a proposal that makes financial sense. In this builders' session, you'll use AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities paired with Discovery Agent data to assess your existing environment, generate cost estimates, and build a compelling business case for migration. You'll work through the end-to-end workflow from discovery and analysis to financial modeling, and leave ready to present a data-driven migration proposal to your stakeholders.

title: Build agents that take orders like your best sales reps, with PepsiCo
speakers: Bharathi Srinivasan (AWS); Ganapathi Krishnamoorthi (Amazon); Muralidhar Ambekar (Pepsico)
abstract: Your best sales reps understand what a customer means, remember the conversation, check the right systems, and close the order in one exchange. This session shows how to build conversational agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that work the same way: stateful sessions on runtime, memory for multi-turn context, enterprise APIs as tools, and deterministic controls that keep the agent accurate and on task. PepsiCo shares how it built a WhatsApp ordering agent for roughly one million retailers in India, where a shopkeeper can order by text, voice note, or a photo of a handwritten list in their own language.

title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
speakers: Ted Trentler (AWS)
abstract: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.

title: Build a KMS key lifecycle dashboard with usage and cost insights
speakers: Jeremy Stieglitz (AWS); Tobias Nickl (AWS); Alex Goff (AWS); Svenja Moehring (Amazon Web Services); Jonas Buecker (Amazon)
abstract: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.

title: Build and optimize data transfers with AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
speakers: Harshi Surampalli (Amazon Web Services); Phani Surampalli (Amazon Web Services); Shaguna Awasthi (Amazon Web Services); Santhosh Arunuri (AWS); Mathieu Riverin (AWS)
abstract: When you're moving petabytes from on-premises file servers and multicloud object stores into AWS, transfer speed and operational visibility are equally critical. In this builders session, you'll configure AWS DataSync Enhanced mode to move data from diverse source environments into AWS using its parallel pipeline for high-throughput transfers. Enhanced mode generates detailed task reports and transfer logs as it works. You'll then use Amazon Bedrock to analyze that data, surfacing performance bottlenecks and generating optimization recommendations. Walk away with reusable patterns for fast data movement and AI-powered transfer visibility.

title: Build a Research Co-Scientist Using Amazon Quick
speakers: Lisa McFerrin (AWS); Ariella Sasson (AWS); Sujaya Srinivasan (Amazon web services); Atul Chaudhari (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how to build your own co-scientist with Amazon Quick. In this builder session, you'll gain hands-on experience with loading life sciences domain skills directly into Amazon Quick, and work through your own scientific questions with guidance from AWS's life sciences experts. Learn how to bring expert-level reasoning to everyday research workflows.

title: Build a SaaS control plane with Kiro specs and Strands multi-tenant constructs
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Steve Drew (AWS); Ashley Chen (AWS); Andrew Powell (Amazon Web Services); Pranjal Gururani (Amazon Web Services); Daniel Wirjo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint - all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

title: Build event-driven applications with AWS Streaming and Messaging
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK);Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
speakers: Ashley Millette (AWS); Amar Surjit (Amazon AWS); Charishma Makineni (AWS); Mayank Juneja (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Dive deep into AWS messaging services in this hands-on workshop where you'll build a real-world, event-driven application. Learn to architect sophisticated event-driven systems using Amazon SQS, SNS, MSK, and Amazon MQ. Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

title: Building Advanced Agentic AI Systems on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Thomas Utsey (AWS)
abstract: Multi-agent systems unlock powerful workflows, but production demands more than chaining agents together. This bootcamp covers advanced patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement agent-as-tool communication, share memory across agents, optimize context windows for cost and performance, and secure deployments with policy-based access control and VPC integration. Configure distributed tracing, build evaluation frameworks, and design deployment strategies that take your agentic systems from prototype to production-ready state.

title: Building conversational AI with Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic
speakers: Gui Ruggiero (Amazon); Logan Campi (AWS)
abstract: We'll explore how bidirectional audio streaming enables natural, low-latency dialogue, with expressive voices across multiple languages. See how new capabilities like cross-modal voice-and-text switching, asynchronous tool calling for multi-step tasks, and a large context window let you build voice agents, customer service automation, and conversational apps.

title: Building Proprietary Multi-Agentic AI Workflows for Low Latency and High Reliability (sponsored by Capital One)
speakers: Kel Vanee (Capital One Financial Corporation)
abstract: Enterprise AI requires scalable, multi-agentic workflows capable of handling complex reasoning without sacrificing real-time speed. This session explores how Capital One designs proprietary multi-agent systems on AWS, optimized for governance, performance, and reliability. You’ll hear how state-of-the-art serving frameworks like vLLM, efficient distributed serving platforms like llm-d, and advanced agentic inference optimization techniques can enhance latency and boost throughput. We’ll showcase these principles through real-world applications, including complex real employee- and customer-facing banking use cases while meeting rigorous business standards around accuracy, reliability, and risk management. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

title: Building Serverless distributed data processing workloads
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda;AWS Step Functions
speakers: Mukunthan Doraiswamy (Amazon); Anshuman Chakravarty (Amazon Web Services); Theophilus Ajayi (Amazon Web Services); Praveen Koorse (Amazon Web Services); Jesus Bernal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Processing large-scale data shouldn't require provisioning clusters or managing batch infrastructure. In this builders' session, design and deploy a distributed data processing pipeline using AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. Working in small groups, you'll implement fan-out patterns that process thousands of objects in parallel, handle partial failures gracefully, and optimize for cost and throughput. Learn when Distributed Map is the right choice versus other parallelization strategies, and walk away with a reusable pipeline template. Bring your laptop.

title: Build mission-ready software in regulated industries faster with Kiro
speakers: Kirk Horne (AWS); Christian Bates (AWS); Tushar Jagdale (AWS); Kaushik Elangovan (Amazon Web Services); Shawn Asfeld (AWS)
abstract: Federal dev teams struggle to ship fast while meeting compliance requirements. In this workshop, build a real app using Kiro's agentic IDE. Automate testing and docs with hooks, enforce AI behavior with steering rules, and extend capabilities through powers. Ideal for federal devs and architects.

title: Build Self-Service AI Experiences with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents
speakers: Rohit Sharma (AWS India)
abstract: Customers expect instant answers about their orders, accounts, and open cases. In this hands-on lab, build a self-service AI agent in Amazon Connect that autonomously resolves customer requests by looking up profiles, searching and creating cases through MCP tools, and retrieving FAQ answers from a knowledge base. Configure AI Guardrails for content safety and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context for human agents.

title: Build, simulate, and validate physical AI-driven robotic systems
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Kiro
speakers: Fabrizio Manfredi (AWS); Vikram Krishna (AWS); Jan Metzner (AWS); Gezim Musliaj (Amazon Web Services); Hubert Asamer (AWS)
abstract: Commissioning industrial robots typically takes weeks of physical testing. Digital twins with real-time physics simulation and multi-agent AI optimization can compress that timeline from weeks to hours. In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.

title: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe
speakers: Venkat Gomatham (Amazon); Deepthi Devanira (AWS)
abstract: We'll use Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe to add natural speech and accurate transcription to your applications. With Polly, you'll build expressive, emotionally engaged voices using its generative and long-form engines, covering streaming audio, speech marks for word-level timing, and newscaster styles. With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.

title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
speakers: Mike George (Amazon Web Services); Shawn Abdi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.

title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
speakers: Nina Mishra (AWS); Amin Saberi (AWS)
abstract: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage service
speakers: Hiren Chandiramani (Amazon); Christian Smith (AWS)
abstract: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.

title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect (sponsored by Deloitte)
abstract: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
speakers: Grant McAlister (AWS)
abstract: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

title: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera)
speakers: Sean Cordero (Cyera)
abstract: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

title: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Trainium
speakers: Megan McKenzie (AWS); Bashir Mohammed, PhD (AWS); Michaelangelo Battaglia (AWS); Steven Warren (Amazon Web Services); Gyanesh Kumar (Amazon)
abstract: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics, which powers interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving, but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. In this builders session, we deploy and optimize a real-time video world model on AWS Trainium using AWS Neuron Agentic Development skills that automate compilation, profiling, and kernel optimization through natural-language interaction. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. You will apply these agentic tools yourself to reach optimized, real-time inference on silicon built specifically for AI.

title: Digital sovereignty with verifiable controls in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud
speakers: Stephane Israel (Amazon Web Services); Mustafa Isik (AWS)
abstract: New regulations and geopolitical shifts are pushing organizations to rethink how they protect data and control access in the cloud, while still adopting AI. This session covers how AWS helps customers meet digital sovereignty requirements without giving up capability, through offerings that include the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and controls you can verify and enforce. You learn what AI sovereignty means in practice, get answers to the questions customers ask most, and hear how AWS and partners help organizations meet sovereignty requirements as they change.

title: Evaluate Enterprise AI Agents with an Eval-First Approach
speakers: Jonathan Dion (AWS)
abstract: A successful agent demo does not guarantee production readiness because agents can behave inconsistently across question types and multi-turn sessions. In this spotlight lab, you build two custom evaluators for an agent: THELMA, which scores single-turn RAG quality across seven dimensions including hallucination detection via groundedness scoring, and Mind the Goal, which computes Goal Success Rate across entire conversations and attributes failures to root causes. You register both as native AgentCore evaluators, run batch evaluations, and use diagnostic outputs to pinpoint exactly what to optimize first.

title: Find and Fix Exploitable Code at Machine Speed with AWS Continuum
speakers: Shweta Shrestha Thapa (Amazon Web Services); Lily Ashidam (AWS); Poornima Venkatesan (AWS); Kafayat Adeyemi (AWS); Meriem SMACHE (AWS)
abstract: In this hands-on builders' session, you integrate AWS Continuum into your development workflow, where a frontier agent scans and remediates code before it leaves your IDE. Write code with intentional vulnerabilities, run context-aware code reviews that go beyond pattern matching, review prioritized findings with structured evidence, and use Kiro to fix issues in real time. Leave with three controls you can reuse: a pre-commit scan, a pull request gate, and a context-aware pentest you can revalidate.

title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Application Discovery Service;AWS Compute Optimizer
speakers: Thiago Mantovani (Amazon Web Services); Vitor Euphrasio da Silva (AWS); Thiago Sousa Goncalves (Amazon); Luciano Bernardes (AWS); Nits Jeganathan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.

title: From AI Tasks to Autonomous Multi-Agent Workflows with Amazon Quick
speakers: Mike Hogan (Pennymac); Ramon Lopez (AWS)
abstract: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. Amazon Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with Amazon Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.

title: From Demo to Production: The Craft Behind AI Agents at Scale
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Gerardo Arroyo Arce (West Monroe); Diana Castro Cordero (Bac)
abstract: Your agent reasons, calls tools, and demos beautifully. Then production happens. This session is about the craft that lives after the demo: the unglamorous engineering that separates agents that ship from agents that stay in notebooks. Using real AWS accounts and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, I'll walk through deterministic guardrails that make destructive actions impossible (not just discouraged), spend limits an agent can't prompt-inject its way past, evaluation you can trust, and the IAM that silently breaks first. You'll leave with a production-readiness framework for agentic systems—and honest stories about everything that failed on the way there.

title: From Manual to Autonomous: Agentic AWS Partner Growth via Quick & MCP
speakers: Abhisheikh Lahoti (Amazon Web Services); Jing Ning (AWS)
abstract: Expertise locked in SMEs doesn't scale, and manual partner operations are expensive. The answer is architectural. Amazon Quick, Partner Central MCP Server, and Marketplace AI experiences cut three costs. Cost of sales: AI Listing Experiences, prospecting and co-sell PC agents, demand generation, Funding Agents, and Express Private Offers. Cost of customer operations: Tools to manage customers at scale, auto-renewals, adoption-nudging and reporting agents. Cost of partnerships: automated AWS Specializations, onboarding and journey agents, and Partner revenue telemetry. We cover real-time SME guidance, MCP integration, and orchestration across Partner Central and Marketplace. Leave ready to build your own workflows at scale.

title: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale with Amazon Quick
speakers: Gayatri Ohri (AWS); Rekha Seshadrinathan (Amazon AWS)
abstract: EchoStar evaluated 11 AI assistants before selecting Amazon Quick, which was then deployed to 8,000 employees with training and pre-populated skills. Next in EchoStar’s plans are integrating Quick with a third party gateways for observability and governance. Come and hear how this was done, uptake and innovations improving the efficiency of employees and teams. Discover some of the challenges integrating into existing enterprise systems, the continued activities needed to keep advancing high value usage and what are the appropriate metrics to track. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking Amazon Quick from pilot to production and enterprise efficiency.

title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Trainium
speakers: Jianying Lang (Amazon)
abstract: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration: apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. You will build the skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents across large clusters.

title: How a Brand Turned AI Governance Into a Strategic Advantage with Amazon Quick
speakers: Srikanth Baheti (AWS); Steve Vinsik (Amazon Web Services); Avinash Kalyankar (Cox Automotive Inc)
abstract: AI adoption rarely waits for governance. When employees adopt AI faster than policy keeps pace, scale becomes a liability. Cox Automotive, the world’s largest automotive services and technology provider and home to brands including Autotrader, Kelley Blue Book, Manheim, vAuto and Dealertrack, defined a governance strategy to empower adoption. Hear how Cox Auto alongside AWS is building an agentic control plane spanning agent identity, ownership, security, cost accountability and more – and why Amazon Quick fit the everyday AI needs of its 29,000 person workforce. Leave with a practical seven pillar framework that simplifies safe and smart adoption in the enterprise.

title: How Deutsche Bahn made 10 years of cloud modernization pay off in AI
speakers: Rene Schneider (Deutsche Bahn AG); Matthias Patzak (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You've invested in cloud. Maybe migrated. Maybe modernized. Your board wants AI yesterday, but 88% of companies use AI and only 1% believe they're at maturity. The gap isn't infrastructure. It's whether your organization can move fast enough. In this fireside chat, an AWS executive-in-residence sits down with Deutsche Bahn leadership to unpack how they built that speed: 550+ autonomous teams, AWS migration completed 18 months early, and enterprise-scale agentic AI now in production. You'll leave with: (1) what "AI-ready" requires beyond cloud, (2) a governance model for agents at scale, and (3) a framework for pilot to all-in.

title: How Docusign built a scalable data foundation for AI (sponsored by Fivetran)
abstract: Modern analytics and AI depend on trusted data that teams can access without adding engineering overhead. In this session, learn how Docusign standardized ingestion and transformation with Fivetran + dbt Labs, reducing manual pipeline work and creating a scalable data foundation across finance, go-to-market, product analytics, customer data, and data science. Hear how simplifying the data stack frees engineering teams to focus less on pipeline maintenance and more on delivering trusted data that powers analytics and AI across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Fivetran, an AWS Partner.

title: How Hyundai Is Transforming Customer and Vehicle Experiences on AWS
speakers: Yunsang Hwang (AWS); Eundoo Song (42dot); Eunjee Moon (Hyundai Motor Company)
abstract: Hyundai Motor Group is redefining mobility, and AWS is helping pave the way. Discover how Hyundai is using AWS to help deliver Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs) that evolve through continuous updates, an in-vehicle AI agent that lets drivers manage vehicle functions through natural voice, and an app marketplace that allows drivers to customize their driving experience. Hear how Hyundai is using AI agents to better understand the needs of their customers, deploying Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to monitor, study, and address customer feedback across 17 languages. Walk away with real-world lessons on bringing agentic AI and connected vehicle platforms to production scale.

title: How ISVs ship agent products faster: Twilio and Typeform on AgentCore
speakers: Peter Janovsky (Twilio); Veena Vasudevan (AWS); Andy Kuszyk (Typeform)
abstract: Customers now expect AI agents inside the software they buy. For an ISV, shipping agents to many customers means solving multi-tenancy, per-customer isolation, identity delegation, and cost attribution before writing any agent logic. This session shows how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles that undifferentiated work. Twilio and Typeform join on stage to share how they built agent products on AgentCore and serve large numbers of end users without building custom infrastructure. Both stayed framework-neutral and spent their engineering effort on the agent experience rather than the plumbing beneath it. Expect specific isolation, identity, and cost-attribution patterns that move an ISV's agent product from prototype into production.

title: How Nordstrom, Coca-Cola Andina & Mondelez use agentic supply chains
speakers: Pawan Kushwaha (Nordstrom); Sanjay Gurbuxani (Mondelez International, Inc.); Fernando Jana Vergara (Coca-Cola Andina); Aparna Galiasso (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Supply chain leaders are moving from dashboards that report problems to agents that resolve them, sensing disruption, optimizing routing, and acting in real time. Hear how three retail and CPG leaders deployed agentic AI on AWS at scale. Nordstrom built a multi-agent framework on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, starting with an agent that cut audit investigations from five weeks to thirty seconds. Coca-Cola Andina developed Miruta, a multi-agent routing solution optimizing supply chain operations across its bottling network. And Mondelez is modernizing production and distribution across 150+ countries. Each shares their architecture, what changed for their teams, and measurable results.

title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
aoi: Generative AI;Responsible AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Rachel Kelley (Amazon Web Services); Kartik Garg (Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios)
abstract: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months, with plans to extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.

title: How Rail Operators Are Using Agentic AI to Improve Service Reliability (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Marc Schulmeyer (Deutsche Bahn AG); Morten Wetjen (PwC Germany); Leila Fathallah (PwC); Tobias Hackbarth (Deutsche Bahn AG); Srikanth Dola (Norfolk Southern Corporation)
abstract: Many organizations successfully pilot generative AI but struggle to scale adoption. Rail operators worldwide are now exploring how agentic AI can transform mission-critical operations and improve service reliability. Deutsche Bahn (DB) and Norfolk Southern are among the organizations leading this journey. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, they are transforming rail operations through AI agents embedded into the systems that support daily operations across their transportation networks. The solution combines AI agents and human oversight to automate incident resolution, support operations teams, and improve service reliability. This session explores the journey from proof of concept to production, the governance and safety guardrails required for adoption, and how lighthouse programs are becoming blueprints for enterprise-wide agentic process transformation. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: How Stripe built an enterprise agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Hasan Tariq (Amazon Web Services); Anupam Upadhyay (Stripe); Sharadh Krishnamurthy (Stripe)
abstract: Operating global payments infrastructure requires AI that is secure, reliable, and scalable across internal and customer-facing experiences. Learn how Stripe built a shared agent platform for Kai, its company-wide AI coworker, and hundreds of other AI workflows. Stripe will share how it integrated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter with its existing infrastructure, data-access controls, and security model. Discover the architectural decisions that helped Stripe move rapidly from prototype to company-wide adoption, supporting more than 10,000 employees and nearly 500,000 Kai sessions each week.

title: How to assess your environment to migrate & modernize with confidence
speakers: Mike Briggs (AWS); Maya Newhagen (AWS)
abstract: Without a clear picture of what's running in your environment, teams carry forward outdated assumptions, inherit unplanned tech debt, and miss the fastest path to value. Assessment is the foundational step that sets everything else up for success. Learn how to go hands-on with AWS Transform, an agentic assessment experience that delivers results fast, or work with AWS specialists and partners who leverage this technology alongside decades of migration experience. Use assessment data to make informed decisions, optimize environments, and eliminate redundant licensing.

title: How to improve your security and governance maturity and prove it to your auditor
speakers: Dario Goldfarb (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: With so many security best practices available, knowing what to do first is a challenge. In this session, you learn how to use the AWS Security Maturity Model to systematically identify and prioritize security improvements for your AWS workloads through a phased approach. You discover how to extend your governance capabilities to manage security consistently across multi-cloud environments. Finally, you see how automatic evidence collection helps you continuously demonstrate compliance to auditors, turning security posture into provable assurance.

title: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
speakers: PJ Ng (AWS); Shane Carragher (Amazon Web Services); Shanna Chang (AWS); YoungMin Joung (Amazon Web Services); Yash Doshi (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic - they can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behaviour with no warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you will use Amazon CloudWatch to observe live agents from both the console and your IDE: trace what an agent actually did, spot failures, and surface anomalous behaviour. Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

title: Innovating with agentic AI inside Amazon, powered by AgentCore
speakers: Amanda Lester (AWS); Mihir Patel (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon runs thousands of AI agents internally, built on the same AgentCore platform available to every AWS customer. Teams across the company have replaced manual workflows with agents that act autonomously, cutting process times from weeks to hours and eliminating thousands of lines of custom orchestration code. This session brings together the Amazon builders behind these transformations to share the AgentCore capabilities that made it possible, the failure modes they hit at scale, and the design patterns that separate agents that demo well from agents that survive production. Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.

title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Liran Alon (Amazon)
abstract: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose-built AI chips for better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference. You will leave able to write your own custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

title: Inside T-Mobile's Kinetic Edge: Real-Time Physical AI at Scale
speakers: Matthew Feider (T-Mobile); Waqar Afzal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In a Physical AI world, tokens traveling across a telecom network must trigger real-world actions with sub-millisecond latency. Learn how T-Mobile built its Kinetic Edge Platform using AWS Outposts, Amazon SageMaker, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, delivering deterministic performance, ultra-low latency, and precise synchronization on a network serving 130M+ customers. We'll cover how to assess Physical AI network requirements and map them to AWS infrastructure options. You'll leave knowing how to build AI into the network edge and where it creates the most value.

title: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Alan Yao (Airbnb); Rashim Gupta (Amazon Web Services); Jayadev Vadakkanmarveettil (AWS)
abstract: Your AI workload is live. You own three questions: what broke, whose spend is it, and are you still running the right model. Answer the first two with Amazon Bedrock metrics: why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer, why throttling starts before you reach your quota, and how to attribute spend by caller identity and request metadata. Answer the third with evals: see how Airbnb sets a model and reasoning effort per workload across 3,000 engineers.

title: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Bruno Pistone (Amazon Web Services); Daniel Wirjo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. The completed code covers all three patterns and can be adapted to your own agents.

title: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
speakers: Meir Raviv (Amazon); Efrat Caspi (Amazon)
abstract: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

title: Modernize a Legacy Telecom Billing App with AWS Transform Custom
speakers: Rabindra Shakya (Amazon); Albeda Siddique (Amazon (AWS)); Guy Ben-Baruch (AWS); Efrat Nir-Berger (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Anil Maheshwari (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Got an old telecom application buried under decades of technical debt? In this hands-on session, you'll take a legacy BSS billing system and modernize it using AWS Transform Custom. Start by analyzing the codebase to understand business logic, dependencies, and technical debt. Then apply a built-in catalog transformation to upgrade the language and framework instantly. Next, define your own custom transformation in natural language to convert legacy interfaces to modern APIs. Validate, test for functional equivalence, and deploy to AWS. Walk away with a running modernized app and reusable transformation recipes, plus hands-on experience modernizing real-world telecom applications.

title: Modernize legacy batch into event-driven with AWS Transform & Kiro
speakers: Rene Simoes (Amazon Web Services); Subramanian (Subu) Karuppiah (AWS); Sourav Sarkar (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Ramachadra Desaraj (AWS); Pablo Alonso Prieto (AWS)
abstract: Batch processing has powered critical enterprise workloads for decades, from mainframes running COBOL and PL/I to distributed systems on legacy Java. The trade-off? Overnight batch cycles that business processes can no longer afford. In this session, reimagine batch as event-driven microservices using Domain-Driven Design. AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.

title: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
speakers: Doug Perkes (Amazon Web Services); Lasse Christiansen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.

title: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
speakers: Eyal Tamir (AWS)
abstract: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.

title: Multi-cloud security with AWS security services
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
speakers: Anthony Verleysen (AWS); Scott Ward (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Many organizations do not operate in a single cloud provider, creating the need for security solutions that cover multiple providers. In this lightning talk, see how AWS security services deliver unified multicloud security across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. From posture management and vulnerability detection to risk correlation and asset visibility, learn how security teams can gain a consolidated view and respond to risks across their entire cloud estate.

title: Observe, investigate, act: smarter ops with Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Jon Handler (AWS); Rohin Bhargava (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are becoming your best investigators, triaging alerts, correlating telemetry, and performing root-cause analysis across metrics, logs, and traces in seconds. And agents are a critical workload to observe: you need LLM trace monitoring, per-call cost attribution, and multi-agent workflow debugging to keep token spend and accuracy under control. Whether you're scaling an existing observability platform or modernizing your stack, Amazon OpenSearch Service addresses both sides. In this session, we present capabilities including native OpenTelemetry ingestion, MCP-based agent skills for natural-language issue investigation, and an optimized log-analytics engine delivering 4× price-performance at petabyte scale. Learn how to put AI agents to work on your observability data and how to keep them accountable in production.

title: Optimize AI apps on Amazon Bedrock for cost, latency, and control
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Billing and Cost Management
speakers: Andy Brown (AWS); Steph Gooch (AWS)
abstract: As AI workloads scale, engineers face complex trade-offs between cost, latency, and response quality. This code talk explores advanced optimisation techniques for production AI applications on Amazon Bedrock: prompt engineering, model selection, caching, and context window management. Through live coding, attendees examine the reasoning behind each design decision, observe cost impact via AWS Billing and Cost Management, and learn to instrument apps to detect performance regressions. Understanding the tokenomics of your AI stack is essential to operating efficiently at scale.

title: Optimize a .NET application for Graviton 5 using AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
speakers: Shubhendu Dubey (AWS); Jitesh Kumar (AWS); Kumar Shubham (Amazon Web Services); Pranjali Rawat (AWS); Chintan Agrawal (AWS)
abstract: Take a Windows .NET application, run AWS Transform end-to-end (assess, modernize, deploy), and benchmark on Graviton. Compare against the original x86 baseline, inspect what Q got wrong, and tune the result. Covers .NET Framework to modern .NET migration, Lambda packaging on Graviton, and CI integration patterns from production migrations.

title: Orchestrating AI Agents with AgentCore Runtime
speakers: Navi kaur (AWS); Ryan Gallaway (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You need more than one agent to reason across inventory, shipments, forecasts, and suppliers at the same time. In this lab, you deploy a multi-agent supply chain system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. You load data into DynamoDB, build container images with CodeBuild, and deploy specialist agents plus a supervisor orchestrator powered by Amazon Nova models. The orchestrator classifies questions, routes them to the right specialists in parallel, and synthesizes their responses into one coherent answer.

title: Post-quantum readiness at scale with AWS and DXC Technology
speakers: Rushir Patel (AWS); Douglas Skirving (DXC Technology)
abstract: Post-quantum migrations succeed when organizations can discover cryptographic assets, assign ownership, and continuously manage risk. Organisations are facing a rapid increase in machine identities, service identities, APIs, containers, AI workloads, and other cryptographic assets. At the same time, certificate lifetimes continue to shrink, making manual lifecycle management increasingly unsustainable. AWS and DXC Technology show how enterprise governance connects with crypto agility. See how DXC built a cryptographic asset intelligence and orchestration platform on AWS to discover and correlate assets across AWS and enterprise PKI, automate certificate lifecycles, and assess post-quantum readiness. A live proof of concept demonstrates inventory, prioritization, and continuous reassessment. Leave with an operating model aligned with NIST and CNSA 2.0 timelines.

title: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
services: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Lambda;AWS Secrets Manager
speakers: Sahil Bhimjiani (Amazon Web Services); Parnab Basak (Amazon Web Services); Ezzel Mohammed (Amazon Web Services); Abhishek Agawane (AWS); John Lee (AWS)
abstract: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

title: PyTorch optimizations: Faster AI and lower costs with AWS Graviton
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EC2 Linux
speakers: Juan Mestre (AWS); Hellen Avila Rosa (AWS)
abstract: Explore the latest PyTorch optimizations for Arm-based hardware, from improved kernel performance on AWS Graviton to faster training and inference at lower compute cost. We cover real benchmark results, the open-source contributions driving these improvements, and what it looks like to run modern AI workloads on Arm today. Whether you are tuning a model, contributing upstream, or just curious about what the community has been shipping, come get a grounded view of where things stand and where they are heading.

title: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Christian Melendez (AWS); Santosh Kumar (AWS India); Esra Kayabali (Amazon Web Services); Saurabh Modh (Amazon Web Services); Nati Cohen (AWS)
abstract: Container orchestration promises to improve resource utilization, but often we find ourselves with nodes that over-provision CPU, and therefore overspend. This might happen when our workloads have a high memory footprint, or when the number of replicas is driven by resilience targets and not actual load. In this session, we'll learn how easy it is to save cost in these situations without losing performance by taking advantage of EC2 Flex instances (e.g., C8i-flex, M8i-flex, R8i-flex). You'll migrate existing EKS cluster nodes, monitor relevant metrics, and measure the actual cost improvement.

title: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
speakers: Sahil Bhimjiani (Amazon Web Services); Jay Colodner (Amazon Web Services); ISHITA CHAKRABORTY (AWS); Anup Rajpara (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Jay Formosa (AWS)
abstract: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
speakers: Alessandra Romero (AWS); Jonathan Gaytan (AWS)
abstract: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.

title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
speakers: Venkata Sistla (Amazon Web Services); Dhanika Sujan (Amazon)
abstract: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.

title: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
speakers: Amit Sukhwal (AWS)
abstract: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.

title: Securing AI Agents on AgentCore
speakers: Joe Huang (AWS); Prabhu G (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents decide at runtime which endpoints to call, and that decision can bypass your security review. In this SimuLearn session, you deploy an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in VPC mode and route its outbound traffic through AWS Network Firewall. You configure a default-deny policy with an approved-domain allow list, then prove it works: an approved call succeeds while an unapproved call gets dropped. The firewall log becomes your audit evidence.

title: Sell to AI agents through AWS Marketplace
abstract: Today, buyers are using autonomous AI agents for discovery and digital purchases on their behalf. AWS Marketplace enables buyers' agents to discover partner solutions, transact securely, and meet their enterprise governance controls. As a seller in AWS Marketplace, learn how to sell products that support agentic discovery and procurement to position your offerings for this new frontier.

title: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
speakers: Jeff Falcon (Amazon); Christopher Spandikow (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

title: Serverless streaming data processing with AWS Lambda and Apache Kafka
services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK);AWS AppSync;AWS Lambda
speakers: Diego Casas (Amazon Web Services Colombia); Nikita Tibrewal (Amazon); Franklin Aguinaldo (Amazon Web Services); Kensuke Shimokawa (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.); Matt Kahn (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build a serverless streaming data pipeline in 60 minutes. In this builders' session, you design and deploy a real-time location tracking app that ingests events from Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK), processes them with AWS Lambda, and pushes live updates to a dashboard through AWS AppSync—no consumer fleet to manage, no scaling logic to write. Experiment with Lambda event source mapping for Kafka, applying recent improvements in filtering, batching, and error handling. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Serving world models on AWS Trainium with native PyTorch
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Josh Longenecker (AWS); Diwakar Bansal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave able to move world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

title: Ship AI Agents Faster with AgentCore Harness
speakers: Nidhi Seth (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Building a production-ready AI agent meant writing orchestration code, packaging containers, and managing deployment pipelines. AgentCore Harness eliminates all of that. In this hands-on lab, you declare what your agent does through configuration and let AgentCore handle the execution loop. You create a harness agent, iteratively add tools, attach AWS Skills, swap models mid-session to suit your output requirements, and publish versioned endpoints for safe rollout to your customers.

title: Spec-Driven AI Development with Kiro
speakers: Frank Spiess (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) brings structure, traceability, and human oversight to every phase of high-velocity, Agentic-AI powered software delivery. In this bootcamp, apply AI-DLC in Kiro to build a production application through Feature Specs, control agent behavior with steering files and execution modes, extend capabilities with MCP servers and Kiro Powers, and automate workflows with hooks. Leave with a governed, repeatable process for shipping quality software with AI assistance.

title: Specs, not vibes: Strangling the monolith in the IDE
speakers: Steve Wolfe (Amazon); Patrick Duffy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your architecture is full of pets: brittle EC2 instances run by manual runbooks, with no contract between decisions and infrastructure. In this code talk, we abandon slides and prove the Strangler pattern live in the IDE with Kiro and spec-driven development. We decompose a monolith into bounded contexts, generate CDK from the spec, and shift traffic from pets to serverless cattle, confronting the hard parts: where to cut the seam, running old and new together, keeping data consistent. Every architectural decision becomes a machine-verifiable contract you can apply to your own monolith.

title: Taking Every Interaction from Mundane to Magic: Agentic CX with Connect Customer
speakers: Srinivas Akella (U.S. Bank); Cecilia Bolich (AWS); Pasquale DeMaio (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every brand is racing to put AI in front of its customers, the biggest opportunity in a generation, but also a risk. In 2026, deflection is dead. Even the customers you help are quietly leaving, because being processed isn't the same as being known. In this session, the VP, Amazon Connect Customer, and SVP, Client Operations Technology, U.S. Bank, show what's possible when serving customers is AI-first by design: your brand shows up before they ask, and every customer feels like your only customer. If you own the customer relationship, this is the one session you can't afford to miss.

title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
speakers: Shiva Kasiviswanathan (AWS); Krishna Balasubramanian (Amazon)
abstract: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

title: The AWS Console in the age of agentic compute
speakers: Olga Madejska (AWS); James Gray (Amazon)
abstract: From model testing to capacity planning, compute can be complex and costly to get wrong. As development moves into an agentic era, see how AWS Console innovations provide a trusted tool to support your workflow, verify instances, save costs, govern with confidence. Move faster. Stay in control.

title: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
speakers: Tejas Ghadge (Amazon Web Services); Rajesh Kumar Pandey (Amazon)
abstract: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.

title: Threat modeling the agentic SDLC: from user story to deployment
speakers: Brad Dispensa (Amazon); ionut ionescu (AWS)
abstract: "Threat modeling the agentic SDLC with ThreatForest Agentic development is speeding up, and traditional threat modeling assumes a person makes the decisions. In this code talk, you follow one process end to end. You threat model a user story with the autonomous threat modeling built into AWS Continuum, carry it through the developer workflow, and take it to deployment. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. We also show where traditional threat modeling can be used for agentic systems."

title: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
speakers: Pranav Sharma (Amazon Web Services); John Masci (Amazon); Alex Iankoulski (AWS)
abstract: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.

title: TP ICAP: Driving revenue through faster decisions with agentic AI
speakers: Animesh Kundu (AWS); Shahen Bokhari (TP ICAP); Erica Martin (TP ICAP)
abstract: Trading opportunities slip away when teams can't synthesize fragmented data fast enough to act. In this session, global broker TP ICAP will share how it built First Mate on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, an AI sales-trading tool that uses generative AI to identify and act on opportunities in global markets more effectively. Discover how First Mate ingests real-time data, applies domain reasoning, and delivers actionable recommendations to brokers in seconds. We’ll discuss the architectural decisions and outcomes behind the journey from prototype to production. You’ll learn how to bring agentic AI to time-sensitive operations where speed-to-insight can drive revenue.

title: Trust, built in seconds: AI-powered banking at scale
speakers: Aly Galal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In financial services, trust is earned in seconds: the lost card, the emergency funds, the vulnerable customer who nearly gave up. Those seconds demand that you know who the customer is, understand their need, and resolve it on the spot. Hear how one of the UK's largest banks reimagined customer experience on Amazon Connect Customer, reaching 96% first-point-of-contact resolution across millions of calls monthly. Trace a multi-year journey: real-time AI that helps agents act in seconds, analytics and self-service at scale, and an active-active, multi-region architecture that keeps service running under strict European regulatory and data-residency requirements.

title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more freedom without losing control
speakers: Erin Kraemer (AWS); Cami Novelli-Killeen (AWS); Brooke Jamieson (AWS)
abstract: You're accountable for what your AI agents do, but they act faster than anyone can review. So capable agents wait while the work piles up. There's a way out of that bind. Join this panel for a candid discussion of how you build trust across the agent lifecycle: scope the agent to its job, know which agents are acting, bound what it does and says, and see what it did after. Then learn how provable bounds let you set how far an agent goes, and prove it stays there. Come ready to question your own systems. Leave able to answer.

title: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
speakers: Fei Yuan (Amazon Web Services); Guilherme Greco (AWS)
abstract: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.

title: Turning Data into Decisions: Pacific Life's Modern Insurance Operations with AWS AI (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Dominic Smith (PwC)
abstract: Abstract: PwC-built Generative AI data processing solution for Pacific Life Re, hosted on AWS. The solution automates the ingestion, transformation, validation, schema mapping, and PII redaction of client actuarial datasets that arrive in different formats, languages, and quality levels. In short, it helps PLRe move from manual, time-consuming data preparation to a secure, auditable, AI-enabled workflow that can reduce processing times from weeks to days, improve data quality, and provide clean, validated outputs for actuarial, pricing, and R&D teams. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Quick Suite
speakers: Rosa Corley (AWS); Rajani Guptan (AWS)
abstract: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis.
