Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.

title: Web grounding on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Veda Raman (AWS); Kalyan Garimella (Amazon); Priya Holikatti (Amazon)
abstract: Learn about the ways in which customers can ground their AI applications in current web information with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
speakers: Arshad Zackeriya (Xero); Dipin Thomas (Xero); Geethika Guruge (Mantel Group)
abstract: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.

title: What's new in Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Sharadha Kandasubramanian (Aws); Shalendra Chhabra (Amazon)
abstract: AI moves fast: new models, new economics, and new governance capabilities. Attend this breakout to learn about the latest innovations across Amazon Bedrock. We cover recent model additions from OpenAI, Anthropic, and more, along with advances in inference and updates across security, governance, and cost management. Whether you are new to Bedrock or tracking the latest releases, see what is available today and where to focus next.

title: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Fargate
speakers: Raphael Beamonte (Ramp); Abhishek Nautiyal (Amazon Web Services); Olly Pomeroy (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving you access to the latest GPUs and accelerators. In this session, explore how to launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale based on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, and automatically recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances to serve GPU-backed workloads while optimizing cost and operational agility.

title: Agentic AI for Security: How AWS CIRT reduced triage time to minutes
aoi: Monitoring & Observability;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI
speakers: Joshua McKiddy (Amazon); Brian Poole (AWS)
abstract: When a security event hits a customer account, every minute counts. Learn how AWS CIRT built an agentic AI system using Amazon Kiro that performs investigation workflows autonomously: ingesting case data, baselining environments, analyzing indicators, and producing triage assessments. We cover architecture decisions for AI agents with live AWS API access, evaluation frameworks measuring accuracy against expert answer keys, and guardrails keeping humans in the loop. Leave with patterns for applying agentic AI to operational workflows where accuracy is non-negotiable.

title: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
speakers: Bhargav Talluri (Amazon Web Services); Jeffrey Damick (AWS)
abstract: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI-Catalog (Linux Foundation) to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.

title: AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC)
speakers: Karim Benzidane (AWS)
abstract: The AI Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) reimagines how teams plan, build, and ship software with AI as a first-class participant. In this bootcamp, learn the three phases (Inception, Construction, Operation) , apply the Intent-Unit-Bolt framework to decompose requirements into AI-executable work items, then use Kiro IDE's Spec-Driven Development to generate domain models, application code, tests, and infrastructure. You leave with a working application built entirely through the AI-DLC methodology.

title: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
speakers: Rossana Suarez (Naranjax)
abstract: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.

title: A leader's guide to predicting and proving AI value
aoi: Cost Optimization;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Chris Hennesey (AWS); Lindsey Drake (Amazon)
abstract: Every organization faces the same AI questions: How do we predict and manage costs? How do we prove value when outcomes are hard to measure? How do we move fast without losing control? Two finance leaders, one advising enterprise executives and one managing AI economics at scale inside Amazon, share what is working, what is not, and where teams go wrong. Learn how to measure AI cost and value in terms finance and technology leaders agree on, which guardrails to set as investment grows, and how to make the case for AI value to your board.

title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
speakers: Ishit Vachhrajani (Amazon Web Services); Matt Wood (AWS)
abstract: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

title: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Dan Backhaus (AWS); Paul Sharpe (Epic Games, Inc.); Mattias Jansson (Epic Games, Inc.)
abstract: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.

title: AWS AI from chips to agents: The end-to-end production AI foundation
speakers: Alex Thewsey (Amazon Web Services); Denis V Batalov (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The AI experiment is over. Now it has to work. This session walks through the AWS AI Platform end-to-end, starting at the chip layer with AWS Trainium and AWS Graviton delivering up to 40% better price performance. From there, model inference and customization through Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Then production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every layer co-designed so workloads move across the stack without rearchitecting. You will leave knowing which service handles which job, where the layers connect to accelerate production timelines, and how to keep your architecture open as your AI strategy evolves.

title: AWS AI League Championship Grand Finale: Agentic Football Cup
abstract: Experience the ultimate AI showdown from your theater seat as fifty finalists from the AWS AI League season battle head-to-head in real time for the $50,000 championship prize. This electrifying viewing experience offers ML practitioners, developers, and AI enthusiasts unique insights into agent orchestration, model customization, and multi-agent coordination at scale, as five-versus-five AI agent squads face off live in Agentic Football, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK.

title: AWS Partner: Build the AgentCore agent your demo pretends to be
speakers: Parvesh Chopra (AWS)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. A good prompt gets you a chatbot. Everything else on AgentCore turns it into an agent. Build a customer support agent from scratch and progressively add persistent memory so it stops forgetting, tools through Gateway to reach real data, and Cedar policies that enforce boundaries, plus production traces, quality evaluations, and AI-driven optimization with A/B testing. Leave with hands-on experience on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and ready to show customers what separates a chatbot from an agent worth paying for. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS Partner: Your agent can wait. Go fix the app it depends on.
speakers: Andy Kroll (Amazon)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. An agent is only as reliable as the services it calls. Before you fix anything, you need to know exactly what's broken. In this workshop you stress-test that claim — probing a service for gaps that break autonomous invocation, reading the findings against your own predictions, and making the call on what gets fixed first. Leave with a ranked fix list and a method that transfers to any service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Become an AWS AI Business Strategist
speakers: Mohamed Gawish (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Turning an AI idea into enterprise reality requires more than technical knowledge. In this bootcamp, you apply the Discover, Design, Deliver framework to diagnose business problems, assess organizational readiness, and scope AI pilots with clear success criteria. You navigate responsible AI tradeoffs, lead change management across cross-functional teams, evaluate agentic AI architectures for autonomy versus control, and build phased scaling strategies from proof of concept through production deployment.

title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
speakers: Weiqing Yang (LinkedIn); Mayank Juneja (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.

title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
speakers: Tony Patino (Transamerica); Adnan Bilwani (Amazon Web Services); Ryan Bachman (Amazon)
abstract: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.

title: Beyond Prompts: Crafting Production GenAI from Scratch
services: Amazon API Gateway;Amazon Bedrock;AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
speakers: Steven Leung (Versent)
abstract: Building reliable GenAI applications requires deliberate systems engineering, not just prompt engineering. After collaborating with AWS Professional Services on an enterprise client, I learned how to build production-grade web apps the official AWS way. Bypassing basic buzzwords, we map a compound serverless conversational assistant engineered from scratch using AWS CDK, CloudFront, Cognito, API Gateway, and ⁠Amazon Bedrock. Examine how to handle real-world token streaming failures, manage state in DynamoDB, and implement strict Infrastructure as Code. Leave with complete source code and a concrete approach to balancing model performance against infrastructure cost in highly concurrent production environments.

title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
services: Amazon FSx for Lustre;Amazon FSx for OpenZFS;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Edward Naim (Amazon); Randy Seamans (AWS); Aditi Garg (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.

title: Build, Govern, Optimize: Trustworthy, Cost-Aware Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Kevon Mayers (NVIDIA); Chris Smith (AWS)
abstract: Bring a laptop and take one multi-agent system through its whole lifecycle on AWS: discover, build, deploy, govern, and optimize. You’ll compose it from versioned parts in an open registry alongside AWS Agent Registry, declare it once, and run it with Strands Agents on your laptop, Amazon EKS, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You’ll govern it with one policy enforced at the model boundary, at every tool call, and at the kernel, using NeMo Guardrails, NeMo Relay, and OpenShell beside Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and AgentCore Policy. Then you’ll optimize it, routing each call across NVIDIA NIM and Amazon Bedrock with NeMo Switchyard and putting every change through CI/CD before it ships. You’ll leave with a working reference deployment in your own AWS account. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Building globally distributed applications with DynamoDB global tables
speakers: Amrith Kumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

title: Building interactive web applications on AWS Lambda Web Functions
speakers: Jan Michael Go Tan (Amazon Web Services); Fabrianne Effendi (Amazon Web Services); Muhammad Khairul Habib (Amazon Web Services); Erica Liu (AWS); Arthi Jaganathan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You want to build web applications on Lambda without changing how you write code. Lambda Web Functions make that direct. In this builders' session, deploy a full-stack web application with AWS Lambda Web Functions. Working in small groups with AWS experts, run an HTTP server on Lambda, serve static assets alongside application routes, render a DynamoDB-backed product catalogue, and stream live activity with Server-Sent Events. Walk away with a working app and deployment patterns for interactive web workloads. Bring your laptop.

title: Building Trust into Agentic AI on AWS in the Age of Autonomous Agents (sponsored by Check Point)
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI
speakers: Dhanil Parwani (AWS); Shahar Tal (Check Point)
abstract: AI agents are evolving from assistants into autonomous systems that call APIs and take actions on behalf of users. Traditional perimeter controls aren't enough; threats now emerge from prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unmonitored tool use. In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Reliable AI Agents on AWS with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Marilia Brito (AWS)
abstract: When your data changes frequently, RAG helps your agent access the latest information at query time. Fine-tuning an LLM with domain data brings precision in how the agent responds and executes. In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

title: Canva's migration to AWS Graviton: from 2% to 54% in 10 months
speakers: Lucky Ray (Canva); Rory McCormick (AWS)
abstract: Canva shifted its massive compute fleet from 2% to 23% Graviton adoption in just two months, then scaled to 54% over the following eight months, delivering meaningful cost savings and performance improvements along the way. This session covers the technical blockers the team encountered and overcame and the strategies that made rapid migration possible at enterprise scale. Walk away with practical, battle-tested patterns for planning and executing large-scale Arm migrations, whether you're just getting started or looking to accelerate an existing effort.

title: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);Amazon VPC Lattice;AWS PrivateLink
speakers: Victor Babasanmi (Amazon); Henning Schroeder (Amazon Web Services); Tega Odjegba (AWS); Mankaran Singh (Amazon Web Services); Kimberley Clements (AWS)
abstract: Organizations scaling across multiple AWS accounts need AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC, driving up costs and fragmenting access controls. In this session, construct a centralized endpoint architecture in a shared services VPC and expose endpoints to consumers through Amazon VPC Lattice. Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management, which eliminates Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

title: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
speakers: Matt Lewis (IBM)
abstract: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.

title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
speakers: Sajjan Gundapuneedi (Amazon); Christina Andonov (AWS); Salva Jung (LG Uplus)
abstract: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

title: Deep dive into recent Amazon S3 launches
abstract: Join this session to learn about the latest storage and AI innovations from Amazon S3, why they matter, and how to get started.

title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
speakers: Smitha Sriram (Amazon Web Services); Jimmy Zuber (Amazon Web Services); Amir Levy (Amazon)
abstract: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

title: Developing Apps from Specs with Kiro
speakers: Sam Shalil SHALIL (Amazon); Bruno Marcondes (AWS)
abstract: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. In this SimuLearn session, you build a city event management application by guiding Kiro through its spec-driven workflow: generating EARS-format user stories, reviewing architecture decisions, and executing a sequenced task list that produces a working MVP. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.

title: Edge-to-Action: Powering Agentic AI via Cloudera's Anywhere Cloud (sponsored by Cloudera)
speakers: Tony Davis (Cloudera); Morgan Bowling (Cloudera, Inc.)
abstract: Distributed edge assets, remote sensors, and transactional systems often leave operational data isolated from cloud AI platforms. This session demonstrates how to break down these boundaries using Cloudera Anywhere Cloud. Discover an event-driven architectural blueprint that standardizes real-time streaming on-premises, unifies hybrid pipelines, and lands telemetry directly into Cloudera’s Open Data Lakehouse on AWS. Learn how grounding autonomous AI agents on AWS with continuous edge context simplifies data sovereignty, eliminates bottlenecks, and enables real-time, closed-loop enterprise automation. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: Enhance Production Applications with AI-Assisted Development in Kiro
speakers: Javier Martinez Nohales (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enhancing production apps requires balancing delivery velocity with code safety. Kiro gives you both. In this hands-on lab, add features to enhance a live application using AI-assisted development on Kiro. Define coding standards with steering files and specs, generate UI components from natural language prompts, automate quality checks with agent hooks, install powers for domain expertise, and delegate backend analysis to custom subagents. Deploy your changes confidently to production environments.

title: From Gen AI to Agentic AI: Transforming Finance Operations on AWS with Barclays (sponsored by Capgemini)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Lambda
speakers: Avin Handa (Capgemini)
abstract: Barclays is transforming finance operations through an AWS-powered AI platform that combines Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector knowledge bases, and Agentic AI. The platform unifies structured and unstructured finance data to automate SOX controls, enhance management reporting, enable finance data enrichment, and support intelligent decision-making across strategic finance initiatives. Built with enterprise-grade governance, explainability, and auditability, the solution helps strengthen control effectiveness, improve regulatory compliance, and accelerate reporting outcomes. Learn how AI-powered agents, explainable workflows, and governed human-in-the-loop processes are driving operational efficiency, enhancing regulatory confidence, improving audit readiness, and laying the foundation for autonomous finance operations. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: From migration to continuous modernization: reduce tech debt at scale
speakers: Everett Dolgner (AWS); Neha Goswami (Neha)
abstract: Learn how agentic AI is transforming enterprise modernization from one-off projects into an always-on practice. In this session, we explore how organizations are accelerating cloud migration, modernizing mainframe, Windows, and custom applications, and continuously reducing tech debt across their entire portfolio, evolving their pipelines from CI/CD to CI/CD/CM (continuous modernization). See how teams are compressing modernization timelines from years to months while keeping codebases current and AI-ready. Hear from product leader Neha Goswami on the latest innovations and what's ahead.

title: From our Agents to yours: Build, Optimize and Certify
speakers: Ivan Kopas (AWS)
abstract: AWS builds its certification exams, from foundational cloud to agentic AI, using production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this session, we show how we built our reasoning agents with AWS Well-Architected practices to solve real operational challenges: climbing latency, spiraling token costs, and non-deterministic failures. You’ll leave with concrete patterns to apply on AWS, plus a clear path to validate those skills through AWS Certification

title: From reactive operations to autonomous resilience: How Agentic AI is redefining SRE (sponsored by HCLTech)
speakers: Ramesh Ramakrishnan (Verizon)
abstract: Traditional SRE was built to restore systems quickly, but today’s complex, distributed environments demand more than reactive operations. This lightning session explores how agentic AI is redefining SRE by enabling autonomous detection, decision-making, remediation, and continuous learning. It examines how observability can extend beyond infrastructure metrics to connect system health with customer experience and business outcomes. Attendees will learn how AI, observability, and operations are converging to create resilient, self-optimizing environments, why autonomous resilience is becoming a competitive advantage, and the practical steps organizations can take to progress toward Level 5 autonomous operations while retaining appropriate human oversight and governance This presentation is brought to you by HCLTech, an AWS Partner.

title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
speakers: Pooja Giri (AWS); Doug Clauson (AWS); Ricardo Britto (Ericsson)
abstract: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.

title: Fuel Intelligent AI Agents with Trusted Enterprise Data (sponsored by Informatica)
speakers: Rajeev Srinivasan (Salesforce)
abstract: To unlock transformative business outcomes, AI agents require a foundation of trusted data with rich enterprise context. Delivering success means bridging the knowledge, trust, and action gaps across a highly complex data landscape. In this session, learn how Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) provides the comprehensive AI-ready data needed to power reliable agentic workflows. Explore how headless IDMC architecture via integrations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Agent Registry and Amazon Quick fuels agents with trusted enterprise context and end-to-end governance, driving impactful results and long-term project success. This presentation is brought to you by Informatica, an AWS Partner.

title: Go from Code to Deployed Agent with AgentCore CLI
speakers: Fabrizio Angelelli (AWS)
abstract: Go from zero to a deployed, observable AI agent in under an hour. Use the AgentCore CLI to scaffold a Strands agent with a custom tool, test it locally against the Runtime contract, then deploy to AgentCore Runtime via CDK. Invoke the agent to demonstrate session isolation, inspect automatic CloudWatch logs and X-Ray traces, and confirm the framework-agnostic contract by replacing the agent with a plain Python function.

title: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI (sponsored by Atos)
services: AWS Transform;AWS DevOps Agent;AWS Security Agent
speakers: Damien VEUGEOIS (ATOS International SAS); Justin Cook (ATOS International SAS); Mark Ross (Siemens AG)
abstract: Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it. What you'll learn ⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots ⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve ⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments ⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps This presentation is brought to you by Atos, an AWS Partner.

title: Graviton5 for data workloads
abstract: Data workloads are bottlenecked by how fast they can access and process information — whether that data lives on local storage, in memory, or behind a lightweight service. New Graviton5 instance families are purpose-built for each tier.

title: How Bayer modernized R&D analytics into an agentic decision engine
speakers: Subbu Dandamudi (Bayer); Saurabh Saxena (Amazon)
abstract: Bayer's R&D analytics relied on manual pipelines, fragmented tooling, and engineering-heavy workflows that bottlenecked scientists. In this session, hear how Bayer modernized that stack into an agentic decision engine on AWS, cutting token costs by roughly 600% and saving scientists 70% of their engineering time. We'll trace the modernization journey from legacy analytics architecture through the migration to cloud-native services and show how that foundation enabled autonomous multi-agent workflows that now orchestrate R&D decisions at enterprise scale. Leave with a framework for modernizing analytics into agentic AI capabilities.

title: How Chamberlain and Daikin power smart product innovation with AWS
speakers: Tyler Splitt (Chamberlain Group); Steve Blackwell (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Manufacturers are transforming products into connected, intelligent offerings that deliver proactive, personalized customer experiences. Discover how AWS helps you build, connect, and monetize smart products at global scale. Hear how Chamberlain Group migrated its myQ smart home product platform, with 15M+ devices and 12M+ users, to AWS—eliminating multi-cloud complexity and furthering their AI and video intelligence offerings. Also learn how Daikin is using AWS to deliver 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive control across an extensive network of HVAC systems. Walk away with proven patterns for scaling connected products and unlocking AI-driven service revenue.

title: How Delta Air Lines achieved always-on code modernization
speakers: Venugopalan Vasudevan (AWS); Vidheer Gadikota (Delta Air Lines); Jas Chhabra (Amazon)
abstract: Every enterprise carries the same growing list: outdated dependencies, end-of-life runtimes, and security vulnerabilities that nobody has time to fix. In this session, learn how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to find these issues across your entire portfolio and fix them without waiting for a human to intervene. We'll cover how to maintain a living inventory of what needs upgrading, prioritize by risk, and automate remediation at scale. Hear how Delta Air Lines drove autonomous remediation across 100+ development teams, turning tech debt from a never-ending backlog into an always-on process.

title: How LG U+ cut migration time 50% with AI-powered app refactoring
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Transform;Kiro
speakers: Bhavna Sarathy (AWS); Yoojong Lee (LG U+)
abstract: Moving servers to the cloud without modernizing the applications on them just moves your technical debt to a new address. LG U+ needed to modernize applications before they could migrate them, and doing both sequentially would have taken too long. In this session, LG U+ shares how they ran AI-powered modernization and migration in parallel across 87 systems spanning 1,579 virtual servers and 107 physical servers. The result: roughly 20% migration velocity improvement and a 50% reduction in Java migration time through AI-assisted refactoring. You'll learn how to modernize at scale without slowing down the move.

title: How Marriott built AI-powered travel search with agents on AWS and model on GCP
speakers: Bharat Lakhiyani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Marriott's guest-facing AI travel search, Ask Bonvoy, runs across two clouds by design: Gemini Flash on GCP handles conversational reasoning, while AWS powers the agentic backbone — EKS for orchestration, Aurora PostgreSQL with pgVector for RAG retrieval, and Bedrock Guardrails for real-time safety. This split lets Marriott pick the best model for the job without re-platforming, and scale across 9,000+ properties. In this lightning talk, learn how Marriott's engineering team wired a multi-cloud agentic architecture with model portability built in — and walk away with cloud-agnostic patterns for inference routing, agentic orchestration, and safety guardrails across clouds.

title: How startups ship faster with Kiro
speakers: Rene Brandel (Casco); Helen Hasbun (Amazon)
abstract: Startups live and die by velocity. Small teams, big ambitions, and no time to waste. In this session, hear how fast-moving startups are using Kiro to punch above their weight: turning ideas into working software with spec-driven and agentic development, keeping a lean team focused on product instead of boilerplate, and shipping features that would normally demand far more engineers. We'll describe real patterns startups use to move from concept to production quickly, and share practical takeaways any team can apply. Whether you're a founder, an early engineer, or scaling quickly, learn how agentic development helps small teams build big.

title: Human search to agent retrieval: Rearchitecting with OpenSearch Service
speakers: Tia White (AWS); Archal Kumar (Intuit); Sohaib Katariwala (AWS)
abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory across sessions, and demand, verified answers before taking action. Traditional search architectures weren't built for this, and at agent scale, latency budgets compress, relevance requirements compound, and retrieval failures cascade into hallucinated outputs. In this session, we walk you through how the shift from human search to agent retrieval is reshaping infrastructure requirements and how the latest capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service help you address these unique challenges. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, why it matters, and how to get started.

title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
speakers: Liz Fong-Jones (honeycomb.io)
abstract: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.

title: Lambda Managed Instances: EC2 Power with Serverless Simplicity
abstract: AWS Lambda Managed Instances enables you to run Lambda functions on your choice of EC2 compute. With Lambda Managed Instances, you can optimize the performance and cost efficiency of your functions by utilizing specialized EC2 instance types and EC2 pricing benefits, while maintaining the familiar Serverless programming model and benefits like automatic patching, scaling, and 200+ AWS services integration for event-driven workloads. This session will provide an in-depth overview of how to get started with Lambda Managed Instances, recent launches like 90-minute function timeout, enhanced observability, and a behind-the-scenes look at how Lambda manages and scales your instances to ensure a seamless serverless experience.

title: Launch a production container app in under 5 minutes
speakers: Alessandro Micco (AWS); Pasha Digori (Amazon Web Services); Luana Fares (Amazon Web Services); David Ugarte (AWS); Sid Ahmed boudboub (Amazon Web Services EMEA France)
abstract: Amazon ECS Express Mode reduces container deployment to three required inputs and a single CLI command. In this builders session, deploy a web application with built-in load balancing, autoscaling, TLS, and canary deployments configured automatically. Explore the full service lifecycle from creation through updates to deletion and see how shared ALBs keep costs low across multiple services. Ideal for developers new to Amazon ECS or looking to simplify their deployment workflow. Bring a laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Learn new AI development skills with Kiro
speakers: Rafael Ramos (Amazon Web Services); Dror Helper (Amazon); Simon Rawlings (Amazon Web Services); Marco Frattallone (AWS); Matt Laver (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Discover Kiro, the IDE for structured agentic development. In this builder’s session, explore how to use Kiro as your intelligent partner - helping to understand complex codebases, crystalize detailed requirements, and deliver quality solutions at unprecedented speed. You will iterate with Kiro to finalize your detailed design, before using Kiro to orchestrate AI agents and implement a fully working solution – all while maintaining complete control throughout the development process. You must bring a laptop to participate in this session.

title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation Through the Deployment of AI Agents
speakers: Jeffrey Eckhaus (AWS); Junjie Tang (AWS); Bruno Arnal (Amazon)
abstract: AI agents on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at velocity and scale. Discover how Amazon Finance Operations, supporting 6,000+ analysts across nine global service centers, deploys AI agents to resolve millions of contacts and hundreds of thousands of cases annually, automating low-value tasks and running autonomous workflows in a high-stakes finance environment. Then explore how Amazon Operation’s Workforce Intelligence & Scheduling Engine (WISE) enables them to orchestrate the operating, management, and adjustment of labor and flow across more than 1,200 facilities. When a gap in a tool, process, or service appears, it spins up autonomous coding agents on Bedrock AgentCore to build, test, and deploy solutions or mechanisms to close the gaps. Leaders will share the innovations that enabled them to stop managing systems and start orchestrating them.

title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
speakers: Erik Anderson (AWS); Archana Balakrishnan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.

title: Making foundation models performant on AWS Trainium3
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Matthew McClean (AWS)
abstract: Many of today's largest foundation models are mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, and modern MoE models place several performance demands on AI chips and their HPC systems. This session walks through those demands and how AWS Trainium3 and the Trn3 UltraServer respond. See how to train and serve with PyTorch, TorchTitan, and vLLM, then profile with Neuron Explorer and choose between a config change, an NKI Library kernel, or a custom NKI kernel. Two customers share their experience running on Trainium3.

title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
speakers: Marc Olson (AWS); Jody Gibney (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.

title: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
speakers: Kiran Chukkala (AWS); Martyn Storey (AWS)
abstract: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.

title: Modernize .NET Applications with AWS Transform and Kiro
speakers: Clayton Markos (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Legacy .NET Framework applications tied to Windows limit your deployment options and increase operational costs. In this lab, you use AWS Transform for .NET in Interactive Mode to automatically port a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor application. You review the AWS Transform generated assessment report and migration plan, accept the automated transformation, then use Kiro to identify and fix the residual runtime issue that remains after the port.

title: Modernizing file transfer with AWS Transfer Family
speakers: Ulili Nhaga (NVIDIA); Madhukumar Adavi (Amazon Web Services Inc); Randy Boutin (AWS)
abstract: Legacy file transfer platforms are costly to maintain and fragile under pressure. When outages and bottlenecks start compounding, patching isn't enough. In this session, learn how AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed foundation for secure file exchange that scales with demand. We'll cover core capabilities including managed SFTP servers, connectors, browser-based web apps, and event-driven automation. A customer joins to share how they replaced a failure-prone platform with a modern, AWS-native architecture on Transfer Family and S3.

title: Monetizing your applications with AWS
abstract: In this session, learn how to transform your finished application into a revenue-generating SaaS product. Learn about analyzing your cloud infrastructure, choose pricing models, and instrumenting code for usage metering. You'll see how to manage the complete billing lifecycle, from subscription management and invoicing to tax calculation and payment processing. Walk away with a clear path to accelerate your time-to-market and start charging customers.

title: Netflix on Aurora PostgreSQL: Operating 40TB+ after fleet migration
speakers: Grant McAlister (AWS); Sabrina Zhao (Netflix)
abstract: In this session, learn why Netflix moved workloads from a self-managed, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database on EC2 to Aurora, and how they operate 40TB+ today. Aurora shared storage eliminated cross-node coordination overhead, delivering up to 75% lower latency. Explore the operational model developed by the platform team, featuring NVMe tiered cache for multi-TB datasets using optimized reads instances, cluster cache management for resilience following failover, query plan management for plan stability, and how PostgreSQL statistics and CloudWatch Database Insights power on-call triage and cost optimization.

title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
speakers: Claire Edgcumbe (Amazon); Jordan Dolman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.

title: Reduce token costs by caching inference results on ElastiCache
speakers: Madelyn Olson (AWS); Meet Bhagdev (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multi-agent AI systems now orchestrate complex workflows requiring frequent foundation model calls. In this session, learn how you can reduce latencies to single-digit milliseconds from single-digit seconds with for Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in agentic AI applications using semantic and KV caching, while also reducing the cost incurred from your foundation models for production workloads. By implementing these caching strategies in agentic architectures like RAG-powered assistants and autonomous agents, customers can create performant and cost-effective production-scale agentic AI systems.

title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
speakers: Sylvain Bruas (TEAMWORK)
abstract: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.

title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
speakers: Stephan Schiller (Amazon Web Services); Marco Jahn (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Requirements like replay, ordering, high throughput and more, increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Throughout the talk we will build a real world architecture and will provide guidance when to choose messaging, streaming or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.

title: Scale agentic development with automated orchestration
speakers: mac Merritt (Amazon); Rodrigo Azevedo (HERE Technologies); Romain Dura (AWS)
abstract: As you delegate more complex development work to AI agents, manual coordination can limit how much you can take on. Learn how to automate multi-agent orchestration to reduce supervision while maintaining your quality standards. This session explores patterns for dividing work among focused agents and building reusable processes that include verification. Through examples from the Kiro team and HERE Technologies, see how these principles apply in Kiro workflows and learn the trade-offs in context management, execution time, and cost.

title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
speakers: Chad Schmutzer (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.

title: Securing software and AI supply chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Network Firewall
speakers: Sang Won Kim (Coupang); Amish Shah (Amazon Web Services); Andrew (Kyungshik) Shin (AWS)
abstract: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that volume, each open source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. This session goes deep on the AWS Network Firewall architecture and its newer capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. Coupang shows how it built egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and limits exposure to rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads without slowing developers down.

title: Speed up latency-sensitive workloads with Amazon S3 Express One Zone
speakers: Mallory Gershenfeld (AWS)
abstract: For data-intensive workloads such as ML training, analytics, and AI search, every millisecond spent waiting on data costs money without advancing the work. When workloads make millions of small, random reads and writes, low-latency storage keeps compute productive without provisioning for peak demand. S3 Express One Zone brings this low latency to Amazon S3, with single-digit millisecond data access up to 10x faster than S3 Standard. In this session, we walk through the design patterns customers use in production to add low-latency performance to data already in S3, and how to tell whether your workload is a fit.

title: Take control of how AWS credits are allocated across your accounts
abstract: In this lightning talk, learn how to split any credit into precise amounts and transfer them to the accounts that need them. We walk through real-world workflows in the Console and API, show how split credits work seamlessly with sharing and pausing for full lifecycle control, and demonstrate how to replace monthly chargeback spreadsheets with a 5-minute workflow. Walk away with a playbook for giving every team a predictable credit budget as your organization scales.

title: The Best Engineer in the Room Doesn’t Write Code (sponsored by Anaconda)
speakers: Emilie Schario (Anaconda (FKA Continuum Analytics))
abstract: AI generates code faster than teams can review and ship it. The bottleneck has moved, and so has the work of the highest leverage engineers. Engineers build coding factories: repeatable systems that combine user intent, persistent context, agent execution, automated checks, and human judgment. Drawing on AWS’s AI-Driven Development Life Cycle, we’ll see how Kilo by Anaconda meets developers where they work and how Amazon Bedrock brings model choice into the factory, tracing one build failure through verification and escalation. Attendees leave with a framework for agent workflows that deliver, and a clearer view of where engineering judgment matters. This presentation is brought to you by Anaconda, an AWS Partner.

title: The Physical AI Blueprint: A Full-Stack Solution with AWS and NVIDIA (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Shaun Kirby (AWS); Ali Shahrokni (NVIDIA); Abhishek Srivastav (AWS)
abstract: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. Walk away with a working blueprint you can apply to manufacturing, logistics, or autonomous systems. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
abstract: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with 3 architectural changes on AWS: - Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. - Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. - Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Transforming legacy core to agentic AI with Nissan & Bread Financial
speakers: Ilene Eng (Bread Financial); Tim Gray (AWS); Kalyan Chunduri (Nissan Group of Americas)
abstract: Legacy mainframe applications were built for stability, scale, and batch-oriented processing, but they were never designed to power real-time, intelligent, agentic experiences. Modernization changes that. Discover how Nissan reimagined core operations into a cloud-native platform designed for responsiveness, adaptability, and AI-ready workflows. Hear how Bread Financial is evolving beyond credit-processing architectures to accelerate innovation by decomposing monolithic capabilities into bounded context services, creating a modern foundation for autonomous workflows. See how both used AWS Transform to extract business rules from decades-old applications and Kiro to forward-engineer production-ready code. Learn how modernized applications unlock the architecture that makes agentic AI possible.

title: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI (sponsored by Qlik)
speakers: James Welsh (Qlik)
abstract: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

title: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
speakers: Nadia Labai (AWS); Brian Beach (AWS)
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.

title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
speakers: Andrew Baird (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.

title: What to do next after your cloud migration
speakers: Caio Ribeiro Cesar (Amazon Web Services); Baruch Waknine (AWS)
abstract: Rehosting gets workloads to AWS, but that's just the beginning. This session covers the first 90 days after cutover: stabilizing the environment, building observability so decisions are based on real utilization data instead of pre-migration assumptions, applying auto-scaling and right-sizing adjustments that accelerate ROI, and knowing when a workload is ready to modernize versus when to leave it alone. AWS specialists share the decisions and strategy to turn your freshly migrated environment into one worth the investment.

title: Your playbook for modernizing 988K lines of .NET in 2 days
speakers: Mustaali Dehnuwala (Transaction Network Services, Inc.); Anitha Deenadayalan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Transaction Network Services (TNS) needed to modernize their Altitude payments platform that included 274 projects, 988K lines of code, and 20 years of legacy .NET Framework to .NET 10. Their estimate: six months. The result: two days, 26 modules migrated, and 34 security vulnerabilities resolved. In this session, you'll learn what made it possible - from upgrading shared libraries first, running deterministic tools before AI, using human-verified tests, to keeping engineers on the keyboard after the tools stop running. Walk away with a practical, repeatable playbook for accelerating large-scale .NET modernization.

title: Your playbook: turn your scattered databases into AI-ready infrastructure
speakers: Aarthi Raju (AWS); Sudhir Balasubramanian (AWS)
abstract: Business-critical data scattered across Oracle, SQL Server, and VMware or Nutanix-hosted databases is the number one blocker to deploying agentic AI at scale. In this lightning talk, you'll get a practical playbook for database migration to AWS: real licensing challenges, cost optimization strategies, and modernization pathways that accelerate the path to cloud-native databases using AWS Transform and agentic AI. You'll leave with a clear migration framework that turns fragmented data estates into AI-ready infrastructure, no matter where your databases live today.

title: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
aoi: Innovation & Transformation;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Eva Knight (Amazon Web Services); McLaren Stanley (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.

title: Accelerating cost optimization on AWS
services: AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS Compute Optimizer;AWS Savings Plans
speakers: Mary Nachimov (AWS); Jimmy Yang (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Finding and implementing cost optimization recommendations sustainably require constant monitoring and action. Join this session to learn how you can accelerate your optimization outcomes while maintaining flexibility in how savings are distributed across your organization. See how you can also measure, share and continuously improve your results.

title: AI Powered Business Intelligence with Amazon Quick
speakers: Anabel Montero (Instructor Enablement)
abstract: Amazon Quick brings AI-powered analytics, automation, and research into a single workspace. In this bootcamp, build interactive dashboards and visualizations with Quick Sight, organize team knowledge resources in Spaces with appropriate permissions, create custom Chat Agents to surface insights conversationally, automate repetitive workflows with Quick Flows, and conduct multi-source research with proper validation. The three hands-on labs give you practical experience to apply these skills immediately in your organization

title: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
services: Amazon Redshift;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon Quick Suite
abstract: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.

title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
speakers: Scott Malkie (Amazon Web Services); Art Baudo (AWS Village - Compute (EC2 / Graviton))
abstract: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.

title: Automating migration incentives using Agentic AI
abstract: The biggest bottleneck in large-scale migrations isn't technical. It's the time between customer commitment and first workload moving. Agreements, partner funding approvals, and credit disbursement today require manual coordination across multiple teams and systems. AWS Transform automates the entire incentive lifecycle: one-click agreement acceptance, auto-populated partner fund requests, and threshold-based credit triggers that disburse automatically when tagged resources hit spend targets. In this session, learn how AWS Transform is removing administrative friction so incentives accelerate migrations instead of delaying them.

title: Build Agentic AI That Understands Your Business with SAP and AWS (sponsored by SAP)
speakers: Haridas Nair (SAP); Ted Way (SAP)
abstract: Enterprise AI falls short when agents lack live business context. See how SAP's Business AI Platform and AWS solve this: Joule Studio enables developers and business users to build and deploy custom AI agents grounded in SAP's process knowledge, while bidirectional, zero-copy integration between SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon Athena gives AWS services secure access to trusted SAP data. Watch a live demo of building agents that reason with business context, collaborate across SAP and AWS, and act across enterprise processes with governance.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

title: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
speakers: Cornelia Davis (Temporal)
abstract: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.

title: Building 10x Organizations - Using Modern Productivity Metrics (sponsored by Atlassian)
services: AWS IAM Identity Center;AWS Marketplace;AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Justin Reock (DX // Atlassian)
abstract: 10x developers may be a myth, but 10x organizations are very real, as proven by the influential study performed in the 1980s, ‘The Coding War Games.’ In this keynote-style session, teams will take a detailed, granular look at the barriers to productivity developers face today and modern approaches for removing them. You’ll learn about the history of productivity theory, and how previous practices have influenced our current understanding. DevOps and Platform Engineering philosophy is clearly converging on developer experience. But which of these approaches works? DORA? SPACE? DevEx? What should we invest in and create urgency behind today so we don’t have the same discussion again in a decade? This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.

title: Building for Always-On: Resilient Trading to Agentic AI on Modern Data Foundation (sponsored by Cognizant)
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda;Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
speakers: Abhishek Sharma (Lpl Financial Holdings Inc.)
abstract: Learn how LPL Financial built an always-on trading platform on AWS that supports 32,000+ financial advisors with resilient, multi-region architecture for mission-critical, latency-sensitive workloads. Discover how a unified data foundation across trading, brokerage, and custodial systems creates a trusted layer for innovation, and learn the realities of deploying agentic AI in a regulated broker-dealer environment. Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

title: Building lightning-fast web apps
speakers: Samrat Karak (AWS)
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this lightning talk, hear how a customer built a full-stack web application entirely on AWS Serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. They cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical takeaways for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Building the Intelligent Health System, CXO blueprint for the agentic era (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Geoffry Hook (Northwell Health); Abbas Mooraj (PwC)
abstract: The health systems that will lead the next decade are not simply digitizing existing processes. They are reimagining what a health system looks like with AI native to every layer. On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Context to Action: Turning Agent Memory into a Customer Retention Lever (sponsored by MongoDB)
speakers: Srikrishna Srinivasan (T-Mobile)
abstract: When a customer calls, a support rep has seconds to understand what they need, what device they're on, and how to solve it fast. Get it right, and you earn trust. Get it wrong, and churn becomes a real risk. T-Mobile closes that gap with agent memory: session context pre-populated before the call starts, enriched turn by turn as it unfolds, with real-time graph traversal connecting customer, device, and issue so the rep sees the full picture. MongoDB Atlas runs it all, from vector search over T-Mobile's knowledge corpus to in-call graph traversal to the live session-memory documents. Afterward, AWS Neptune turns that history into a graph shaping future routing and retention. Walk away with an architecture pattern for building agent memory in real time, and a way to decide what belongs in short-term memory versus what should persist. Featuring T-Mobile, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Conversational AI at Scale: S&P Global Energy's 30+ Genie Agents
services: Amazon CloudFront;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon EC2 - Graviton
abstract: S&P Global Energy serves the world's largest financial institutions and energy traders with trusted commodities data — pricing, supply and demand, LNG cargoes, outages, and contracts. To make that data estate conversational, they built an external-facing AI product powered by 30+ Databricks Genie Agents, each scoped to a specific energy domain, then composed into cross-commodity endpoints via MCP servers. The system handles 300K+ queries per month, with customers asking complex analytical questions in natural language and getting governed, auditable answers backed by Unity Catalog. Subject-matter experts publish new conversational experiences in days — without writing agent code. Leave with a blueprint for turning governed data into production conversational AI on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

title: Cost optimization techniques for Amazon EBS
abstract: Learn about the latest Amazon EBS capabilities and how they help you optimize your storage volumes. We cover new features, use cases, and guidance for getting started.

title: Ctrl+Alt+Ship: Hands-On with Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer
abstract: Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a choose-your-own-adventure experience with self-paced labs spanning Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer. Start with the Kiro IDE for AI-native development, or level up to multi-agent workflows. Solve an escape-room-style corporate crisis using Quick, your AI work assistant, choosing between a guided investigation or an advanced multi-step operation to plan, execute, and automate your way to cracking the case. With Connect Customer, see how AI resolves customer issues, gives agents context, and helps supervisors improve service—or go hands-on with the agentic CX designer, a no-code visual canvas, to build conversational AI. AWS facilitators from each product team will be available to answer questions. Labs are 30-60 min. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed.

title: Cutting manual accounts payable work
abstract: Enterprise customers pay for cloud services across dozens of payer accounts and countries through procurement/accounts payable platforms like SAP Ariba and Coupa and track it all in spreadsheets and email threads. Purchase orders run out unnoticed. Payments land on the wrong invoices. Disputes take months. In this session, see how a new first-party application gives Accounts Payable teams one live view of purchase orders, invoices and payments matched against billing records no console login required.

title: EC2 instances from launch to fleet orchestration
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon EC2 Spot
speakers: Brian Phillippi (Amazon); Shubham Sarin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon EC2 now offers over 1,000 instance types, five purchasing models, and a growing set of fleet and capacity tools. How do you bring it all together? This session is your comprehensive guide to AWS compute today. We cover the full EC2 portfolio from Graviton5 to accelerated instances, walk through On-Demand, Spot, Savings Plans, and Capacity Reservations, and show how EC2 Fleet, Auto Scaling, and Capacity Manager help you run the right instances at the right price. Whether you're new to EC2 or a seasoned practitioner, leave with a clear map of modern compute on AWS.

title: Engineering the Context that Makes Enterprise AI Work (sponsored by Impetus Technologies Inc)
speakers: Deepak Khosla (Impetus Technologies)
abstract: Every enterprise has access to the same AI models. The real differentiator is context. Discover Impetus’ Context Engineering Delivery Lifecycle, a proven methodology than ensures no AI agent reaches production without a signed-off context bundle, evaluation record, and explainability trace. Learn how to engineer enterprise data, domain knowledge, industry ontologies, business rules, and governance into a robust context layer agents need to deliver accurate, trusted outcomes. Get practical insights on building AI systems on AWS that are grounded, explainable, reliable, and ready to scale. This presentation is brought to you by Impetus Technologies Inc, an AWS Partner.

title: From First Workload to the Autonomous Enterprise: Transform and Scale with SAP on AWS (sponsored by SAP)
speakers: Steve Van Wyk (SAP America, Inc.)
abstract: Agentic AI is making ERP modernization more urgent than ever. To coordinate decisions across the organization enterprise, AI must be grounded in a modern cloud ERP foundation—one that connects data, processes, business rules, and controls. ERP is no longer just where work is recorded. It has become the operational foundation that enables enterprise agentic AI and ultimately the Autonomous Enterprise.​ SAP and AWS are partnering to help clients accelerate their AI vision Autonomous Enterprise where people set direction, AI executes operational tasks, and organizations respond faster to change leveraging a single intelligent system with full business context. Join us to explore how SAP on AWS helps moves organizations of all sizes to move beyond isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide outcomes delivered with reliability and confidence.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.

title: From On-Premises to Agentic AI: Bayer's Amazon Connect Transformation Journey (sponsored by Capgemini)
speakers: Vivek Sandell (Capgemini America, Inc.); Andreea Manolache (Bayer LLC)
abstract: Capgemini transformed 414 contact center hotlines across more than 68 countries by replacing Cisco UCCE with Amazon Connect and introducing AgentX, an AWS-native agentic AI platform deployed across the Bayer enterprise. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Connect, Amazon Lex, AWS Lambda, and other AWS services, AgentX delivers real-time agent assistance, automated call summarization, governance controls, predictive analytics, and autonomous workflow execution. Learn how Bayer established a "build once, deploy globally" operating model that enables consistent AI innovation across business units while reducing operational complexity, improving agent productivity, and delivering significant cost savings. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.
