title: Hands-On Workshop: Build & Deploy AI Agents with Cloudera Agent Studio (sponsored by Cloudera)
speakers: Nijjwol Lamsal (Cloudera INC)
abstract: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera Agent Studio. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will build multi-agent workflows without code, develop agentic chatbots for data access, learn Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration with AWS tools including Amazon Bedrock and PuppyGraph, and explore the latest Cloudera AI and Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: High Growth. Bold Innovation. The Kiwibank Story. (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: Serena Smorti (Accenture); Dusshyant Roy (Accenture)
abstract: How does a nationally owned bank out-innovate much larger competitors? Kiwibank, New Zealand's only 100% NZ-owned bank, must compete against four far larger Australian-owned banks — with a fraction of the resources. Working with Accenture and AWS, Kiwibank is building a governed enterprise AI layer that every future application can draw from. The result: a compounding AI advantage that grows with each new use case, letting the bank launch products faster, serve customers more intelligently, and scale without proportional cost growth. Hear how Kiwibank is using Accenture and AWS to build the AI foundation for its next decade of growth. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: How A+E Global Media Manages Storage Sprawl and Optimizes Cost (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: As data-intensive and AI workloads drive continued growth in cloud infrastructure and storage, the complexity of understanding usage, ownership, and cost is increasing. In this session, we'll walk through how A+E Global Media gained visibility into the drivers behind rising S3 spend, connected costs to application owners, and established stronger FinOps governance. Attendees will walk away with best practices for architecting cost-efficient systems with Datadog by identifying inefficiencies and connecting cost, storage, and operational context to drive continuous optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: How Bayer simplified their genomics pipeline with Amazon S3 Files
speakers: Ben Gonzalez (Bayer)
abstract: Bayer's genomics and research teams relied on a patchwork of workarounds to support specialized software, user scripts, and ad-hoc analysis on cloud-stored data. AWS DataSync and Storage Gateway handle high-throughput data uploads to S3, but downstream access meant managing multiple data copies, manual downloads, and unstable FUSE mounts, adding cost and operational overhead. Bayer shares how adding S3 Files to their architecture eliminated these access workarounds by providing a simple, mountable file interface directly on their S3 data. Learn how their team reduced data duplication and gave researchers access to petabyte-scale genomics datasets without changing their existing tools or workflows.

title: How FINRA automated dependency lifecycle management with AI agents
speakers: Mahesh Duraisamy (FINRA); Elio Damaggio (AWS); Brandon Webb (Amazon)
abstract: With 2,300 components and over 700,000 dependencies, FINRA uses Kiro and AWS Transform custom to deploy GenAI upgrade agents across Python, Java, and Angular. Learn how governed automation and monthly "Transform-a-thons" reclaimed 1,800 engineering hours across 25 teams in three months, and how to shift from reactive patching to predictable dependency lifecycle management. Discover how FINRA's move to continuous modernization reduces the effort of maintaining technical debt.

title: How Philips accelerated sales quoting with Agentic AI (sponsored by EPAM)
abstract: Philips, a global health technology company, identified an opportunity to accelerate customer quoting for complex solutions combining equipment, software and services. Working with EPAM, Philips built the solution on AWS using an AI-native approach. A team of fewer than 20 used Amazon Kiro across the software development lifecycle, with Amazon Bedrock and the Strands Agents SDK powering an agentic architecture. The result is Sensei, an AI-powered sales experience. This session shares practical lessons for applying agentic AI, accelerating development and business operations, embedding governance, and moving from prototype to enterprise production at scale. This presentation is brought to you by EPAM, an AWS Partner.

title: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier, from silicon to application
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Colin Brace (Amazon)
abstract: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack: chips, servers, software, and the models built on top, each layer making the next one faster and cheaper to run. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. You will see how each layer of innovation compounds and learn where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.

title: How YipitData Builds AI-Native Analytics with AWS, Databricks, and OpenAI (sponsored by Databricks)
services: Amazon CloudFront;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon EC2 - Graviton
speakers: Sully Clark (Databricks); Ankith Ede (OpenAI); Anup Segu (YipitData)
abstract: YipitData gives customers a self-service way to answer analytical questions using agents grounded in its data, completing custom requests in 30 minutes compared with the two weeks previously needed. This session walks through the production architecture behind that experience, combining Databricks for data governance and observability, OpenAI for reasoning and intelligence, and AWS for application resiliency and hosting. Learn how a custom agent harness connects OpenAI frontier models to Databricks SQL Warehouses, with Amazon ECS and ElastiCache supporting the application and asynchronous agent execution. We cover Unity Catalog access boundaries, dedicated agent identities, durable session state in Lakebase, and evaluations that check SQL, tool use, and answer consistency. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
speakers: Chris McPeek (AWS); Eric Johnson (Amazon)
abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

title: Next-gen threat detection: GuardDuty advanced security capabilities
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Cost Optimization;Machine Learning
speakers: Baris Coskun (AWS); Justin Criswell (AWS)
abstract: Amazon GuardDuty protects millions of accounts using AI and ML models purpose-built for cloud security, and the detection engine keeps getting smarter without requiring action from you. In this session, the lead scientist behind GuardDuty's detection engine takes you inside the research. Learn how the team designs models for security inference at scale, uses distillation and reinforcement learning to keep detection cost-efficient without sacrificing accuracy, and distinguishes normal from anomalous behavior without using customer data for training. See how these advances translate into expanded coverage, faster detection of sophisticated threats, and deeper investigation workflows. You leave with an understanding of the engineering tradeoffs behind AI-native threat detection at AWS scale and how to operationalize the latest capabilities.

title: Rise of Autonomous Clinical Data Management: AI Agents Accelerating Drug Development (sponsored by Cognizant)
speakers: Nareen Katta (AbbVie); Gaurav Sharma (Cognizant)
abstract: Explore how autonomous AI agents are transforming clinical data management from a collection of manual processes into an intelligent, continuously learning system that improves quality, accelerates study execution, and shortens the path from protocol to patient impact. Clinical trials generate unprecedented volumes of complex data, yet many Clinical Data Management (CDM) processes remain highly manual, resource-intensive, and constrained by siloed workflows. Critical activities such as protocol interpretation, clinical trial data systems build and configuration, edit check generation, data review, data quality management, reconciliation, and database lock often reside on the critical path to study completion. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

title: Running SAN workloads on Amazon EBS
abstract: Amazon EBS delivers the performance, durability, and enterprise features that mission-critical SAN workloads depend on. In this session, learn how the latest EBS capabilities map to what you run on premises today, which workloads are the best fit, and how customers are moving databases and enterprise applications off storage arrays and onto EBS. Leave with practical guidance to get started.

title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
speakers: Amit Shah (Kong); Bryce Macher (FanDuel Inc); Jonathan Kindberg (FanDuel)
abstract: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.

title: Take Voice and Image AI into Production with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
speakers: Teri Yu (OpenAI)
abstract: Build production AI workflows that turn language, vision, voice, and structured data into useful action. This session explores how developers can combine varied enterprise inputs with tool use on Amazon Bedrock. Learn approaches for model routing and evaluation, and explore the security and governance considerations involved in making voice and image workflows dependable in production. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: The Control Plane for Your Agent Workforce: Governance, Cost and ROI at Scale (sponsored by Cognition)
abstract: Cognition has rolled out Devin, the autonomous software engineer, at the world's largest Fortune 500 companies. Along the way, we learned that scaling an agent workforce hinges on three questions every enterprise asks: How do we onboard agents? How do we know they're delivering value? How do we ensure they only do what they're supposed to? Drawing from real deployments, this session introduces the practical patterns we developed to answer them — governance, cost controls, ROI measurement, and federated configurations. You'll leave with a playbook for turning agents from a promising pilot into a trusted, scaled workforce. This presentation is brought to you by Cognition, an AWS Partner.

title: Trusting an Autonomous Agent With Your Production Environment (sponsored by NeuBird)
services: AWS CloudTrail;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Hub
speakers: Andrew Lee (NeuBird)
abstract: The biggest barrier to autonomous operations isn't capability, it's trust.Handing an incident to an autonomous agent raises a fair question. How do you know it is not guessing from raw log lines. This session shows how NeuBird AI reasons over your live environment and shows the causal chain behind every root cause, not a coincidence in the metrics. We’ll examine the guardrails that make production deployment safe: VPC-native execution, zero external data retention, complete auditable reasoning paths, and human-gated action approvals. Learn how to safely transition from human-driven triage to trusted, autonomous production operations on your own terms. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird, an AWS Partner.

title: Unlock Secure Vibe Coding on AWS Today (sponsored by Superblocks)
aoi: Responsible AI;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management
abstract: Your business teams already build apps with AI, often on real company data. Most of those apps never make it to production. The rest run without guardrails, and IT can't see who built what or what data it touches. Blocking the tools doesn't stop the building. This session lays out a third option: a reference blueprint for governed vibe coding in your own AWS account. Learn how to set guardrails once for every AI-built app, catch vulnerable code before it ships, keep a full audit trail, and make sure every app still has an owner when its builder leaves. This presentation is brought to you by Superblocks, an AWS Partner.

title: Using AI to scale legacy app modernization with Experian & Itaú
speakers: Douglas Suryan (Itau Unibanco S A Bank Group); Rao Panchomarthi (Amazon); Gaurav Arora (Experian Services Corp.)
abstract: A successful modernization approach only matters if it scales beyond the first pilot. Experian and Itaú share how they grew their approach with AWS Transform and Kiro from a single engagement into an enterprise-wide operating model. Experian compresses mainframe analysis from months to days, then standardizes modernization across 550+ workloads and multiple regions with a fully agentic reverse-engineering pipeline. Itaú expanded to 43 business domains, processing nearly 140 million lines of code in a single month. Leave with the operating models that scale modernization from one application to the entire portfolio, unlocking AI-driven capabilities along the way.

title: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Vamshi Vijay Nakkirtha (AWS); Navneet Verma (AWS)
abstract: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: 4 foundations for building the agentic enterprise on AWS​ (sponsored by IBM)
speakers: Neel Sundaresan (IBM)
abstract: Agentic AI is moving fast—but isolated agents and one-off experiments won’t transform the enterprise. To create value at scale, companies need a foundation that helps them build and modernize applications faster, orchestration across systems and workflows, governed execution, and control over the infrastructure, performance and cost behind them.​ Join IBM and industry leaders to discover what’s new from IBM on AWS. Hear real-world lessons and measurable business outcomes while exploring the four foundations organizations need to move from disconnected agents to secure, governed, enterprise-wide execution.​ This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: AI flight plan: How British Airways’ parent builds and measures AI ROI (sponsored by NTT DATA)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda
speakers: Luis Huerta (IAG/BRITISH AIRWAYS PLC); Charlie Doubek (NTT DATA Deutschland GmbH)
abstract: British Airways’ parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), has moved rapidly from AI experimentation to production deployments delivering measurable results. This session explores how IAG and its partner NTT DATA assess AI opportunities by giving business units ownership of value realization, build momentum by prioritizing high-impact use cases, and operationalize AI through scalable technology, operating models, governance and change management. Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NTT DATA, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Governance: The Framework, The Pitfalls, The Playbook (sponsored by Vanta)
abstract: The AI revolution is upending organizations’ security and GRC programs. Shadow AI is exploding as employees adopt new agent harnesses, workflows, platforms, and plugins. Even sanctioned AI poses new challenges that don’t yet have standardized solutions. Meanwhile, developers are moving AI applications from experimentation to production, introducing new risks. This session will break down what AI Governance is all about, cover common concerns that it’s meant to resolve, and provide attendees with practical tips for solving some of their most pressing AI Governance challenges. What you’ll learn. What AI Governance entails, from practical policy to active protections. How to solve AI Governance concerns across different layers of the AI stack. This presentation is brought to you by Vanta, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Meets Production: The New Reliability Playbook for Financial Services (sponsored by Traversal)
abstract: Financial services depend on software that needs to be available around the clock. When that software fails, the consequences can affect millions of customers and create regulatory, financial, and reputational risk. This panel brings together technology leaders from some of the world’s largest financial institutions across banking, payments, and investment management for a conversation moderated by Anish Agrawal, CEO & Cofounder of Traversal, the AI SRE helping diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents across complex enterprise environments. Together, they’ll discuss how AI is changing production reliability across financial services, where it’s already being used, the emerging role of AI SREs, what teams look for when evaluating new approaches, and what it takes to deploy AI safely in highly regulated environments. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond pilots: agentic AI transforming mortgage operations and IT at scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
abstract: Mortgage lending still runs on handoffs, exceptions, and manual review. See how a leading US mortgage lender is rebuilding origination and servicing with agentic AI on AWS, cutting cycle times while keeping controls and auditability intact. We will also show how the same agent patterns reach IT operations, resolving incidents before customers feel them. Tata Consultancy Services shares the reference architecture, guardrails, and adoption model behind both. Built for financial services business and operations leaders, CIOs and IT operations heads, and data and AI leaders, this session gives you a practical path from promising pilots to production at enterprise scale. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond the Build: Scaling and Governing AI Agents with Dataiku and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Dataiku)
abstract: As enterprises move from experimenting with AI agents to deploying them at scale, the challenge is no longer just how to build agents, it’s how to maintain visibility, performance, and control across the growing agent ecosystem. This session will explore how Amazon Bedrock and Dataiku Agent Management support the agent lifecycle from creation through enterprise-wide management. Attendees will see how organizations can build and deploy agents with AWS while using Dataiku to discover agents, monitor performance, and identify risk across environments, helping teams scale agentic AI with greater confidence and governance. This presentation is brought to you by Dataiku, an AWS Partner.

title: Build an Agentic Enterprise to Enable Autonomous Action (sponsored by Snowflake)
speakers: John Pulikkottil (Hyatt); Santiago Giraldo (Snowflake)
abstract: Building an agentic enterprise empowers organizations to automate complex work and drive measurable business outcomes. True transformation happens when autonomous AI operates across systems using trusted data, flexible models, connected applications, and a unified, agentic control plane. By bringing knowledge workers and technical builders into a shared agentic environment, teams move faster without sacrificing governance. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud unifies enterprise context, model choice, and app connections into a single architecture. Discover how to turn enterprise data into reliable, autonomous action and long-term competitive advantage in your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
abstract: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA);Amazon SageMaker AI
speakers: Mikhail Shapirov (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Josh West (Red Hat, Inc.)
abstract: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.

title: Deploying Frontier Voice Agents Privately on AWS (sponsored by ElevenLabs)
speakers: Nicolas Bernier (ElevenLabs)
abstract: Frontier voice agents are already handling live customer calls inside health systems, banks and insurers, without audio ever leaving the customer's AWS account. This session covers the architecture that makes that possible, from in-VPC deployment and zero data retention to integration with their existing stack. Working from a production deployment taking real calls, we walk through the latency budget that keeps conversational voice feeling human, the trade-offs private deployment brings, and how to size it for your own environment. Leave with an understanding of where ElevenAgents fits in your current environment, a reference architecture and a deployment checklist. This presentation is brought to you by ElevenLabs, an AWS Partner.

title: Drive AI at full speed: The enterprise blueprint (sponsored by HashiCorp)
speakers: Kyle Ruddy (HashiCorp, an IBM company); Cole Morrison (HashiCorp)
abstract: AI gave teams a faster car. It did not fix the roads. As teams create more applications, infrastructure and complexity, the challenge shifts from moving faster to operating smarter. Enterprises need context to understand what is happening, agency to act across the tools they already use, and control to keep speed from becoming chaos. In this session, see how Terraform and Vault together with Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore and IBM Concert to standardize delivery, secure access and connect application context to action across hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
speakers: Mike Worthington (Mike Worthington)
abstract: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. This presentation is brought to you by Neo4j, an AWS Partner.

title: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EC2 Linux
speakers: Abhipal Singh (Bain Capital, LP); Nicky Pike (Coder); John Zink (Bain Capital)
abstract: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.

title: Fresh Threats, Stale Defenses: The Race for Real‑Time Security (sponsored by Booz Allen)
speakers: Emilio Rodas (Booz Allen)
abstract: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.

title: From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by Dynatrace)
speakers: Jon Griffiths (Dynatrace); Margarita Rubio (United Airlines)
abstract: As enterprise AI matures, the opportunity extends far beyond software development. Join United Airlines, AWS, and Dynatrace to discover how insights powered by AI, full stack cloud observability, and runtime intelligence are helping engineering and operations teams improve reliability, accelerate delivery, and reduce operational complexity. Learn how leading organizations are using real-time data to automate investigations, predict issues before customer impact, and move toward autonomous operations. The session will cover real-world adoption lessons, AI governance considerations, and practical steps to balance automation with accountability while unlocking greater value from AI across the software lifecycle at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

title: From AI Pilots to Enterprise Impact: NJIT's Blueprint for AI Governance and Adoption (sponsored by Kyndryl)
abstract: Many organizations are racing to implement AI use cases but struggle to scale beyond isolated experiments. New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT) faced a similar challenge, with AI activity emerging across the institution without a unified strategy, governance model or operating framework. In partnership with Kyndryl, NJIT established an AI governance strategy, operating model and leadership alignment process that transformed fragmented experimentation into a coordinated, institution-wide programme. Join NJIT, Kyndryl and AWS to learn how governance, stakeholder alignment and dedicated operating models can accelerate AI innovation with confidence. Discover why successful AI transformation begins with strategy before technology, and how organisations can move from experimentation to scalable impact. This presentation is brought to you by Kyndryl, an AWS Partner.

title: From Signals to Action for Sempra: AI-Powered Cybersecurity on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: JONATHAN HOLT (Accenture); Ben Gordon (Sempra Energy)
abstract: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. Sempra Energy, AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: Ghost agents: Governing ephemeral AI & machine access in real-time (sponsored by SailPoint)
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Identity & Access Management;Machine Learning
speakers: Stephen Cortese (SailPoint)
abstract: Ephemeral AI agents and cloud workloads spin up, access resources, and vanish in minutes, never landing in traditional identity registries. How do you govern what you can’t track? The answer lies in securing the non-human identities (NHIs) they leave behind. Join SailPoint for a live demo on governing ephemeral agent behavior. We’ll show you how to untangle NHI ownership, expose over-privileged access, and establish real-time governance over transient machine identities before they expose your cloud. Walk away with a blueprint to manage non-human access risk at cloud scale. This is clarity you can act on. This presentation is brought to you by SailPoint, an AWS Partner.

title: Give Your Best Engineers Back to the Roadmap, Not the Pager (sponsored by NeuBird)
services: Amazon CloudWatch;AWS Billing and Cost Management;AWS Compute Optimizer
speakers: Ara Zarifian (NeuBird)
abstract: Forty percent of engineering time goes to firefighting instead of the roadmap you funded. The problem isn’t a lack of dashboards or headcount, it’s that these engineers are forced to act as the glue across these fragmented tools. Between incidents, an autonomous Production Ops Agent keeps working. It deepens its model of your environment, right sizes observability spend, and turns every incident into a captured fix nobody has to relearn. This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird, an AWS Partner.

title: How TeleTracking runs AWS at a 30:1 ratio with Grafana Cloud AI (sponsored by Grafana Labs)
abstract: TeleTracking's platform is air traffic control for hospitals: 200K+ beds and 100+ command centers depend on it. Re-platforming onto an AI-native foundation has taken its service-to-engineer ratio from 6:1 to 30:1. The lever isn't headcount: It’s relying on one agent to pair gcx and the Grafana Cloud MCP server with AWS MCP tooling. Oren Lion replays an MSK incident where Grafana Assistant identified a cluster-wide broker disruption in minutes, pairing Frontend Observability with Amazon CloudFront to line up what hurt with what changed. He closes with Assistant Investigations, read-only guardrails, and a recipe you can run yourself.. This presentation is brought to you by Grafana Labs, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
abstract: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.

title: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler)
speakers: Mark Ryan (Zscaler, Inc.)
abstract: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Move Fast With AI Agents Without Betting the Business (sponsored by MontyCloud)
speakers: Eric Morrissey (MontyCloud)
abstract: You are under pressure to put AI agents to work fast, without betting the business. Everyone is racing to build agents, but no one is governing them. MontyCloud is an AI-native, autonomous CloudOps platform built on one conviction. As agents become easy to create, value moves to trusted execution. Walk away with a blueprint for turning insights into governed workflows, and governed workflows into trusted outcomes. See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. This presentation is brought to you by MontyCloud, an AWS Partner.

title: Multicloud in the Real World: Financial Services, Healthcare, and Manufacturing (sponsored by Oracle)
speakers: Edwin Upson (Oracle)
abstract: Oracle AI Database@AWS gives organizations a new way to bring mission-critical Oracle data closer to their applications, analytics, and AI services in AWS. This session shares a clear overview of the multicloud value proposition, including application proximity, operational simplicity, enterprise performance, security, and access to AWS services. Three Oracle industry leaders will explore what that value looks like in practice. Hear how financial institutions can strengthen fraud detection, risk management, and customer experiences; how healthcare organizations can generate trusted clinical and operational insights; and how manufacturers can improve forecasting, supply chain decisions, asset performance, and operational efficiency. Leave with a practical understanding of Oracle AI Database@AWS and concrete examples of how multicloud can support industry-specific AI and business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

title: No room for error: deploying trusted AI when the stakes are high (sponsored by Monte Carlo)
speakers: Brenda Remy (GE HealthCare); Barr Moses (Monte Carlo)
abstract: Deploying agents at scale is a major endeavor for any organization; in healthcare, the stakes are especially high. Unpredictable behaviors & unreliable outputs pose a risk to patients, invite scrutiny from regulators, & erode hard-won institutional trust. Regulated industries must balance accuracy alongside their drive to innovate. Barr Moses, co-founder & CEO of Monte Carlo, will delve into this challenging topic with leaders from GE Healthcare. They’ll dissect some of the most difficult failure modes for agents & discuss how reliability practices have to evolve as teams scale agentic workflows in high-stakes environments. Discussed: how AI itself can be turned back on the problem of observing, resolving, and optimizing agents as well as building the guardrails, ownership models, & trust infrastructure that let a highly regulated organization move quickly without compromising on trust. This presentation is brought to you by Monte Carlo, an AWS Partner.

title: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi)
speakers: Mani Gill (Boomi); Patricia Moore (Boomi)
abstract: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

title: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security)
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Ian Weyenberg (NetDocuments)
abstract: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.

title: Own Your Harness: Control Cost & Risk in Enterprise-Wide AI Adoption (sponsored by Presidio)
speakers: Maharajan Rathakrishnan (Presidio); Rob Kim (Presidio Networked Solutions, LLC)
abstract: The fastest way to lose control of AI is to let agents multiply without a harness. This talk walks through Presidio's journey from scattered pilots to enterprise-wide adoption, built on a custom orchestration layer that treats cost, identity, and policy as first-class concerns. Attendees will get an inside look at the architectural decisions, guardrails, and economic models that let us scale AI use predictably across the business. If you're weighing governance (cost and risk) against velocity, this is the playbook you want from day one. This presentation is brought to you by Presidio, an AWS Partner.

title: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
speakers: Siddhartha Srivastava (Adobe Inc)
abstract: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Architecting AI Governance & Security at Scale
speakers: Omkar Deshmane (Amazon); Dodd Pfeffer (Amazon); Omar Gonzalez (AWS)
abstract: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without security and governance. In this Rodeo, you'll join a team and face three demanding stakeholders: a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead, racing to get Agentic AI live. Your team's mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all three happy. Together, you'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island)
abstract: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.

title: Secure Coding Agents for Regulated Environments with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Act Security)
aoi: Culture of Security;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Offir Levy (Act Security)
abstract: Learn how HUB International, a top-five global insurance broker, partnered with AWS and Act Security to securely bring autonomous coding agents into a regulated enterprise environment, without giving the agents standing credentials or expanding the attack surface. The team transformed the local Claude Code experience into a secure, per-user cloud sandbox on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preserving the familiar IDE and terminal workflow while moving execution to the cloud. See how OIDC authentication through the corporate IdP, per-call token minting through AgentCore Identity, and Cedar-based authorization for tools exposed through AgentCore Gateway enforce per-user, per-action access. Finally, discover how Act Security sustains least privilege over time and enforces narrower policies - whether you are deploying AgentCore for the first time or hardening an existing environment. This presentation is brought to you by Act Security, an AWS Partner.

title: ServiceNow: The Super Intelligence Control Tower for Business Reinvention (sponsored by ServiceNow)
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Gian Mario Deluigi (ServiceNow); Alex Mastrodonato (ServiceNow)
abstract: AI without workflows is just expensive advice. The next generation of AI leaders are moving beyond disconnected copilots and isolated use cases to reinvent how work gets done. Join ServiceNow to learn how the Super Intelligence Control Tower for Business Reinvention helps organizations govern AI, connect enterprise data, and orchestrate work across every agent, model, and workflow. Discover how AI that thinks and workflows that act enable enterprises to deploy AI quickly while maintaining trust, security, and control. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.

title: Setting up the Right AI Architecture: Bringing Together Agents, Teams, and Context (sponsored by Notion)
abstract: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.

title: Ship agents, not chaos: a 90-day pattern for production on AWS. (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
abstract: AI agents are moving from pilots into production faster than most organizations can govern them, and independent teams building in parallel are creating what practitioners now call agent sprawl. This session presents a repeatable 90-day pattern that converts sprawl into governed agents ready for production, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Guardrails, and Kiro alongside NIST AI RMF and the Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Architects, platform owners, and public-sector leaders see how a governed runtime, evidence-based mission KPIs, and cost discipline turn compliance into an accelerator. Audit-ready patterns from CDW customer engagements across regulated commercial and public-sector missions are included This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop building agents that stop short of enterprise execution (sponsored by IBM)
abstract: AI value doesn’t come from creating more agents. It comes from putting agents to work—securely, reliably, and across the systems where business gets done. In this session, see how IBM Bob helps developers build and modernize applications with agentic AI, while watsonx Orchestrate coordinates agents, tools, and workflows across the enterprise. Discover how IBM helps teams move from code and intent to governed action—with the visibility and control needed to scale.​ This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: The Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Postman)
abstract: Autonomous agents are no longer assisting the software development lifecycle. They are rewriting it. When agents write, review, test, and ship code at machine speed, the SDLC stops being a sequence of human handoffs and becomes a control problem. This session covers the failure modes that only appear at scale: review queues that no human can absorb, test suites that validate the wrong invariants, provenance gaps that make incidents unexplainable, and CI/CD pipelines built for tens of commits a day now absorbing thousands. It closes with the specific architectural decisions engineering leaders should be making now, drawn from our own experience running agents in production. This presentation is brought to you by Postman, an AWS Partner.

title: The Frontier Doesn't Hold Still: Running Claude Agents at Scale on AWS (sponsored by Anthropic)
speakers: Lauren Polansky (Anthropic)
abstract: Enterprises are moving faster with AI than ever. And they're falling further behind. Once the first agents land and the numbers look good, most teams turn to cost control while the frontier keeps moving. This session covers how to do both with Claude on AWS: the security and compliance controls enterprises require, execution inside your own boundary, observability and cost governance, and the safeguards that let you trust agents with more. Then how to keep expanding what agents do as new models arrive, so efficiency doesn't become the ceiling. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: The Governance Gap Keeping AI Agents Out of Production (sponsored by WSO2)
speakers: Rania Khalaf (WSO2)
abstract: Every leader is under pressure to show AI value now. Some move fast, and agents sprawl across teams with no shared controls. Others lock everything down, and pilots never reach production. Both point to the same gap: governance maturity hasn't kept pace with agent speed. This talk covers how governance becomes an accelerator, not a blocker, to production AI. You’ll learn how to design identity, policy, and guardrails from day one, so agents ship with the same controls whether they run on AWS Bedrock, hybrid, or otherwise. Get the principles right early, and agents move from pilot to production without every team reinventing governance on their own. Takeaways: Why AI programs sprawl or stall, and what governance maturity looks like in between. How trusted AI governance turns into speed instead of slowing teams down. What governance principles to design in from day one, on AWS & beyond. This presentation is brought to you by WSO2, an AWS Partner.

title: Uncover the Opportunity. Build the AI Agent. Scale It Live. (sponsored by NiCE)
speakers: George Downey IV (NiCE Cognigy)
abstract: Your CX data already knows where automation will pay off. See Agentic Analytics pinpoint the opportunity, then watch that recommendation become a working AI agent — built, tested, and scaled live. ​ This presentation is brought to you by NiCE, an AWS Partner.

title: When agentic AI meets critical infrastructure (sponsored by IBM)
aoi: Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI;Cryptography and Post-Quantum
abstract: Agentic AI can transform how utilities serve customers, manage infrastructure and respond to operational events. Join IBM Consulting and industry leaders to see how organizations are putting agentic AI to work on AWS across complex operational workflows. Through real client stories, explore how modern platforms, trusted data and secure software foundations help teams improve service, strengthen resilience and move AI into production with confidence. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace)
speakers: Margaret Cunningham (Darktrace)
abstract: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Darktrace, an AWS Partner.

title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo)
abstract: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.

title: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix)
speakers: Martin Holste (Trellix)
abstract: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.

title: Winning the War on Fraud with Network-Powered Intelligence (sponsored by Vonage, Part of Ericsson)
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Oscar Rodriguez (Vonage); Ramesh Krishnan (Vonage)
abstract: Fraud is winning. SIM swaps have surged over 1,000%; synthetic identity cases are up 60% year-over-year, legacy OTP defenses are structurally broken — and fraudsters know it. Every industry feels it. Banks, healthcare providers, retailers, rideshare and delivery platforms, all fighting the same battle, all demanding the same answer: security that doesn't sacrifice the customer experience. As the first and only communications and Network API provider to achieve the AWS Financial Services Industry Competency, Vonage is changing the equation. Discover how enterprises are moving to a model where identity is verified silently at the network layer, before fraud happens. Built on AWS, powered by direct carrier intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by Vonage, Part of Ericsson, an AWS Partner.

title: 3rd party risk management tabletop experience
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Innovation & Transformation
abstract: Embark on "Third Party Risk Management," an engaging tabletop designed to challenge and refine your approach to managing external partnerships and vendor relationships. In this immersive experience, leaders are thrust into a high-stakes environment where they must navigate complex scenarios involving third-party risks. This tabletop not only enhances your ability to manage third-party risks effectively but also equips you with practical insights and strategies to safeguard your organization’s interests and strengthen its external partnerships. Join us to elevate your risk management acumen and drive resilient, forward-thinking approaches in an interconnected business landscape.

title: Accelerating Data Processing: GPU Accelerated Amazon EMR at the Enterprise Scale (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Felix Cheung (NVIDIA)
abstract: As AI agents ask increasingly complex and frequent questions, analytics systems must become more responsive, scalable, and efficient, over hundreds of Terabytes and trillions of rows. This session explores how GPU acceleration integrated with Amazon EMR can improve performance and efficiency, with the NVIDIA cuDF Router that enables seamless migration and simplifies adoption across a large enterprise setting. Applying operational metrics to AI-driven optimization, the smart router continuously directs workloads for better performance and cost efficiency. See how enterprises can operate this architecture over hundreds of jobs in a fraction of time and hear the practical lessons learned along the way. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI governance tabletop experience
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance;Agentic AI
abstract: Navigate AI-driven security threats as they escalate in real time. In this immersive executive tabletop, participants allocate a constrained governance budget, then respond to live crisis events scored across six dimensions. Practice navigating high-stakes scenarios including autonomous AI deployment failures, third-party security incidents, and emerging regulatory obligations. Confront real attack techniques, compliance frameworks, and enterprise liability exposure while aligning cross-functional teams under pressure. This experience sharpens governance instincts and crisis fluency—equipping leaders to govern Agentic AI risks, enforce accountability, and make decisive resource allocation calls before a real crisis demands it.

title: AWS AI League: Build agents with AgentCore (Agentic Football Cup)
speakers: Parth Desai (Amazon Web Services); Gonzalo Ron (AWS); Ian Holtz (AWS)
abstract: Coordinating agents is where multi agent systems break. They duplicate work, drop handoffs, and burn tokens. In this workshop, build and deploy five autonomous agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Kiro and the Strands Agents SDK, then field them five versus five in live Agentic Football matches. Write the tools your agents call, orchestrate multi turn reasoning across a maze like arena, and solve coordination problems that decide the match. Tune prompts, roles, and tactics between rounds and watch your score climb a live leaderboard. Leave with working code, production ready multi agent patterns, and a shot at the Finale.

title: AWS AI League: Train with RLVR on SageMaker, deploy in AgentCore
speakers: Ruchi Bhatia (AWS); Dana Bullukian (AWS); Seyha Kry (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Turn a generic model into one that wins on your task, and prove it with data. In this hands-on workshop, you customize a foundation model on Amazon SageMaker AI using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), with no infrastructure to manage. Then you build an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates the model end to end: preparing datasets, triggering training, registering models, evaluating with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploying to a real-time endpoint. Your score posts to a live leaderboard, and you tune between rounds to climb it. You walk away knowing when customization beats a strong prompt.

title: Benchmarking Bedrock knowledge bases for agents in production (sponsored by Braintrust)
abstract: In this talk, we’ll walk through an independent eval of Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which manages the ingestion, parsing, and retrieval steps in a RAG application. In the first half, we’ll cover our methodology, including how we developed a dataset that queries documents such as tickets, wiki pages, and product docs, and what we decided to score: latency, cost, relevance, and citation support. We’ll also cover how we analyzed the results with research rigor, including p50 and p95 latency and confidence intervals around our metrics. In the second half, we’ll expand this into a conceptual understanding of evals and observability: why they’re important, how other companies are implementing them in production, and the terminology you need to know. This presentation is brought to you by Braintrust, an AWS Partner.

title: Boost Performance: Salesforce, Slack and AWS Headless Connectivity (sponsored by Salesforce)
speakers: Nehal Padia (Salesforce); Hrushikesh Gangur (AWS); Sameer Vuyyuru (Capita)
abstract: Disconnected systems slow teams down. See how Agentforce, Slack and AgentCore Bedrock enable your Headless agentic strategy to unlock seamless collaboration and boost productivity across teams in real time. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Building AI Agents with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
speakers: Hedieh Zandi (Vercel); Andrew Barba (Vercel)
abstract: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Building an Open and Real-time Fraud and Decisioning Engine with Mastercard and Redis (sponsored by Redis)
speakers: Siva Palanisamy (Mastercard Incorporated)
abstract: Ever get a text that your Mastercard was used in a transaction you didn't make? That's because every card swipe has to be evaluated before it's cleared to keep fraud from slipping through. Join Sivakumar Palanasami, Mastercard's EVP of Data Platforms, to learn how his team's real-time fraud decisioning model built with Redis on AWS and for a sneak peek of what they're doing next. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Secure AI Agents on AWS: XAA, Bedrock AgentCore and the AI Blueprint (sponsored by Okta)
speakers: Wayne Smiley (Okta); Steven Tamm (Okta)
abstract: Building AI agents is easy, but securing enterprise data access without slowing development is hard. Teams often rely on static, over-privileged credentials, creating major security risks. But there’s a solution. This session explores how to secure agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Okta. We’ll introduce the Blueprint Alliance, of which AWS and Okta are founding members, and cover how standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and SCIM for Agents transform AI identity. You'll learn how replacing static keys with dynamic, delegated permissions enables real-time policy evaluation at every tool call, empowering developers to build scalable, trusted AI agents that operate strictly within verified boundaries. This presentation is brought to you by Okta, an AWS Partner.

title: Build the Agentic Workplace: What's New on the Slack Developer Platform (sponsored by Salesforce)
speakers: Josh Milas (Slack)
abstract: Slack is becoming a multiplayer work operating system, where humans and AI agents build together, not just chat. This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. Leave with a clear path to build your first agentic app on Slack. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom)
speakers: Mike Ostrowski (Slalom)
abstract: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Slalom, an AWS Partner.

title: Change. Wait. Debug. Let AI drive the infrastructure loop. (sponsored by HashiCorp)
speakers: Kyle Ruddy (HashiCorp, an IBM company); Cole Morrison (HashiCorp)
abstract: Make a change. Deploy it. Wait. Dig through the logs. Try again. For years, that loop has cost infrastructure engineers countless hours—time that could be spent shipping what comes next. In this session, discover how to take engineers out of the routine operational loop without giving up oversight. Define the outcome, let AI work through the iterations, and step back in only when a real decision needs you. See the pattern in action with Terraform, Vault, Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and more. This presentation is brought to you by HashiCorp, an AWS Partner.

title: Cloud migration journey tabletop experience
abstract: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture.

title: Engineering AI Agents You Can Trust in Production (sponsored by Workato)
speakers: Zayne Turner (Workato)
abstract: Your agent nails the demo, then breaks in production. More often than not, the model isn't what failed, it's everything around it. We'll walk through a methodology for making agent actions reliable, recoverable, and observable in production. You'll leave with patterns you can build yourself, drawn from lessons learned over 100+ enterprise MCP deployments. This presentation is brought to you by Workato, an AWS Partner.

title: Everyone Says They Have an Ontology. Almost Nobody Does (sponsored by TextQL)
speakers: Ethan Ding (TextQL)
abstract: Ontology has become one of the defining ideas in enterprise AI. Every cloud and data platform now claims to have one. They rarely converge on the same structure, conventions, or architecture. Those differences determine whether an ontology can support agentic AI. That test comes down to three things: how it's structured, how it's generated from the systems and context already in place, and how it stays current as the business changes. This talk lays out the practical requirements for an ontology built for agentic AI, drawing on the architecture TextQL runs across the messiest data estates at Fortune 50 companies. This presentation is brought to you by TextQL, an AWS Partner.

title: From discoverable to buyable: Commerce stacks for agent-driven shoppers (sponsored by Stripe)
speakers: Danny Smith (Stripe, Inc.)
abstract: Join Stripe on how AI is changing how shoppers find and buy products—and what it means for your commerce stack. With 20% of holiday ecommerce traffic projected from AI agents, this session is designed for retail leaders moving from "exploring" to "ready." Converting this traffic requires a different approach to catalog readiness, checkout, fraud, and fulfillment. Attendees will leave with clear priorities to act on today and carry into 2027. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

title: From Legacy to Agentic: Modernization Beyond the Code (sponsored by SoftServe)
speakers: Ruslan Kusov (SoftServe)
abstract: What if modernization started beyond the code? SoftServe is reimagining application modernization by working backwards from business needs and desired outcomes to determine what should change and why. In this session, see how SoftServe Agentic Application Modernization combines this outcome-driven approach with CAST Software, AWS Transform, Kiro, AI-DLC and specialized AI agents to accelerate discovery, assessment, transformation, and validation. Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.

title: From Risk Signal to Recovery: Building Agentic Resilience with MCP (sponsored by Commvault)
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Akshay Joshi (Commvault Systems Inc.); Lawrence Chang (Commvault Systems Inc.)
abstract: AI agents are changing cloud operations from human-led workflows to machine-speed decisions and actions. But when agents can access, modify, and move critical data, resilience must become part of the operating model, not a recovery step. Join experts from Commvault, Wiz, and AWS to explore an architecture where MCP connects security context, data intelligence, and recovery capabilities. We'll demonstrate how security signals can guide protection and recovery decisions across Amazon S3 and other cloud services, turning risk insights into governed actions. Learn the guardrails, controls, and architectural patterns behind the workflow, and leave with practical insights for bringing these capabilities into your own cloud-native environments. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.

title: How Hertz Made Karpenter Smarter with autonomous AI-Driven Optimization (sponsored by Cast AI)
speakers: Sonal kumar sinha (Sonal Kumar Sinha)
abstract: Hertz used Cast AI agents to make Karpenter much smarter: the agents autonomously analyze every workload, rightsize it, then continuously instruct Karpenter how to rearrange nodes to cut waste. Hertz's platform engineering team deployed this across their multi-cluster EKS fleet entirely through Terraform. Sonal will show the real numbers: where the extra savings hid, how infrastructure-as-code took onboarding from pre-dev to production, and what it takes to automate cost optimization at fleet scale without babysitting it. This presentation is brought to you by Cast AI, an AWS Partner.

title: How Observability Evolved From Dashboards to Agents Writing Code (sponsored by Honeycomb)
speakers: Martin Thwaites (Honeycomb.io)
abstract: Observability's real job has always been closing the feedback loop between what you ship and what happens next. We'll trace how that loop evolved at Honeycomb: from dashboards you stared at, to SLOs that quantified what mattered, to Canvas, agents that investigate with you, and now MCP tools feeding production reality straight back into software written by agents This presentation is brought to you by Honeycomb, an AWS Partner.

title: How Vanguard Scales AI Oversight Without Scaling Human Review (sponsored by Capgemini)
speakers: Piyush Saxena (Vanguard); Jithin Pradeep (Vanguard)
abstract: Human review can't scale linearly with generative-AI volume. Vanguard's AI Center of Excellence built a closed-loop oversight system where every AI response is scored by an LLM-as-judge, confirmed or overturned by a subject-matter expert, and routed through a confusion matrix: confirmed catches sharpen the agent, disagreements calibrate the judge. Each SME label grows a benchmark that resets how much oversight the next cycle needs, proving mathematically that coverage can fall while risk holds flat. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda-hosted detector SLMs, SQS, DynamoDB, and SageMaker, the loop moves toward real-time interruption of harmful responses before customers see them. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: Incident response tabletop: supply chain
aoi: Disaster Response & Recovery;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Governance, Risk & Compliance
abstract: Join the "Supply Chain Incident Response" tabletop exercise, where executive leaders tackle supply chain disruptions in a realistic, interactive simulation. Collaborate to develop and execute strategies for managing crises, explore decision-making and risk assessment, and enhance communication skills. This exercise strengthens your organization's preparedness and resilience, helping you safeguard operations and improve response capabilities. Build robust strategies to handle and recover from supply chain disruptions effectively.

title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
abstract: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.

title: MCP Meets GraphQL: A Typed Foundation for Enterprise AI Agents (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL)
speakers: Matt DeBergalis (Apollo GraphQL)
abstract: Enterprises connecting AI agents to systems of record face three unsolved problems: can an agent discover what data exists and what it means, get that context without runaway token cost, and touch only what it's authorized to touch. GraphQL, the proven Linux Foundation-backed standard beneath many of the world's largest customer experiences at brands like Netflix, AirBnB, Shopify, Walmart, and countless others, already solves all three through self-describing schemas and field-level queries. This talk lays out the architecture for combining GraphQL with MCP, including Apollo's approach to graph-based orchestration for cost and reliability. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.

title: Move AI agents from prototype to production with 1Password (sponsored by 1Password)
abstract: An AI agent can be easy to prototype but hard to take to production once it needs access to real systems. For developers, platform engineers, and security teams building with AWS AgentCore, this session shows how 1Password uses the same governed credential workflow from a local sandbox to the cloud without code changes. Attendees will see how this approach helps engineering teams move faster, limits the blast radius of a compromised agent, and gives security teams a clear audit trail. The session covers short-lived credential delivery through the AgentCore gateway and policies that apply consistently from development through production. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.

title: Open source agent observability and evals with AgentCore and Langfuse (sponsored by ClickHouse)
speakers: Marc Klingen (Langfuse (by ClickHouse))
abstract: Production agents need more than infrastructure. They need an open source foundation for understanding behavior, evaluating quality, and improving continuously without sacrificing control of their data. In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse combine secure agent infrastructure with open source observability and evaluation, powered by ClickHouse. See how teams capture OpenTelemetry traces, debug trajectories and tool calls, evaluate production quality, turn failures into datasets, and prevent regressions before deployment. We will share a practical architecture for unifying policy and telemetry across AgentCore, EKS, and other runtimes so teams can ship trustworthy agents faster. This presentation is brought to you by ClickHouse, an AWS Partner.

title: Planning for migrations, and operating databases on AWS with Redgate (sponsored by Red Gate)
services: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS);AWS Transform
speakers: Kellyn Gorman (Redgate); John Martin (Redgate Software)
abstract: Moving a database from on-premises to the cloud is easy to get wrong: undersized instances, surprise costs, unplanned downtime. Join Kellyn and John as we look at Redgate Monitor's new database migration planning feature, designed to help you size, plan, and cost a move with real data instead of guesswork. We will also explore how Redgate Monitor is evolving to support the next generation of database operations, supporting teams who are using AI assistants and Agents who need access to observability data quickly, giving operational staff faster answers and smarter recommendations when managing complex database systems. This presentation is brought to you by Red Gate, an AWS Partner.

title: Post-quantum cryptography tabletop experience
abstract: Quantum computing is advancing—is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence.
