Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Designing Agentic AI Applications
speakers: Avichal Chum (AWS); Viraj Padte (Amazon Web Services); Piyali Kamra (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Ever stared at multiple disconnected systems held together by manual handoffs and thought, "there has to be a better way"? Agentic AI is that better way. In this hands-on Rodeo session, you team up to design an end-to-end agentic solution for a real-world scenario: multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop decision points, and MCP integration. Swap ideas with other teams, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns for turning manual chaos into autonomous workflows. Bring your A-game, the best design rides off with the win.

title: Re-Engineer Enterprise Processes for Agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Camunda)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Daniel Meyer (Camunda)
abstract: Enterprise AI is moving from experimentation to production, but legacy workflows designed without AI in mind keep agents disconnected from the processes, systems, and controls that determine successful business outcomes. Understand why reengineering now matters: organizations that preserve legacy workflows risk slowing AI adoption while others redesign operations for an AI first world. Discover how Camunda ProcessOS works with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to discover, re-engineer, and improve end-to-end processes. See how Camunda’s agentic orchestration combines deterministic controls with dynamic AI agents, human approval, observability, and auditability. Learn why you need to re-engineer now, and stop adding agents to yesterday’s workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Camunda, an AWS Partner.

title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speakers: Drew Curd (Simply Business); Rob Solomon (CrowdStrike)
abstract: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

title: Small Language Models, Total Control: Sovereign AI Agents, Lower Cost (sponsored by Boomi)
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Thomas Benjamin (Boomi); Chris Hallenbeck (Boomi)
abstract: Enterprises are waking up to a hard truth: the AI their business now depends on runs on infrastructure, models, and pricing they don't control. In this session, Boomi's engineering and AI leadership show a different path — AI agents that run anywhere you choose (your Amazon VPC, your data center, behind your firewall) powered by small language models fine-tuned to each agent's job and served entirely on infrastructure you govern. You'll see the full architecture on AWS — Amazon EKS, EC2 GPU instances, Amazon S3, Aurora, MSK, and Amazon Bedrock as a governed escalation path — plus the fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA SFT + DPO), the evaluation gate that decides when a small model is ready, and a live demo of an agent reasoning locally at a fraction of the latency and cost of a frontier LLM. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

title: Token-efficient retrieval for production AI agents (sponsored by Exa)
abstract: Most agent bills aren't driven by the model, they're driven by the context it's given. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This presentation is brought to you by Exa, an AWS Partner.

title: Accelerating Fusion Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS HPC, Analytics, and Agentic AI (sponsored by AMD)
speakers: Manish Amin (AMD); Brody Bassett (Pacific Fusion); Hardeep Sullan (Pacific Fusion); Arijit Choudhury (AWS); Adam Reyes (Pacific Fusion)
abstract: Learn how Pacific Fusion is leveraging AMD EPYC-powered AWS infrastructure to build a scalable platform for high-performance computing, advanced analytics, and agentic AI. By unifying simulation, data processing, and AI-driven research workflows, Pacific Fusion can accelerate scientific discovery while optimizing cost and resource utilization. Discover how AWS elasticity and AMD EPYC performance enable researchers to rapidly scale from compute-intensive simulations to data-rich analytics and intelligent automation, helping transform scientific data into actionable insights and accelerating the path toward commercially viable fusion energy. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: govern agents at enterprise scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
abstract: Enterprises are moving from a handful of agents to hundreds. Without a shared layer for identity, policy, orchestration, and observability, that growth stalls. In this 20-minute launch session, we introduce the Agentic AI Control Plane on AWS: a governed foundation for building, deploying, and running agents across business and IT workflows. See how it handles agent onboarding, guardrails, cost and performance visibility, and human oversight, with a live look at the platform. Built for CIOs, data and AI leaders, and platform and risk teams who need agent fleets to scale safely, with the controls their auditors expect. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI on AWS with Intel® Xeon® 6 (sponsored by Intel)
speakers: Diego Bailon Humpert (Banco BPM); Farid Chalouhi (intel); Mickey Iqbal (AWS)
abstract: Intel and Databricks are collaborating to optimize price-performance for workloads running on AWS. This session covers optimizations for ISVs running Photon/Spark on Databricks leveraging custom Amazon EC2 instances powered by Intel Xeon processors, delivering advanced AI capabilities and high core density. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) with the UK Home Office (sponsored by Capgemini)
abstract: The UK Home Office is tasked with keeping the UK Safe and Prosperous. Capgemini is working with the Home Office to increase effectiveness and efficiency of its digital and cloud services. Key areas include case management, legacy modernization and SDLC efficiency. This is being delivered in collaboration with AWS and Anthropic. Using Claude agents via AWS Bedrock, this capability is forecast to deliver >30% cashable savings compared to existing processes and improve quality by >20% through better informed decisions. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: Agents demand context. Build them a Streamhouse. (sponsored by Confluent)
aoi: Event-Driven Architecture;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI
speakers: Sean Falconer (Confluent)
abstract: Your agents can't act on yesterday's data. In this session, see how to connect streaming events, governed data, and agent orchestration into one production-ready streamhouse architecture on AWS. Learn how to build a complete, performant, and open streamhouse that delivers real-time context, elastic scale, and mission-critical reliability across every cloud and private environment without data silos. You'll leave with practical patterns for moving from brittle data pipelines to AI built on data streams, designed for speed, trust, and scale. This presentation is brought to you by Confluent, an AWS Partner.

title: Automate and Scale Cloud Operations with Purpose-Built AI Agents (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: Engineering teams lose time correlating telemetry, triaging alerts, investigating threats, and turning findings into fixes. This session explores how Datadog’s purpose-built AI agents can reduce that operational burden by applying organizational context and production telemetry to focused developer, SRE, and security workflows. Using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, we’ll examine where agents can improve operational excellence, reliability, security, performance efficiency, and cost optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: AWS Jam: All-in Builder Showdown
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Mohammad Arbabshirani (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Dive deep into AWS with our All-In session — hands-on environments covering AI-powered solutions, DevOps automation, and cloud security. Explore cutting-edge AI services, streamline deployments, and implement security best practices. Challenges are designed for all skill levels, with helpful clues and AWS expert support throughout. Work solo or as a team on real-world scenarios, expand your AWS expertise, and connect with fellow cloud enthusiasts. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Build What’s Next with an AI-Ready Programmable Network (sponsored by Lumen)
speakers: Marc Andre Oriani (Lumen Technology)
abstract: As AI, cloud, and data-intensive applications reshape business, infrastructure must become as dynamic as the workloads it supports. In this session, Lumen explores how programmable networking helps organizations simplify connectivity, improve performance, and securely scale across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Learn how real-time network orchestration gives teams greater agility and control while accelerating AI and modernization initiatives. Through examples, including Lumen’s collaboration with AWS to streamline enterprise connectivity, discover how a programmable network creates the resilient digital foundation needed to build what’s next. This presentation is brought to you by Lumen, an AWS Partner.

title: Cleared for Takeoff Hybrid Observability at the Busiest Airport (sponsored by SolarWinds)
services: Amazon GuardDuty;AWS CloudTrail;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Cedric Reed (City Of Atlanta - Dept Of Aviation); Gregory Fetterhoff (SolarWinds, Inc)
abstract: Managing over a thousand network nodes across terminals, baggage systems, and cloud infrastructure requires more than reactive troubleshooting. Join Cedric Reed, Network Administrator at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and SolarWinds to discover how the world’s busiest airport replaced manual oversight with proactive observability. Learn how unified visibility across on-premises hardware and AWS Cloud eliminates noise, reduces downtime, and keeps critical systems online for millions of daily travelers. Discover how hop-by-hop visualization and real-time telemetry seamlessly monitor a vast network of surveillance systems covering the entire 7-mile campus to optimize operational resilience and passenger safety. This presentation is brought to you by SolarWinds, an AWS Partner.

title: DevOps and Modernization Jam
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Sushma Nagaraj (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Tackle hands-on DevOps environments to improve applications and modernize architectures using multiple AWS services. What are the limitations of the current solution? How can you do it better? Whether you're new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this is your chance to demonstrate and grow your skills. Guided exercises, helpful clues, and AWS expert support throughout. All you need: a laptop, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

title: Elasticsearch - the Search database for Context Engineering and AI (sponsored by Elastic)
abstract: Your agentic applications have an accuracy and cost problem, and it's not your model choice. Sound familiar? If you're a developer trying to get LLMs to work effectively with your business context, this session is for you. Come learn how we rearchitected Elasticsearch as the database of choice for the different data types your enterprise knowledge is buried in — docs, logs, metrics, tickets, sales call transcripts, and more. From foundational innovations like Columnar and VectorDB mode with no ETL, to best-in-class retrieval that combines vector search, Jina embedding models, and native inference, Elastic is the context database for your production needs. Join this session to learn the best practices, from optimizing data preparation to retrieval patterns, to make your agents a production reality. This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

title: Enterprise-Grade Outcomes. Within Reach for Growing Businesses. (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: Chris Wegmann (Accenture); Dusshyant Roy (Accenture)
abstract: Discover how Accenture Edge for AWS helps growing organizations (under $3B in annual revenue) achieve the same transformative outcomes as larger enterprises through pre-built, outcome-driven solutions designed for speed, simplicity, and value. We are taking enterprise-grade talent and tools and making them accessible and approachable. Translation: Big outcomes at lower costs thanks to pre-configured solutions. Hear real examples of customers that accelerated cloud adoption, reduced costs, strengthened security, and modernized faster with Accenture and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
speakers: Matty Stratton (TigerData fka Timescale)
abstract: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.

title: FinOps for AI: Open the black box on AI spend (sponsored by Apptio)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Andrew Midgley (IBM)
abstract: AI spend often arrives as a black box: a rising bill with little clarity into which teams, models or features drove it. In this breakout, learn how Cloudability helps teams apply FinOps discipline to AI on AWS by categorizing costs, connecting spend to business goals and identifying waste. Discover how we turn that visibility into action for AI workloads running on Amazon EKS, improving GPU efficiency, Kubernetes workload right-sizing and application performance. Then apply the same cost discipline to Amazon Bedrock, including smarter provisioned throughput decisions, so teams can explain, defend and optimize AI spend. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.

title: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
speakers: Tatum Tummins (Kion)
abstract: Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it. FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate. This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.

title: From Databases to Agentic AI: Powering Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS (sponsored by AMD)
speakers: Jeremy Girven (AMD); Ray Prado (AMD)
abstract: Today's organizations need infrastructure that can efficiently support everything from mission-critical databases to next-generation AI applications. Join AMD and AWS to explore how customers are leveraging Amazon EC2 instances powered by AMD EPYC processors across Amazon RDS, analytics, Agentic AI, HPC, and cloud-native applications. Learn how AMD-powered AWS infrastructure delivers compelling price-performance, scalability, and operational efficiency while helping organizations accelerate innovation, optimize costs, and meet growing compute demands. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: How Cox Achieved 7x ROI with Agentic AI on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Nova
abstract: Cox Communications partnered with Accenture and Anthropic's Claude on AWS to transform B2B marketing and sales, generating a 7x return on its first-year AI investment. By deploying AI-powered marketing and sales agents across 120 micro-industries and eight customer segments, Cox replaced one-size-fits-all campaigns with personalized engagement at scale. The initiative delivered 55% faster speed to market, a 2-point increase in B2B conversion, 40% higher campaign efficiency, and an 86% reduction in lead management costs while improving data accuracy from 18% to 97%. Today, Cox is operating an end-to-end agentic go-to-market system with human oversight. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: How Iberdrola Increased Marketing Capacity 4x with Agentic AI (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: Xabier Muruaga (Iberdrola); Arturo Negredo (Accenture S.L. Sociedad Unipersonal)
abstract: Iberdrola, a Spanish multinational electric utility company, is transforming marketing with CreatIA, an agentic AI platform co-developed with Accenture and AWS. Facing rising demand for content, faster decisions and accelerated campaign delivery, Iberdrola adopted a new operating model powered by specialized AI agents across the marketing lifecycle. CreatIA unifies market intelligence, insights generation, content creation, validation and campaign activation in a single enterprise platform. The solution has reduced time spent analyzing and processing information by 80%, accelerated strategic decision making by 40%, increased creative production capacity by up to four times, and reduced content production costs by 60%. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: How SoCalGas Is Using Agentic AI for SAP Migration Hypercare on AWS with Accenture (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: Ben Gordon (Sempra Energy); Brent Shaffer (Accenture)
abstract: SoCalGas is migrating its decades-old Customer Information System to SAP IS-U, where hypercare is a critical phase for customer and regulatory impacts. Traditional command centers require teams to manually correlate signals across ServiceNow, Azure DevOps, dashboards, logs, and staffing systems, which may slow response times. SoCalGas worked with Accenture on a multi-agent AI command center using Amazon Bedrock. A Commander agent is designed to orchestrate Platform Health, Business KPI, Knowledge, and Situational Awareness agents, while every recommendation is intended to be citation-grounded and human-supervised. Learn about SoCalGas’s project experience using agentic AI to unify operational intelligence in a mission-critical utility environment. References are for informational purposes only and do not constitute endorsement, recommendation, warranty, certification or representation. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: Make AMD Your Default on AWS: Efficient EC2 for the Agentic AI Era with EPYC (sponsored by AMD)
speakers: Madhusudhan Rangarajan (AMD); Stuart Bunyan (LSEG); Mike Thompson (AMD)
abstract: What if you could run agentic AI for over 30% less on Amazon EC2—within the contracts you already have? As autonomous agents call inference models and tools, compute demand explodes and the CPU-to-GPU ratio inverts from 1:8 to 8:1, making processor choice the defining ROI decision. This session proves how 5th-Gen AMD EPYC "Turin" on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, delivering >30% OpEx savings you can redirect from IT overhead into AI budgets. Partners see how MAP-aligned migration funding, POC support, and co-sell turn efficient, variety-ready AMD infrastructure on AWS into bigger, faster customer wins. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.

title: Optimizing Kubernetes in the Age of AI (sponsored by Zesty)
abstract: Agentic development dramatically reduces the cost of writing code, but it hasn’t removed the cost of operating it. Infrastructure teams are now responsible for the cost, performance, and reliability of workloads they didn’t build. In this session, we'll explore how these shifts are changing Kubernetes optimization. We'll discuss why CPU, Memory, and GPU resources are often miscalibrated, why native tools like HPA and Karpenter don't solve resource inefficiencies, and how platform teams can maintain cost accountability without slowing developer velocity. You'll leave with practical strategies to continuously optimize resources, improve utilization, and keep Kubernetes infrastructure cost-efficient as AI adoption scales. This presentation is brought to you by Zesty, an AWS Partner.

title: Optimizing SAP RISE for Cost and Scale with Intel (sponsored by Intel)
speakers: Emanuele Baldassarre (Accenture); Caitlin Anderson (Intel Corporation)
abstract: Discover how Intel's custom SAP-certified Intel® Xeon® 6 processor, exclusively available on AWS, transforms and accelerates your SAP RISE journey. Engineered to deliver the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel cloud processors, this powerful solution unlocks up to 50% higher SAPS performance. Whether migrating, consolidating, or scaling SAP workloads, Intel Xeon 6 on AWS empowers organizations to optimize costs, enhance efficiency, and maximize their SAP RISE investment — driving faster, smarter, and more cost-effective outcomes for modern enterprise demands. This presentation is brought to you by Intel, an AWS Partner.

title: Powering Interactive Agents with Live Context (sponsored by Materialize)
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK);Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
speakers: Nate Stewart (Materialize)
abstract: How do you keep an agent's understanding of the world fresh enough for it to act on? Interactive agents need current context about the customers, orders, inventory, accounts, and other entities they reason about. But assembling that context from constantly changing operational systems is complex, forcing teams to choose between stale data, expensive recomputation, or complex pipelines. This talk will show how to build continuously updated context in SQL that is trustworthy enough for agents to rely upon. You'll learn how to transform operational data into agent-ready representations, keep attributes and relationships up to date as the underlying data changes, and propagate those changes to search indexes and embeddings when needed. Attend if you're deploying AI agents to production and want to give them fresher, more complete context and tighten their read-act-react loop. This presentation is brought to you by Materialize, an AWS Partner.

title: Ring's Security Evolution: From Doorbell to Enterprise Platform (sponsored by Ring LLC)
services: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams;AWS Lambda;AWS Marketplace
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Harish Komaragiri (Amazon)
abstract: Ring started with a simple mission: make neighborhoods safer with a video doorbell. That mission has scaled — from 100M+ residential cameras to SMB storefronts and jobsites with mobile security towers, to an AI-powered Appstore unlocking entirely new use cases across elder care, workforce analytics, and beyond. Now, Ring is making its boldest leap yet: a cloud-native enterprise platform built on AWS, combining video management, intelligent alerting, third-party camera ingestion, and access control. Join this lightning round to trace Ring's evolution and see what's next for enterprise security. This presentation is brought to you by Ring LLC, an AWS Partner.

title: Self-Healing Enterprise-Wipro & AWS Moving from System of Record to System of Action (sponsored by Wipro)
speakers: Saurabh Vadhera (WIPRO)
abstract: For decades, enterprises have invested in technologies that digitize, automate and optimize work. Yet when disruptions occur, decisions still depend on emails, escalations, meetings and manual coordination across teams. The next phase of enterprise transformation is about creating enterprises that can sense change, assess impact, coordinate responses and drive outcomes at speed. Wipro and AWS demonstrate how intelligent agents, enterprise systems and human expertise come together to create a Self-Healing Enterprise, one that can proactively identify issues, orchestrate actions across functions and continuously adapt while keeping humans accountable for critical business decisions. Through a realistic business disruption scenario, see how organizations can evolve beyond visibility and automation towards systems of action that improve resilience, responsiveness and operational efficiency. This presentation is brought to you by Wipro, an AWS Partner.

title: Shipping AI Code with Confidence Using Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro (sponsored by Dynatrace)
speakers: Jason Ostroski (Dynatrace LLC); Angel Marchena (Western Governors University)
abstract: See how Western Governors University uses Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro to deliver AI-generated code with greater confidence. By combining live production intelligence with AI-assisted development, teams can provide agents with real runtime context, detect issues quickly, and create evidence-backed GitHub Issues for rapid remediation. Learn how Bluebox supports the software lifecycle before, during, and after deployment, helping teams validate fixes, reduce risk, and accelerate software delivery. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

title: Skip Refactoring and Simplify Operations with Nutanix on AWS (sponsored by Nutanix)
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS GovCloud (US)
speakers: Jeff Adams (Nutanix)
abstract: Cloud migrations often stall when rewriting applications takes too long. As projects drag on, organizations are left managing a fragmented, expensive mix of on-premises and cloud silos. Nutanix Cloud Clusters on AWS addresses this friction by establishing a single control plane and a consistent operating model across environments. In this session, learn how to move workloads to AWS bare metal quickly without refactoring. Discover how to eliminate management silos, accelerate migration timelines, and simplify hybrid cloud operations. This presentation is brought to you by Nutanix, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop paying for idle GPUs on Amazon EKS (sponsored by Apptio)
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA)
speakers: Andrew Midgley (IBM); Joe Dahlquist (IBM)
abstract: AI workloads can consume millions of dollars in infrastructure before anyone notices whether they're being used efficiently. GPUs sit idle, clusters become overprovisioned, and engineering teams struggle to balance performance with rapidly growing costs. In this session, learn how engineering teams running Amazon EKS can identify wasted GPU capacity, understand the true cost of AI workloads, and automate optimization without sacrificing application performance. We'll share practical techniques to improve utilization, reduce waste, and optimize AI infrastructure at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.

title: Taming AI Token Costs and Security Risks with Cribl and AWS (sponsored by Cribl)
speakers: Bill Emmett (Cribl, Inc.); Joshua Andre (Hubspot)
abstract: Govern enterprise AI: Optimize costs, control prompt risks, and gain visibility with Cribl and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cribl, an AWS Partner.

title: Teaching agents to pay with Stripe (sponsored by Stripe)
speakers: Ben Smith (Stripe)
abstract: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

title: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
speakers: ryan ries (Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
abstract: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. This session breaks down why that happens and what to do about it. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS (sponsored by Deloitte)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Quicksight Q;Amazon Quick Suite
speakers: Mohamad Said (Deloitte)
abstract: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
speakers: Amit Kinha (DoIT International Ltd)
abstract: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.

title: When Telemetry Steers the Robot: Observability for Physical AI
speakers: Noam Levy (groundcover)
abstract: Path Robotics is pushing physical AI beyond the lab into tough industrial environments. Its Obsidian AI model autonomously welds production parts, while Rove brings that intelligence into shipyards on a Boston Dynamics quadruped. When AI moves into the physical world, observability becomes mission-critical. Built on AWS, Path needs visibility into AI applications, robot motion, and welding arcs, where traditional observability tools fall short. In this session, Path Robotics and groundcover share how they replaced legacy SaaS observability with a BYOC architecture spanning commercial and sovereign environments. groundcover’s eBPF sensor delivers instant visibility into agentic applications and field robotics, providing critical production context.

title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps (sponsored by ManageEngine)
speakers: Ananthkumar KS (Zoho Corporation Pvt. Ltd.)
abstract: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment. This presentation is brought to you by ManageEngine, an AWS Partner.

title: AWS GameDay - Platform Engineering & Cloud-Native Architecture ft. Red Hat
speakers: Joseph O'Such (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join us for a collaborative learning exercise to develop practical skills in platform engineering and cloud-native architecture on AWS. Dive into a live AWS environment where you will build and operate internal developer platforms, design cloud-native applications, and implement container orchestration at scale. Build skills in containerization, container orchestration platforms, service mesh, platform APIs, and self-service infrastructure as you construct golden paths that empower development teams. Face scenarios that challenge your ability to balance developer experience with operational governance! Whether you are a seasoned platform engineer or just exploring cloud-native patterns, this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with Red Hat. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Agentic AI & AI Application Monitoring ft. New Relic
speakers: Lillian Pham (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative learning exercise to build practical skills in deploying and monitoring AI-powered applications on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll engineer production-ready AI systems and ensure reliability through comprehensive observability. Leverage Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock Agentcore, foundation models, AI agents, prompt engineering, model evaluation, and ML pipeline monitoring as you build and operate AI workloads end-to-end. Face challenges demanding both engineering excellence and operational awareness for AI systems in production! Whether you're an experienced ML engineer or just starting to build with AI, this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with New Relic. Walk-ups welcome.

title: Agentic AI Jam - sponsored by Nvidia
speakers: Varad Ram (AWS); Nir Pilo (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of four or join a team and meet new friends in the session. Are you ready to build and deploy agentic AI solutions on AWS? We provide hands-on environments where you can architect intelligent and production-ready agents. How do you orchestrate multi-step agent reasoning with tool use? How can you design agents that plan, act, and self-correct autonomously? Whether you are new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this Jam is your chance to demonstrate your skills and learn new ones. Structured for all experience levels, our sessions include guided exercises, helpful clues, and support from AWS experts to accelerate your agentic AI expertise. Team up, compete with others, climb the leaderboard, and win prizes based on speed and accuracy. With expert guidance every step of the way, all you need is a computer, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.

title: AWS Jam: All-in Builder Showdown - sponsored by Vonage
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Mohammad Arbabshirani (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Tackle AI, DevOps, and security scenarios across AWS services - including a sponsored challenge from Vonage to add real-time voice, video, and messaging to applications using Vonage communications APIs. Challenges suit all skill levels, with AWS expert guidance and helpful clues throughout. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: DevOps and Modernization Jam – sponsored by LaunchDarkly
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Jerad Engebreth (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Tackle hands-on DevOps scenarios to modernize architectures and implement best practices - including a sponsored challenge from LaunchDarkly to ship safely with feature flags and progressive delivery. Whether you're new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, guided exercises and AWS experts support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: 15 Minutes Is Too Late: Stop AWS Intrusions with CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speakers: Vinayak Shastri (Crowdstrike Inc)
abstract: In seconds, adversaries can move from a stolen credential to the AWS control plane, workloads, and Kubernetes before the SOC even begins triage. In this session, see how CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security turns a complex AWS attack into one high-confidence incident. Follow an end-to-end intrusion as adversary-informed correlated detections connect identity, control-plane and workload activity; AI-based anomaly detection exposes behavior static rules miss; and Real-Time CDR analyzes AWS activity as it streams in. Then watch CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent investigate, enrich and prioritize the intrusion, staging rapid response actions for human analyst approval before it becomes a breach. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

title: 1 Customer, 1 Context, From all the Channels: (sponsored by Redis)
speakers: Jon Fritz (Redis (Redis Labs)); Toshish Jawale (Invoca (fka RingRevenue, Inc.))
abstract: Join Toshish Jawale, Head of AI Engineering at Invoca, to learn how his team is putting context at the center of the business’ customer journeys. Hear how Invoca and Redis are delivering real-time, mutli-source context for Invoca’s agents, how they’re helping customers interact with their brand in exciting ways, and how they’re delivering complete pictures of user brand experiences. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

title: 20-minute guide to automating post-migration validation
abstract: Migration teams spend weeks per wave coordinating connectivity tests, performance comparisons, application health checks, and compliance reviews across disconnected tools. This lightning talk examines how to move post-deployment validation from a manual, multi-tool process into an integrated part of the migration workflow. You will learn approaches for automating infrastructure checks at deployment time, incorporating Well-Architected compliance into wave execution, and running day-one modernization actions so workloads land production-ready. Ideal for migration engineers and cloud architects managing large rehost and network modernization programs.

title: 3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response (sponsored by PagerDuty)
speakers: Samrat Ghosh (Liveramp); Alice McElroy (Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.)
abstract: Every SRE knows the pattern: an alert fires, and the next 20 minutes disappear into triage before you've even confirmed what's broken. Context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and tribal knowledge, and much of incident response is just reconstructing what already happened. This session explores how autonomous operations changes that story. PagerDuty’s SRE Agent investigates before a human is even involved and proposes fixes you simply approve. See it firsthand through PD Labs, a hands-on site for trying autonomous workflows, and SRE Workbench, launching in early access, where humans, agents, and automation meet in order to investigate, diagnose, and remediate issues. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

title: 3-step blueprint for scaling AI with a modern enterprise core (sponsored by IBM)
speakers: Laxman Challa (Southwest Gas); Kristen Bennie (Barclays); Dan Kusel (IBM); Brian Bohan (AWS)
abstract: AI is a catalyst for growth and innovation, yet only 17% of AI initiatives reach full-scale production. Join IBM and AI trailblazers to explore the three-step blueprint for scaling AI on AWS: modernizing the enterprise core across applications, data and infrastructure; fostering a culture that moves innovation forward; and putting digital labor to work in real workflows. Discover how IBM Consulting helps organizations move beyond isolated use cases, accelerate ideas into production and make AI work inside the enterprise, not around it. This presentation is brought to you by IBM, an AWS Partner.

title: 4 primitives to evaluate your on-call agent's autonomy (sponsored by Resolve AI)
speakers: Steven Karis (Resolve AI (clouddatalabs.io)); Varun Krovvidi (Resolve AI)
abstract: AI that handles on-call autonomously requires agents to take on alert triage, investigations, acting on production, and learning from what happened. Autonomy progresses unevenly as investigations are bottlenecked on quality while actions are limited by trust. In this session we will walk through how we build each primitive of our autonomous agents at Resolve AI, and how we help engineering teams handle on-call and incident resolutions. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

title: 50k daily iOS builds with virtualization on Amazon EC2 Mac
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Kyle Krall (Amazon Web Services); Francisco Costa (Critical Techworks, SA); Jonas França (Critical Techworks)
abstract: A leading automotive manufacturer migrated its CI/CD infrastructure from on-premises to AWS to support over 130,000 daily builds (50k + iOS) across 1,300+ microservices. To accelerate iOS mobile app development, the team adopted Amazon EC2 Mac instances with virtualization using OpenAI Tart virtualization toolset, enabling ephemeral macOS VMs that boot in seconds with pre-configured toolchains. This approach reduced average build times from 90 to 35 minutes, a 61% improvement, while eliminating hardware management overhead. The platform now scales to 50,000+ daily iOS builds, serving 3,000+ developers with cost-optimized, reliable, and secure pipelines across hundreds of AWS accounts worldwide.

title: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
speakers: David Ugarte (AWS)
abstract: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. AZ spread off means one zone failure takes your service down. Short health check grace periods kill containers that are still starting. Disabled circuit breakers let bad deploys roll forward across every task. Default dependency timeouts turn one slow call into a cascading outage. Placement constraints pack tasks onto too few hosts. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.

title: 5 Questions Terraform, OpenTofu, and CloudFormation Can't Answer (sponsored by Spacelift, Inc.)
speakers: Jonah Kowall (Spacelift)
abstract: Every infrastructure change is one run: code, an engine, a plan, an apply. That run is still a wall of unstructured log text, and the questions about your estate go unanswered. Five to ask of your IaC: Did Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, or Ansible run it, and does it matter? Where does the time go, and can OpenTelemetry tracing show you? What happens outside the engine: providers, state, policy-as-code, drift, queue time? What about unmanaged resources, the half of your AWS account no run ever touched? Who gets self-service, and can an AI agent be trusted with an apply? This presentation is brought to you by Spacelift, Inc., an AWS Partner.

title: 5 steps to faster data center exits with AWS Transform
speakers: Jonathan Shapiro-Ward (AWS); Ahuva Hazan-Fuchs (AWS)
abstract: 70% of applications still sit on-premises, and the longer they stay, the more tech debt compounds. AWS Transform uses agentic AI to compress the entire data center exit journey from assessment through execution. Start with AI-powered discovery that right-sizes thousands of servers, compares cost scenarios, and builds a business case that gets executive buy-in in days. Move into automated wave planning and landing zone deployment. Then see how network architectures convert into production-ready VPCs and workloads rehost to Amazon EC2 at scale. We follow one customer's real timeline from plan to exit and unpack what made it work.

title: Accelerate application development with Amazon ECS Express Mode
speakers: Jay Russo (Amazon Web Services); Mike Brandin (Meta); Mike Rizzo (AWS)
abstract: What if deploying a containerized application on Amazon ECS required just your code and a few configuration choices? Amazon ECS Express Mode makes that possible by handling observability, networking, and security out of the box. In this session, learn how Express Mode accelerates development for individual developers and platform teams without sacrificing control. Discover practical techniques to optimize your workflows, enhance reliability, and reduce operational overhead. Leave with actionable strategies to increase development velocity using the latest Amazon ECS innovations.

title: Accelerate data migrations with AWS DataSync at any scale
speakers: Sravan Rachiraju (Amazon Web Services); Tugba Goksel (AWS)
abstract: Long migration windows, limited visibility, and complex source environments can slow your data migrations to AWS, whether you are transferring data from on-premises file servers, Hadoop clusters, or multicloud object storage. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts show you how AWS DataSync Enhanced mode's parallel pipeline simultaneously lists, prepares, transfers, and verifies your data to dramatically reduce those timelines. You will learn how to configure for maximum throughput, design endpoint connectivity for secure and efficient data movement, and use richer metrics and monitoring to gain full visibility into your transfer pipeline.

title: Accelerate intelligent document processing with Amazon Textract
speakers: Keith Mascarenhas (Amazon Web Services); Wrick Talukdar (AWS); Sneha Choudhury (Amazon)
abstract: Accelerate intelligent document processing with Amazon Textract Abstract - Building custom extraction pipelines on foundation models is powerful but expensive to maintain. Textract Intelligence gives you the same GenAI flexibility as a managed service: custom-field extraction, document classification, splitting, and summarization, all backed by purpose-built OCR instead of a vision model guessing at pixels. In this session we compare approaches head-to-head on accuracy, latency, and cost, then show how 40-language support and trustworthy confidence scores close the gaps that push teams to DIY solutions.

title: Accelerate legacy Java modernization with custom AI-powered transformations
speakers: Rachel Yen (Amazon); Ritik Khatwani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Legacy applications on outdated frameworks and deprecated runtimes represent a growing modernization challenge. In this workshop, use AWS Transform custom to build and execute transformations that accelerate Java modernization at scale. You'll define transformation rules using natural language and code examples, execute multi-step upgrades (Java 8 to 21, Spring Boot 2 to 3, Jakarta EE), refine quality through the agentic AI feedback loop, validate with built-in testing, and run campaigns across multiple repositories. You'll leave with reusable transformation definitions you can apply to your own Java codebases. Laptop required.

title: Accelerate Physical AI development with NVIDIA on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Shaun Kirby (AWS); Abhishek Srivastav (AWS)
abstract: Physical AI is reshaping manufacturing, robotics, and autonomous systems, but realizing that potential requires robust infrastructure and purpose-built tools. AWS and NVIDIA have partnered to simplify the entire Physical AI development lifecycle: from synthetic data generation and model training through sim-to-real validation and hardware-in-loop testing. In this session, discover how the Physical AI Toolchain from AWS provides access to AWS managed infrastructure and NVIDIA’s foundation models and training applications to accelerate every stage of development, reduce time-to-market, and optimize resource utilization across your pipeline.

title: Accelerate your agentic AI mission from prototype to ATO in weeks
speakers: David Schatzman (Amazon Web Services); Shawn Asfeld (AWS)
abstract: Agencies, the industrial base, and technology partners want agentic AI in production, but few have navigated the path across classification levels. In this chalk talk, learn real-world patterns for taking Bedrock agents and foundation models from prototype to authorized production across commercial and AWS Government Regions (FedRAMP, DoD CSP SRG IL2/4/5, classified) on one portable security baseline, without a rebuild; what is authorized at each level; the tradeoffs at each level; and ATO strategies that turn guardrails, observability, and evaluations into control evidence your assessor can use. Guardrails and audit-trail demos. Ideal for architects and security leads.

title: Accelerating AI adoption and realized value with Amazon Quick
speakers: John Brock (AWS); NEAL CAULEY (Amazon Web Services); Stefan Schulz (3M)
abstract: Most AI investments stall because leaders hand off adoption instead of leading it. 3M did the opposite. It put Amazon Quick in the hands of its top 75 executives first, so the people who set strategy saw the value before they asked their teams to adopt it. With governed access to enterprise data, senior leaders now use Quick to make decisions faster, bring their teams onto shared workflows and turn AI from a personal tool into a team-wide advantage. Learn what executive sponsorship changed, what leaders gained in speed and focus and how to build the same momentum in your organization.

title: Accelerating AI inference with Amazon EBS
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Sooraj Prasannan (Amazon); Joe Stubenrauch (AWS)
abstract: As organizations optimize AI workflows to keep GPUs highly utilized, Amazon EBS plays a distinct role in the AI pipeline where key business data is close to compute. In this session, learn how EBS minimizes pre-staging time for model weights with low latency, accelerates data preparation and checkpoints on high-performance EBS volumes, and reduces response times by serving vector embeddings at sub-millisecond latencies during inferencing, all while delivering elasticity and configurability in storage and performance. Leave with architecture patterns, volume configurations, and a framework for extending your storage architecture with EBS for AI/ML workloads.

title: Accelerating AI-powered business transformation and SAP Modernization
speakers: Tim Speicher (MSA The Safety Company)
abstract: The legacy ERP systems that once drove competitive advantage now creates technical debt and blocks innovation and yet modernizing it remains complex, costly, and risky. In this panel, discover how AWS AI services are changing the economics of SAP modernization, making it possible to transform business processes by through AI-powered automations, while delivering breakthrough performance, cost savings and innovation.

title: Accelerating Applications with Data on AWS Marketplace
abstract: Every enterprise building AI applications hits the same wall: procuring third-party data and licensed content takes months of negotiations, bespoke contracts, and custom integrations. In this session, learn how you can more easily discover, subscribe to, and access the datasets and content your applications and AI workloads demand.

title: Accelerating semiconductor design, simulation and verification on AWS
speakers: Syam Parvathaneni (Marvell Semiconductor, Inc.); Gautham Panth (Amazon)
abstract: EDA workflows demand different compute across frontend, backend, and production phases. This session covers how AWS EC2 instances map to each design phase. Learn how to select instances for throughput-heavy frontend simulation versus memory-intensive backend verification, and hear how ISVs are qualifying tools on AWS Graviton and other CPU processors to unlock better price-performance for chip design workload.

title: Accelerating with NVIDIA Omniverse: VW’s Battery Manufacturing Digital Twin (sponsored by NVIDIA)
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon FSx for Lustre;Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Joerg Clobes (Volkswagen AG); Martin Jaster (Volkswagen Group Components)
abstract: Deloitte helped Volkswagen Group Components design and deploy a cloud-native, AI-ready digital twin on AWS, powered by NVIDIA Omniverse and the OpenUSD standard, for the GS7 battery production environment. By consolidating fragmented factory data — CAD models, robot programs, camera configurations, and defect imagery — into a photorealistic, simulation-ready scene on AWS, the team enabled virtual commissioning, synthetic inspection data generation, and earlier production validation. The result is a reusable, scalable platform built on AWS infrastructure and NVIDIA's industrial metaverse stack that reduces physical trial effort, accelerates line ramp-up, and creates a foundation for AI-driven quality inspection at scale. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: A closer look at AWS Lambda durable functions
speakers: Eric Johnson (Amazon)
abstract: Lambda durable functions let you write reliable, long-running workflows as sequential code. We start with how durable execution works: checkpointing, replay-based recovery, and the programming model. Next, we explore production patterns including sagas, fan-out/fan-in, and human-in-the-loop waits. Finally, we cover observability, a decision framework to help you choose when to use durable functions versus AWS Step Functions, and operational considerations like concurrency, cost, and versioning.

title: A day in the life of a Serverless builder
speakers: Mohammed Atiq (Amazon Web Services); Sean Kendall (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this code talk, follow a Serverless application from first line of code to production deployment, all live. Start with an AI coding agent generating infrastructure and function scaffolding, iterate locally with hot reload, deploy in one command, then debug a failing request by tracing it across Lambda, EventBridge, and DynamoDB using native OpenTelemetry. Along the way, see how recent Serverless launches change the workflow: faster deploys, built-in observability, and simplified local testing. No slides, no diagrams. Just a terminal, an editor, and the workflow a Serverless developer uses in 2026.

title: A Day Without Handoffs: Telecom Operations With Amazon Quick
abstract: See how telecom employees use Amazon Quick to handle billing disputes, automatically address network issues, and manage service requests from a single workspace. Pulled from real-world use cases at telecom companies around the world, these demos pull context from OSS/BSS, run complex workflows, and close the loop without handing off to another team!

title: A DevOps Approach to Recover at Scale from Disaster or Ransomware
services: AWS Backup;AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery;AWS Lambda
speakers: Samantha Eliot (Commvault)
abstract: Recovering your cloud workload completely after a regional event or ransomware attack is not a checklist; it demands a culture of resilience that turns individual craft into reliable recovery. That culture is built through DevOps. Clear communication, team empowerment, and frequent experimentation and measurement are what separate teams that recover from teams that hope. This session covers the technical requirements for recovering cloud workloads at scale, and the DevOps practices that make those requirements actually work under pressure. You'll leave with practical knowledge to drive full recovery in the face of the worst disasters.

title: Adopt evolving Amazon DynamoDB resiliency design patterns
speakers: John Terhune (Amazon Web Services); Jason Hunter (Amazon)
abstract: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. Learn how to use the global tables architecture with specific metrics and thresholds that drive effective failover decisions, as well as DR patterns that achieve low RTO and RPO without global tables overhead. Through whiteboard discussion, explore a variety of resilient DynamoDB workload solutions for specific use cases, including incremental export for undoing bad writes, which is faster and less disruptive than a full PITR table restore, approaches to protect against ransomware and data destruction, and cross-account table migration strategies.

title: Advanced AWS network security: defending against emerging threats
services: Amazon Route 53;AWS Firewall Manager;AWS Network Firewall
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response
speakers: Lawton Pittenger (Amazon Web Services); Brian Westmoreland (AWS)
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, master AWS network security techniques using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Gain practical experience configuring URL category filtering to detect unauthorized AI service usage, and explore recent feature improvements for container workload protection and advanced DNS-layer defenses. Through real-world scenarios, you'll implement IDS/IPS filtering, east-west traffic controls, and domain-based policies using fully managed AWS services. Leave equipped to build resilient network defenses that address both traditional and emerging threats.

title: Advanced data modeling for Amazon ElastiCache
speakers: Yaron Sananes (Amazon); Kevin McGehee (Amazon)
abstract: This session delves into the intricacies of Amazon ElastiCache data modeling using the purpose-built Valkey data types to optimize application performance and scalability. Explore the use of strings, sets, sorted sets, hashes, bitmaps, and geospatial indexes to model complex relationships and solve use cases such as caching, session store, feature store, real-time analytics, geospatial applications, and rate limiters.

title: Advanced data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: Jason Hunter (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB is a popular choice for modern applications because it’s a serverless database that provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Optimizing your usage of DynamoDB requires a different approach to data modeling than traditional relational databases. In this session, explore advanced techniques to help you get the most out of DynamoDB. Learn how to “think in DynamoDB” by learning the DynamoDB foundations and principles for data modeling. Further, learn practical strategies and DynamoDB features to handle difficult use cases in your application.

title: Advanced S3 performance engineering: From multipart to resilience
speakers: Mark Twomey (Amazon Web Services); Bob Holmes (Amazon)
abstract: Master advanced Amazon S3 performance optimization techniques across storage classes, including S3 Standard for general purpose storage and S3 Express One Zone for the highest performance needs. This expert-level workshop focuses on implementing sophisticated data transfer patterns using multipart uploads and Transfer Manager. Design and deploy resilient applications with advanced retry strategies and robust error handling mechanisms. Through technical exercises, build high-performance solutions for large-scale data transfers across different S3 storage classes. Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

title: Advanced security patterns on Amazon S3
speakers: Kavitha Viswanathan (Amazon Web Services); Mourya Gudladona (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon S3 security settings and access controls suit virtually any workload, but as data estates grow to millions of buckets across organizational boundaries, standard policy approaches hit limits. In this chalk talk, equip yourself with proven patterns for managing access at scale: optimizing policy evaluation with access points and access grants, scaling beyond IAM policy limits with cross-account structures, implementing attribute-based controls that adapt as teams and datasets grow, and securing your data lake perimeter with resource control policies. Join the S3 security team for a structured discussion of the patterns that solve the hardest multi-account access problems at scale.

title: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
speakers: Vivek Mishra (Amazon); Fathima Kamal (Amazon)
abstract: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.

title: Advanced VPC design and new capabilities
speakers: Dave DeRicco (AWS); Andrew Gray (AWS)
abstract: Amazon VPC is a foundational service on AWS, giving you control over your virtual networking environment. Every year, AWS makes updates to Amazon VPC to help improve functionality, security, and usability. In this session, learn about the latest updates to Amazon VPC and how you can use them to enhance your current architectures.

title: Advancing the Mission with AI and HPC Supercomputing Pods on AWS
speakers: Nicci Neal (AWS); J. Lowell Wofford (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Cloud supercomputing has become a technology imperative for American competitiveness. In this session, discover how AWS's up to $50B investment in U.S. Federal Supercomputing on AWS promotes rapid innovation for national security, defense, weather, and research. Learn how our new AI and HPC Supercomputing Pod on AWS delivers a fundamentally new supercomputing model, and how AI and HPC are converging to elevate mission outcomes. Ideal for mission owners, architects, and tech leaders.

title: Aflac’s Modernization journey to a resilient and innovative future (sponsored by Kyndryl)
speakers: DJ Goldsworthy (Aflac); Tohru Futami (Aflac Life Insurance Japan Ltd.); Jamie Rutledge (Kyndryl)
abstract: Modernizing critical systems is never just about technology. In this executive panel, leaders from Aflac, Kyndryl, and AWS share the real-world experience behind Aflac’s transformation journey, from overcoming operational challenges and reducing downtime risk to enabling future innovation & continuous modernization. Learn how a strong customer-partner relationship helped balance transformation with business continuity, security, and regulatory requirements. Gain insights into managing large-scale transformation, avoiding common pitfalls, and building a roadmap that delivers measurable business value while preparing for the next generation of cloud and AI-driven innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Kyndryl, an AWS Partner.

title: After the Agents Write the Code: A Field Report From 100 Million Code Reviews (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
speakers: David Loker (CodeRabbit Inc.)
abstract: What does it take to move from human-centered software development to fully agentic development, so you can ship dramatically faster without sacrificing quality or security? More than 2 million times a week, CodeRabbit reviews a change before it merges, whoever or whatever wrote it. From where we sit, we see teams solving agentic coding, but not yet agentic shipping. Now that code is cheap to write, four things have become bottlenecks: review, understanding, prioritization, and security. CodeRabbit hit all four and cleared them, which is how it ships 10x more software without adding engineering headcount. David Loker, VP of Applied AI, shares the four practices that helped, how roles and workflows changed, and why a team has to build trust to ship fast. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Meets ‘Human-Guided-Autonomy’ (sponsored by Terra)
abstract: AI is accelerating how fast code ships and how fast attackers find exploitable weaknesses, and annual pentests cannot keep pace. This session looks at what it takes to make security validation genuinely continuous rather than just more frequent, tracking what changed instead of retesting everything from scratch. Self-driving cars, robotic surgery, and other sensitive actions all became viable the same way: not by removing the human, but by defining exactly which actions the machine takes on its own and which ones need a hand on the controls. This talk will cover the delegate balance between autonomy, safety and control in Offensive Security. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Meets the Line-of-Business Buyer
speakers: Shreyans Gautam (Amazon); Usha Rao (AWS)
abstract: Budget authority is migrating from CIOs to line-of-business leaders - CFOs, Chief Medical Officers, Heads of Manufacturing - who buy outcomes, not infrastructure. At the same time, agentic AI is making it possible to automate entire business processes end-to-end, not just assist them. The partners who win are the ones who can connect these two shifts: framing autonomous agents as measurable business outcomes (revenue acceleration, cost compression, speed-to-market) in the language LOB leaders understand.

title: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS (sponsored by ScaleOps)
speakers: Gilad Elyashar (ScaleOps)
abstract: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself. This presentation is brought to you by ScaleOps, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic development with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
speakers: Matyas Boros (AWS); Momo Kornher (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI coding agents can write application logic, but can they provision your infrastructure too? In this chalk talk, explore AWS Cloud Development Kit's (AWS CDK) latest capabilities—Mixins, the CDK Toolkit Library, and programmatic synth/deploy APIs—make CDK a first-class target for agentic workflows. See how agents reason about constructs, compose infrastructure from natural-language intent, and validate results before deployment. We'll discuss patterns that work, guardrails that keep agents safe, and where human judgment still matters. Bring your questions—this is an interactive session for anyone curious about the intersection of AI agents and infrastructure as code.

title: Agentic-Led Modernization: First Movers' Winning Formula with AWS Transform
speakers: Joe Lan (Amazon Web Services); Sabeena Irani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Continuous modernization isn't optional — it's the engine of speed and competitive advantage. In this session, hear what early-adopter AWS Partners discovered building on AWS Transform, how composability lets them embed their own IP while harnessing AWS's customer reach, funding, and brand, and where the roadmap

title: Agentic Modernization with AWS Transform
speakers: Paul Colmer (AWS)
abstract: AWS Transform orchestrates AI agents that analyze, refactor, and convert legacy applications without manual line-by-line rewrites. In this bootcamp, set modernization objectives, let AI agents decompose and transform .NET Framework code to cross-platform .NET on Linux, then migrate a SQL Server database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Practice agentic assessment, wave planning, code transformation, and schema conversion end to end.

title: Agentic platform design engineering: scaling AI agents across the enterprise.
speakers: Rajeswari Malladi (Amazon Web Services); Manuj Arora (Amazon)
abstract: Your teams are building AI agents in every line of business and also using third-party agents. How do you evolve them into an enterprise agentic platform where you know what exists, reuse it instead of rebuilding, keep it secure, and control what agents spend? This hands-on workshop applies agentic platform design engineering for enterprises. Learn how AWS Agent Registry and an open-source registry let teams discover and reuse agents. Secure cross-account calls with short-lived tokens, trace each request end to end, and let agents pay for data within limits they can't override. Leave with a blueprint for your platform.

title: Agentic Powered AWS Frontier Agents
speakers: Jonathan Dion (AWS)
abstract: Application failures and security vulnerabilities demand fast answers to reduce downtime. In this bootcamp, learn how to setup AWS DevOps Agent and automate investigation failures through logs, metrics, and code changes, then generate remediation plans. Learn how to use AWS Security Agent to configure domain-scoped penetration tests, monitor real-time execution, and interpret severity-rated findings. Gain hands-on experience with two agents that compress hours of investigation into minutes.

title: Agentic Process Transformation at Enterprise Scale
speakers: Mark Mac Ewen (AWS)
abstract: Your customers don't need another automation tool, they need the leap forward they're actually looking for with AI. Agentic Process Transformation (APT) is the framework partners use to help customers move past isolated task automation and into enterprise-wide process reinvention: redesigning entire processes from the ground up to grow revenue and improve the bottom line at a scale automation alone can't reach. We'll share how to spot these transformation opportunities and the architectural patterns that turn them into production solutions. Leave with a concrete strategy for helping your customers make that leap today.

title: Agentic Selling: Scaling Revenue through Expertise on Demand
speakers: Aaron Barton (Amazon Web Services); Prerit Panwar (Amazon Web Services); Simone Thompson (ThoughtWorks)
abstract: AWS Partners are moving faster than ever, into new regions, new AI-native solution categories, and more complex deal structures, while manual selling processes haven't kept pace. The expertise that wins deals is still locked in a few people and a separate portal. This session reveals how a new generation of AI agents puts that expertise on demand: surfacing co-sell intelligence and funding eligibility in the tools Partners already use, so every seller works with the best of the organization behind them.

title: Agents on call: Autonomous DB ops on Amazon Aurora with Expedia Group
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon DevOps Guru;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Hao Nguyen (Expedia Group); Anum Jang Sher (Amazon)
abstract: Expedia Group manages thousands of database instances across hundreds of AWS accounts. When incidents strike at this scale, every second counts. In this session, learn how a customer-driven vision for agentic AI evolved into a joint design partnership for autonomous database operations on Amazon Aurora. Discover how agents diagnose incidents across fleet-scale telemetry and deliver actionable recommendations to engineers. This joint initiative demonstrates how AI agents reduce incident response time and serves as a blueprint for teams seeking to automate database operations at scale. Learn how AWS is building the underlying capabilities to make autonomous operations real.

title: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
speakers: Eric Carter (Sysdig)
abstract: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.

title: AI agents for HPC operations
speakers: Manu Pillai (AWS); Marissa Powers (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Managing HPC infrastructure shouldn’t slow down science and engineering. Learn how AI-powered agents with AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) automate workload placement, detect and recover from failures, and simplify day-to-day cluster operations. Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

title: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL
speakers: Chirag Dave (AWS); Jim Mlodgenski (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

title: AI Agent Teams at Scale
speakers: Prashanth Krishnamurthy (Amazon Web Services Inc); Pavan Dusanapudi (Amazon)
abstract: When one event impacts hundreds, or even thousands, of customers simultaneously (a cancelled flight, a power outage, a system failure), contact centers cannot scale human agents fast enough. In this hands-on workshop, you orchestrate parallel AI agent teams using Amazon Connect Customer. You configure AI agents that fan out across dozens of affected customers at once: rebooking flights, issuing credits, and scheduling callbacks, all while a single human orchestrator monitors progress, approves exceptions, and intervenes only where needed. Walk away with a working parallel orchestration pattern and the configuration to deploy 1-to-many AI response at scale. This is not 1-to-1 AI coaching. This is 1-to-many crisis orchestration.

title: AI-assisted data modeling for Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: Kevin Willis (Amazon); Keren Tseytlin (AWS); Robert McCauley (AWS); Greg Krumm (Amazon Web Services); Lee Hannigan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this session, learn practical Amazon DynamoDB data modeling through an AI-assisted approach. Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.
