title: AI-assisted incident response: preparing for AI-assisted offensive
speakers: Robert Saul (AWS); Lindsey Henry (AWS)
abstract: The tools to raise the bar on incident response are here. AI can handle the volume so your team can focus on the nuance. But making that shift in practice, earning trust, building feedback loops, securing the tools themselves, is where we have seen teams get stuck. In this chalk talk, AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) leaders share exactly how we made that transition and what we learned along the way. We'll diagram the pipeline live, simulate an investigation, and spend real time working through your scenarios at the whiteboard.

title: AI at Lennar: Driving 80,000 Home Deliveries with Bedrock & Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
speakers: Ralph Gootee (Lennar); Isaac Gabay (Lennar Corporation)
abstract: Lennar is bringing AI into the everyday work behind more than 80,000 home deliveries a year, from land research and acquisition to construction, customer engagement, and sales. Join Ralph Gootee, CTO of Lennar, and Ariel Assaraf, CEO of Coralogix, for a practical look at moving AI from experimentation into production. They’ll share how Lennar is building and scaling AI agents on Amazon Bedrock, using AWS inference services and open-source models, and how Coralogix helps teams understand adoption, performance, cost, and business impact. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

title: AI-driven customer experience with Amaze, Byte by Yum! & Amorepacific
speakers: Joey Ahnn (AMOREPACIFIC); Jeremiah Sheehy (Yum! Brands); Chatnapang Wuthiwatana (Ascend Commerce - Amaze)
abstract: Customer experience in retail and consumer goods used to depend on how much staff you could put on the floor, the screen, or the line. Agentic AI changes the math: agents guide shoppers, support team members, and adapt to what a customer needs in real time. Hear how three brands put agents to work. Amaze, CP Group's super app, built an AI shopping assistant for shoppers across the group's brands, including 7-Eleven Thailand; Byte by Yum! powers personalized ordering and team member tools at Taco Bell; and Amorepacific built an AI beauty concierge delivering precision skin diagnoses across 10 countries.

title: AI-driven optimizations for HPC configurations on AWS
services: Amazon SageMaker;AWS Lambda;AWS Parallel Computing Service
speakers: Nicola Venuti (AWS); Francesco Ruffino (AWS)
abstract: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.

title: AI innovations across network monitoring and operations
abstract: Join us to explore how AI is transforming network monitoring and observability. This session dives into new capabilities for traffic analysis, network health monitoring, and faster issue resolution that shows how intelligent, automated tooling helps you move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive insight. Whether you want to cut time-to-resolution or get a clearer, real-time pulse on your network's health, come see what's new and what's on the horizon.

title: AI is Breaking Data Security… And Fixing It (sponsored by Concentric AI)
abstract: AI is rapidly becoming one of the biggest drivers of productivity and innovation in the enterprise — and one of the fastest-growing sources of data security risk. As copilots, assistants, and public AI tools become integrated into daily work, sensitive data is flowing into systems that most security teams can’t fully see, understand, or control. The problem is that traditional data security controls were never built for this. In fact, many organizations were already struggling to operationalize data security before AI accelerated the challenge. The good news? AI isn’t just creating the problem — it’s also enabling a smarter, more effective way to solve it. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is reshaping data security — and how they can use that same technology to gain control, minimize exposure, and support safer AI adoption across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Concentric AI, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Is Getting Smarter. AI-Generated Code Isn’t Getting Safer. (sponsored by Veracode, Inc.)
speakers: Christian Dalomba (Veracode)
abstract: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

title: AIOPs for cloud data infrastructure (sponsored by NetApp)
abstract: Cloud data infrastructure rarely stays optimal — workloads change, configurations drift, and data infrastructure expertise is scarce. AIOps applies AI-powered, agentic automation to cloud data storage operations: continuously assessing the environment, analyzing it against workload-specific best practices, recommending fixes, and applying them at the level of autonomy you choose. In this lightning talk, we’ll explore how NetApp Workload Factory does all this while providing customers with right-sized cost, on-target performance, stronger resilience and protection — without the need for deep data infrastructure expertise, and while always staying in control. This presentation is brought to you by NetApp, an AWS Partner.

title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
speakers: Adam Hill (Amazon Web Services); John Gray (Amazon)
abstract: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then deploy an AI agent that will enable proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days with your own agent.

title: AIOps strategy: foundations before capabilities
speakers: Brian Simpson-Adkins (Amazon Web Services); Rovan Omar (AWS)
abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before thinking about how they will scale. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We discuss areas your strategy should consider that will allow you to scale to additional capabilities more quickly and where Frontier Agents could help. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity discussion for your team.

title: AI-Powered Migrations: AWS Transform Across the Lifecycle
speakers: Luca Gorgoglione Certini (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Transform's composable AI agents automating the full migration lifecycle. Qualify using AI-powered agents to automate migration and modernization deal qualification along with funding orchestration. Migrate and modernize by leveraging Transform Custom agents to modernize legacy workloads at enterprise scale. Finally, measure by implementing Partner Revenue Measurement (PRM) to attribute revenue and impact to your delivery.

title: AI-Powered Profitability: How Partners Are Winning with AWS
speakers: Julia Chen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI is reshaping partner economics. Hear from AWS VP Julia Chen about how to build a profitable AI-first business. This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. You'll leave with insights about where to invest and pathways for growth.

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
speakers: Keita Watanabe (Amazon Web Services); Aravind Neelakantan (AWS)
abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profiling kernels, tuning collectives, keeping the GPUs fed, and handling the failures that grow with scale. In this hands-on workshop, work through the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, covering compute, network, storage, and the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks. Set up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer, measure, attribute, and fix with the right tool. The workshop concludes with self-built dashboards and a goodput methodology for training clusters.

title: AI That Answers: Customer Experiences Reimagined with Amazon Connect (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Mathew Thomas (Autodesk); Alex Halper (PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP); Harsha Desai (PepsiCo, Inc.)
abstract: Join PwC and four leading clients across industries to hear real examples of how Amazon Connect is transforming customer experience and delivering business outcomes. This session showcases cutting-edge omnichannel solutions across voice, chat, and messaging, along with agentic AI capabilities driving automation in areas like order management and real-time updates. Hear how organizations are deploying next-generation, AI-powered voice solutions in production, with new innovations continuing to emerge. Discover how these advancements deliver measurable business value, backed by PwC's outcome-based approach that ties technology investment directly to efficiency gains and improved customer and business performance. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Transformation: Redesigning How Work Gets Done (sponsored by Lucid Software)
abstract: Every major technology shift starts the same way. We use new technology to do the old thing. Early factories replaced steam engines with electric motors, but real transformation came when they redesigned the factory around what electricity made possible. We’re doing the same thing with AI. AI transformation isn’t about adding agents to existing workflows. It’s about redesigning how work gets done. That starts with context. In this session, we’ll show how teams can make work visible, give humans and AI a shared understanding of it, redesign workflows around agents, and turn that understanding into action. This presentation is brought to you by Lucid Software, an AWS Partner.

title: AI Under Fire: How to Stop AI-Powered Attacks and Secure AI Coding (sponsored by Palo Alto Networks)
speakers: Andy Piazza (Palo Alto Networks)
abstract: Frontier AI is transforming cyber threats, acting as a force multiplier across the kill chain. Adversaries leverage AI to scale social engineering, accelerate vulnerability discovery, and iterate malicious code. In this session, we highlight Palo Alto Networks’ approach to securing the frontier, by combining AI-powered Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) and Frontier Virtual Patching (FVP) to preemptively block zero days, alongside identity controls and Secure AI Coding to protect developer workflows. Attendees will learn how threat intelligence and proactive defense outpace machine scale adversaries. This presentation is brought to you by Palo Alto Networks, an AWS Partner.

title: A leader's guide to advanced teams models in an agentic world
aoi: Workforce Development;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Jonathan Allen (AMAZON WEB SERVICES); Carrie Wood (Amazon)
abstract: Agents made execution cheap. The work did not disappear. It moved into deciding what should exist, checking what agents produce, and owning it when something breaks. Most team designs were not built for that. This session gives you four questions to ask of any piece of work: what is it for, what does it touch, how will we check it, and whose name is on it. Then we walk through the team models leaders reach for, what each gets wrong, and where the pager and the name should sit. You leave knowing who does what now.

title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
aoi: Workforce Development;Innovation & Transformation;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Stephen Brozovich (Amazon Web Services); Ian Wilson (Amazon)
abstract: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
aoi: Data Protection;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Anas Fattahi (Amazon); G2 Krishnamoorthy (Amazon)
abstract: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
speakers: Matthias Patzak (Amazon Web Services); Sree Ratnasinghe (Amazon Web services)
abstract: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
speakers: Simone Zucchet (Amazon Web Services); ヘレナ・イン Yin Koeppl (Amazon Web Services); Romeo Romeo (Thomson Reuters (UK))
abstract: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
speakers: Matthias Patzak (Amazon Web Services); Laura Tacho (AWS)
abstract: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
speakers: Tom Godden (AWS)
abstract: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
speakers: Jihye Kwon (AWS); Swami Jayaraman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
speakers: Marc Bowes (Amazon Web Services); Raluca Constantin (Amazon)
abstract: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

title: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
speakers: Grant McAlister (AWS); Tim Stoakes (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.

title: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
speakers: Inderpreet Singh (Amazon DocumentDB); Douglas Bonser (AWS)
abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
speakers: Craig Howard (Amazon); Amrith Kumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.

title: Amazon ECS Gateway: Managed ingress for containerized applications
abstract: Amazon ECS Gateway is a new account-level resource that simplifies ingress for containerized applications by provisioning and managing networking infrastructure in your account. In this lightning talk, learn how platform teams define organizational networking standards once on a gateway and associate it with one or more clusters, creating a centralized way to govern how traffic reaches ECS services. Service teams simply opt in and inherit those standards with no networking expertise required. We cover host-based routing with Application Load Balancers, how up to 25 services can share an ALB to optimize cost, and how ECS provisions, scales, and removes ALBs as services connect and disconnect. We close with gateway routes, ALB metrics, and service action logs that give you full visibility into every operation ECS performs on your behalf.

title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Balachandra Hebbagilu Nagaraj (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Frank Fan (AWS); Swarna Kunnath (AWS); Shyam Sunder Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services); Luis Arcega (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
services: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Alessandro Germer (AWS); Sebastien Allamand (AWS)
abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

title: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
services: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);Amazon Elastic VMware Service (EVS)
speakers: Alastair Pooley (Accelya); Andy Reedy (AWS)
abstract: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.

title: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo)
aoi: Internet of Things;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Nick Matthews (Amazon Leo)
abstract: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.

title: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon EC2 Linux
speakers: Frederick Lefebvre (AWS); Sree Sunku (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.

title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
speakers: Greg Benjamin (Amazon); Jonathan Wong (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.

title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
speakers: Erick Dame (AWS); Christie Lee (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
speakers: Suresh Poopandi (Amazon Web Services); Alak Eswaradass (AWS)
abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
speakers: Lucas Soriano Alves Duarte (AWS); Manmohit Pal Singh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: Craig Howard (Amazon)
abstract: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver single-digit millisecond performance at any scale - whether your application has tens of thousands or hundreds of millions of simultaneous users - for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn how some basic data structure decisions led to these characteristics. And how those same decisions provide immutable, point-in-time restore. Leave with a better understanding of why DynamoDB can operate at the scale it does, and a framework on how to use it for decisions in your own applications.

title: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda
speakers: Sudipto Dasgupta (Aon); Hasan Mehdi Rizvi (AWS)
abstract: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.

title: API Gateway unleashed
speakers: Eduardo Rodrigues (Amazon Web Services); Peterson Larentis (AWS)
abstract: Gain essential hands-on skills to create, deploy, and manage APIs efficiently with Amazon API Gateway. Learn message transformation, request validation, and security best practices. Master deploying APIs using Infrastructure as Code and integrating with AWS serverless services. Dive into monitoring and debugging to ensure your APIs perform optimally, and explore building and testing WebSocket backends. Whether you're creating REST APIs or real-time communication layers, this workshop equips you with the knowledge to streamline application development and enhance API management. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Applying the Well-Architected Framework to AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
speakers: Adam Duffield (AWS); Manthan Raval (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones bring cloud closer to your end users and workloads but introduce architectural decisions that do not exist in a purely cloud-native model. Designing for resilience when infrastructure sits in your facility, and balancing security and cost across hybrid topologies, calls for rethinking each pillar. In this chalk talk, the session walks through the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. The session draws out real-world patterns, discusses trade-offs, and builds a practical mental model for well-architected hybrid solutions.

title: A practical guide to Amazon S3 data protection
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Backup
speakers: Ed Gummett (AWS); Denton He (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn step-by-step methods to protect your critical Amazon S3 data against accidental deletion, ransomware, and corruption, even at billion-object and petabyte scale. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.

title: A practitioner’s guide to migrating from 3rd-party CDN and WAF to AWS
speakers: Etienne Munnich (Amazon Web Services); Achraf Souk (AWS)
abstract: Considering migrating from a third-party CDN/WAF provider to AWS services? In this chalk talk, we’ll walk through the migration phases together: defining success criteria, running low-risk proof of concepts, designing your target architecture with Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and edge compute, executing the DNS cutover, and managing post-migration operations. Most of this session is open discussion: you bring your questions and stories, and we’ll share what we’ve learned running these migrations in production.

title: Architect and optimize your VMware environment on Amazon EVS
services: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);Amazon Elastic VMware Service (EVS)
speakers: Ben Lipman (AWS); Talha Kalim (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Dive deep into the architectural decisions that shape a resilient, high-performing VMware environment on Amazon EVS. Explore VCF 9 support, Windows Server license-included entitlements, networking designs, storage configurations tuned for performance and cost, and operational patterns for backup, patching, and disaster recovery. Hear from a customer running production workloads on EVS and leave with actionable architectures tailored to your VMware workloads.

title: Architecting AWS Outposts networking for enterprise and ultra-low-latency workloads
speakers: Harsha Sanku (Amazon Web Services); Leonardo Solano (AWS)
abstract: This session covers networking on second-generation AWS Outposts, spanning scalable multi-site topologies and ultra-low-latency bare-metal deployments. Learn how the second-generation dedicated network rack, local gateway routing domains, and intra-VPC and inter-VPC communication form the foundation for segmentation and local connectivity. See how the design extends to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and AWS Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in AWS Well-Architected principles. Explore how bare-metal instances with high-throughput accelerated networking and rack topology support co-located workloads where every microsecond matters.

title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
speakers: Ellliott Cordo (Data Futures Inc.); Namrata Shah (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association - (TIAA-CREF))
abstract: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.

title: Architecting for five nines with multi-region: Capital One’s journey (sponsored by Capital One)
speakers: Mats Lannér (Capital One Financial Corporation); Prem Dhayalan (Capitalone Bank)
abstract: Five nines of availability leaves an annual downtime budget of just 5.2 minutes, meaning a single regional failover can consume your entire year. Traditional disaster recovery models simply don't scale to meet this standard. In this session, discover how Capital One evolved its multi-region architectures to sustain regional outages while supporting critical production workloads. We share lessons learned from building and operating active-active topologies, focusing on real-world data consistency models, fault isolation via cell-based architecture, and continuous fault-injection testing. Attendees will walk away with a field-tested matrix for architecting high-availability cloud workloads. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
speakers: Kunle Adeleke (AWS); John Walker (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
speakers: Mike Haken (Amazon); Jamie Pasterick (AWS); Andy Orlosky (Amazon)
abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

title: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
speakers: Bimal Gajjar (Amazon); Arik Porat (AWS); David DeLuca (Amazon)
abstract: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

title: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
speakers: Joseph Shih (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Diego Colombatto (AWS)
abstract: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

title: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
speakers: Javeed Mohammed (Amazon Web Services); Eric Felice (AWS)
abstract: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Architect with validated best practices drawn from real customer deployments.

title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
speakers: Folarin Ayodeji Alamu (Amazon Web Services); Nayan Karumuri (Amazon web services); Oren Waldman (Amazon Web Services); Cheng-Lun Chen (Amazon Web Services); Srividhya Pallay (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Armis from ServiceNow:  See Everything, Know What Matters: Powered by AWS (sponsored by ServiceNow)
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Zero Trust
speakers: Steve Clark (Servicenow); Alex Mutschler (Circa Casino)
abstract: Cyber threats are evolving faster than traditional security tools can respond. In this session, discover how Armis - now part of ServiceNow - delivers complete asset visibility and real-time threat detection across IT, OT, and IoT environments. Hear directly from a customer who faced these challenges head-on and learn how Armis, powered by AWS, helped them identify risk, respond faster, and build a stronger security posture across their entire enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.

title: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
abstract: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Assess your workloads with SELinux compatibility on Amazon Linux 2027
speakers: Chris Bilbo (Amazon); Frederick Lefebvre (AWS); Ovais Siddiqui (AWS); Steve Zarkos (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Stewart Smith (AWS)
abstract: AL2027 preview enforces SELinux by default. In this session, deploy an application that hits SELinux denials, learn to read audit logs, diagnose the root cause, and write a custom policy that resolves it. You will leave with the practical skills to adopt AL2027's security defaults.

title: Assume breach, prove recovery: A ransomware resilience workshop
aoi: Resilience;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Christopher Strug (Amazon); Danny Wright (AWS)
abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

title: At Petabyte Scale: Building an AI Telemetry Lake with Coralogix (sponsored by Coralogix)
abstract: The Access Group is turning petabytes of telemetry from hundreds of teams into an engine for business performance. Its telemetry lake gives teams a clearer view of product health, helping them spot risks sooner, solve problems faster, and understand how technology shapes the customer experience. Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. Hear how it is sharpening decisions, focusing teams on what matters most, and creating the trusted data foundation needed to advance The Access Group’s AI ambitions. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
speakers: Tristan Ravitch (AWS)
abstract: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.

title: AT&T Expands Connectivity with AWS Interconnect and Amazon Leo
speakers: Anudeep Athlur (Amazon); Jad Naim (Amazon Web Services); Gordon Shannon (AT&T)
abstract: As a telecom operator, your customers demand resilient, scalable last mile connectivity for their AI workloads. This session shows new options for delivering that. You'll learn how to integrate AWS Interconnect - last mile with your control plane, provisioning connections directly from the AWS Management Console. AT&T shares how they're deploying Interconnect last-mile to expand their connectivity portfolio. They'll also share how they're working with Amazon Leo to bring broadband satellite connectivity to underserved locations. Leave with a clear model for extending your own connectivity offerings.

title: Automated forensics at scale with generative AI
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon GuardDuty
speakers: Chris Lamont-Smith (Amazon Web Services Australia); Barry Conway (AWS)
abstract: In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.In a live demo, we deploy malware built from APT41 tradecraft onto a Kubernetes cluster and watch an AI agent autonomously investigate the forensic evidence — acquiring volatile memory, identifying injected code, and tracing the attack chain without human intervention.

title: Automated Reasoning as Agent Guardrails
speakers: Mackenzie Zastrow (Amazon Web Serv); Liz Radway (AWS Velocity Labs)
abstract: Your agent is only as safe as the constraints it can’t bypass. This chalk talk covers how to enforce hard invariants on LLM-driven agents using formal policy languages: Cedar for stateless authorization, Dogwood for temporal reasoning over action history, and human-in-the-loop for the decisions machines shouldn’t make alone. We’ll look at different techniques for integrating this kind of enforcement with agents, including the Strands Agents intervention system and how deterministic policy can sit alongside a probabilistic model.

title: Automate Investigations to Resolve Application Failures with AWS DevOps Agent
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: David Carbone (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

title: Automate Penetration Tests with AWS Security Agent
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Security Agent
speakers: Alan Meridian (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.

title: Automate threat detection and response across your logs
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon CloudWatch Logs;AWS Security Hub
speakers: Vikash Agrawal (Amazon Web Services); Ravikumar Sola (AWS); Vinod Kisanagaram (Amazon Web Services); Rizwan Mohammed (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Jean Velez Torres (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.

title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
speakers: Raj Kandaswamy (AWS); Jesus Rodriguez (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

title: Automating macOS at scale: AMI build, TCC, and provisioning on EC2 Mac
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Systems Manager;EC2 Image Builder
speakers: Kyle Krall (Amazon Web Services); Caitlin Rawlins (AWS)
abstract: Automating macOS in the cloud brings challenges Linux and Windows don't. Going from a fresh EC2 Mac instance to a production-ready fleet means clearing non-obvious hurdles: building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder and Packer, pre-approving TCC permissions, bootstrapping Systems Manager, and working with Apple's security model. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the real friction points teams hit: image pipelines, the TCC dialog problem, remote access, MDM enrollment, and fleet provisioning. Bring your toughest macOS automation questions; most of the session is open Q&A.

title: Automating Serverless migrations at scale with AWS Transform
speakers: Ana Barragan (Amazon Web Services); Jonathan Tuliani (Amazon Web Services); Dan Fox (AWS); Bhuvan Annamreddi (Amazon Web Services); Robert Hanuschke (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Runtime deprecations pile up. API migrations stall. Legacy code sits untouched because manual upgrades across hundreds of functions take weeks your team doesn't have. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to assess, plan, and execute Lambda runtime upgrades and API migrations at scale. Working hands-on, you'll run the full agentic loop: codebase assessment, transformation planning, incremental code changes committed to Git, and self-validating test execution. You'll scale transformations across hundreds of functions in parallel using AWS Batch and Fargate. Walk away with patterns for automated, large-scale modernization. Bring your laptop.

title: Autonomous AI Ops with AWS DevOps Agent and New Relic Autopilot (sponsored by New Relic)
speakers: Elliot Markowitz (Verisk Analytics); Anush Jayaraman (New Relic, Inc.); Bill Fine (Amazon)
abstract: Incident investigation still consumes 1-2 hours of engineering time per event. See how New Relic's Intelligent Observability Platform integrates with AWS DevOps Agent to: Autonomously triage incidents, pinpoint root cause, and deliver actionable remediation with no custom tooling required. Investigate incidents agentically correlating telemetry, code, and deployments across AWS, multi cloud, and on-prem environments. Demonstrate how this innovation proactively prevents future incidents by analyzing patterns and recommending improvements. Learn how customers are cutting MTTR by 75% and shifting from firefighting to prevention, and walk away ready to get started. This presentation is brought to you by New Relic, an AWS Partner.

title: Autonomous DBOps: Agentic AI for maintaining databases
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)
speakers: Shirish Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services Australia Pty Ltd); Paola Lorusso (AWS); Rinisha Marar (Amazon Web Services); Sudhir Amin (Amazon Web Services); Dustin Brown (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. In this builders' session, learn how to leverage agentic AI solutions implementing LLM-powered autonomous agents to monitor, diagnose, and optimize relational databases in real time. We will demonstrate how AI agents can analyze slow query logs, recommend or apply tuning actions, and trigger intelligent alerts using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Cloudwatch, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Systems Manager. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
speakers: Jones Zachariah Noel (New Relic); Julia Furst Morgado (Dash0)
abstract: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.

title: AWS AI agents accelerate SAP migration and modernization on AWS
speakers: Beth Sharp (AWS); Nikhil Chetwani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The legacy ERP system that once gave you a competitive edge may now be limiting your ability to innovate. Modernizing SAP can be complex, expensive, risky, and every delay is a missed opportunity to innovate. In this Chalk Talk, you will learn how AI Agents can make it possible to upgrade to SAP's Cloud ERP safely and cost-effectively in weeks, not months. Whether you're running SAP ECC, moving to RISE with SAP, modernizing ABAP and PI/PO, or migrating SAP Business Warehouse (BW), discover how AI-powered agents can take on the heavy lifting for you

title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
speakers: Pranav Chachra (AWS); Gareth Tucker (Amazon Web Services); Daniel Xu (Anthropic)
abstract: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.

title: AWS AI League: Build domain specific AI with Forge
speakers: Rajesh Babu Nuvvula (Amazon); Jai Vumma (Amazon Web Services); Natasya Idries (AWS)
abstract: In this hands-on workshop you’ll compete head-to-head with other builders to build your own domain specific AI. You’ll tackle real-world challenges as you generate synthetic datasets, experiment with model customization, and fine-tune models to improve accuracy, clarity, and relevance. You’ll learn just how accessible and cost-effective AI customization can be. Whether you’re chasing the championship or simply sharpening your AI expertise, this session delivers practical techniques you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate

title: AWS Backup: Centralized data protection for your cloud environment
speakers: LeelaVinod Bandla (Warner Bros. Discovery); Heather Munoz (AWS); Mathew Patrick (Capital One); Bisman Sethi (Amazon)
abstract: Managing data protection across a growing cloud environment requires a centralized strategy. AWS Backup was designed around this principle, giving more than 150,000 organizations a fully managed service to automate backup operations, enforce protection policies at scale, and safeguard 20+ AWS services from a single console. From human error to infrastructure failures to targeted attacks, AWS Backup helps ensure you can recover the right data, at the right time, with confidence. In this session, learn how AWS Backup works, how you can use it to protect mission-critical workloads, and hear directly from customers about their implementation strategies and operational outcomes.

title: AWS Backup clean room recovery: Comprehensive resilience framework
speakers: Wali Akbari (Amazon Web Services); Sabith Venkitachalapathy (AWS)
abstract: Having an isolated vault is only half the battle. When a cyber event hits, you need confidence your backups are clean and recoverable. In this chalk talk, learn how to design an Isolated Recovery Environment using AWS Backup that validates and restores data in a secure space separate from production: reducing blast radius, breaking the kill chain, and proving recoverability on demand. We'll cover immutable air-gapped copies, automated restore testing with malware scanning, and Multi-party approval to control recovery access during account compromise. Leave with a framework for building recovery confidence into your backup strategy.

title: AWS Certification & Proficiency Path: How to be Proficient in the Age of AI Agents?
speakers: Satabdi Das (AWS)
abstract: Skills decay at unprecedented speed as AI reshapes what proficiency means. Certifications still validate expertise, but practitioners now need to demonstrate they can design, build, and optimize AI-powered systems alongside traditional cloud architecture. This lightning talk explains how AWS Training and Certification developed exam content, hands-on labs, and simulation-based assessments for agentic AI domains. You will also see how our team validated new competency frameworks, mapped learning paths to job roles, and built assessment experiences that measure real-world readiness rather than knowledge recall alone.

title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Rajeev Kapoor (Amazon)
abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate by playing this 3D virtual escape room game. Enter a 3D virtual environment, select your avatar, and navigate rooms locked behind AWS Solutions Architect Associate challenges and design your way out. Build VPCs, select storage and database services, configure high availability, and implement fault-tolerant architectures while solving exam-aligned puzzles and completing hands-on labs. Each room builds on the previous, testing progressively deeper architectural knowledge. Collaborate with peers or compete solo and escape first to claim the leaderboard.

title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified AI Practitioner
speakers: Alie Ibarra (AWS)
abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified AI Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Generative AI knowledge unlocks doors here. Enter a narrative-driven 3D world, choose your avatar, and tackle progressively harder puzzles tied to AWS Certified AI Practitioner exam domains. Each locked room blends exam-style questions with hands-on labs covering foundation models, responsible AI, prompt engineering, and agentic workflows. Collaborate with teammates, solve challenges under time pressure, and race to escape before your peers to top the leaderboard.

title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)
speakers: Rajeev Kapoor (Amazon)
abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Step into a 3D virtual world, choose your avatar, and race other players through rooms locked behind AWS Cloud Practitioner exam-style challenges. Each room combines interactive puzzles with hands-on labs that reinforce foundational cloud concepts like Compute, Storage, Networking, Security, and pricing models. Solve challenges collaboratively or compete solo, unlock rooms, and escape first to claim the leaderboard.

title: AWS GameDay - Application Security & AI-Powered Penetration Testing
speakers: Emma Higashikawa (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative exercise to develop practical skills in application security on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll configure security agents, launch AI-driven penetration tests, and remediate critical vulnerabilities before the biggest production launch of the year for Unicorn.Rentals. Build skills in agent-based security assessment, OWASP Top 10 vulnerability identification, and shift-left security practices. Every unpatched vulnerability is an open door. You and your AI-powered security agent are the only things standing between your application and compromise! Whether you're a security engineer, DevOps practitioner, developer, or cloud architect, security is your responsibility, and this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Cybersecurity & Threat Detection ft. SentinelOne
aoi: Application Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Threat Intelligence
speakers: Lorenzo Ciaravola (Amazon)
abstract: Join us for a collaborative learning exercise to develop practical skills in cybersecurity and threat detection on AWS. Dive into a live AWS environment where you will hunt for threats, analyze attack patterns, and defend your cloud workloads against sophisticated adversaries in real time. Build skills in threat intelligence, security analytics, and automated threat remediation as you protect your environment from active cyber threats. Face off against real-world attack scenarios with multi-stage threat patterns that will test your ability to detect and respond under pressure! Whether you are a seasoned security analyst or just exploring cybersecurity, this GameDay will sharpen your skills. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with SentinelOne. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Developer Productivity & DevOps ft. Dynatrace
speakers: Maya Flores (AWS)
abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative exercise to develop practical skills in maximizing developer productivity on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll streamline development workflows, optimize CI/CD pipelines, and accelerate software delivery using modern tools and practices. Leverage build automation, deployment pipelines, code quality, and performance optimization as you race to ship features faster without sacrificing quality. Face challenges that push your ability to eliminate bottlenecks, automate toil, and deliver software at speed! Whether you're a seasoned DevOps engineer or a developer looking to level up, this GameDay will put your productivity skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with Dynatrace. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Resilience & Disaster Recovery ft. Clumio by Commvault
speakers: Maya Flores (AWS)
abstract: Join us for an immersive, collaborative exercise to develop practical skills in data protection and automated disaster recovery on AWS. Dive into a live environment where you'll design backup strategies, recovery procedures, and resilience architectures that keep workloads safe and recoverable. Leverage cross-region replication, recovery point and time objectives, and automated failover as you protect workloads. Face challenges that simulate real-world disasters where every second of downtime counts! Whether you're a seasoned systems architect or new to disaster recovery, this GameDay will put your resilience skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with Clumio by Commvault. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS GameDay - Service Reliability & Agentic Remediation ft. Datadog
speakers: AM Grobelny (AWS)
abstract: Join us for a collaborative learning exercise to develop practical skills in operational excellence and service reliability on AWS. Dive into a live AWS environment where you will build and maintain highly reliable services while responding to incidents, managing deployments, and ensuring system health at scale. Build skills in monitoring, incident response, runbook automation, deployment strategies, and SLO management as you keep critical services running under pressure. Face scenarios that test your ability to detect, diagnose, and resolve operational issues before they impact customers! Whether you are a seasoned SRE or just exploring operations, this GameDay will put your skills to the ultimate test. Come solo or bring a group. Either way, you'll compete on a team. This session features integrated use cases with Datadog. Walk-ups welcome.

title: AWS infrastructure as code: A year in review
services: AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK);AWS CloudFormation
speakers: Aakash Deshpande (AWS); Mark Rambow (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your infrastructure code deserves the same developer experience as your application code. This session recaps what's new for AWS CloudFormation and the AWS CDK: early change-set validation, the CloudFormation Language Server for your IDE, Stack Refactoring without downtime, drift-aware change sets, CDK Mixins for composable abstractions, cross-account output references, and the CDK Toolkit Library. See how these capabilities shorten your dev-test cycle and strengthen deployment safety.

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs: Strong isolation for agents & beyond
speakers: Anton Aleksandrov (AWS); Alexander Vladimirov (AWS); CJ Avilla (Anthropic)
abstract: Agents running generated code, multi-tenant platforms, and untrusted workloads all need strong isolation, but each traditional compute option forces a tradeoff. VMs isolate well but start slowly. Containers are fast but share a kernel. Functions scale to zero but limit state. Teams close the gaps with isolation logic they build and maintain themselves. Lambda MicroVMs offer sandboxes with VM-level isolation for each agent, tenant, or task: state that persists across invocations, automatic suspend on idle, resume on demand. This session covers how MicroVMs work, the security and isolation model, lifecycle management, and patterns for agentic sandboxing and untrusted code execution.

title: AWS Nitro System deep dive: Security, isolation, and innovation
speakers: Alexander Graf (Amazon Web Services Development Center Germany GmbH); Scott Peterson (Amazon)
abstract: The AWS Nitro System underpins every modern Amazon EC2 instance — purpose-built hardware and firmware delivering security, performance, and continuous innovation. In this deep dive, explore the Nitro architecture from custom silicon and modular design to networking and storage offload. Learn how the sixth-generation Nitro System introduces the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine, bringing formal verification to cloud isolation and extends Nitro-level isolation to containers. Discover how Nitro enables enhanced networking and confidential computing.

title: AWS Partner: Agentic AI workflows for business users on Amazon Quick
speakers: Diana Diaz (AWS)
abstract: This bootcamp is for AWS Partners only. Walk through a hands-on business scenario using Amazon Quick, the agentic AI workspace that connects to your tools and learns your workflows. Create knowledge spaces, run deep-research agents, connect external APIs, automate multi-step processes with Flows, and build a custom AI agent in a browser. Leave able to help customers put agentic AI to work across their teams and business applications. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: AWS re:Invent 5K Race
abstract: Get ready for a 5K unlike any other. Skip the traditional point to point course. Instead, you will conquer 3.1 miles in six high energy laps around the perimeter of Allegiant Stadium alongside the global AWS community. Completely free and open to all paces. This fun run supports AWS customer, the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research. Sign up now at the attendee experience desk located in the artist foyer at Venetian.

title: AWS Security Incident Response Challenge: Defend the Cake
speakers: Ben Fletcher (AWS); Geroen Joris (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The Magic Unicorn Cake recipe needs defending, and the Grumpy Cats are on the move. In this hands-on workshop, you become an AWS Security Engineer protecting critical assets. Working in teams, you strengthen security posture, establish continuous monitoring, and execute incident response playbooks while a live threat actor works to exfiltrate the recipe. A live leaderboard tracks every scored action. Through this immersive experience you learn threat modeling and the detection and response methodologies the team behind AWS Security Incident Response applies daily. Practical techniques that translate directly to your own environment. Bring your laptop.

title: AWS Technical Essentials
speakers: Deepika Nair (AWS)
abstract: AWS Technical Essentials gives you the foundation to start building on AWS with confidence. In this bootcamp, navigate the AWS Management Console, configure IAM security controls, deploy compute workloads across EC2, Lambda, and containers, set up databases with RDS and DynamoDB, manage storage with S3, explore networking services, and monitor resources with CloudWatch. Hands-on labs reinforce each topic, so you leave ready to design available, scalable, and cost-effective solutions.

title: AWS wherever you need it: From the cloud to the edge
speakers: Spencer Dillard (Amazon Web Services); Ian Cottingham (Amazon Web Services); Rama Raghavan (AT&T Inc.)
abstract: While most workloads can run in the cloud, some remain on-premises or at the edge due to low latency, local data processing, or data residency needs. AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories extend AWS services, APIs, and tools to metro areas, on-premises data centers, and the far edge. Explore how these infrastructure offerings power a broad range of hybrid cloud and edge computing use cases such as financial trading, manufacturing, and AI. Learn how AWS helps you run regulated workloads with edge requirements, power generative AI with edge data, and migrate workloads with on-premises dependencies, featuring AT&T's migration and modernization at scale.

title: Best path forward: Rehost & replatform to containers with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Transform
speakers: Yogesh Bhatia (AWS Australia Pty Ltd); Diego Dalmolin (AWS)
abstract: Not every app needs the same migration path, and figuring out which ones to rehost versus containerize is where teams get stuck. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to plan a combined migration and modernization across your application portfolio, then execute a mix of container and rehost migrations deploying to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll work through the full lifecycle. Learn how to order waves and coordinate cutover across a mixed portfolio. Leave with a realistic multi-wave plan you can apply to your own environment. Laptop required.

title: Best practices for AI-powered software development on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Ajit Mahareddy (Amazon Web Services); Alfredo Castillo (AWS)
abstract: You already use a coding agent for software development. It touches your codebase, infrastructure, and production environment and needs guardrails, permissions, and rules to operate safely. In this workshop, you connect an agent of your choice, such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, to Amazon Bedrock and deliver a real application from brief to production. You define specs the agent can act on, wire in automated test gates, apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and lock down permissions before anything reaches infrastructure. The app serves as a tested reference implementation your team can adapt to its own development workflows. Laptop required.

title: Best practices for building an observability strategy in the age of AI
speakers: Helen Ashton (AWS); Adam Rubinsky (AWS)
abstract: Most observability strategies were built for a pre-AI world and are no longer enough. Your data foundation remains critical, but the way you use that data is changing fast. In this chalk talk, we explore what stays the same, what must evolve, and what's new as AI reshapes observability. We'll cover the shift from static dashboards to dynamic experiences, from reactive alarms to AI-driven insights, and the new questions you need to answer, like how well your agents are performing. Join us as we share what AWS is learning as we embrace AI-led observability.

title: Best practices for helping agents understand code you didn't write
abstract: Most production code has no spec. It was written by teams that moved on, and its docs went stale long ago. Before a refactor, migration, or incident fix, developers spend days on code archaeology, and AI agents have to rediscover the same behavior in every new chat with little prior context. Learn how to turn an existing codebase into a structured, persistent model of what the system does: its properties, invariants, component interactions, and hidden assumptions. See how that model helps you onboard faster, baseline behavior before a refactor, and give your AI agent context that's reusable across sessions.

title: Best Practices for Successful Multiplayer Game Launches
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon GameLift
speakers: Juho Jantunen (AWS); Chad Lingmann (AWS)
abstract: The session covers best practices, architectural guidance and lessons learned for successful multiplayer game launches at scale. It's based on experience from helping hundreds of game customers from indie studios to AAA titles launch their games on AWS.

title: Best practices for working with shared coding agents on your team
abstract: Software development happens through teamwork, but agent work is often trapped in individual sessions. The developer who starts the work becomes the coordinator who needs to relay feedback, reconstruct decisions, or keep agents moving. Working with agents as a team has many paper cuts, but there are best practices you can implement. Follow an issue from investigation through implementation, testing, and review, with requests, decisions, and approvals attributed along the way as work progresses. Learn how team-scoped knowledge, reusable practices, and clear permission boundaries let agents take on ongoing responsibilities while people keep control of what ships.

title: Better, faster, cheaper: How Valkey is revolutionizing caching
speakers: Madelyn Olson (AWS); Meet Bhagdev (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Discover how the powerful combination of open source Valkey and Amazon ElastiCache is transforming the landscape of distributed caching. In this session, explore recent innovations including advanced search capabilities such as full-text search, a memory-efficient dictionary that reduces memory usage by up to 40%, and a multi-threaded architecture that enables instantaneous scaling by up to 230%.
