Learn about the infrastructure that enables ElastiCache to patch hundreds of thousands of customers while maintaining high availability, even for extreme workloads like Prime Day's trillion requests per minute.

title: Beyond Batch: Modernize with Event-Driven Architecture & Serverless
speakers: Sundar Shanmugam (Amazon Web Services); Ramesh Mathikumar (Amazon Web Services); Elie Elmalem (AWS); Ray Chang (Amazon Web Services); Rajdeep Banerjee (Amazon)
abstract: In this builders' session, transform a batch-oriented data processing pipeline into a real-time, event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AWS Step Functions. Working hands-on in small groups, you'll decompose a monolithic batch process into discrete event-driven steps, implement file-processing triggers, and design fan-out patterns for parallel execution. Learn when to keep batch and when to go event-driven, and leave with a working modernization pattern. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
speakers: Weitong Ruan (Amazon); Qian Hu (Amazon)
abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

title: Beyond English: Architecture Patterns for Multilingual AI Voice Agents
speakers: Mark Macdonald (Amazon Web Services); Prabhakar Rajasekar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Deploying AI voice agents beyond English introduces unique challenges: accent handling, language detection, code-switching between languages mid-conversation, and cultural nuances in conversation flow. In this chalk talk, we share architecture patterns for building multilingual voice agents using Amazon Connect Agentic Voice. We cover real-world scenarios from deployments like Spanish and English coexistence, German with regional dialects, and Italian conversational AI. We discuss when speech-to-speech models work natively, when to fall back to TTS pipelines, how to handle polyglot but non-native accent scenarios, and practical approaches to knowledge base localization. Bring your language challenge and we'll design your multilingual architecture on the whiteboard.

title: Beyond Evals: Setting up your agents and your enterprise for success (sponsored by LangChain)
speakers: Joel Johnson (LangChain)
abstract: We are witnessing models and agents continually becoming more capable, all while the process of meaningfully evaluating them continues to be a challenge. In this session, we will dissect eval best practices observed both in the field and internally at LangChain. This session will go beyond just your technical evaluation toolkit and provide practical organizational and process takeaways and a better understanding of what future capabilities are unlocked downstream of good evaluation. This session will be especially relevant to teams deploying agents in cross-functional domains. This presentation is brought to you by LangChain, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Hiroshi Tokoyo (Amazon Web Services Japan); Maen Suleiman (Annapurna Labs)
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning enables your model to follow instructions, but teaching it to reason requires reinforcement learning. RL workflows demand iterative loops that multiply compute costs, making the price performance of AWS Trainium, a chip built specifically for deep learning AI, critical. In this chalk talk, we explore what techniques like RLHF and GRPO bring to the table and how to run them on Trainium with the AWS Neuron software stack, Torchtitan, HuggingFace TRL, vLLM, and native PyTorch. We compare co-located and disaggregated RL architectures. You'll leave ready to implement cost-effective RL loops that train agents to reason.

title: Beyond Next-Token Prediction: World Models for Human Health
speakers: Chenyan Xiong (Xlue Inc.)
abstract: Next-token prediction has been effective for language, but is it the right learning objective for achieving clinical intelligence from longitudinal human health data? In this talk, we show that treating health records as flat token sequences limit the advancement of foundation models in healthcare. We then introduce a Health State–Action World Model that abstracts longitudinal records into learned representations of patient health states and clinical actions, and models how these states evolve under different interventions. This abstraction enables pretraining models to predict future health events, diagnoses, treatments, and responses to treatment. Across large-scale datasets, we show that moving from token-level prediction to state–action modeling enables clinical intelligence that cannot be achieved through token prediction alone, while generalizing strongly to unseen patients.

title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Optimize the Agent Harness
speakers: Jonathan Buck (Amazon Web Services); Po-Shin Chen (AWS)
abstract: An agent’s performance depends on far more than its model or system prompt. Tools, instructions, context management, memory, orchestration, and runtime policies form an agent harness that can determine whether the same model succeeds or fails. This session introduces harness optimization: a systematic, evaluation-driven approach to improving the complete agent system. Learn how to identify high-leverage changes, design controlled experiments, optimize for quality, latency, and cost, and avoid overfitting to benchmarks. Leave with a repeatable method for turning agent development into an engineering discipline.

title: Beyond Search: How Gilead Built a Multi-Agent AI That Reasons Like a Scientist (sponsored by Thoughtworks)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Shayan Mohanty (Thoughtworks)
abstract: Gilead is pivoting from virology leader to oncology and immunology powerhouse, targeting 10+ transformative therapies by 2030. With Thoughtworks, Gilead built an AI co-scientist on AWS that reasons across 1M+ ELN assay records, 3M+ internal documents and external literature. It reads assay, compound and target data like a scientist, returning one cited answer with conflicts flagged. Scientists now reach evidence-backed decisions in minutes, not days. Gilead and Thoughtworks share how the solution earned scientists' trust. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond the Buy Button: Cisco on AWS Marketplace, a Partner-Led AI Win (sponsored by Cisco)
speakers: Dave Gervon (Cisco Systems, Inc.)
abstract: AWS Marketplace isn't just a procurement channel, it's a financial lever. A typical ISV saves a procurement cycle. Cisco draws down committed spend against the infrastructure your agents run on: connectivity from cloud to edge, visibility into agent behavior, and protection for models, identities, and data. Partners add the expertise to deploy it right, turning a procurement decision into an architectural one, a true better together win with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cisco, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond the Docs: Operating Scoped VPC Endpoints in Real Environments
speakers: Meg Ashby (Abnormal AI); Kenneth Attard (Betsson)
abstract: Scoped VPC endpoint policies look simple, until production traffic proves otherwise. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through real-world failures we've encountered while deploying account- and org-scoped endpoint policies and trace the identity flows, auth chains, and hidden dependencies behind them. Together, we'll explore a key lesson: endpoint policies evaluate the request that's actually made, not the request you think you're making. Bring your questions and experiences as we whiteboard the assumptions that lead to outages and learn how to spot them before they impact production.

title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Direct Connect
abstract: You have enough GPUs in your server to cover your software requirements. But is that all you need to consider? In a world where everyone is fighting for GPUs, picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes an engineering team makes at scale. This session shares lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately. You'll see how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and how to use AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. Leave with a cloud and bare metal architectural pattern and a GPU selection framework covering workload fit and server tradeoffs.

title: Beyond the simulator: Quantum chemistry workflows on real hardware
speakers: Tyler Takeshita (AWS); Sebastian Stern (AWS); Nick White (Amazon Web Services); Nicola Smyth (AWS)
abstract: Get hands-on experience running quantum computing experiments using the Kvantify SDK; the same workflow used by researchers. In this workshop, participants will set up and execute computational workflows, testing them locally, on a classical simulator via Amazon Braket, and finally on a real quantum processing unit (QPU). Through practical exercises in enzyme engineering and battery development, learners will see how quantum computing accelerates discovery in life sciences and materials science, bridging the gap from simulation to real quantum hardware.

title: Booking.com's playbook for cloud transformation at global scale
speakers: Gary Krige (Booking.com); Mainu Kalita (AWS); Valentina Muñoz (Booking.com)
abstract: Booking.com connects millions of travelers to over 28 million listings across 43 languages. Their cloud transformation had to match that scale. In this session, hear how Booking.com dissolved organizational silos, broke through bottlenecks, and compressed timelines to fundamentally change how they build, operate, and innovate. You'll learn the architectural decisions, migration frameworks, and repeatable patterns that scaled cloud adoption across the enterprise, and how embedding AI from the ground up now powers next-generation customer experiences. Leave with a playbook for turning cloud transformation into continuous, cloud-fluent competitive advantage.

title: Bootstrapping GitOps on Amazon EKS with Argo CD, ACK, and kro
speakers: Jesse Butler (AWS); Carlos Santana (AWS)
abstract: Deploying an application to Kubernetes is straightforward. Provisioning its AWS resources, IAM roles, policies, and supporting infrastructure is more complex. Separate infrastructure and application toolchains create fragmented workflows and increase the risk of drift. In this session, we'll build a GitOps platform using EKS Capabilities, Argo CD, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK), and kro. See how kro packages Kubernetes workloads and their AWS dependencies behind a single, self-service custom resource. Learn how Argo CD continuously reconciles the entire application stack from one Git repository. Finally, watch several microservices deploy, with their cloud resources provisioned and continuously managed alongside their workloads.

title: Break free from on-premises NAS: Migrating to AWS
services: Amazon FSx;Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP;Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
speakers: Eugene Kiliar (Amazon); Saurav Majumder (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how Amazon FSx storage simplifies the migration of on premises workloads to the cloud while keeping the compatibility and performance your apps depend on. With fully managed, block and file storage that eliminates operational overhead, see real-world migration patterns for user file shares, high-performance applications, enterprise databases like Oracle, SAP, and SQL Server, and VMware migration with AWS Transform and FSx for ONTAP. Discover how organizations are reducing costs and accelerating innovation.

title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
services: AWS Fault Injection Service;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Serafin Sedano Arenas (AWS); Shivani Sharma (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Bridging clouds: Building global multicloud and hybrid networks on AWS
speakers: Mike Jager (AWS); Mike Bentzen (AWS)
abstract: It's no secret, enterprises today run workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers, but stitching together global connectivity without complexity remains a challenge. In this workshop, easily extend AWS connectivity to other clouds and on-premises environments using AWS Interconnect, AWS Direct Connect, and AWS Cloud WAN. Build a global multicloud network, then apply Amazon VPC Lattice to enforce security and handle overlapping IP address spaces without complex NAT configurations. Leave equipped to architect and deploy hybrid network architectures using modern application networking patterns. Bring your laptop.

title: Bring Oracle Databases to AWS Without Starting Over (sponsored by Oracle)
speakers: Vishal Patil (Oracle)
abstract: Organizations want the flexibility and innovation of AWS, but they cannot afford to rearchitect the mission-critical Oracle Database applications their businesses depend on. This session explains how Oracle AI Database@AWS provides a simpler path from on-premises Oracle Exadata and RAC environments to AWS with minimal to no database or application changes. Explore how customers can maintain full database capabilities and architectural compatibility, connect Oracle data to AWS applications with low latency, and unify data with AWS analytics, machine learning, and agentic AI services. We will also examine the operational value of familiar AWS tools, collaborative support, integrated security, and simplified purchasing. Attendees will learn how migration can reduce infrastructure constraints while creating a stronger foundation for innovation across Oracle and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
speakers: Prabir Sekhri (AWS); Andrew Peng (AWS)
abstract: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.

title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
speakers: Gokul Sarangaraju (Amazon); Suresh Natarajan (AWS); Dinesh Balaaji Prabakaran (Amazon Web Services); Shivansh Singh (AWS); Chetan Makvana (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: British Airways: Using agentic AI to modernise Java services at scale
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
speakers: Avi Nidumbur (Amazon); Gary Holland (British Airways); Shane Routley (AWS)
abstract: You have hundreds of services stuck on aging infrastructure, and your engineers are spending more time maintaining them than building new experiences. British Airways faced the same challenge with 590 Github repositories and 200 business services on EC2. Using AWS Transform custom, they built an agentic AI platform that autonomously migrates services to ECS Fargate on Graviton, cutting costs by 48% without compromising business logic. They also extended it to improve test coverage and patch security vulnerabilities continuously. In this session, you'll learn how to build a repeatable transformation engine and give your engineers time back.

title: Brownfield development across large codebases with AI agents
abstract: Most production code has no spec. It was written by teams that moved on, and its docs went stale long ago. When you inherit a service, prepare a migration, or chase an incident, you spend days reconstructing what the system does, and your AI agent rediscovers the same behavior in every new chat. We'll first sketch how to generate a structured model of an existing system from its code: its invariants, dependencies, and hidden assumptions. Then it's your turn. Bring your questions and your hardest brownfield problems, and we'll work through them together at the whiteboard.

title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
speakers: Salih Güler (AWS)
abstract: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.

title: Build a community portal with Connect Customer agentic voice in 60 minutes
speakers: Pramod Halapeti (Amazon Web Services); Archit Malpure (Amazon Web Services); Doug Gartner (Amazon Web Services); Lawrence Gohar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: City governments face rising citizen expectations with shrinking staff. In this builders' session, learn how to deploy a fully functional AI-powered community engagement portal using Amazon Connect Customer agentic voice in under one hour. See how to build a voice agent that answers common citizen inquiries about permits, utilities, parks, and city services, routes callers to the right department, and seamlessly escalates to live agents with full conversation context when needed. Walk away with a production-ready reference architecture that operations team can configure, deploy, and manage independently.

title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
services: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS);AWS Signer
speakers: Andre Baumeier (AWS); Andrea Rossi (AWS); Desiree Brunner (AWS); Michael Tschannen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.

title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
services: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus;Amazon OpenSearch Service;AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: Anirudha Jadhav (AWS Opensearch); Lucas Vieira (AWS)
abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.

title: Build agentic observability workflows with AI tools from AWS Marketplace
speakers: George Maroulakos (AWS); Tuan Vo (Amazon Inc.)
abstract: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
speakers: Ananta Khanal (Amazon Web Services); Samuel Ouvrard (AWS); Beerinder Mann (AWS); Sebastien Perreault (AWS); Matt Boyd (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
speakers: Nina Lopatina (MongoDB)
abstract: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a multi-Region, active-active rewards app with Aurora DSQL
speakers: Eric Kraemer (Amazon); Dan Blaner (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this session, get hands-on experience with Amazon Aurora DSQL, a serverless distributed SQL database that delivers active-active high availability. Learn how to build a retail rewards points application with active-active resiliency across multiple Availability Zones and two Regions. Explore how ACID transactions and active-active replication work in Aurora DSQL. Discover best practices for data model and application design and more. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Build an Agentic AI Marketing Engine Powered by Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Vanessa Ji (Amazon Web Services); Sanhawat Taongern (Amazon Web Services); Jeremy Bartosiewicz (AWS); Hari Radhakrishnan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this hands-on builder session, construct a multi-agent AI system that automates campaign planning, activation, and optimization. Build four specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock including a planner, media buyer, analyst, and creative generator that turns campaign parameters into audience targeting, budget allocation, performance forecasts, and localized creative grounded in your brand guidelines and historical data. Activate campaigns through Amazon Ads DSP, then add an optimizer agent with human-in-the-loop approvals that reallocates budget across channels as performance shifts. You'll build a running multi-agent workflow and take away the Bedrock agent definitions to adapt for your own campaigns.

title: Build an AI agent that understands customer intent
abstract: Today's AI agents start every session cold. They don't know what the customer was just browsing, whether they're frustrated or exploring, or whether this is a service moment or a buying moment. So they waste the first few turns asking what your data already knows. In this hands-on builders' session, you close that gap. You unify customer data into Profiles, then turn it into real-time signals about what each customer needs. You wire those signals into an AI agent with calculated attributes and event triggers, so when the customer makes contact the agent already understands why they're there and responds with the right answer and the right offer. You leave with a working prototype ready for your own environment.

title: Build an automated evaluation pipeline for AI agents
speakers: Aishwarya Gavili (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Sam Palani (AWS); Suyin Wang (AWS); Wale Akinfaderin (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Dheeraj Hegde (AWS)
abstract: Stand up a continuous evaluation pipeline for your generative AI applications. In this hands-on workshop, you'll build an end-to-end evals infrastructure using Amazon Bedrock and open-source tooling. We cover designing evaluation datasets, implementing automated scoring (LLM-as-judge and programmatic metrics), tracking model performance over time, and triggering alerts on quality regressions. Leave with a working pipeline you can adapt for your organization's models and prompts.

title: Build and Deploy an eve Agent with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)
abstract: Build and deploy a personalized eve agent with Vercel and AWS in this hands-on innovation lab. You'll start from zero, scaffold an open-source eve.dev agent framework, configure it with your own instructions, connect it to Amazon Bedrock through Vercel Al Gateway, and deploy it to Vercel. The lab is designed for a range of builders: beginners and non-technical users can quickly build and launch a functional agent, while more advanced engineers can explore how the same agent architecture can connect to AWS services and enterprise data sources such as Aurora, S3, or DynamoDB using Vercel and AWS native integration and advanced Vercel networking. Along the way, you'll learn how Vercel and AWS work together to help teams move from Al prototype to production-ready application. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Build and test HA/DR architectures for Microsoft workloads on AWS
services: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery;AWS Systems Manager
speakers: Kevin Sookhan (AWS); Chase Lindeman (Amazon); Luciano Bernardes (AWS); Sagal Farah (AWS); Sivasekar Elumalai (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Can your Windows Server applications and SQL Server databases survive a system outage? In this builders' session, you'll find out by building and testing HA/DR architectures against simulated failures. Get hands-on experience with Elastic Disaster Recovery and Systems Manager to construct resilient infrastructure and recovery automation. Measure RTO and RPO in real time as you purposely break production workloads. Explore additional topics like RDS, S3, Elastic Beanstalk, and AWS Managed AD. You'll leave with a validated resiliency blueprint and the confidence to protect your most critical Microsoft workloads.

title: Build an intelligent contact center with Zendesk and AWS (sponsored by Zendesk)
speakers: Nuri Gocay (Zendesk, Inc.)
abstract: Contact center teams need to resolve issues consistently across channels while giving agents the information and tools to act. In this session, discover how Zendesk and AWS work together to create a native contact center experience within Zendesk that connects customer interactions, workflows, and systems in one connected environment. Learn how AI can enhance voice support by handling routine needs, guiding conversations, and helping customers reach resolution faster. See how human handoffs preserve the customer’s history, needs, and progress, giving agents the context they need to step in seamlessly, personalize the experience, and move each interaction toward resolution. This presentation is brought to you by Zendesk, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a per-tenant observability stack for Agentic SaaS
speakers: Rocket . (AWS); Matt Tichenor (AWS); Venkatavaradhan Viswanathan (Amazon Web Services); Yoginder Sethi (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Ulli Hinze (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. In this session, build a per-tenant observability stack for agents. You'll instrument agent invocations with tenant-aware traces and session replay, build tenant-scoped dashboards that surface noisy neighbors and latency outliers, and configure alerting that fires on per-tenant thresholds rather than aggregate signals. By the end, you'll have an observability setup that scales with your tenant count without a separate data pipeline — and patterns to extend it as your agent architecture grows.

title: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
speakers: Nicolas Jourdan (AWS); Nathan Arnold (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.

title: Build a production multi-tier application on Amazon ECS
speakers: Simone Tallevi-Diotallevi (AWS); Guillaume Delacour (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tier containerized architecture on Amazon ECS from scratch. Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build a team shared agent workflow from issue to tested PR
abstract: How do you let agents carry development work across teammates without handing over control? In this code talk, build an issue-to-review workflow that you can share with your team. Follow the code and configuration for setting up guardrails, permissions, shared workflows, logging, and best practices, so teammates can steer the implementation or review who requested or approved each action alongside the evidence the agent produced. Bring questions and follow along as we explain why each boundary exists and how to adapt the pattern to your toolchain and approval process.

title: Build a unified student insight platform on AWS Quick
speakers: Jumana Nagaria (Amazon Web Services); Akash Doshi (Amazon Web Services); Mohamed Salah (AWS); Mohammed Reda Mohammed Reda (AWS); Abdilmajide Ali (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Advisors triaging at-risk students, deans auditing course difficulty, executives tracking retention: every university role needs student-success insights, but the tools they rely on today are disconnected, static, and slow to surface risk before it becomes attrition. In this builders’ session, learn how to use AWS Quick to understand your institutional data and deliver explainable, persona-aware insights through one architecture. See how advisors can identify at risk students with cited data, trigger early intervention when a student’s risk score changes, and generate executive ready reports that connect student outcomes to optimized resource allocation and institutional strategy.

title: Build Autonomous Agents and Run AI-Powered AppSec on Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon CloudWatch;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
abstract: Go hands-on with OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock across two builder tracks. First, stand up a fully managed autonomous agent with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents: define instructions and tools, wire action groups for API access, and ground responses in your own data through knowledge bases. Then shift to code security, using OpenAI's Codex Security to review a real vulnerable app by running scans, threat modeling, triaging findings, and fixing one with verified remediation. Throughout, inference runs securely on Bedrock under your account's controls. You'll leave with repeatable blueprints for building agentic OpenAI applications and for AI-assisted application security on AWS. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Build deeper into AWS with a traffic layer you own (sponsored by HAProxy Technologies)
speakers: Nathan Wehrman (HAProxy Technologies); Eric Martinson (HAProxy Technologies)
abstract: Most teams on AWS accumulate separate systems for load balancing, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and Kubernetes routing. Each brings its own config model and failure domain, another hop in the request path, and a configuration that does not travel. This session makes the case for one layer, on Graviton, benchmarked at over 2 million HTTPS requests per second, with no traffic leaving your VPC for inspection, managed and observed from one control plane. Because that layer runs unchanged in every environment you add, it becomes the one part of your architecture that never has to move. This presentation is brought to you by HAProxy Technologies, an AWS Partner.

title: Build End-to-End AI Pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod
speakers: Tomonori Shimomura (Amazon Web Services); Anoop Saha (AWS); Chakravarthy Nagarajan (AWS); Ioan CATANA (AWS); Varun Rajan (Amazon)
abstract: Modern AI pipelines demand unified frameworks for petabyte-scale data prep, large-model training, and low-latency serving. In this hands-on workshop, build a complete data processing → distributed training → model serving pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, fine-tuning and serving an LLM end-to-end. Experience HyperPod's native distributed computing integration with managed orchestration, embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Leave with a working serving endpoint, production patterns, and a resilient platform that eliminates the infrastructure toil of running distributed AI workloads at scale.

title: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI
speakers: Pallavi Bhat (AWS); Abilashkumar P C (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations are accelerating their deployment of AI agents, yet the critical gap remains: proving they work reliably and responding when they don't. This workshop delivers a hands-on framework for the complete testing and operational lifecycle of agentic AI on Amazon Connect Customer. First, build a layered testing strategy using native Testing & Simulation — functional, integration, and regression tests for flows and bots, wired to dashboard-driven observability. Then, implement automated operational responses such as threshold-based alerting triggers pre-approved remediations. You will leave with a reusable testing playbook and an implementable pattern for closed-loop operational automation — reducing manual validation effort and moving toward self-managing AI agents at scale.

title: Build full-stack observability for agents and apps
abstract: When your applications include AI agents that reason, plan, and act autonomously, observability has to evolve too. Disconnected tools and siloed signals slow teams down right when speed matters most. In this chalk talk, we walk through real scenarios and trace an agent's chain of thought across services, correlating agent failures with infrastructure, and using natural-language investigation to cut resolution time. We diagram how service discovery, dependency mapping, evaluations, and IDE-native telemetry come together so you can ship agents with confidence.

title: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
speakers: Diego Santiviago (Amazon Web Services); Swarna Kunnath (AWS); Rahul Pisal (Amazon Web Services); Michael Hume (AWS); Jas Narula (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build hybrid data planes for government GenAI pipelines
speakers: Usama Salama (AWS); Mohamed Salah (AWS)
abstract: Strict national security mandates block government agencies from adopting cloud GenAI. To resolve this, architects deploy a decoupled edge-to-cloud tokenization pattern. In this workshop, use AWS CDK to build a three-phase data plane that isolates sensitive citizen data in a simulated edge environment. You will deploy local data tokenization, route masked payloads to Amazon Bedrock for stateless inference, and reconcile state on-premises. Leave with an infrastructure-as-code blueprint to unlock frontier AI and satisfy federal localization mandates.

title: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
speakers: Tyler Takeshita (AWS); Sebastian Stern (AWS)
abstract: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like physics and chemistry. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for your own projects.

title: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
speakers: Debasis Rath (Amazon Web Servcies); Michael Hume (AWS); Chris Wells (Amazon Web Services); Jay Formosa (AWS); ISHITA CHAKRABORTY (AWS)
abstract: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge for inter-agent communication. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building and scaling low latency web applications with AWS Lambda Web Functions
speakers: Fabrianne Effendi (Amazon Web Services); Jan Michael Go Tan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this code talk, join us to build a full-stack application live with AWS Lambda Web Functions. See how each execution environment handles concurrent HTTP requests, serving server-sent event streams alongside API traffic while scaling on demand. Using Express and React without Lambda-specific adapters, add routing, static assets, runtime configuration, business logic, and DynamoDB persistence. Then go global with multi-Region latency routing, observability, canary deployments, and fast rollback. Leave with practical patterns for building and scaling low-latency web applications on AWS Lambda.

title: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
services: Amazon Braket;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Parallel Computing Service
speakers: Benchen Huang (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

title: Building Beyond the Hardware: Transforming IBM i/AIX Workloads with AWS (sponsored by Lightedge)
speakers: josh patterson (Lightedge); Aileen Curtin (Lightedge)
abstract: IBM Power organizations support mission-critical workloads across industries. Now, there are more infrastructure options than ever before, providing hybrid transformation opportunities and challenges. This session explores how to develop a hybrid strategy that balances performance, resiliency, security, and business objectives. Hear how enterprises are exploring a phased modernization strategy that rehosts IBM workloads in a hybrid cloud environment, connects to AWS, and evolves their infrastructure. Learn how they establish secure, low-latency AWS connectivity and integrate IBM business logic with cloud-native services. This session provides proven frameworks, architectural insights, and modernization strategies to reduce risk, accelerate transformation, and maximize infrastructure value. This presentation is brought to you by Lightedge, an AWS Partner.

title: Building enterprise-scale event buses with Amazon EventBridge
speakers: Tolga Orhon (Amazon Web services); David Roberts (Amazon Web Services); Rana Kiziltoprak German (Amazon Web Services); Rodrigo Cabrera (AWS); Robert Hanuschke (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Discover how Amazon EventBridge enhanced Custom event bus simplifies enterprise-scale event routing across accounts and teams. In this hands-on builders' session, you will create a central Custom event bus that connects multiple domains, so teams can publish and consume events without depending on each other. Bring existing producers onboard by publishing events in open formats, configure Subscribers for each application independently to receive only the events it needs, recover from missed events with point-in-time replay, and keep related events in sequence with ordered delivery. Work in small groups with AWS experts. Bring your laptop and come ready to build!

title: Building event-driven architectures in the age of AI agents
speakers: Rajesh Kumar Pandey (Amazon); Tarun Rai Madan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Event-driven architectures have powered serverless applications for a decade. Now AI agents bring non-deterministic producers, multi-step reasoning chains, and agent-to-agent coordination via events. Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.

title: Building event-driven, multi-agent swarms on serverless
speakers: Alexander Günsche (AWS); Ben Freiberg (AWS)
abstract: Multi-agent AI systems need communication that is decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we show how to coordinate swarms of independent agents through event choreography on Amazon EventBridge. Each agent reacts to events and emits new ones rather than being told what to do by a central controller. We discuss how to handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and runaway event loops (circular delegation), and how to prevent independent agents from taking conflicting actions.

title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
speakers: Rajeev Joshi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

title: Building hybrid satellite and cloud networks with Amazon Leo
abstract: Learn how low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite connectivity is changing the way organizations build hybrid networks. This session explores how Amazon Leo satellite constellations integrate with AWS networking services to extend cloud connectivity to remote and hard-to-reach locations. We cover new innovations in space-based networking, including how to add network resiliency and architect hybrid satellite-cloud networks. Whether you're looking to improve coverage for distributed operations or exploring new connectivity options, come learn how satellite networking fits into your cloud network strategy.

title: Building migration readiness when the timeline is tight
speakers: Katherine Garber (The Vanguard Group); David Piet (Amazon Web Services); Sean Lewis (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most organizations don't get years to plan a large-scale migration. Licensing changes, compliance requirements, or rising hardware costs can compress your timeline fast. This session covers how to build readiness quickly so your team can move hundreds of workloads with confidence. Learn how to assess your environment, build team capability, and match the right migration pathway to each workload. Hear Vanguard who moved hundreds of applications under real pressure with zero critical outages. Walk away with a practical framework for getting your organization ready to move at any speed.

title: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless
speakers: Erik Hanchett (Amazon Web Services); Felix Gerberding (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, discover how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services—from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Building optimized enterprise HPC systems for CAE and CFD
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Sandeep Sovani (Amazon Web Services); Francesco Ruffino (AWS)
abstract: High-fidelity Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations require significant compute infrastructure. We’ll discuss how organizations are migrating CAE and CFD workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development. Learn how to architect your enterprise HPC system to optimize cost, queue wait times, and throughput with Amazon EC2 HPC-optimized instances, Savings Plans, and Amazon FSx.

title: Building production-ready agents securely: lessons from AWS at scale
aoi: Generative AI;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Max Tybar (AWS); Hardik Thakkar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

title: Building real-time applications with event-driven architectures
speakers: Diego Casas (Amazon Web Services Colombia); Cheryl Joseph (AWS); Thomas Moore (Amazon Web Services); Simon Dean Lovering (AWS); Sean Kendall (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build real-time features using AWS AppSync Events in this hands-on builders' session. Working in small groups with guidance from AWS experts, you'll implement in-app notifications and live updates, configure WebSocket connections, and design data persistence strategies. Using provided code samples, you'll gain practical experience creating responsive, event-driven applications that push updates to connected clients instantly. By the end of this 60-minute session, you'll have working real-time patterns you can apply directly to your own applications. Bring your laptop and come ready to code!

title: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
speakers: Palak Desai (Amazon); Sabith Venkitachalapathy (AWS); Ivan Velickovic (Amazon)
abstract: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.

title: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
speakers: Nitheesha Myneni (Amazon Web Services); Sai Kumar Samala (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.

title: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
services: Amazon API Gateway;Amazon Cognito;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Edward Sun (Amazon Web Services); Abrom Douglas III (AWS)
abstract: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.

title: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Fargate
speakers: Mike Rizzo (AWS); Islam Mahgoub (AWS)
abstract: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
speakers: John Councilman (Amazon AWS); Brian Bedard (AWS)
abstract: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap. They expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.

title: Building Smarter Self-Service Experiences with AI
speakers: Saurabh Dey (Amazon)
abstract: Great customer self-service starts with the knowledge your team already has, but getting it into customers' hands can be a challenge. In this builder session, explore how AI can help you transform existing resources into live self-service experiences quickly and easily. Learn how teams are reducing time-to-launch without heavy engineering lifts.

title: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration
speakers: Anushree Umesh (Amazon Web Services); Surya Sai D (Amazon Web Services); Theophilus Ajayi (Amazon Web Services); Sahithi Ginjupalli (Amazon Web Services); Leandro Cavalcante Damascena (AWS - Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI workflows need state such as conversation history, intermediate results, and human approvals, but managing it shouldn't require a database and custom recovery logic. In this builders' session, build a stateful AI workflow that checkpoints progress, recovers from failures automatically, and pauses for external callbacks. Working hands-on with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-step reasoning chains with retry semantics, compare orchestration approaches for different workflow shapes, and deploy a working agent pipeline. Bring your laptop.

title: Building the Construction Cloud: How Procore AI &Amazon Bedrock Power the Built World (sponsored by Procore)
speakers: Thiago da Costa (Procore Technologies, Inc.)
abstract: Construction generates massive volumes of structured and unstructured data, such as drawings, RFIs, and safety reports, that most AI infrastructure isn't built to handle. In this session, we'll break down how Amazon Bedrock's model access, guardrails, and enterprise controls power Procore AI, and why that combination is what makes construction-specific AI viable at enterprise scale. You'll leave with a clear picture of the architecture, and why we think this is the first real blueprint for AI in the built environment. This presentation is brought to you by Procore, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the Intelligent Utility: PG&E’s AI and Cloud Transformation on AWS (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Puneet Goel (PriceWaterHouseCoppers); Satish Patharkar (PG&E); Madhav Ravipati (Pacific gas and electric)
abstract: PG&E and PwC will share how they are harnessing AWS to modernize utility operations through AI, automation, and cloud-native engineering. Learn how a unified data and observability foundation delivers real-time operational intelligence, improves system resilience, and enables faster, more informed decision-making. Hear practical lessons on scaling AI responsibly, operationalizing automation, and creating measurable business outcomes across complex enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with a blueprint for transforming traditional operations into intelligent, data-driven services while building a foundation that can support the next wave of generative AI and autonomous operations capabilities. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Building the machine that builds the machine
speakers: Matt Goldberg (AWS); Lennart Schneider (AWS)
abstract: At AWS, we're constantly looking for ways to automate parts of the building process with agents. An upcoming launch takes this to the extreme, releasing an application that was built entirely by autonomous agents without a human ever touching the code base. The agents built a first version over a weekend. But turning that into a robust application was a much longer journey than we expected. In this talk, we pull back the curtain on this upcoming launch and talk about the machine that builds the machine.

title: Building Worlds for Machines: VAMS and 3DGS for Autonomy
speakers: Eric Cornwell (AWS)
abstract: Autonomous platforms are only as capable as the environments they train and validate in. In this Lightning Talk, see how AWS uses the Visual Asset Management System (VAMS) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to turn real field data collected during Project MAVERICK exercises into high-fidelity, simulation-ready environments. We walk the pipeline from sensor capture to reconstructed, simulation-ready worlds, and the content management that makes them reusable. These environments are not the autonomy; they are what builds, improves, and validates it. If you build or validate autonomous systems, you leave knowing how to turn field capture into reusable simulation-ready environments.

title: Building Your AI Practice: From Business Model to Partner Revenue
speakers: Scott Bends (Amazon Web Services); Erik Farr (AWS)
abstract: Enterprises expect agentic outcomes. That changes how solutions are built and deployed. Traditional delivery practices are evolving to agentic delivery, outcome-based models, and scalable IP transacted through AWS Marketplace. Partners moving first are delivering measurable business outcomes faster and building new revenue alongside their customers. In this session, learn the three-stage practice-building path. See how Forward Deployed Engineering gives partners a new engagement architecture and faster delivery: pod-based, and time-boxed. See where AWS co-investment programs and AI-specific enrollment paths de-risk each stage of practice growth. Walk away with example GTM models and a concrete action plan.

title: Building your first event-driven application
speakers: Tamas Santa (Amazon Web Services); Vinodh Kannan Sadayamuthu (AWS); Akanksha Bodhankar (Amazon Web Services); Mohammed Atiq (Amazon Web Services); Sarath Kumar Kumar (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: J.D. Bean (Amazon)
abstract: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.

title: Build interactive web apps with AWS Lambda
speakers: Julian Wood (AWS); Salih Güler (AWS)
abstract: Web applications need persistent connections, session state, and native HTTP handling - capabilities that don't map obviously to Lambda's request-response model. In this session, see how to run web frameworks like Express, Hono, and Next.js directly on Lambda using runtime adapters that preserve the framework's native patterns. If you're running containerized web apps today, we walk through practical migration paths that move your existing framework code to Lambda with minimal changes.

title: Build It, Govern It, Ship It: CI/CD for AI Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Kevon Mayers (NVIDIA)
abstract: Shipping an AI agent once is easy. Shipping it again, cheaper, better, and still within policy, is the hard part. In this session we treat an agent like any other software, using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit on AWS: every part it’s built from, its skills, tools, models, and policies, goes through a pipeline before an agent can use it. We pull a skill from a public registry, test whether it actually helps with NVIDIA SkillEvaluator, and publish it to a private registry alongside AWS Agent Registry, pinned by version and digest. Then we route each call to the right model across NVIDIA NIM and Amazon Bedrock with NeMo Switchyard, and turn what the run’s checks caught into the next policy rule. Leave knowing how to make each release of your agent cheaper, better, and safer than the last. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Build It or Bring It: Getting AI Agents into CX Faster
speakers: Matt de Neef (AWS); Soumya Unni (AWS)
abstract: Getting agentic AI from prototype to production in your customer experience application is slow, and the gap is widening. In this chalk talk we give you two levers to close it on Amazon Connect Customer. Build new AI agents on the agentic CX designer canvas, describing what you want in natural language and applying enterprise guardrails to reach production-grade quickly. Or bring the agents your business has already built, anywhere, and orchestrate them through Connect Customer using the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. We demonstrate both, then whiteboard how they fit together architecturally. Come ready to challenge the design and share where you would use each.

title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Josh Longenecker (AWS); Pinak Panigrahi (Annapurna ML, AWS)
abstract: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose-built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training across data preparation, distributed configuration, and model test practices with interactive chat, showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. You'll walk away with knowledge to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.

title: Build Once, Deploy Anywhere: Agentic AI from Data Center to Edge with Qualcomm & AWS (sponsored by Qualcomm)
abstract: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.

title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
speakers: Dmitry Soldatkin (Amazon); Apoorva Chandra (AWS)
abstract: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end to end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands on workshop, use GenAI Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations, cutting model deployment time to days instead of weeks, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results. Then, configure capacity aware instance pools with priority based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI compatible APIs. You keep the working notebooks to reuse on your own endpoints.

title: Build production agent skills on Amazon Quick: automate your own work
speakers: Jed Lechner (Amazon Web Services); Mrunal Shridhar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agent skills turn repeatable work into instructions an agent carries out reliably. In this hands-on workshop, you build production skills on Amazon Quick. You author skills from scratch with AI-powered assistance and apply engineering best practices as you build. You put your agents and skills to work automating real business use cases, measure the impact of what you built, and leave able to build and refine skills and agents that automate your own work.

title: Build Production Grade Agents with OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
speakers: Chris Dickens (OpenAI)
abstract: Learn how to ship agents for your applications with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents, powered by OpenAI, and accelerate development with Codex agents. Explore architecture patterns for reliable, governable workflows across enterprise systems, covering tool use, evaluations, observability, identity, and permissions. See how to keep agent behavior measurable, access secure, and actions aligned with organizational policies. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
speakers: Ameen Khan S (AWS); Santosh Setty (AWS)
abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll work through a simulated account compromise using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults. You'll configure vault isolation policies to put backups out of reach, validate their integrity through restore testing, and orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised. Backup Audit Manager ties it together with compliance monitoring to prove your posture holds. You'll finish with a tested recovery playbook built against a live compromise scenario. Participants must bring a laptop.

title: Build real-time applications with AWS Amplify
speakers: Andrés Aguilar (Amazon); Pranav Malewadkar (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to create applications that use real-time data to keep users engaged. In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build Resilient AI Platforms with Oracle AI Database@AWS (sponsored by Oracle)
speakers: Muneer Mirza (Oracle Corporation)
abstract: AI applications demand continuous access to trusted, business-critical data. In this lightning session, learn how Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture helps protect AI workloads running on Oracle AI Database@AWS. Explore proven patterns for high availability, disaster recovery, data protection, and automated failover across AWS Availability Zones and Regions. See how capabilities such as Oracle Active Data Guard and integrated backup and recovery services help minimize downtime, reduce data loss, and keep AI applications operating through planned maintenance and unexpected disruptions. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.

title: Build resilient apps on AWS: AI-driven recovery at any scale
services: AWS Fault Injection Service;AWS Resilience Hub;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Juan Ga Quintero (Amazon Web Services); Jonathan León (AWS)
abstract: Most teams discover resilience gaps during outages, not before. In this interactive chalk talk, you'll use the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub to map user journeys, define recovery objectives, discover dependencies, and run AI-powered failure mode assessments. You'll implement high availability improvements, deploy multi-region disaster recovery, and run the right automated disaster recovery tests that fit your architecture and use case. Walk away with a repeatable framework you can plug into your own environment next week.

title: Build, run, and improve: inside a production AI inference platform (sponsored by Baseten)
abstract: Getting a model to work is the easy part. Keeping it fast, cheap, and reliable in production is the hard part. Sai Maddali, Product Manager at Baseten, walks through the platform behind some of the highest-volume inference workloads running today: how GPU capacity is sourced and managed across clouds, how runtimes are tuned per workload, and how dedicated inference, model APIs, and training sit on one pool of compute. He shows why the teams pulling ahead treat build, run, and improve as a single loop, and what that changes about latency, cost, and model quality. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

title: Build self-healing Serverless applications with AWS DevOps Agent
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Parnab Basak (Amazon Web Services); Itziar Olivera Goicolea (AWS); Jay Colodner (Amazon Web Services); Sahithi Ginjupalli (Amazon Web Services); Udit Parikh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. In this builders' session, work with a deployed serverless application and use AWS DevOps Agent to resolve real-world failures autonomously. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
speakers: Chris Haddad (Amazon Web Services); Umair Khalid (Amazon Web Services); Brian Warwick (AWS); Laks Sundararajan (AWS); MIRZA BAIG (Amazon)
abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

title: Build the right inference strategy on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services); Chintan Vyas (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Generative AI workloads place very different demands on inference. Customer support chatbots and coding assistants may prioritize responsiveness, while large-scale document processing can favor greater cost efficiency. Some workloads can tolerate flexible processing times, while others need predictable capacity and performance. Healthcare applications may also need inference processing to remain within a specific geography. Learn how to match Amazon Bedrock inference offerings to different workload needs, balancing performance and cost while meeting data residency requirements.

title: Build-time context for faster agentic incident response
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon CloudWatch Logs;AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Jared Nance (AWS); Arun Chandapillai (AWS)
abstract: AI agents can fix production issues, but only with the right context. In this talk, an AI agent builds a feature and, in the same pull request, creates the context it needs on call: instrumentation, alarms, dashboards, and skills, all as code. Then you break the live app. Watch an agent use those skills with Amazon CloudWatch Omni and AWS DevOps Agent to triage, find the root cause, and ship the fix. Leave with patterns that give agents the context to operate what they build.

title: Build Trust in AI with Agent Observability​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
speakers: Greg Leffler (Cisco (Splunk))
abstract: AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.​ ​ In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack, optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate and control agent behavior with guardrails to stop harmful or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real- time and at low cost.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Build Voice AI experiences with Amazon Polly and Transcribe
speakers: Veerdhawal (Veer) Pande (Amazon); Nikie Xiong (Amazon)
abstract: Give your applications a voice and ears. This session shows how Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech. See how to build real-time voice agents, and multilingual experiences, with practical patterns for latency, accuracy, and scale.

title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
speakers: Cy Hopkins (Amazon Web Services); Allyn Henderson (AWS)
abstract: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

title: Build Your Defense Factory for Continuous Defense with OpenAI (sponsored by OpenAI)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Inspector;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Matt Boyle (OpenAI); Shikhar Kwatra (Open AI)
abstract: Put agents to work discovering vulnerabilities and driving fixes autonomously with OpenAI and AWS. Learn how to implement continuous defense with OpenAI tooling, Daybreak cyber models, and AWS infrastructure including Amazon Bedrock, drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory. Explore routing findings to the right owners, reducing duplicate findings, and using development environments to validate vulnerabilities and test fixes. As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

title: Can You Stop ALTERED SPIDER? A Live AWS Cloud Breach Challenge (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speakers: Allie Barnes (CrowdStrike); Jay Flora (CrowdStrike)
