abstract: The breach is underway. Watch CrowdStrike Experts put cloud detection and response into action during a live, audience-driven investigation of a simulated AWS intrusion. They will uncover evidence, determine the next move, and capture flags hidden across identities, workloads, and cloud activity. Get briefed on cloud-focused adversary ALTERED SPIDER, then connect the clues, contain the threat, and stop the attack. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

title: Catch bad agent behavior before your users do
speakers: Manish Dhawaria (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic. The same prompt can call the wrong tool, pick up bad context, or quietly degrade and you won't know until users feel it. Amazon CloudWatch Omni gives agents a first-class observability home built on open standards. Instrument an agent and trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Run built-in evaluators to score response quality, then compare configurations against golden datasets. Correlate agent behavior with the services it depends on and investigate in natural language. Leave able to evaluate, debug, and operate agents with confidence.

title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon CloudWatch;AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: Siddhesh Kumbhare (Amazon Web Services); Puneeth Ranjan Komaragiri (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
speakers: Mark Jones (AWS); Jennifer Tipecska (AWS)
abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
speakers: Gonzalo Escarrá (Amazon Web Services); Harold Morales (Amazno Web Services); Elshan Hasanov (AWS); Anuj Saxena (Amazon.com); Rob Fulton (AWS)
abstract: Your application works perfectly in the lab, but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

title: Choosing the right hybrid deployment for your AI workloads
speakers: Shivam Saggar (Amazon Web Services); Chris McEvilly (AWS); Shelby Seward (T-Mobile)
abstract: Organizations are running AI workloads for model training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and inference, across an expanding set of environments, including AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. See how customers deploy accelerated AI across the hybrid spectrum: NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances in Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time inference. Hear how customers navigate these decisions, including Databricks tapping GPU capacity on AWS Local Zones and T-Mobile running latency-sensitive distributed inference, and learn which environment fits each AI workload without compromising performance and compliance.

title: Claude Code: From first feature to optimized agentic workflows (sponsored by Anthropic)
abstract: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Point it at a codebase and choose your path, self-paced in the browser on Amazon Bedrock. In the Build with Claude track, give Claude project context, explore an unfamiliar repository, then plan, implement, and test a change you watch run - no experience required. In the Scale with Agents track, orchestrate parallel subagents across an agentic app, add review and verification gates, then apply Anthropic-authored skills to improve its performance and lower cost. Terminal experience assumed. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: Claude It Your Way: Anthropic on AWS
speakers: Ayan Ray (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your teams want Claude for coding, agents, and knowledge work, and there are more ways than ever to reach it. This session maps every path to Anthropic on AWS. Start with the models, served two ways: Amazon Bedrock, with Haiku for speed, Sonnet for balance, and Opus for long-running agentic work, or Claude Platform on AWS for Anthropic's first-party API. Add applications on top: Claude Code for agentic development, Claude Desktop for broader knowledge work. Govern both with the Claude apps gateway, one control plane across them. See how these layers fit your teams' needs.

title: Claude Keeps Building: How Coding Agents Change Software Development (sponsored by Anthropic)
abstract: Coding agents make sustained, autonomous progress on real software. The question is what happens to the rest of the software development lifecycle. Claude Code runs for hours unattended, works beyond the terminal, and takes on more of the work around the code. We'll show where it stands and how engineering changes when the whole lifecycle becomes automatable: what engineers do, how review and testing evolve, where quality comes from when code is cheap. Live demos on AWS and numbers from our engineering, where Claude writes most of our code. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: Clinical Trials, Reimagined at the Speed of AI (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: Chuck Liu (AbbVie); Terry Morris (Lilly)
abstract: Bringing a new drug to market takes over a decade, and much of that time is lost to paperwork rather than science. This session tells how pharma leaders are transforming clinical development with agentic AI on AWS. Attendees will hear how PwC’s Digital Trial Core turns clinical protocols into structured, machine-readable data, powering AI agents that draw on historical insights and reusable, modular content to streamline study startup activities such as vendor selection, budgeting, negotiations, and trial documentation. Industry leaders will share how these solutions move from proof of concept into live studies, bringing treatments to patients sooner. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
speakers: Himanshu Verma (AWS); Ryan Holland (AWS)
abstract: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.

title: Close the gap between code and production
abstract: Why is it so hard to connect a production alert to the code change that caused it? Metrics and traces reveal something is wrong but stop short of the function responsible. Developers guess which deployment introduced the regression, manually correlating dashboards with recent commits. Meanwhile, AI coding agents that could help write fixes are blind to runtime behavior. In this code talk, we'll explore how to close the gap between observability signals and the code your team owns, what new signals make that connection possible, how developers and AI agents can consume them, and what changes when observability reaches the code level.

title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
speakers: Wei Chen (AWS); Jason Schamp (Amazon Web Services); Patrick Duffy (Amazon Web Services); Sanghwa Na (AWS); Jonathan Woods (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Closing the Loop: How Cognition’s AI Continuously Improves Itself (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: As AI accelerates software development, production systems are changing faster than teams can understand manually. Cognition is closing that gap by giving Devin, its software engineering AI agent running on AWS, access to its own production telemetry through Datadog. Devin uses that context to reason about its production behavior and take action when needed. That feedback loop turns production insights into improvements to Devin’s reliability and future task performance. In this session, we’ll show how Devin investigates alerts, correlates metrics and logs, distinguishes real issues from noise, and uses those insights to improve its harness and workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: Cloud agent work needs infrastructure. We built it. (sponsored by Asana)
speakers: Amritansh Raghav (Asana); Arnab Bose (Asana, Inc.)
abstract: Organizations need an operating layer where humans and agents can run critical workflows together. That’s Asana. As software development shifts toward work performed by agents in the cloud, engineering teams need the same connected approach at enterprise scale. Command brings Asana’s operating layer to engineering, giving developers one surface for project management and coding work—connecting planning, assignment, and execution across the organization. Command works with coding agents teams already use, including Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. See the challenges Command solves for product and engineering teams and how it works against real engineering workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Asana, an AWS Partner.

title: Cloud-native Java on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Andrei Shakirin (Amazon Web Services); Dumitru Pascu (AWS); Sascha Moellering (Amazon Web Services EMEA Sarl); Yuriy Bezsonov (AWS); Laura Schlosser (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Learn how to build cloud-native Java applications based on best practices, and discover ways you can optimize application performance for fast startup and efficient resource usage in containerized environments. In this builders’ session, gain hands-on experience as you learn how to reduce memory overhead, lower cold start latency, and achieve sub-second startup times when building Java applications on Amazon EKS. You will also learn how to use Amazon Bedrock to analyze profiling and thread dump data to uncover performance patterns and generate optimization insights.

title: Code real-time multi-agent AI systems with Amazon ElastiCache
speakers: Kevin McGehee (Amazon); Elad Bernstein (AWS)
abstract: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.

title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
speakers: Serda Kasaci Yildirim (Amazon Web Services); Rana Kiziltoprak German (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

title: Coding event-driven retry patterns that prevent outages
speakers: Dirk Fröhner (Amazon Web Services); Patrick Meiler (AWS)
abstract: In this code talk, you'll instrument an event-driven integration layer with the patterns that contain failure: exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, poison-pill isolation, and replay-from-archive - all live, in code. See how jittered retries prevent thundering herds, how circuit breakers protect healthy services from impaired ones, and how idempotency makes every replay safe. By the end, you'll have hands-on patterns for EventBridge and Step Functions that shrink your blast radius from total outage to graceful degradation.

title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
speakers: Tom Romano (AWS); Matt Kahn (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.

title: Composable Agentic AI: Build Your Partner Offerings for Enterprises
speakers: Sindhura Palakodety (Amazon); Sujatha Kuppuraju (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprises deploying agents in production are converging on a common pattern: distributed systems with stable layer contracts, bounded autonomy, and security and observability built in from day one. That raises a concrete question for AWS partners - does your product plug into the architecture your customers are already standardizing on? In this hands-on workshop for ISVs and consulting partners, you'll learn the composable Enterprise Agentic AI Reference Architecture, see exactly where your product fits at each layer, and build alongside AWS GenAI services, that compose into a single coherent production system. You'll leave with working reference code for an enterprise-ready agentic architecture and a playbook for co-building on the AWS agentic stack.

title: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
speakers: Dan Ronald (AWS)
abstract: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.

title: Compute innovation with the AWS Nitro System
speakers: Filippo Sironi (Amazon Web Services); Sudeep Sharma (AWS)
abstract: The AWS Nitro System has fundamentally changed how we build and deliver EC2 instances, accelerating our pace of compute innovation while improving security and performance for customers. This session explores the Nitro architecture and the latest innovations it enables: multi-host for smaller metal sizes, reduced blast radius, higher performance, how Nitro has helped us in accelerating the pace of innovation, and delivering Flex instances. We'll dive deep into how the Nitro System continues to push the boundaries of what's possible in cloud compute.

title: Computing‑Power‑Cooling Synergy: Building the Future of Global Data Infrastructure (sponsored by Kehua Tech)
speakers: Lane Peng (Kehua Data Co., Ltd.)
abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads is driving new demands for large-scale data center infrastructure, with challenges in power supply, high-density cooling, and system integration. In this session, we will share real-world deployment practices and introduce end-to-end infrastructure solutions, including highly reliable UPS power systems, liquid cooling technologies, and turnkey integrated solutions. We will explore how computing, power, and cooling synergy can optimize data center efficiency, improve deployment agility, and accelerate the development of AI-ready infrastructure. This presentation is brought to you by Kehua Tech, an AWS Partner.

title: Connect and secure service-to-service networking on Amazon ECS
speakers: Radhika Nayar (AWS); Irene Garcia Lopez (Amazon Web Services); Danilo Silva (Amazon Web Services); Pedro Henrique Oliveira (AWS); Henrique Santana (AWS)
abstract: When your containerized services grow beyond a single cluster, networking becomes the bottleneck. Security groups block health checks, cross-VPC traffic needs custom solutions, and encrypting traffic feels like a full-time job. In this builder's session, configure secure service-to-service communication on Amazon ECS using Service Connect for discovery and encryption, VPC Lattice for cross-account connectivity, and load balancer patterns for external traffic. Implement end-to-end TLS, test failover between services, and observe traffic flows in real time. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Connect everything, everywhere: AWS global connectivity
speakers: Shridhar Kulkarni (Amazon); Sidhartha Chauhan (AWS)
abstract: Point solutions don't scale globally. Stitching together and managing dozens of them creates gaps. In this session, discover what's new in AWS Cloud WAN and AWS Direct Connect: simplified hybrid connectivity, smarter segmentation, and real-time visibility across global traffic. See how AWS Cloud WAN's policy engine and AWS Direct Connect's latest capabilities combine to deliver seamless connectivity from anywhere to anywhere. Discover patterns to build a borderless, resilient global network.

title: Connecting sellers with their AWS Marketplace buyers
abstract: AWS Marketplace connects buyers and software sellers at subscription. In this lightning talk, explore how you can capture a buyer's contact details earlier during procurement to reduce friction from purchase to onboarding, support, and initial product engagement.Â

title: Connectivity strategies across AWS Partitions
speakers: Kunal Kumar Sharma (AWS); Rohit Aswani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations increasingly operate across AWS commercial, GovCloud, Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions to satisfy regulatory, data residency, and national security requirements. But connecting them introduces networking challenges that go well beyond standard multi-Region design. In this session, learn cross-partition connectivity patterns using AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and application-layer proxies alongside DNS resolution strategies, compliance boundary enforcement, and operational trade-offs. We walk through architectural blueprints for securely linking partitions while preserving the isolation guarantees they exist to enforce, and share lessons learned from customers navigating ITAR, GDPR, and national sovereignty mandates at scale.

title: Connect NetApp FSx for ONTAP File Data to AI Apps with S3
services: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Nava Ajay Kanth Kota (AWS); Beerinder Mann (AWS); Sean Phuphanich (Amazon); Virgil Ennes (AWS)
abstract: Your AI workloads need enterprise data including documents, datasets, and unstructured content already sitting in ONTAP. The usual answer is to copy it to S3, build a sync pipeline, and hope nothing drifts. There's a better option. This session shows how to use FSx for ONTAP file shares directly via the S3 API so Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker can read them in place with no migration, no pipeline. Your existing access controls and data management policies stay intact. We'll cover the architecture, configuration steps, and how to pair ONTAP's data management capabilities with S3-based AI/ML services.

title: Connect your Amazon ECS services without the complexity
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon VPC Lattice
speakers: Simone Tallevi-Diotallevi (AWS); Henrique Santana (AWS)
abstract: Service-to-service communication in containerized environments introduces routing, discovery, and encryption challenges. This chalk talk explores when to use Service Connect, VPC Lattice, load balancers, or direct service discovery on Amazon ECS and how to combine them as your architecture grows. Understand the trade-offs across latency, cost, and operational overhead so you can match the right pattern to each workload. Bring your architecture questions for an open technical discussion.

title: Conquer Suricata: simplify rule writing on AWS Network Firewall
abstract: Writing and maintaining firewall rules at scale can be complex. In this code talk, join AWS Network Security experts as they walk through practical techniques, and new capabilities, to simplify rule-writing experience with AWS Network Firewall. Through live examples, learn to structure rule groups to meet common use cases and deploy according to best practices. This session will dive deep to keep policy writing easy to manage as your environment grows. Walk away with hands-on patterns you can apply immediately to tame rule complexity and ship changes with confidence.

title: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
speakers: Anubhav Mehrotra (Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.); Mateo Thompson (AWS); Robert Raver (AWS)
abstract: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish in near-real time. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.

title: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra)
speakers: Ofek Haviv (Terra Security)
abstract: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
speakers: Emil Lerch (AWS); Leo Zhadanovsky (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. In this session, learn how to build a CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild using infrastructure as code. The pipeline will utilize AI agents running on Amazon Bedrock to review every change—pull requests and direct commits alike—for security flaws, code quality, architecture, and accessibility. The agents report what they find, while you write rules to determine whether ship...or stop. AWS CodeDeploy will orchestrate canary deployments that roll back automatically when an issue is detected by an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.

title: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
abstract: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She'll share what LaunchDarkly learned building its own AI software factory, and how engineers stay in charge. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

title: Control what goes out: egress security for AI workloads
speakers: Sofía Aluma (AWS); Bashuman Deb (Amazon Web Services); Akshay Choudhry (Amazon)
abstract: Most AWS workloads send traffic out in two ways, DNS queries and network connections, and attackers can abuse both to exfiltrate data. This session shows how to lock down both paths. We cover DNS Firewall enhancements for the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how running DNS Firewall and Network Firewall together gives you one view of DNS security. We also cover URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protection to containerized and AI workloads.

title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
speakers: Alex Livingstone (AWS); Phani Kumar Lingamallu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.

title: Co-Sell to Co-Marketing: An AI-powered, end-to-end partner motion.
abstract: AWS Partners manage account planning, lead management, and campaign execution across multiple workflows. Discover how to unify these activities and build a seamless co-sell-to-co-marketing motion.

title: Crossing the kill chain: IR when attackers pivot between clouds
speakers: Ameya Paldhikar (AWS); Geoff Sweet (Amazon, Inc.)
abstract: When a threat actor compromises credentials in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool can follow. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the detection and response patterns for cross-cloud lateral movement using Security Hub, Inspector, and multicloud telemetry sources.

title: Crypto escape room: race to migrate to quantum resistance
services: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
speakers: Jay Viera (Amazon Web Services); Phoebe Sorkin (Amazon Web Services); Arun Krishnaswamy (Amazon Web Services); Shankar Rajagopalan (Amazon)
abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway and here's a chance to hone your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, ML-DSA key for code signing, quantum ready PKI, and an audit of your PQ posture. Teams complete quests using the AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Private Certificate Authority, and AWS Secrets Manager services. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence to build quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructure.

title: Customer paths to production grade domain-specific AI with Forge
speakers: Deepak Rupakula (Amazon Web Services); Sharlina Keshava (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Domain-specific AI delivers accuracy that is difficult for general models to match. In this session, see how real customers use Amazon Nova Forge to accelerate the path from idea to production..

title: Customize workspaces and build guided workflows using AI in Connect Customer
speakers: Taylan Unal (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Freddy Jimenez (Amazon Web Services); Jen Featherling (AWS); Douglas Park (AWS); Michael Prappas (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this workshop, you build the complete agent and business user experience in Amazon Connect Customer. First, you create persona-specific workspaces using the no-code UI builder, customizing page layouts, applications, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors each see only the information, tools, and guidance they need. Then, you create AI-powered guided workflows using natural language: describe the experience you want, and AI generates the step-by-step workflow automatically. You test and validate end-to-end in the Agent Workspace, seeing how custom layouts and AI-built guides work together to accelerate resolution. Walk away with persona-tailored workspaces and working guided workflows built in minutes instead of days.

title: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: Saurabh Garg (Amazon Web Services India); Yagr Xu (AWS); Debojit Roy (Amazon Web Services); Francis Valbuena (Amazon Web Services); Ankita Saxena (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.

title: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
services: AWS Direct Connect;AWS Transit Gateway;AWS Interconnect
speakers: Jordan Rojas Garcia (AWS); Daniel Neri (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services, including AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN. But when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Attendees gain clear guidance and discover practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
abstract: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS  (sponsored by Veeam)
speakers: Johan Huttenga (Veeam Software); Roy Adiel (Veeam)
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.

title: Data Environments for Agents
speakers: Eugene Wu (DAPLab, Columbia University)
abstract: AI agents increasingly query databases, modify files, and operate applications. Their effectiveness depends on the environments in which they act: what information they can discover, which alternatives they can explore, and what happens when they make mistakes. This session examines how data environments can help agents accomplish more while bounding the consequences of failure. Drawing on research from Columbia’s Data, Agents, and Processes Lab, we explore branching and recovery across databases and live execution state, data flow controls that enforce policies and guide agent behavior, and evaluations that reveal bottlenecks in finding and using information. Participants will leave with a framework for reasoning about the responsibilities of models, execution systems, and human interfaces when building agentic applications.

title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
speakers: Shreyas Adiyodi (Amazon Web Services); Xulong Gao (Amazon Web Services); Haoming Li (Tencent)
abstract: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.

title: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
speakers: Danny Christian Johnston (AWS); Stuart Lupton (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Risks to data availability are intensifying, and the cost of getting recovery wrong is rising. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. The result is a playbook for how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.

title: Decision Frameworks, Evaluation, and Cost Management with Amazon Quick
speakers: Sagar Rao (Amazon Web Services); Sandhya Khanderia (Amazon)
abstract: Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path — Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents — and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We'll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog — you'll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and ROI story.

title: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Step Functions
speakers: Masatoshi Hayashi (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.); Matthew Meckes (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora DSQL and its architecture
speakers: Seung Yeol Hyun (Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.); Marc Bowes (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that uses decades of Amazon innovation and operational excellence. In this session, dive into the design and key innovative technologies that make Aurora DSQL the ideal choice for new applications and applications that require the highest level of resilience. Learn how active-active architecture in Aurora DSQL delivers single- and multi-Region resiliency and virtually unlimited scale

title: Deep dive into Amazon DocumentDB and its innovations
speakers: Jim Mlodgenski (Amazon Web Services); Robin Golden (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a serverless, fully managed, MongoDB API-compatible document database service. In this session, take a deep dive into the most exciting features Amazon DocumentDB offers including serverless, enhanced compression, performance upgrades, and the latest query APIs. Learn how the implementation of these features in your organization can improve resilience, performance, and the effectiveness of your applications.

title: Deep dive into Elastic Load Balancing for modern workloads
services: Amazon Route 53;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
speakers: Felipe da Silva (AWS); Milind Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, GWLB transparent inspection architecture, and deployment patterns. Topics include performance optimization, troubleshooting methodologies, QUIC support, and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS, learn practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance.

title: Deep dive into networking architectures for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes
speakers: YoungJoon Jeong (AWS); Sheng Chen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore hybrid networking design patterns for Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.

title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
speakers: Perry Carpenter (KnowBe4, Inc.)
abstract: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.

title: Defense-in-Depth for Containers on Amazon EKS: A Layering Story
abstract: On a default Amazon EKS cluster, a single pod is a compromise away from the whole cluster - shared node credentials, flat networking, implicit trust, open egress. In this code-first session we start there, then trace how EKS security grew layer by layer as the threat model matured. We rebuild an over-privileged workload live, adding one control at a time: scoped pod identity, admin and DNS network policies, and private certificate trust with zero-downtime CA rotation. We finish by running a lateral-movement attempt against the hardened workload and watching it fail at multiple layers — the whole point of defense-in-depth.

title: Delivering Measurable Customer Business Outcomes
speakers: Peter Andrew Gratzke (Amazon Web Services); Winston Chung (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Proving business impact at the C-suite level is what separates a deployment partner from a strategic advisor. That's where the Value Realization Plan (VRP) comes in, the structured approach at the heart of the AWS Business Value Realization motion. We'll cover building a compelling case for change, defining KPIs that resonate with executives, and driving adoption through change management. Learn the pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact in terms executives act on. Leave with a repeatable approach for your next engagement and a foundation for a customer success practice that scales.

title: Delivering next-generation quantum hardware on Amazon Braket
speakers: Eric Kessler (AWS)
abstract: In this session, we discuss bringing next-generation quantum devices to Amazon Braket and dive deep on how our hardware and software capabilities unlock fault-tolerant quantum computing for our customers. We share early results and outline how organizations can begin preparing today for the fault-tolerant era.

title: Demystifying Aurora DSQL transactions and concurrency control
speakers: Mike Hershey (Amazon); Aditya Samant (Amazon)
abstract: Join this session to learn about Amazon Aurora DSQL's optimistic concurrency control (OCC). Explore building an application to understand the impact of OCC on your relational workloads, how it differs from traditional databases, and how to achieve the desired semantics in DSQL's OCC model.

title: Demystifying the shared security model on Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Fargate;AWS IAM Identity Center
aoi: Application Security;Network & Infrastructure Security;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Jooyoung Kim (AWS); Sai Charan Teja Gopaluni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running containers in production demands security controls at every layer. This chalk talk covers the Amazon ECS shared responsibility model, including IAM policies for task isolation, VPC networking with awsvpc mode, and runtime protections. Explore how Amazon ECS Managed Instances and AWS Fargate automates security patching and enforces instance refresh cycles while maintaining workload availability. Discuss practical patterns for secrets injection, image scanning, and network segmentation. Bring questions about securing your specific container architectures for an open technical discussion.

title: Deploy a HIPAA-Compliant AI Agent with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
speakers: Adam Birnbaum (AWS); Shreya Singh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your clinical team wants an AI agent that summarizes patient notes—but one leaked SSN means a $1.5M HIPAA penalty. In this session, we build a working Amazon Bedrock Agent with HIPAA controls baked in. Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
speakers: Jeff Underhill (AWS); Kinnar Sen (AWS)
abstract: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. This session explores how customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across distinct patterns, each offering different trade-offs between isolation, latency, and performance across our instance families. We cover isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-second, and capacity planning at scale. Attendees leave with a decision model for selecting the right pattern based on their scale, security posture, and operational maturity.

title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
speakers: Samyak Kathane (Amazon Web Services); Kiran Chukkala (AWS)
abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

title: Deploy AI planning teammates without changing how your team works
speakers: Megha Tak (AWS); Ameet Vaswani (Amazon Web Services); Sid Millspaugh (RealTruck)
abstract: Most planning tools force your team to change how they work. See the opposite approach. Watch AI teammates plug into the workflows your planners already follow, connect to the systems you already run, and improve as they learn your business. You will see a live product walkthrough, learn where AI takes work off your team's plate, and leave with a clear picture of how to add planning capacity without retraining people or rebuilding your stack.

title: Deploy infrastructure with speed and safety using AWS CloudFormation
speakers: Kevin DeJong (AWS); Mihir Surani (Amazon)
abstract: In this workshop, build and test AWS CloudFormation templates hands-on. Create stacks to deploy and manage resources, then use the CloudFormation Language Server to author with real-time validation in your IDE. Explore testing tools—cfn-lint, CloudFormation Guard, and early change-set validation—to catch errors before deployment. Learn language features like Stack Refactoring and drift-aware change sets that help you evolve templates safely over time. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Deploying mission-critical applications with Amazon EBS
services: Amazon CloudWatch Logs;Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Vicky Dewani (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Saurabh Bindoo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Millions of customers run their performance-intensive enterprise applications and databases on AWS. In this workshop, explore deploying a high-performance application on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS for optimized availability, resiliency, and cost performance. Discover and choose the ideal Amazon EC2 instance types and Amazon EBS volume types for various workloads. Learn about on-demand storage flexibility and performance using Elastic Volumes. Monitor and optimize Amazon EBS using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and observe how AWS DevOps Agent autonomously investigates and helps remediate storage performance issues. Build resilience and fault tolerance using AWS Fault Injection Service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Deploying the foundation for successful enterprise AI (sponsored by Glean)
abstract: Successful enterprise AI depends on more than just the latest models. It requires context that connects knowledge across systems, intelligence that turns information into useful action, and protection that preserves permissions, security, and trust. This session presents a practical foundation for deploying AI across the enterprise—using AWS and Bedrock to move from isolated pilots to governed workflows. Learn how leaders are designing for adoption, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement from the start. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

title: Deployment strategies for highly available edge applications
speakers: George Oakes (AWS)
abstract: Organizations need to be able to deploy critical applications that are highly available and fault-tolerant at the edge. These workloads are often some of the most demanding in terms of durability and availability requirements. Deploying workloads on AWS hybrid cloud and edge computing services like AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts requires planning for networking, compute, storage, and other failure modes. In this chalk talk, dig into each of these services, review use cases, and examine reference architectures. Learn design considerations and deployment patterns for high availability and disaster recovery.

title: Deploy your applications with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
speakers: Jorge Diaz Alvarado (AWS); Pahud Hsieh (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this workshop, build and deploy applications using infrastructure as code with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). Create resources using familiar programming languages, apply CDK Mixins to compose reusable behaviors across constructs, and safely reorganize stacks with CDK Refactor. Learn maintenance and operations tips including cross-account output references and programmatic deployments with the CDK Toolkit Library. Get an introduction to building your own constructs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Design for resiliency in Amazon EBS
abstract: Learn about new Amazon EBS capabilities and how they help you build resilient architectures. We cover new capabilities, relevant use cases, and guidance for getting started.

title: Designing for Operability: Catching Performance Gaps Before Scale
speakers: Jofia Jose Prakash (Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI))
abstract: A training workload had plenty of GPU capacity, yet utilization remained low and training time kept increasing. The GPUs were healthy. The real bottleneck was upstream: the data pipeline could not feed them fast enough, leaving expensive accelerators waiting for work. This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.

title: Designing your AWS network for scale: From one VPC to many
speakers: Christian Elsen (AWS); Mokshith Kumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You started with a single Amazon VPC, and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? Bring your architecture challenges, and we'll draw through solutions together on the whiteboard.

title: Design, Simulate, Ship: End-to-End AI Agents on Connect Customer
abstract: Most AI agent projects stall between pilot and production. In this workshop, you go from an idea to a production-ready agentic customer experience in a single session using Amazon Connect Customer. No months-long timeline.

title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
speakers: Deepak Dixit (AWS); Anitha Deenadayalan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
speakers: Xin Chen (AWS); Bin Liu (Amazon Web Service)
abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

title: DevEx 2026: The AI Era (sponsored by Atlassian)
speakers: Andrew Boyagi (Atlassian)
abstract: The hype machine says AI makes developers faster. This was true in 2025, when 68% of devs said they were saving 10 hours per week, but we’re not in 2025. Our 2026 data shows only 26% of devs are still saving 10 hours per week, but are facing more bottlenecks with increasing levels of cognitive load. The role of a developer has shifted, with organisations moving from AI adoption to looking for impact. This is presenting developers with new opportunities and challenges. What are the organisations and developers who are moving faster, and delivering at a higher quality point doing differently to those still looking for impact? In this session, we’ll explore the results from the latest State of DevEx report, diving into how developer roles have changed, and how you can unlock the transformational power of AI. This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.

title: Diagnose Complex Workloads with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Follow an investigation of a complex workload using AWS DevOps Agent. Trace an application-level symptom through multiple layers of your environment across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. See how DevOps Agent analyzes telemetry, correlates signals across layers, identifies likely root causes, and delivers targeted remediation. Learn practical techniques for investigating workloads and reducing the manual effort of diagnosing problems across distributed environments.

title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
speakers: Keita Watanabe (Amazon Web Services); Toshinobu Akazawa (AWS Japan); Alex Iankoulski (AWS); Bailey (Sohyeon) (Sohyeon) Cho (Amazon Web Services); Henan Wang (亚马逊通技术服务（北京）有限公司)
abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall active generations and letting each phase scale independently. There is a trade-off: the KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still perform better depending on traffic. In this hands-on builders session, run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move the KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn a decision framework based on input length, prefix reuse, and latency targets, with runnable configurations.

title: Distributed transactions with Step Functions and durable functions
speakers: Victor Kazuyuki Shinya (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Leticia Dornelas (AWS); Ricardo Marques (AWS); Roberto Perillo (Amazon Web Services); Rogelio Ramirez Rubio (AWS)
abstract: Distributed transactions across microservices break in ways monoliths never did: partial failures, inconsistent state, rollbacks that don't roll back. In this builders' session, build a payment processing using saga pattern that orchestrates multiple serverless microservices using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions. You'll implement compensation mechanisms that handle partial failures, compare orchestration approaches for short-lived versus long-running transactions, and monitor transaction flows across distributed services. Walk away with working saga patterns and the observability setup to troubleshoot them in production. Bring your laptop.

title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: Amrith Kumar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: This session provides a deep dive into Amazon DynamoDB and shares insights into how DynamoDB is architected and how it’s able to deliver the scalability and response times that customers have come to expect. DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. In this talk we explore the architecture of DynamoDB, and of several specific features. You will understand how we architected DynamoDB to deliver predictable low latency at any scale, and how best to develop your own applications to delight your customers.

title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB using design puzzles
speakers: Robert McCauley (AWS); Jason Hunter (Amazon)
abstract: In this session, dive deep into how Amazon DynamoDB works at scale by collaboratively solving a few design puzzles that may seem simple but are actually complex. Learn how to look beyond the obvious solution to find a more effective and scalable one with an understanding of how DynamoDB operates.

title: Dive deep into resilience architectures for Amazon EBS
speakers: Barak Pinhas (AWS)
abstract: Learn about new Amazon EBS capabilities for resilient architectures and how they work. We cover how to plan your approach and optimize your block storage. Bring your questions.

title: Don't build agents, build environments instead (sponsored by Modal)
speakers: Adam Azzam (Modal)
abstract: The hard part of background agents is the background, not the agent. We'll talk about the common design that software factories have converged to and why building environments for agents is still hard. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

title: Drive multi-server migrations from discovery to cutover with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
speakers: Patrick Kremer (Amazon Web Services); Harpreet Virk (AWS)
abstract: Migrating VMware or other on-premises environments to AWS involves dozens of coordinated steps, and most teams spend more time planning handoffs than actually moving workloads. In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience using agentic AI to execute a real end-to-end multi-server migration. Laptop required.

title: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
services: Amazon Braket;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Parallel Computing Service
speakers: Nick White (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. This chalk talk unpacks how AWS hybrid workflows enabled these outcomes and what enterprises should do now to capture ROI with quantum.

title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
speakers: Rashmi Krishnaiah Setty (Amazon Web Services); Abhinav Duggal (Amazon)
abstract: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

title: Earned autonomy: handing production over to agents (sponsored by incident.io)
speakers: Chris Evans (incident.io)
abstract: What does it take to trust an AI agent with production? This talk explores how agents earn increasing responsibility, from investigating problems and recommending fixes to taking action themselves. We’ll look at where human judgment matters and what gives us the confidence to hand over more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by incident.io, an AWS Partner.

title: Easy Self-Service AI: Design Agents with the Agentic CX Designer
speakers: Alex Schrameyer (AWS); Cecilia Bolich (AWS)
abstract: Creating AI-powered self-service shouldn't require prompt engineering expertise - and in this hands-on workshop, you'll prove it. Go from a blank canvas to a deployed, production-ready AI agent in under two hours using Amazon Connect Customer’s agentic CX designer. Design conversational flows on the visual canvas, blending generative AI responses with deterministic business logic for scenarios like payment processing and identity verification. Connect your agent to external data sources, pass context seamlessly across conversation turns, then test and evaluate your agent's performance using built-in analytics and simulation tools. You'll leave with a working multi-channel AI agent, a repeatable design pattern you can apply to your own use cases, and confidence that your team can build and validate self-service experiences without specialized AI skills - no coding required.

title: EFA deep dive: Architecture, evolution, and scaling with OpenAI
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Trainium
speakers: Brian Barrett (Amazon Web Services); Sujith Katakam (OpenAI); John Pangle (Amazon)
abstract: We built EFA to deliver multi-tenant, elastic, high-performance networking with portability across every instance type and accelerator through Libfabric. The architecture that followed, such as multipath packet spraying, out-of-order delivery, and encryption of every byte in transit, has scaled from HPC workloads to the backbone of today's largest AI training clusters. Now it's evolving again to support disaggregated inference and expert parallelism. OpenAI joins to share how they adapted their production inference stack to EFA on EC2 UltraServers, covering Reliable Datagram semantics for GPU-to-GPU collectives, NCCL tuning, and topology-aware communication patterns that unlock new performance.

title: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
speakers: John Pangle (Amazon); Erez Zarum (AWS)
abstract: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus;AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: Michael Wishart (Amazon Web Services); Steve McCurry (AWS)
abstract: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

title: Eliminate wasted compute capacity with Amazon ECS
abstract: Running containers on Amazon EC2 often means paying for capacity you never use, from idle instances to fleets that drift out of shape as workloads change. This chalk talk shows how Amazon ECS Managed Instances tackles that waste through consolidation and infrastructure optimization, automatically right sizing instances to real demand and repacking workloads off underutilized capacity. Work through practical scenarios on the whiteboard to see how these decisions play out and how instance selection and capacity provider design shape your monthly bill. Bring the cost and utilization challenges from your own clusters, because this session is driven by group discussion.

title: Embed Amazon Quick Chat Agents in Enterprise Applications
speakers: Sujit Singh (Amazon); Arun Santhosh (AWS); Stephen Elsaker (Amazon); Manasi Karale (AWS); Ashok Dasineni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Deploy a fully serverless, production-ready solution that embeds Amazon Quick agents and dashboards into your enterprise web applications. Using AWS CDK, configure Amazon Cognito OAuth 2.0 authentication, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, and WAF to create a secure embedding architecture. Implement the Quick Embedding SDK, configure domain security and token validation, and deploy a working chat agent accessible from any enterprise application — turning Quick into the conversational AI layer that meets users where they already work.

title: Empowering 155,000 people without compromising trust: Amazon Quick
speakers: Ben Haller (AWS); Raji Sivasubramaniam (AWS); Lars Nettemann (Allianz)
abstract: Allianz needed to empower 155,000 employees with AI without sacrificing trust. With operations across dozens of regulated markets, the security, privacy, and works council requirements were non-negotiable. Every stakeholder asked the same question: how do you move fast and still earn the trust of those guarding your company's security? Hear how Allianz partnered with AWS to deploy the capabilities that make Amazon Quick enterprise-ready: protection of confidential information, structured approval workflows for agentic actions, custom branding per business unit, and multi-language support. Learn how Allianz navigated the full approval process and moved from "not yet" to "go" in six weeks.

title: Enabling agentic development loops with a local cloud validation layer (sponsored by LocalStack)
abstract: Agentic coding loops let AI develop, test, and iterate on code autonomously. But agents often lack the permissions required to validate how code behaves in the cloud, stalling the cycle and holding back velocity. This session will show how simulating your AWS application environments locally can enable AI agents to identify and fix bugs faster, more securely, and more effectively than human engineers can when building in live cloud development environments. This presentation is brought to you by LocalStack, an AWS Partner.

title: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production
services: Amazon Verified Permissions;AWS IAM Access Analyzer
speakers: Liana Hadarean (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. Of course, this requires modeling your problem in first-order logic, which demands careful thinking to precisely capture all behaviors of your system. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.

title: End-to-end foundation model pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS
speakers: Farrukh Sohail (AWS); Harsh Asnani (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Mayank Gupta (AWS)
abstract: Train, deploy, and serve a foundation model end-to-end on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod with on Kubernetes. In this hands-on workshop, prepare training data at scale leveraging high speed storage, launch distributed fine-tuning across multi-node GPU clusters with auto-healing and checkpointless recovery that maximizes goodput, and transition seamlessly to production inference on the same cluster— eliminating re-platforming. Throughout, monitor cluster health and inference latency. Leave with working notebooks and production-ready patterns you can deploy immediately.

title: End-to-end resilience for your cloud workloads
abstract: In this session, learn how to continuously assess and validate the operational resilience of your end-to-end business services using AWS Resilience Hub. See how GenAI agents automatically discover and map your application dependencies to give you a holistic picture of your resilience posture. Get actionable recommendations to close gaps, generate regulatory compliance artifacts to meet your compliance needs, and put it all to the test with end-to-end resilience testing to prove it.

title: End-to-End Voice Agents with AWS and Deepgram (sponsored by Deepgram)
speakers: Ed Charbeneau (Deepgram)
abstract: Voice agents are growing in popularity, but most fall apart the first time a caller interrupts or asks a hard question. In this session, Deepgram builds one live on AWS: the Deepgram Voice Agent API streams speech in and out within minutes, with Amazon Bedrock as the reasoning layer. You'll see natural, expressive voices, sub-second responses, and barge-in handling that actually works. Compliance requirements? The same models deploy via Amazon SageMaker inside your own VPC, so audio never leaves your AWS perimeter. Leave with running code and an architecture your security team can approve. This presentation is brought to you by Deepgram, an AWS Partner.

title: Enforce encryption in transit using Amazon VPC Encryption Controls
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Transit Gateway
speakers: Salman Ahmed (Amazon Web Services); Ankush Goyal (Amazon Web Services); Ashraf Altalleh (AWS); Hrushikesh Gangur (AWS); Thaddeus Robert Worsnop (AWS)
abstract: Regulated workloads demand encryption in transit, but verifying coverage across VPCs, instances, and endpoints is manual and error-prone. In this session, audit and enforce encryption in transit for Amazon VPC traffic using VPC Encryption Controls. Learn how to enable Monitor Mode to assess current encryption posture, migrate to Nitro instances, activate AWS Transit Gateway encryption for cross-VPC traffic, and switch to Enforce Mode. Analyze encryption status across Amazon EC2, NLB, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon S3 endpoint flows with Amazon VPC Flow Logs. Leave with hands-on experience enforcing encryption for HIPAA, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP compliance.

title: Enhanced container image access & distribution with Amazon ECR
abstract: Amazon ECR is trusted by millions to store and serve container images, but the way teams discover, trust, and consume container software is evolving fast. In this session, the ECR product team shares where container distribution on AWS is heading: making it easier to find the software you need, trust what you run, acquire it simply, and pull it privately and securely inside your own environment. Through practical examples, we'll explore new capabilities that help publishers reach customers at scale and help organizations govern and consume containers with confidence. Whether you publish container software or run it in production, you'll leave with a clear picture of how ECR is becoming the center of the container software supply chain.

title: Essentials for migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
speakers: Mike Revitt (AWS); Pini Dibask (0547778395)
abstract: Migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can be a transformative journey, offering significant cost savings and performance benefits. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. In this session, discover the essential things you need to know to ensure a smooth and successful migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL and the optimal architectures to enable such a migration. Learn best practices and pitfalls to avoid from seasoned experts who have helped many customers walk this path.

title: EU operational autonomy in action: AWS European Sovereign Cloud
speakers: Zoltan Albrecht (AWS)
abstract: The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is built on fully isolated infrastructure within the EU, operated exclusively by EU-resident staff, with no access from outside Europe. In this lightning talk, learn from the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Managed Operations team what independent operations means in practice and how it works day to day.

title: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
speakers: Olivier Leplus (AWS); Luca Bianchi (AWS AI Hero)
abstract: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
speakers: Yongzhe Ren (AWS); Vaibhav Sabharwal (Amazon Web Services); Ramesh Chidirala (Amazon Web Services); Jim Fernandes (Amazon Web Services); John Dougherty (Amazon)
abstract: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

title: ​Every Candidate, Every Time: AI-Led Interviews with Connect Talent
abstract: ​​Who you hire is the most important decision you make, and the hardest to get right at scale. Built on Amazon Connect and grounded in Amazon’s hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent runs AI-led interviews that evaluate every candidate consistently. In this chalk talk, we show how role requirements become evaluation criteria and questions, how AI agents hold a natural conversation while covering each competency and gathering evidence, and how responses are scored against a rubric tied to specific evidence. See a single job posting become a scored, evidence-backed evaluation. Leave knowing how to tell hiring science from gut feel, and why that shows up in better hires and a fairer experience for every candidate.​​

title: Every Flight Has a Story. Here’s What It Takes to Power It. (sponsored by ZS)
abstract: United and ZS go behind the scenes of the data, AI and technology powering personalized flight stories for travelers at scale. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.
