title: Everything your web app needs in one place
abstract: Your coding agent builds fast but builds across providers. The result: a multi-vendor stack you didn't design, limits you can't grow past, and costs you can't predict. In this lightning talk, see a live demo: one prompt to go from code to a full-stack web application, integrated and ready in seconds. One account, one bill, spending caps you set. Built on open source, runs on AWS. Easy to start, built to last.

title: Evolve Amazon DynamoDB data models with no application impact
speakers: Craig Howard (Amazon); Greg Krumm (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Learn versioning strategies, backward compatibility patterns, and migration approaches for production applications. In this session, architect a solution that covers attribute addition and removal, data type changes, and index modifications while maintaining 24/7 availability. Explore real-world migration scenarios, rollback strategies, and handling distributed application dependencies. The best practices covered in this session are essential for teams managing large-scale DynamoDB applications requiring continuous evolution while serving millions of requests.

title: Evolve your observability for the agentic era
speakers: Matheus Arrais (AWS); Nikhil Dewan (Amazon)
abstract: Your agent passed every test last week. Today the same prompt returns a different, pricier answer, and nobody can say why. Agents drift as models and prompts change beneath them, and a green dashboard won't catch it. This session covers what evaluations ("evals") are: automated checks that score an agent's output for quality, accuracy, and cost. You'll learn how an eval-driven loop catches that drift on live traffic, traces it to the change that caused it, compares models and prompts, and attributes spend down to the agent and user, so regressions get blocked before they reach production. Then see how Amazon CloudWatch Omni does this across AWS and other clouds, covering your agents and applications in one place.

title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
speakers: Theo Wu (Amazon Web Services); Leah Tucker (AWS)
abstract: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver strong price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e and G7 fit: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS per dollar) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency help close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. The session covers the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), a TCO comparison, and a decision framework for choosing G7e and G7 versus P-series instances.

title: Expo Welcome Reception
abstract: Kick off re:Invent 2026 at Monday's networking event. Meet AWS experts, discover Partner innovations, and connect with builders. Sponsored by MongoDB.

title: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Local Zones;AWS Outposts
speakers: Eric Vasquez (AWS); Jared Thompson (AWS)
abstract: This chalk talk covers strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. It demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. The session explores deploying a real-world application to an EKS cluster across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. It covers use cases and design patterns for architecting resilient and scalable applications, following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles for consistency and security.

title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
aoi: Application Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI
speakers: Tim Erlin (Wallarm)
abstract: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Direct Connect
speakers: Catalina Villegas (Amazon Leo); Camden Forgia (Amazon Leo)
abstract: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.

title: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
speakers: Parth Soni (Amazon); Parker Bradshaw (Amazon Web Services); Andrew Krug (Fanatics.com); Tim Strayer (Final Fathom Enterprises, LLC); Ron Artinger (Fanatics)
abstract: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their team shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) an AI-assisted dependency mapping approach that surfaced connections no one had documented (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.

title: Faster tech debt remediation without the setup overhead
abstract: In this Code Talk, learn how continuous modernization enables faster tech debt analysis and remediation by starting directly from your cloud accounts. Instead of manually connecting code repositories upfront, you can begin identifying tech debt immediately using lifecycle-event signals from your cloud environment. The platform then provides an easy path to resolution with automatic generation of pull requests. We will walk through the account-first workflow and how it gets you from discovery to remediation faster with less setup.

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
speakers: Jeetendra Vaidya (Amazon Web Services); Sonal Panda (AWS)
abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

title: Fewer Incidents, Faster Fixes: Expert-led Cloud Operations on AWS
abstract: Automation can close tickets, but it takes human expertise to understand your business, anticipate what's coming, and make the judgment calls that keep your cloud resilient at scale. See how AWS combines deep human expertise with AI-powered capabilities to go beyond automated remediation. AWS cloud experts, armed with intelligent tooling and deep environmental context, proactively identify risks, guide architectural decisions, and help your team navigate complex challenges automation alone can't solve. Through real-world examples, see how this expert-led approach reduces incidents, accelerates resolution, and frees engineers to focus on innovation.

title: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: John Terhune (Amazon Web Services); Robert McCauley (AWS); Arjan Schaaf (Amazon Web Services); Greg Krumm (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Anthony Thunyin (Amazon Web Services); Shiju Purushothaman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
speakers: Matthew Lanza (Amazon); Ricardo Piqueras Bonet (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Find, prove, and fix code vulnerabilities with AWS Continuum
speakers: Pat Gaw (AWS)
abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. In this builders' session, use AWS Continuum to close that gap end to end on a live application. You build a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is actually reachable, confirm exploitability through a sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generate a validated fix. You will see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. Leave able to move your team from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.

title: Find the waste hiding in your accelerator fleetÂ
abstract: GPU and AI accelerators are the most expensive resources your teams run â€” and the hardest to observe when shared across teams. Most platform owners can't tell which workload is using which device, whether it's working or idle, or what a stalled run is costing per hour. When something degrades, teams find out after a crash or a surprise bill.Â This lightning talk explores how to spot what's sitting idle, pinpoint a failing device without sacrificing the healthy ones around it, and prioritize fixes by how much spend you can recover.

title: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Open models on Amazon SageMaker (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Curt Lockhart (NVIDIA); Sandeep Raveesh (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Open models using Amazon SageMaker without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting NVIDIA's open models to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: First principles at LLM scale: Architecting Forge
speakers: Omid Razavi (Amazon); Anjali Narayan-Chen (Amazon)
abstract: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we assumed the hardest problems would be ML problems. They weren't. They were classical problems Amazon's been solving for years, at a new scale. Same Well-Architected principles, evolved techniques. We will deep-dive into three workloads from the team behind Forge. First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. Leave with lessons for your own AI platform.

title: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Sai Vennam (Amazon Web Services); Lucas Soriano Alves Duarte (AWS)
abstract: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.

title: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Mona Mona (AWS); Vinay Arora (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.

title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
speakers: Matt Bollinger (Amazon Web Services); Aneel Murari (AWS)
abstract: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Using Bedrock's multi-model routing, each agent selects the optimal foundation model for its task. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.

title: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Trainium
speakers: Chelsie Zhang (Amazon)
abstract: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We'll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. These patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and inference from a single accelerator to 20,000. You will leave able to assemble this resiliency stack yourself and keep training and inference running through hardware failures.

title: From AI proof of concepts to enterprise-grade production systems on Ubuntu (sponsored by Canonical)
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Aaron Whitehouse (Canonical)
abstract: AI stacks are complex, interdependent, and high-stakes. Spinning an AI prototype is easy while making it enterprise-ready is much more challenging. Most organizations can’t keep track of their dependencies within their AI projects, leading to solutions that fail security checks and break easily. How do you move to a robust, secure AI solution that is built to last? Learn how to architect, secure, and maintain a resilient enterprise-grade AI infrastructure on Ubuntu, without sacrificing speed. This presentation is brought to you by Canonical, an AWS Partner.

title: From AI to Action: Powering Agentic Enterprises with AWS and Infosys (sponsored by Infosys)
abstract: As AI evolves from generating insights to driving action, leading organizations are adopting intelligent agents to transform how work gets done. Hear from enterprise leaders as they share their journeys to building agentic businesses with AWS and Infosys, accelerating decision making, improving productivity, and unlocking measurable business value at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Infosys, an AWS Partner.

title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
speakers: Fabio Grimaldi (AWS); Benoit de Chateauvieux (AWS)
abstract: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

title: From code to production in seconds — building web apps that last
abstract: Getting a web application live is fast. Keeping it running, reliable, and affordable as you grow is the hard part. In this chalk talk, we dig into the developer journey from first deploy to production scale: zero-config deployment, full-stack provisioning with open-source building blocks, and how to scale without starting over. Bring your questions about framework support, backend integration, and pricing.

title: From Confirmed Exploit to AWS WAF Rule in Minutes (sponsored by Terra)
speakers: Spencer Chin (Terra Security)
abstract: A confirmed exploit still needs a code fix, and that fix often takes days or weeks. The exploit path stays open the whole time. This session shows how Terra Security turns a validated pentest finding into a scoped virtual patch inside the application's existing AWS WAF: matched to the specific attack, not a site-wide block, activated by a human on your team, and checked against both the exploit and normal traffic before you trust it. You will leave with a clear picture of how the integration works and a model for closing the gap between proof and fix without breaking the app you are protecting. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: From Dashboards to Agents: Building an Agentic NOC (sponsored by Selector AI)
topic: Artificial Intelligence;Hybrid Cloud & Multicloud;Networking & Content Delivery
speakers: Michael Bonnett Jr (Selector)
abstract: For decades, NOCs have been built around dashboards, alerts, and humans manually stitching together signals from dozens of disconnected tools. That model is breaking under the complexity of modern hybrid networks and sprawling multi-cloud estates. Simply bolting AI onto existing monitoring tools isn't enough to fix it. This talk reimagines the NOC around purpose-built agents built for cloud-scale operations, each progressing through a five-stage maturity model (Observe, Monitor, Triage, Optimize, and Act), that governs how much autonomy each agent earns over time. Attendees will leave with a concrete mental model for evolving their own cloud operations stack from tools that observe to agents that act. This presentation is brought to you by Selector AI, an AWS Partner.

title: From dataset to a deployed fine-tuned LLM in hours on SageMaker AI
speakers: Bruno Pistone (Amazon Web Services); Christian Kamwangala (AWS)
abstract: ​Customize a foundation model on your own dataset in hours, with no infrastructure to provision and no GPUs to manage. In this workshop, fine tune LLMs using the Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization APIs. Work through five techniques, including Supervised Fine Tuning for task specific behavior, Direct Preference Optimization for alignment, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards for reasoning, Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback for scalable feedback, and multi turn reinforcement learning for agentic tasks. Prepare datasets, launch training jobs, register models in the SageMaker AI Registry, evaluate with LLM as a judge, and deploy to a real time endpoint.

title: From Fragmented Infra to Golden Path: An Internal Developer Platform on EKS
speakers: Johannes Koch (FICO)
abstract: Every team wanted to ship faster, but each was reinventing the same wheels: clusters, pipelines, infrastructure, access. So we built an internal developer platform on Amazon EKS — one golden path that lets product teams go from idea to running service without becoming Kubernetes experts. This is the honest story of that journey. We'll show how we used EKS as the foundation, Crossplane to provision cloud infrastructure through Kubernetes APIs, and Argo CD to drive everything through GitOps. We'll walk through the challenges that nearly derailed us and share what actually moved the needle. You'll leave with a realistic map of the terrain: what worked, what hurt, and what we'd do differently.

title: From Generic to Industry Expert: The Next Era of AI
speakers: Gregory Mead (AWS)
abstract: AI assistants handle calendars and inboxes but fall short on domain-specific workflows. What if AI could understand your industry's systems, standards, and compliance requirements? In this session, we explore how pre-configured agents, skills, knowledge bases, and ISV connectors can address industry-specific use cases while giving customers the flexibility to extend and customize their enterprise workflows. Learn how AI assistants can go beyond a general-purpose productivity tool into a domain expert for your industry.

title: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda
speakers: Hendrik Schoeneberg (Amazon Web Services); Raphael Hofer (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. This chalk talk shows how to compress that cycle on AWS. SourceFS cuts Android build times from ~3 hours to under 5 minutes, and the Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) lets engineers test against virtual targets in the cloud instead of queuing for physical boards. We'll build up the reference architecture live, show where each piece fits, and walk through the adoption path customers are on today.

title: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia (sponsored by HUMAIN)
speakers: Rahul Randery (AWS)
abstract: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia Building AI at scale means bringing together far more than compute. This conversation will bring together HUMAIN, AWS and technology partners to explore how infrastructure, cloud, data, models and enterprise applications are being connected in Saudi Arabia, and what it takes to make those layers work as one system. The panel will look at partnerships at play across the stack, including the HUMAIN–AWS AI Zone, HUMAIN Fabric on AWS Marketplace and ALLAM on Amazon Bedrock, and discuss what this emerging ecosystem could enable for customers in MENA and around the world. Suggested Panelists: - Tareq Amin, HUMAIN - ⁠Tanuja Randery, AWS - ⁠Enterprise AI Customer (TBC) - Model Provider (TBC: Adobe/Cohere) This presentation is brought to you by HUMAIN, an AWS Partner.

title: From Intent to Interconnection: Building Multicloud Networks in Minutes (sponsored by Equinix)
topic: Cloud Operations;Hybrid Cloud & Multicloud;Networking & Content Delivery
speakers: Ben Thomas (Equinix)
abstract: Modern enterprises span clouds, AI providers, private infrastructure, partners, and sovereign environments, yet networking is still built one connection at a time. Equinix Fabric One introduces a new approach: declare the business outcome you need and let the platform automatically compose the secure, resilient, any-to-any network required to deliver it. In this live demo, see how Fabric One transforms multicloud networking into an intent-driven experience. Watch a simple declaration trigger automated routing, cloud peering, encryption, resiliency, and failover across multiple providers and destinations. See how Equinix enables organizations to move from “choose, design, configure, operate” to “declare, compose, deliver.” This presentation is brought to you by Equinix, an AWS Partner.

title: From Millions of Gamers to AI at Scale: Roblox's Hybrid AWS Architecture Unleashed
speakers: Ivan Marcin (Roblox Corporation); Vandana Tewani (AWS)
abstract: "Auto-scaling was only the beginning. At Roblox, scaling means continuously adapting to changing capacity, hardware availability, GPU constraints, and unpredictable global demand. Join Roblox to learn how they combine AWS with on-premises infrastructure to dynamically place workloads across regions, architectures, and AI providers. Using EC2 Capacity Health Visualizer, hybrid scheduling, multi-region load balancing, self-hosted AI inference alongside Amazon Bedrock, and heterogeneous compute (x86, Graviton, Inferentia, Trainium, GPUs), you will learn how Roblox keeps gaming and AI services responsive under record-breaking load."

title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Resilience Hub;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Ioannis Lioupras (AWS); Jean-Francois Landreau (AWS)
abstract: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

title: From proofs to production: Neurosymbolic AI and provable security
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Byron Cook (Amazon)
abstract: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.

title: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
speakers: Amin Dashti (AWS); gzappia Zappia (AWS)
abstract: Great models start with great data. In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Generate synthetic data to fill coverage gaps, then prepare datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, and RLAIF. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.

title: From Reactive to Proactive: Omnichannel AI Outreach with Connect Customer
speakers: Bernie Valderrama (AWS); Jeremy Puent (AWS)
abstract: Every organization is building AI agents for inbound, but who's automating outreach? In this workshop, you become a carrier responding to a device safety recall. Instead of posting a notice and waiting for calls, you build a system that identifies affected customers, prioritizes them by risk and value, and uses an AI agent to reach them before they ever pick up the phone. Walk away with a working proactive outreach engine and the architecture to deploy anticipatory engagement at scale.

title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
speakers: Sagar Desarda (AWS); Andrew Templeton (CSC Generation)
abstract: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers. AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Discover battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
services: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Ram Maharajapuram (Amazon Web Services); Mohamed Keshk (Amazon (AWS))
abstract: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.

title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
speakers: Tarik Makota (AWS); Andrew Baird (Amazon Web Services); Ryan Law (Grab)
abstract: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.

title: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: closing the loop with AWS Security Services
speakers: Jason Schamp (Amazon Web Services); Aliaksei Ivanou (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Travis Rocco (AWS); Kiran Dongara (AWS)
abstract: You start with a deployed e-commerce web application containing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities like SQL injection and SSRF, hardcoded credentials, and a dependency CVE. Using Amazon Inspector and AWS Continuum (formerly AWS Security Agent), you discover and validate existing flaws, reproduce the exploit chain, and push Continuum-generated fixes through CI/CD. When Amazon GuardDuty detects the active exploitation, including credential theft and prompt injection against an AI assistant, you isolate the compromised instance and harden it. Walk away with a repeatable closed-loop workflow: Inspector finds it, GuardDuty catches it, Continuum fixes it.

title: From Workloads to Agents: Rethinking Cloud Resilience (sponsored by Cohesity)
speakers: Monsef Elalamy (HUB International); Theresa Miller (Cohesity)
abstract: Under the shared responsibility model, you own the security and recoverability of your entire cloud estate - and that estate now includes AI agents. These agents are becoming core infrastructure, executing actions across interconnected systems at machine speed. Yet most organizations can't recover agent memory, credentials, or configurations any better than they could recover a corrupted server a decade ago. Join us to see how Cohesity's resilience platform extends AWS-native protections to agents and infrastructure alike, so risk doesn't outrun your ability to recover. This presentation is brought to you by Cohesity, an AWS Partner.

title: From your first Amazon EKS cluster to a self-serve developer platform
speakers: Jesse Butler (AWS); Nirmal Mehta (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The best Kubernetes platforms are invisible to the people who use them. Developers provision, deploy, and scale through self-service interfaces without needing Kubernetes expertise, while platform teams reclaim the cycles once spent on cluster operations and lifecycle management. That is the standard now that Amazon EKS is engineered to deliver. Come hear how EKS sees developer experience evolving: Auto Mode removing undifferentiated operational load through managed compute, scaling, and add-ons; EKS Capabilities exposing AWS services as governed, self-serve building blocks; and AI agents taking on operational workflows (upgrades, diagnostics, remediation) that platform teams have owned for years.

title: From Zero to 20,000 Desktops: Getting Started with Amazon Quick
speakers: Jose Kunnackal John (Amazon)
abstract: Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat just to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI work companion across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing Amazon Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.

title: From zero to HPC: Build production clusters with AWS PCS
services: Amazon FSx for Lustre;Amazon EC2 Spot;AWS Parallel Computing Service
speakers: Timothy Brown (AWS); Matthew Vaughn (AWS)
abstract: Master AWS Parallel Computing Service at re:Invent. Build fully managed compute environments with zero setup. This hands-on session covers job submission, resource optimization, and intuitive interfaces to accelerate workflows for researchers and engineers. Scale faster without the complexity.

title: Full stack development on AWS: bring your questions
speakers: Avinash Karthik Chalamalasetty (Amazon); Andrés Aguilar (Amazon)
abstract: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. This chalk talk is an open Q&A, so bring your real questions and challenges. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.

title: Fundamentals to scale Kubernetes across your organization
speakers: Math Bruneau (AWS Canada); Raj Athavale (Amazon)
abstract: Ready to get hands-on with Amazon EKS? This modular workshop begins with Kubernetes fundamentals and lets you choose topics that match your interests including generative AI, observability, networking, security, and more. You can learn how to optimize scaling with Karpenter, automate day-to-day operations with EKS Auto Mode, troubleshoot real-world issues, and extend clusters on-premises with EKS Hybrid Nodes. Get hands-on building resilient, production-grade clusters on Amazon EKS following industry best practices and explore the latest Amazon EKS features, choosing only the modules that matter most to you.

title: Future-Proof Your Customer Service with Salesforce, Slack and AWS (sponsored by Salesforce)
speakers: Rielah De Jesus (Amazon Web Services); Swati Deo (Salesforce)
abstract: Modern service demands always-on, personalized experiences. See how Agentforce Service and Slack partner with Amazon Connect Customer, so you can cut handle times, costs & boost CSAT. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

title: Get started on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Ritika Mittal (Amazon Web Services); ANSHIKA SAXENA (Amazon)
abstract: New to Bedrock, or considering it for your next workload? In this hands-on workshop, you go from your first API call to a working application in a single sitting. You choose a model, ground it with Managed Knowledge Bases, apply Guardrails, pick a service tier, then deploy and monitor what you built. Along the way you learn the core building blocks and how they fit together. You leave with an application you built yourself and a repeatable path your team can follow to build the next one.

title: Getting Started with Amazon Quick: How a Customer Went from Curious to Deployed
speakers: Leo Ohannesian (Amazon)
abstract: Your team spends hours on work that should take minutes: summarizing meetings, drafting documents, finding answers buried across systems, pulling data from multiple platforms. You know AI should help, but you need to see it work in a real environment before you commit. In this session, see how a customer put Amazon Quick into daily workflows across their organization and watch live as it composes documents, analyzes data, summarizes conversations, and connects to enterprise systems. Hear what problems they were solving, what changed for their teams after deployment, and what surprised them about adoption. Leave with a clear picture of the problems Quick solves and how to evaluate whether it fits your organization.

title: Global transactions in Amazon Aurora DSQL
speakers: Marc Brooker (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for global scale. In this session, Marc Brooker, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, dives into the exact algorithms Aurora DSQL uses to achieve faster-than-light consistent reads, strong isolation, durability, and atomicity across regions. The session covers the specific tradeoffs each algorithm makes and what those tradeoffs mean in practice.

title: Go Hack Yourself. With AI. (sponsored by Horizon3.ai)
abstract: Defenders often drown in noise while attackers move at machine speed. To truly secure your environment, you must adopt an attacker’s perspective. Horizon3 CEO Snehal Antani shares insights from 250,000+ autonomous pentests across 6,000+ environments, demonstrating how AI hackers find exploitable paths that scanners miss, such as credential theft and domain compromise without CVEs. You’ll learn why vulnerable doesn’t mean exploitable, how to validate controls through a Hack-Fix-Verify loop, and where AI belongs in offense and defense: tool for scale and proof, not a black box. This presentation is brought to you by Horizon3.ai, an AWS Partner.

title: Go-Live to ROI: How Partners Turn Customer Outcomes into Revenue
speakers: Peter Andrew Gratzke (Amazon Web Services); Bhargs Srivathsan (Amazon); Karen Hildebrand (AWS)
abstract: The partners thriving in the AI era aren't the ones who just deploy, they're the ones who prove impact. The Business Value Realization (BVR) motion is how consulting and managed services partners are building their next growth engine: documenting outcomes, unlocking milestone-based funding, and turning deployments into expansion revenue. Explore how BVR helps partners quantify ROI, earn a new Competency, build customer success practices that drive revenue beyond go-live, and where the motion is heading next. As AI moves from pilot to production, the partners who own the value conversation won't just retain customers, they'll shape what is built next.

title: Govern and optimize AI agents for desktop work on WorkSpaces
speakers: Ed Mahlum (AWS); Andrew Morgan (AWS)
abstract: Your most valuable business processes often run inside desktop applications and mainframes that expose no APIs for AI agents to call. In this session, learn how to use Amazon WorkSpaces to give agents a governed desktop where they operate these applications directly, just as an employee would. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into scoping what agents are permitted to do, auditing agent actions, and configuring agent identity. We'll walk through strategies for agent optimization: how to choose the right agent tools, select the right model for your workflow, and build reusable agent skills. Applied together, these techniques cut task time, lower cost, and increase the accuracy of your agent workflows.

title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
speakers: Daniele Stroppa (Amazon Web Services); Obaid Kazi (AWS)
abstract: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
speakers: Harish Rao (Amazon); SooJung Lee (AWS); Keita Watanabe (Amazon Web Services); Natarajan Chennimalai Kumar (AWS); Daisuke Miyamoto (Amazon Web Services Japan)
abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways that single-node debugging does not reveal: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass health checks yet corrupt results. In this hands-on builders session, diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults early. The session provides a failure-signature runbook and a triage method drawn from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

title: GPU orchestration using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Local Zones
speakers: Alex Iankoulski (AWS); Siva Devabakthini (Amazon Web Services Inc); Robert Belson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions across the cloud and edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unshareable integers. In this Level 400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision EKS clusters on Amazon EC2 instances with NVIDIA L4 GPUs, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time.

title: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
speakers: Sudhir Raman (AWS); Ali Saidi (AWS)
abstract: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
speakers: Anuj Purohit (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Anton Valter (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Control Tower;AWS Transform
speakers: Evgeny Karasik (AWS); Efrat Manor Portnoy (AWS)
abstract: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

title: HA and DR design patterns for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Oracle
speakers: Javeed Mohammed (Amazon Web Services); Eric Felice (AWS)
abstract: Explore high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) design patterns for SQL Server and Oracle databases on Amazon RDS. In this session, learn about the features offered by Amazon RDS for business continuity, including Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and cross-region replication. Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

title: Hands-on with the AWS Network Firewall proxy for secure egress
speakers: Anvesh Koganti (Amazon Web Services); Preetkumar Shah (Amazon Web Services); Rahi Patel (Amazon); Geoff Sweet (Amazon, Inc.); Hunter Chilcote (AWS)
abstract: AWS Network Firewall now gives you the flexibility to act as an explicit forward proxy for outbound traffic on the firewall you already run. Clients connect to it directly by its proxy FQDN, so no route-table changes are required. The proxy attaches to a NAT gateway and terminates each client connection, letting one firewall consolidate egress for multiple VPCs regardless of overlapping CIDRs. In this builders session you'll get hands-on deploying the proxy and building layered egress controls, up to and including outbound TLS inspection. You'll leave knowing when and how to use the firewall proxy to centralize and enforce egress controls for private workloads.

title: Happy Hour in Expo
abstract: Turn ideas into innovation at the Expo Happy Hour. Meet AWS experts, see partner demos, and enjoy complimentary drinks. Sponsored by ResolveAI.

title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
speakers: Anahit Pogosova (F-Secure)
abstract: Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose. Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

title: High latency! Is it the code, the container, or the host?
speakers: Oliver Smyth (Amazon); Rodrigue Koffi (AWS)
abstract: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

title: How 3M does multicloud incident management with AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Vijay Sitaram (AWS); Chinnayya Ganachar (3M)
abstract: Incident response in multicloud environments is challenging because of fragmented observability and depth-of-skills gaps in your teams across cloud providers. In this session, learn how 3M used AWS DevOps Agent to investigate failures at scale across 250+ AWS accounts and a connected Azure estate of comparable scale. You will see a quick demo of how DevOps Agent investigates cross-cloud failures, reducing the required human effort from hours to minutes. Walk away with lessons learnt and a deeper understanding of how DevOps Agent helps you in multicloud environments.

title: How A Customer Met Surge Hiring in Hours, Not Weeks
speakers: Kate Totaro (Amazon); Vikram Modgil (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: You expanded fast, but your hiring didn't keep up. What started as seasonal growth has become a scramble of manual screening, scheduling delays, and fragile workarounds that can't keep pace with your brand — forcing the impossible choice between speed and quality. Hear how a customer replaced weeks-long hiring with Amazon Connect Talent, putting AI teammates to work running science-backed candidate assessments and AI-led interviews that take candidates from application to same-day offer — evaluated on the substance of their answers. Built on AWS and informed by Amazon's hiring science, Amazon Connect Talent ensures recruiters stay in control of every decision.

title: How AI is Changing Everything (Computer Systems, Education, Driving, and More)
speakers: Samuel Madden (MIT)
abstract: Reflecting on my roles as Head of Computer Science at MIT, Director of the MIT Education Exch(AI)nge, and Chief Scientist at Cambridge Mobile Telematics, I will discuss how the rise of generative AI is reshaping software, computer science itself, higher education, and the ways data- and AI-driven companies create value from data. In computer science, we are seeing explosive growth both in the range of problems AI can solve and in the new systems and tools required to make AI effective, efficient, and reliable. In higher education, we are rethinking fundamental questions about what students need to learn, as well as how we teach and assess our students. At CMT, we are applying new AI architectures to better understand mobility data, particularly road and driver risk. I will use concrete examples and results to explore the common theme of how to achieve the greatest impact from AI.

title: How AI-native startups run untrusted agent code on Lambda MicroVMs
speakers: Ayush Kulkarni (Amazon); Shotaro Kohama (Snorkel AI)
abstract: AI agents increasingly generate and execute untrusted code that needs a safe, isolated place to run. A growing set of AI-native startups and ISVs are converging on one pattern: one MicroVM per agent session, spun up on demand, torn down when the work is done. In this session, see how [Customer] built production agent sandboxes on Lambda MicroVMs, walking through the full lifecycle that delivers hardware-level isolation per session. See how they scale to thousands of concurrent sandboxes and the operational tradeoffs they navigated to get there.

title: How AI-Powered DevSecOps Fueled Intuitive Machines' Race to the Moon (sponsored by GitLab)
speakers: Cherry Han (GitLab); James Blakeslee (Intuitive Machines)
abstract: In 2019, Intuitive Machines won a NASA contract to land a spacecraft near the Moon's south pole — with five years to build every system from scratch and a team of just 50 developers. Join James Blakeslee, Vice President of Engineering at Intuitive Machines, as he shares how the team used AI-powered DevSecOps to ship mission-critical software fast enough to become the first U.S. venture in 50 years — and the first commercial company ever — to land intact on the Moon. You'll learn how they're now using GitLab Duo Agent Platform and Amazon Bedrock to accelerate development toward their next lunar lander. This presentation is brought to you by GitLab, an AWS Partner.

title: How Amazon Ads Built a Service Mesh Without a Control Plane Service
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Lambda
speakers: Garry Galinsky (AWS); Yiwen Luo (Amazon); Soham Kale (Amazon)
abstract: Most service meshes require dedicated infrastructure just to manage the mesh itself. Amazon Ads took a different approach: a fully serverless xDS control plane built with AWS Lambda and S3 that manages hundreds of Envoy proxies serving 100K+ requests per second at 2ms p99 overhead with no long-running control plane servers. In this session, we walk through the architecture end to end: Envoy sidecars on Amazon ECS for service-to-service communication, an edge proxy for external ingress, and the serverless control plane that ties it together.

title: How Amazon Robotics runs AWS Outposts across hundreds of fulfillment centers
aoi: Edge Computing;Global Infrastructure;Robotics;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Ian Cottingham (Amazon Web Services); Gabe Gagliano (Amazon)
abstract: Amazon Robotics operates AWS Outposts across hundreds of fulfillment centers, each supporting multiple teams with distinct workload requirements. In this code talk, learn how the team architects isolation on shared Outposts infrastructure, manages resource quotas across competing workloads, and implements high-availability strategies that keep robotic systems running through hardware and network failures. The session walks through the team onboarding model, failover patterns between Outposts and the parent AWS Region, and monitoring strategies that detect degradation before it impacts fulfillment operations.

title: How a state agency transformed constituent services with Connect Customer
speakers: Pramod Halapeti (Amazon Web Services); Jarbas Carvalho (GA-State of Georgia | Department of Community Supervision); Siddiq Syed (GA Dept of Community Supervision)
abstract: When the Georgia Department of Community Supervision needed to modernize their contact center, they turned to Amazon Connect Customer and AI. In this session, hear firsthand how AI-powered call analysis, real-time transcription, and automated case notes are changing the way officers and staff handle daily interaction. We share lessons learned from discovery through implementation, including how to prioritize high-impact AI use cases and build stakeholder buy-in across a state agency. You’ll leave with actionable strategies to bring AI-powered constituent services to your own agency.

title: How Badger Meter unified customer identity with Amazon Cognito
speakers: Howie Li (Amazon Web Services); Jarred Kohout (Badger Meter); Pranab Bora (Badger Meter)
abstract: Badger Meter provides smart water solutions for utilities that run critical infrastructure. Its applications used to rely on fragmented authentication, including password hashes, siloed SAML integrations, and custom JWT schemes. Managing identity across those platforms stopped working as the portfolio scaled to 4,000+ tenants. Learn how Badger Meter migrated to Amazon Cognito to centralize authentication, improve authentication experience, and onboard new tenants faster. This session covers multi-tenant architecture, AWS Lambda triggers for token enrichment, SAML and OIDC federation, and managed login.

title: How Bayer Designed 50K Proteins on Amazon Bio Discovery
speakers: Christoph Berns (Bayer AG); Milton Yu (AWS)
abstract: This chalk talk explores how to architect agentic AI workflows for generative protein design at enterprise scale. Using Bayer's oncology nanobody campaign as the reference implementation, we walk through the technical and scientific decisions behind a pipeline that generated 50,000 candidates and 3,000 prioritized candidates in weeks using Amazon Bio Discovery. Topics include: model orchestration patterns for generative and predictive models, designing scoring functions that encode biological mechanism (not just binding affinity), iterative feedback loops between computation and wet-lab validation, and scaling considerations for enterprise drug discovery programs. Attendees will leave this session with a reusable architectural blueprint for building agentic biomolecule design workflows on AWS.

title: How Bridgewater Associates uses agentic SDLC to accelerate change
speakers: Sayan Chakraborty (Amazon Web Services); Henry Olschofka (Bridgewater Associates); Peter Sideris (Amazon Web Services); Jason Kowalewski (Bridgewater Associates)
abstract: Learn how Bridgewater Associates, a leading macroeconomic investment manager, built an agentic SDLC platform that transformed the way technology and investment teams work by leveraging AI agents to automate the software development lifecycle. Built as an AI teammate in Slack and powered by an orchestration service running these agents in secure sandboxes, the platform automates every stage of the SDLC—from idea inception through merge requests in GitLab to deploying code that generates investment signals. Amazon Bedrock powers their coding agents, orchestration stages, and custom agents built using agent SDKs. This session will also discuss integration with AWS frontier agents like AWS DevOps Agent.

title: How Context Graphs Cut AI Token Usage by Up to 70% (sponsored by Sphinx AI)
abstract: Context graphs can reduce token usage by up to 70% while maintaining accuracy. This session explores how context graphs help AI agents understand relationships, definitions, and business meaning across enterprise data. We will look at how context graphs capture knowledge that traditional data models miss, and how organizations are applying them. You will see real examples of the architecture and results involved in giving AI the context it needs to reason effectively. This presentation is brought to you by Sphinx AI, an AWS Partner.

title: How Datadog optimizes cost per token for GenAI at scale
abstract: Datadog embeds AI across its product portfolio, and every product team has different needs for cost, latency, and model capability. Serving GenAI at production scale requires an architecture that flexibly routes across frontier models, open-weight models, fine-tuned variants, and Datadog's own specialized models — without runaway spend. In this session, Datadog shares how it built a multi-tenant serving platform on AWS to power dozens of AI workloads. Learn the patterns for model routing and fallback, the techniques that reduced cost per token, and the platform-and-product team operating model that lets Datadog ship AI features quickly and reliably.

title: How EchoStar Turned CX and IT Into One Team to Ship AI Experiences
speakers: Sevrin Huff (Echostar); Tim Baylus (Dish Network Corporation); Brian Dawson (Amazon Connect Customer); Christina Sansone (Echostar)
abstract: Most companies treat conversational AI as a technology rollout. EchoStar, the company behind DISH, treated it as a chance to reset how CX and IT work together. Instead of handing specs back and forth, the two teams now build side by side in Amazon Connect Customer, shaping and testing each experience before it goes live. CX owns the customer experience. IT owns data, security, and standards. Changes that took six to eight weeks now ship in about one week - roughly 6× faster. Hear from Echostar's CX and IT leaders on how they transformed their operating model, and leave with a framework to start the same shift.

title: How Emirates built Multicloud Agents with open-source Agentic AI Gateway
speakers: Shivagami Gugan (Amazon Web Services); Mahmoud Abid (Emirates Group); Rishi Singla (amazon web services)
abstract: Enterprises running AI agents across multiple clouds face fragmented model access, inconsistent pricing, and vendor lock-in. Open-source Gateways provide a unified interface to orchestrate Models across Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI based on use-case requirements and token economics. This session demonstrates how Emirates built a multi-cloud agent architecture using an open-source Agentic AI Gateway as the routing layer and Bedrock as the primary backbone. Learn patterns for cost-based routing, fallback strategies, model selection by capability, and unified observability across model and cloud providers.

title: How event driven architectures go wrong and how to fix them
speakers: Matthew Meckes (Amazon Web Services); Deepali Tandale (AWS)
abstract: Event-driven architectures promise decoupling and scalability, but production systems reveal hard-won lessons. In this chalk talk, we dissect the most expensive anti-patterns teams encounter such as unbounded fan-out, missing dead-letter queues, chatty event schemas that drive up costs, and orchestration gaps that silently drop work. We whiteboard fixes using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Step Functions, and proven enterprise integration patterns, then walk through designs that keep event-driven systems reliable, cost-effective, and observable at scale.

title: How Flybuys Cut Costs by 24% and Scaled AI Agents Across 10M Members
speakers: Elias Sayigh (AWS)
abstract: 10 million members. Limited visibility into support interactions. High costs. Flybuys needed a new path. In 7 months, they migrated to Amazon Connect Customer, bringing operations in-house, and deploying AI agents that now handle 100% of member interactions. The result of the migration has been a 24% cost reduction while improving customer satisfaction. Join this session to hear how Flybuys took control of their member experience, unlocked deep visibility across every interaction, and are now moving quickly to scale agentic AI across voice and digital channels.

title: How Infor Uses AWS Agentic AI to Transform Cloud Operations at Scale
speakers: Durga Dash (Infor (US), LLC); Saurabh Saxena (Amazon)
abstract: Infor (a Koch Industries company) runs one of the largest enterprise footprints on AWS. As that footprint grew, manual release gates, incident investigations, and periodic security assessments couldn't keep pace. Hear how Infor is adopting AWS agentic AI to reshape operations: DevOps Agent for incident triage and release readiness, Continuum for continuous security validation, and the Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens for production guardrails. Leave with a blueprint for agentic AI at scale.

title: How Itaú built cell-based resilience for critical workloads across clouds
speakers: Bruno Emer (Amazon Web Services); Jorge Rua (Itaú Unibanco); Guilherme Greco (AWS)
abstract: Mission-critical workloads require extreme resilience without the latency penalty of multi-region architectures, especially when strong consistency and real-time external integrations are required. In this session, discover how cell-based and shard-based architectures reduce blast radius and contain failures across cloud providers while keeping latency within strict thresholds. Explore traffic management patterns between cloud providers, data replication strategies including synchronous and asynchronous approaches, and consistency models. Learn how architectural adapters enable workload portability and provider independence. Gain practical patterns for cross-cell replication and automated failover, with examples from Itaú Unibanco's production environment.

title: How IT leaders actually pulled off their cloud migrations
speakers: Ravi Kishore (CI Financial Inc.); Boatner Blankenstein (Amazon Web Services); Rama Kolli (CoupangPay Ltd)
abstract: How did other organizations get their on-premises environments to AWS? In this panel, migration leaders from global organizations share exactly how they did it, including those moving off VMware and other aging infrastructure. You'll hear the real planning decisions, execution strategies, and lessons learned that made their transitions successful. They'll also share where they're headed next with modernization and innovation. Whether you're just getting started or pushing past roadblocks, you'll leave with proven strategies and practical insights to accelerate your own cloud migration.

title: How Jack in the Box delivers personalized store reporting at scale
abstract: Franchise operators run restaurants, not BI tools. In this session, learn how Jack in the Box delivered store-specific performance reports and actionable insights straight to every operator's inbox across 2,100+ locations. We'll cover throttle-aware parallel orchestration, failure isolation patterns, and how this approach turns business intelligence into a scalable, zero-friction communication channel that drives operator engagement and revenue. Walk away with a reusable blueprint for high-volume, per-location reporting in any multi-unit retail or restaurant business

title: How leading AI builders push the frontier with AWS Trainium
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Trainium
speakers: Kamran Khan (Amazon)
abstract: Hear from four AI leaders building experiences that didn't exist a year ago: real-time video generation, world models, physical AI, and LLMs for drug discovery. These breakthroughs demand both high performance and low cost to work at all. AWS Trainium helped turn that future into production reality. Each panelist walks through their use case: the specific technical barrier they hit, how they used Trainium to get past it, and what shipping it to customers unlocked.

title: How Netflix auto-selects the right storage for every ML training workload
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon FSx for Lustre;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Shweta Keshavanarayana (Amazon Web Services); Jake Luszcz (Netflix)
abstract: ML training workloads demand fast data access, but choosing the right storage for a given workload is complex. At Netflix, we solved this by building an intent-driven storage layer that takes workload characteristics and automatically selects, provisions, and mounts the optimal storage for that workload. Our users write code once; the backend adapts transparently. In this session, we share the architecture behind our selection framework, how we built a high-throughput S3 disk cache, and how you can apply the same pattern using generally available AWS storage services to reduce cost and eliminate storage guesswork.

title: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
speakers: Aman Goel (AWS); Dimitra Giannakopoulou (AWS)
abstract: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rules—financial, legal, regulatory—yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logic—capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.

title: How Novartis is Reimaging an AI-Native Drug Development with AWS
speakers: Sander Timmer (Novartis); Daniel Pitman (AWS)
abstract: Developing a new medicine takes 10 to 15 years and $2.6 billion, and timelines are getting longer. Novartis decided not to optimize the old model but to replace it, building an AI-native ecosystem spanning information, decision, and physical AI across the drug development lifecycle. In this session, hear how AI now writes over 80% of their RWE protocols in production, then go deep on intelligent decision systems that optimize clinical trial planning, and formulation optimisations that improve the medicines Novartis creates. Learn how Novartis and AWS are compressing the path from AI prototype to production, turning ambition into patient impact.

title: How Paytm powers millions of customer journeys with AI agents on AWS
speakers: Punit Jain (Amazon Web Services); Yana Tarasova (Paytm Labs); Naveen Setia (Paytm Mobile Solutions Pvt. Ltd.); Tanmoy Bhowmik (Paytm Mobile Solutions Pvt. Ltd.)
abstract: Every Paytm customer and merchant leaves a trail—payments, transfers, loans, logins, chats, and voice conversations. Together, these events form a story. Pi Agents, Paytm's multimodal agentic platform on AWS, turns that story into action across acquisition, retention, monetization, and support for 50M+ merchants and 80M+ monthly users. A Paytm-built foundation model learns from 100B+ activity sequences, while specialized SLMs and voice models enable sub-second interactions across 10+ languages. Beyond the customer lifecycle, Pi Agents powers sales, marketing, support, and operations. This session explores how Paytm combines these models with agents to understand, decide, and act.

title: How Securian Uses Agentic AI to Prioritize CIO Investments (sponsored by PwC)
speakers: José Blanco (Securian Financial Group, Inc)
abstract: CIOs face a question: where should they invest next to strengthen technology capabilities? Securian Financial Group and PwC built an agentic AI Capability Maturity Measurement Instrument (CMMI) engine using Amazon Quick that turns evidence into a repeatable view of capability gaps, investment priorities, and recommendations across 20 IT domains and 2,000+ capability criteria. The solution ingests documents and surveys, applies consistent scoring, and translates results into prioritized actions spanning skills, resources, processes, and tools. Learn how Securian moved from periodic, manual assessments to an on-demand decision engine that helps technology leaders' direct investment where it matters most. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

title: How Southwest Airlines migrated 4,500 agents in just 2.5 weeks
speakers: Jeff Grant (Southwest Airlines); Ryan Clayborn (Southwest Airlines); Ayesha Borker (Amazon); Ryan Champ (Southwest Airlines)
abstract: In just 2.5 weeks from decision to go-live, Southwest migrated 4,500 agents across 17 business units to Amazon Connect Customer without losing a single call. Join this session to hear their key lessons learned from the migration, and how the move unlocked more comprehensive analytics capabilities, giving leadership real-time visibility into previously hidden metrics. Discover what’s next for Southwest, including how they’re implementing agentic AI throughout the customer experience.

title: How T&C Empowers Partners to Build AI-Ready Teams and Drive Customer Impact?
speakers: Mark Daigle (Amazon, Inc.)
abstract: Join this session to discover how AWS Training and Certification empowers partners to transform their workforce through strategic AI skills development. A partner shares their firsthand journey of designing AI learning pathways, implementing gamification that drove engagement at scale, and building sustainable certification programs tied to measurable business outcomes. You'll see how T&C enables this transformation, from foundational cloud fluency through advanced GenAI and Agentic AI readiness and leave with a concrete action plan to accelerate AI readiness across your teams.

title: How Telecom leaders are putting AI to work
speakers: Ishwar Parulkar (AWS)
abstract: Leading Telecom operators are putting AI to work on the industry's toughest problems. Carriers are using AI to build revenue, improve network efficiency, deliver next-generation customer experiences, and modernize legacy systems. Yet fragmented data, legacy systems, and complexity create headwinds. This session explores the trends reshaping the industry and the challenges operators face. Through real-world examples and technical details, you will hear about the latest solutions and how leading carriers are building on AWS to scale their early experiments into production results.

title: How the most advanced teams manage the full SDLC on an agentic stack (sponsored by Cursor)
abstract: This 201 technical deep dive covers the AI Software Development Lifecycle featuring the Grok product family. SpaceXAI experts and customers in production will demo proven patterns, covering which parts of the SDLC to delegate to agents first, how to structure review and testing when agents write most of the code, and where the Grok API and Grok Voice fit a production workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

title: How to Build Omni-Channel AI Agents with Twilio + AWS (sponsored by Twilio)
speakers: Safdar Jaffari (Twilio)
abstract: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.

title: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
speakers: Deepti Chugh (Amazon Web Services(AWS)); Ankit Maheshwari (Innovaccer)
abstract: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

title: How to run parallel coding agents without sitting in the loop (sponsored by Cursor)
abstract: Running multiple coding agents in parallel can increase throughput, but only if technical leads and engineers avoid being pulled into every agent’s execution loop. Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon SageMaker
speakers: Tyler Jones (AWS); Kinnar Sen (AWS)
abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

title: How Vanguard uses SageMaker HyperPod from training to inference for custom LLMs
speakers: Kareem Syed-Mohammed (Amazon Web Services); Swapnil Palod (Amazon Web Services); Ritesh Shah (The Vanguard Group)
abstract: Enterprises that own their AI lifecycle across training and inference can adapt their models as fast as their users' need change. Vanguard outgrew off the shelf models and built infrastructure that runs custom large language models (LLMs) and specialized small language models (SLMs) side by side.
