Go inside the implementation to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod powers resilient multi node training and high throughput inference. Hear lessons from engineering alongside AWS product teams.

title: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
speakers: Dr. Nage Sethu (Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc.); Ken Sam Kanagaraj (AWS)
abstract: Buying and selling media has historically been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. This converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self-improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.

title: How Woodside handed SOC monitoring to AWS SIR to focus on threat hunting
speakers: Philip Winstanley (AWS)
abstract: Routine monitoring and alert triage leave security teams stretched thin. In this session, hear how a global energy company worked with AWS Security Incident Response to change what its SOC spends time on. The company handed eyes-on-glass monitoring and incident response operations to AWS, which freed its security staff for proactive threat hunting. You see how integration with existing ITSM workflows made adoption straightforward, and how the combined team sped up detection, containment, and resolution during a real supply chain attack.

title: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
speakers: Saurav Mohanty (Amazon); Prajwal Nag Ramesh (AWS)
abstract: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.

title: Human+AI Collaboration: How Amazon Deploys Autonomous Operations on AWS
speakers: Chris Keane (Amazon Robotics); Elad Dwek (Amazon); Joseph Rosing (Amazon Web Services); Romi Patel (AWS)
abstract: Amazon deploys humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, and humans as a unified workforce operating side-by-side on the fulfillment floor. Learn how Amazon evolved an AI-powered verification pipeline, built with Amazon Nova on Bedrock to validate 200K+ items, into a fleet orchestration platform dispatching foundation-model inference across humanoids, quadrupeds, AMRs, and drones. We deep-dive into the architectural patterns enabling humans to work alongside robots at scale: a serverless Lambda backend that abstracts the robot form factor, multi-vendor humanoid integration, and edge deployment strategies. You'll leave with a framework for physical AI orchestration of heterogeneous fleets while optimizing throughput and cost.

title: Hybrid Kubernetes made simple: EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway for on-prem and edge AI
speakers: Gaurav Priyolkar (Amazon Web Services); Bruno Lopes (AWS); Karan Thanvi (Amazon Web Services); Karine Ferrari (Amazon Web Services); Jarod Oliver (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprises are migrating from legacy hypervisors to Kubernetes-native stacks but need hybrid connectivity without complex network changes. In this builder session, attendees set up the newly launched Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway to seamlessly connect on-premises worker nodes to a cloud EKS control plane without modifying existing network infrastructure. They deploy an AI inference workload spanning cloud and edge, configure pod-to-pod communication across environments, implement data residency controls, and validate failover scenarios.

title: I didn't know AWS WAF did this
speakers: Kartik Bheemisetty (AMAZON WEB SERVICES); David MacDonald (Amazon)
abstract: Think AWS WAF is just for blocking SQL injection and XSS? Think again. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into creative, real-world use cases, from deploying honeypots and shedding traffic, to stopping account fraud and mitigating DDoS at scale. We'll explore advanced configurations, walk through customer-tested patterns, and whiteboard strategies that make WAF a powerful tool in your security arsenal. Bring your questions and experiences, we're here to discover the "AWS WAF does that?" moments together.

title: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
speakers: Eran Balan (AWS); Yaron Sananes (Amazon); Kevin McGehee (Amazon); Elad Bernstein (AWS); Madelyn Olson (AWS)
abstract: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Improving your database agility with Amazon FSx
services: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS);Amazon FSx
speakers: James Kuhlke (Amazon); Andrew Peng (AWS)
abstract: Customers self-manage databases on AWS to maintain full control over architecture, functionality, availability, and performance. Amazon FSx provides the high-performance, highly available storage they need to do this at scale. This workshop will whiteboard production architectures for self-managed databases on Linux and Windows using Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, NetApp ONTAP, and Windows File Server. Learn how to architect for high performance and high availability, implement zero-copy snapshots and clones for rapid database refresh, and accelerate backup and recovery. Whether you run Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL, bring your architecture questions.

title: Innovation in identity security: how we protect the cloud & help you do it too
services: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Organizations
speakers: Kristen Haught (Amazon Web Services); Ilya Epshteyn (AWS); Alan Garver (Millennium Management)
abstract: Learn how AWS approaches identity as the foundation of cloud security - both protecting AWS infrastructure and enabling customers to operate securely at scale. Explore how AWS innovates in access management and develops prescriptive, service-specific guidance helping organizations adopt services confidently, drives secure-by-default authorization across 300+ services, and ensures IAM policies work predictably. Millennium Partners will share how they use AWS guidance and threat modeling to evaluate new services, strengthen their security posture, and give developers freedom to innovate faster.

title: Innovations across the AWS Backbone
abstract: In this session, we explore how AWS innovates on the backbone and improves the customer experience. We cover new capabilities that help deliver higher performance and reliability for mission-critical workloads. Learn about the challenges and innovations throughout this multi-year journey to improve network availability across the AWS backbone.

title: Innovations at the Edge on AWS
abstract: Modern applications demand networks that are fast, flexible, and built to scale. Join us for a practical look at architecture patterns that help you deliver high-performance, low-latency connectivity across your AWS environment. We'll cover approaches for optimizing network performance, supporting demanding workloads, and designing for resilience - giving you a toolkit of patterns you can apply to your own network.

title: Innovations in DNS and Amazon Route 53
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in Domain Name Systems (DNS) and Amazon Route 53. This session covers new capabilities in DNS resolution and new approaches to private and public domain resolution. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify DNS at scale.

title: Innovations in DNS and Amazon Route 53
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in Domain Name Systems (DNS) and Amazon Route 53. This session covers new capabilities in DNS resolution and new approaches to private and public domain resolution. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify DNS at scale.

title: Innovations in Elastic Load Balancing and application networking
abstract: Discover the latest innovations in application networking. This session covers new capabilities in Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) and simplified application delivery across all compute environments. Learn how new approaches to application networking help you save time and money. Whether you're building microservices, modern application architectures, or AI agent workloads, see what's next for application networking on AWS.

title: Innovations in network security on AWS
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Zero Trust;Identity & Access Management
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in network security on AWS. This session covers new capabilities in traffic protection and new approaches to securing internet traffic across your environment. Join us for architecture patterns and best practices that simplify network security at scale.

title: Innovations in Secure Service Edge architectures on AWS
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations and capabilities in Secure Service Edge (SSE) and cloud networking. Whether you're simplifying your security stack or scaling secure connectivity, see what's new across SSE architectures.

title: Inside Amazon EKS: the resilient foundation for critical workloads
speakers: Sri Saran Balaji Vellore Rajakumar (Amazon); Shane Corbett (AWS); George John (Amazon)
abstract: Real-time financial systems, large-scale AI, and mission-critical platforms run on Kubernetes, and they demand a robust engineering foundation. This session goes under the hood of what makes Amazon EKS the backbone for the most demanding workloads. See how cellular isolation contains blast radius and EKS Provisioned Control Planes eliminate downtime during peak operational periods, backed by an industry-leading SLA as clusters scale into large fleets. Learn how EKS Auto Mode integrates with Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to protect the control plane and running pods during an impaired Availability Zone, keeping critical applications available with no extra configuration.

title: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
speakers: James Bornholt (AWS); George Porter (Amazon AWS)
abstract: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.

title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
speakers: Jonathan Nolen (); Timothy Cook (LaunchDarkly)
abstract: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness)
speakers: Nick Durkin (Harness, Inc.)
abstract: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
abstract: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside UK AISI: stress-testing frontier AI safety on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Kyle McMaster (AWS)
abstract: The UK AI Security Institute leads global research into harmful AI capabilities, assessing frontier models for risks like offensive cybersecurity, bioweapon design, and psychological manipulation. In this talk, UK AISI representatives walk through how they built their evaluation infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock, from model access and prompt orchestration to result analysis. Hear highlights from recent research projects and the engineering decisions that make safety evaluation repeatable at scale. Together, these examples show how rigorous AI safety research runs in production on AWS.

title: Instant Play Demos on Twitch – Increasing Player Engagement
services: Amazon GameLift;Amazon Interactive Video Service (Amazon IVS)
aoi: Front-End Web & Mobile;Amazon Builds on AWS;Customer Enablement
speakers: Frank Zhu (Twitch Advertising); Todd Sharp (AWS)
abstract: From game builds to live campaigns, take a deep dive into the best practices and constraints around launching Instant Play Demos on Twitch, powered by Amazon GameLift Streams. This innovative approach to game marketing enables developers to reach potential players and let them try your game before they buy it. No downloads or installs required, just a WebRTC enabled browser and an internet connection. Learn what kind of content makes for a great demo, engine-specific best practices, and the benefits of launching a campaign and how they perform compared to traditional marketing channels.

title: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
speakers: Phani Kumar Lingamallu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.

title: Intelligent Co-Sell in Action
speakers: Raj Kandaswamy (AWS); Tom Thayer (AWS)
abstract: A new generation of agentic capabilities now works alongside AWS Partners at every stage of the deal—anticipating the next move, cutting the busywork, and surfacing opportunity right where sellers already work. This high-energy demo session follows a deal from first opportunity to proven outcome.

title: Intelligent document processing with generative AI on AWS
speakers: Roop Bains (AWS); Niklas Breuer (Amazon.com)
abstract: Description: In this workshop, you build an intelligent document processing pipeline on AWS that turns unstructured documents into structured, verifiable data. First, extract text, tables, and layout in the format and granularity your downstream application expects. Then configure a pipeline that splits a multi-document package, matches each document to the right schema, and extracts the fields you need. Each value comes with a confidence score and its source location, so you can decide what to automate and what to send for human review. You leave with a working pipeline you can adapt to your own documents. Bring your laptop.

title: Intelligent, right-sized compute on Amazon EKS
abstract: Running Kubernetes at scale is a constant trade-off between performance, availability, and cost. This session covers the year's advances in Amazon EKS compute: faster node provisioning and consolidation, finer control over how and when your data plane changes, and new capabilities that match capacity to what workloads actually use rather than what they request. Whether you run Karpenter directly or fully managed EKS Auto Mode, you will see how to cut waste, raise utilization, and get more predictable efficiency for demanding CPU, GPU, and AI/ML workloads. Expect practical patterns and live demos you can apply to your own clusters.

title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
speakers: Abhishek Hingnikar (WorkOS)
abstract: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.

title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
speakers: Laks Sundararajan (AWS); Chaitanya Vejendla (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

title: Japan Wrap-up Session
speakers: 泰宏 Kose (Amazon Web Services Japan G. K.); Taro Hirose (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K); Kempei Igarashi (Amazon Web Services); Issei Kawasaki (Amazon Web Services Japan G.K.)
abstract: This session will be delivered in Japanese and provides a comprehensive recap of the major announcements and strategic updates from the keynote sessions throughout the event. Experienced speakers will summarize the most impactful innovations and key messages from AWS leadership. Designed for a broad audience, from developers and engineers to business decision-makers, this session will help you identify and prioritize the announcements most relevant to your organization. It will also help you prepare to share what you learned at re:Invent with your teams when you return to the office

title: Journey to post-quantum (PQ) authentication in AWS
speakers: Avni Rambhia (AWS); Oren Nachman (AWS)
abstract: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

title: Keep sleeping at 3am: Elastic watches your Prometheus metrics so you don't have to (sponsored by Elastic)
speakers: Jessee Miller (Elastic)
abstract: When your kubernetes cluster fires at 3am, who's investigating? In this session we'll show Elastic Nightshift — our autonomous AI SRE — detecting a real Kubernetes incident and working it end to end: from alert to root cause to remediation, with its reasoning made transparent at every step. Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
services: Amazon Managed Grafana;Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus;Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Nilo Bustani (AWS); Santiago Benavidez (AWS); Lucas Vieira (AWS); Camila Soares Camara (Amazon Web Services); Ingrid Alitzel Sánchez Elguea (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.

title: Koa: NVIDIA Nemotron-Powered CRM Reasoning Inside Salesforce’s AWS Trust Boundary (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Shubham Mehrotra (Salesforce); Petro Junior Milan (NVIDIA)
abstract: Salesforce Koa is a family of CRM reasoning models post-trained from NVIDIA Nemotron open models. Koa is in production on AWS, inside Salesforce's trust boundary. This session covers technical insights on how Koa was built and how Salesforce serves the model on AWS. Additionally, attendees will learn how Salesforce enforces trust and safety controls in the serving layer outside the model. This session is relevant to any team building and deploying custom open models for the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Lab Maker: From Prompt to Personalized Lab in Minutes
speakers: ADAM B (AWS)
abstract: Lab Maker on AWS Skill Builder generates personalized hands-on labs from natural language prompts, allowing you to learn and experiment in the Console without incurring costs or risking production environments. During this session, we will generate a custom lab in real time before saving and sharing it with a team, demonstrating the full creation-to-collaboration workflow. We will then push Lab Maker further by generating a lab for a recently launched AWS service and uploading real organizational constraints to show how the tool adapts to your specific environment. You will leave this session with the knowledge and confidence to create your own labs.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
speakers: Alexander Vladimirov (AWS); Anton Aleksandrov (AWS)
abstract: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
speakers: Darshit Pandya (Serko)
abstract: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.

title: Lambda Web Functions: From Event Handlers to Standard HTTP on Lambda
abstract: If you're running Express, Hono, or Fastify on Lambda today, you're wrapping your HTTP server in an event-handler adapter. Lambda Web Functions drops that requirement. Your code listens on a port, same as localhost. Multi-concurrency keeps sandboxes warm across requests, delivering consistent response times. Active-duration billing charges for CPU consumed, not time spent waiting on a database response. Opt-in multi-region replication puts your app closer to users: pick your regions, code distribution handles the rest. This session covers the execution model, billing mechanics at real workloads, multi-region setup, and a live deployment from zero to global endpoint.

title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
speakers: Siavash Irani (AWS); Shiva Vaidyanathan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

title: Layered security for Amazon EKS: Patterns that scale
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon GuardDuty;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Liz Duke (AWS); Rodrigo Bersa (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Kubernetes gives you powerful primitives for running workloads at scale, but its default configuration prioritizes flexibility over security. In this chalk talk, we work through a layered defense strategy for Amazon EKS: hardening the control plane, implementing least-privilege RBAC and pod security standards, securing the software supply chain, enforcing network segmentation, and building runtime threat detection. We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
speakers: Steve Rice (AWS); Ben Shumpert (AWS)
abstract: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

title: Learnings from resilience testing in AWS
speakers: Gavin McCullagh (Amazon)
abstract: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.

title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
speakers: Tzoori Tamam (Amazon Web Services); Harith Gaddamanugu (AWS)
abstract: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
speakers: Fletcher Woodruff (Amazon Web Services); Todd Neal (Amazon)
abstract: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Erik Hanchett (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

title: Live AI and the Infrastructure Behind It (sponsored by Decart)
abstract: AI is entering a new era: from static generation to live experiences. From shopping to entertainment, digital experiences are becoming live, visual, and personalized. In this session, Decart will explore the infrastructure powering this shift, what it takes to deliver AI-generated video in real time, and how to bring these experiences to scale. Join us for a look at the technology behind Live AI, and where it’s going next. This presentation is brought to you by Decart, an AWS Partner.

title: Lives on the Line: Modernizing National Weather Forecasting on AWS
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon SageMaker
speakers: David Santore (AWS); Rayette Toles-Abdullah (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's National Weather Service (NWS) is modernizing the platform forecasters rely on across 170+ locations. Join AWS and NOAA to whiteboard the NWS Enterprise Cloud (NEC), the foundation providing secure, scalable landing zones where HIVE applications and CIRRUS data services operate. We'll explore decomposing a legacy desktop into micro-frontends and domain microservices on Amazon EKS, decoupling applications from data through an API abstraction layer, scaling independently during severe weather, and maintaining continuous Authority to Operate (ATO). We'll also discuss how Amazon SageMaker brings machine learning assistance to forecasters. Bring your modernization questions.

title: Living Off the Agent: Detecting and Preventing Lateral Movement in Agentic AI
aoi: Generative AI;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI
speakers: Victor Okonyia (Amazon Web Services); Emmanuel Isimah (amazon web services)
abstract: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
services: Amazon EventBridge;Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Step Functions
speakers: Matt Coles (Amazon Web Services); Paul Moran (AWS)
abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

title: Logging strategy for agentic investigations
speakers: Siddharth Bhate (Amazon Web Services); Brad Gilomen (AWS)
abstract: Most logging strategies get built one team at a time. Each team picks its own destination and format, so an AI agent investigating an incident has to search across accounts and reason over a dozen schemas. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard a CloudWatch logging design that centralizes logs and enriches them on ingest with service context, so your agents start every investigation with what they need. We'll debate what to transform at ingest versus keep raw, and which logs earn hot storage. Bring the log setup you run today and we'll redraw it with you.

title: LSEG: Scaling multi-agent AI with assurance on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Zan Kavtaskin (LSEG); Richard Chester (AWS); Christopher Hughes (LSEG)
abstract: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) manages one of the world's largest risk intelligence datasets, processing millions of records that demand continuous curation and validation. In this session, learn how LSEG built a durable agentic AI framework on Amazon Bedrock—orchestrating multi-agent workflows that combines deterministic rules, AI enrichment, and human review to reduce false positives in financial crime screening. LSEG will share their approach to continuous AI assurance with golden dataset evaluations and staged rollout gates with real-time observability and automated rollback to safely scale automation while maintaining the accuracy global financial institutions require.

title: Machines on Call for Humans: Agents to run and fix your prod (sponsored by Resolve AI)
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Manveer Sahota (Resolve AI); Claire Yin (ResolveAI)
abstract: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

title: Maintain accountability when using IAM federation
abstract: Many enterprises access AWS through IAM federation with providers like Okta and Microsoft Entra ID. But if your analysts share an IAM role, downstream services do not distinguish who has assumed that role making per-user access controls and audit more challenging. In this chalk talk, we'll explore considerations when using federated environments, discuss why it matters for compliance and security, and examine what it takes to maintain individual accountability without overhauling your existing federation setup.

title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
speakers: Ryan Bradley (AWS); Thomas Coombs (Amazon)
abstract: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

title: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
speakers: Tim Stoakes (Amazon Web Services); Pini Dibask (0547778395)
abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

title: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon GuardDuty;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Omner Barajas (AWS); Anthony Harvey (AWS); Fabian Serrano Morales (AWS); Shay Grinberg (AWS); Pedro Gadelha (AWS)
abstract: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.

title: Managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at scale: customer lessons
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Direct Connect
speakers: Pratik Mankad (AWS); Dave Gadling (Meta); Robin Douglass Rodriguez (AWS)
abstract: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints, spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Attendees will learn strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.

title: Managing Bots, Mentoring Brains: The Future of Hybrid Leadership
abstract: The traditional playbook for executive leadership is undergoing fundamental change as hybrid ecosystems of human employees and autonomous AI agents become commonplace, with agents acting as co-workers, specialists, and decision-makers. This shift requires executives to expand their skill set, dividing organizational goals between human creative strategy and agentic operational execution. Moving past the AI hype, this session examines how human roles must evolve from executors to context engineers and decision architects, and how career progression must be rewritten when entry-level and repetitive work is owned by digital labor. Explore how women in leadership will adapt and build tomorrow's leaders.

title: Managing Lambda Runtimes at Scale for Platform Teams
abstract: Lambda's managed runtimes work until your platform team needs a pinned language version, a pre-loaded monitoring agent, or an SDK that every function must use. Today that means managing custom layers, coordinating updates across teams, and hoping nobody is running a version you deprecated last quarter. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard strategies for taking control of your Lambda runtime layer. Bring your runtime requirements and the constraints you're working around today.

title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
speakers: Anthony Verleysen (AWS); Nirali Desai (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.

title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Steve Flinter (Mastercard); Gurinder Singh (Amazon web services); Josh Allbright (Mastercard)
abstract: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.

title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon EC2 - Graviton
speakers: Ramesh Mathikumar (Amazon Web Services); Olawale Olaleye (AWS EMEA SARL (Irish Branch))
abstract: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
speakers: Giuseppe Angelo Porcelli (AWS); Rama Thamman (Amazon)
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

title: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
speakers: Ian Bablewski (Amazon Web Services); Qi Wu (Amazon)
abstract: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics—latency, IOPS, and throughput—to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We also demonstrate the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

title: Meet Your AI Teammate for WorkSpaces Administration
abstract: Whether you run WorkSpaces today or are evaluating cloud desktops for the first time, operational overhead follows every virtual desktop deployment: ongoing monitoring, systemic issues that surface as tickets, and end-user requests that consume administrator time. Most teams operate reactively, triaging problems after they surface and manually guiding users through resolution. This session explores how Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor is using AI to reduce resolution time for both IT administrators and end users. We'll walk through the operational challenges we're hearing from customers, share our approach to solving them, and demonstrate early results from production environments. Bring your deployment architecture questions.

title: Migrate and modernize workloads with AWS Outposts
speakers: Brianna Rosentrater (AWS); Vaibhav Phadnis (Amazon)
abstract: Organizations running on-premises workloads on legacy virtualization platforms are looking to migrate applications to AWS and modernize them to be more resilient and operationally consistent with their cloud workloads. AWS Outposts supports customers on this journey and is now available in second-generation single- and multi-rack offerings that deliver new instance types and Amazon EBS storage, up to 40% better price-performance, and enhanced networking features for monitoring and security. This session covers migration and modernization strategies for organizations looking to move to a cloud operating model on-premises, as well as strategies for first-generation Outposts customers to upgrade to the latest generation.

title: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
speakers: Jim Mlodgenski (Amazon Web Services); Douglas Bonser (AWS)
abstract: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Learn a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.

title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
services: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Andrew Crudge (AWS); Luke Miller (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.

title: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
speakers: Kyle Ahn (Netflix); Ryan Coleman (Amazon Web Services); Dharamendra Kumar (Netflix)
abstract: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.

title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services); Mac Stevens (AWS)
abstract: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.

title: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
speakers: Peter Dachnowicz (Amazon); Nikita Buldakov (AWS); Jason Rupard (AWS)
abstract: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.

title: Model customization for industrial use cases on Amazon SageMaker AI
speakers: Oded Vainas (Intuit); Michael Oguike (AWS); Ganesh Hegde (Amazon)
abstract: AI/ML teams want to move fast, experimenting with models, fine tuning them on their data, and serving them in production, without stitching together separate tools at every step. In this session, see how Amazon SageMaker AI lets you build, customize, deploy, and run inference within one service. Learn how to match the right approach to each stage, including fast experimentation for quick iteration, fully managed environments for custom frameworks and training, persistent clusters for large scale research, and optimized endpoints for real time and batch serving in production. See a worked example that starts with a single model and scales to a production deployment without switching platforms.

title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
speakers: Pradeep Natarajan (Amazon); Swastik Roy (Amazon)
abstract: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Transform
speakers: Ian Choi (AWS); Diego Dalmolin (AWS); Jayaprakash Alawala (Amazon); Asiel Bencomo Corona (AWS); Avinash Desireddy (AWS)
abstract: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
speakers: Venugopalan Vasudevan (AWS); Harvinder Nagpal (Amazon)
abstract: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

title: Modernize legacy applications into cloud native event-driven systems
speakers: Chris McPeek (AWS); Nirmal Mehta (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your application modernization using agentic tools. We show how to reverse-engineer your applications and dependencies from existing code, then generate a event-driven cloud native target architecture. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices, deployed as containers or serverless applications, in weeks, and make your applications agent-ready in the process.

title: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
speakers: Aidan Keane (AWS); Gianpaolo (GP) Albanese (AWS)
abstract: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.

title: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
speakers: Phil Seokpil Kang (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Pablo Silva (Amazon Web Services, Inc.)
abstract: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL;AWS Transform
speakers: Jose Guay (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Tekena Orugbani (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress this effort into a single sprint and reduce operating costs by up to 70% by moving off costly licenses. Working from a legacy app, you'll port .NET Framework code to modern, cross-platform .NET, migrate SQL Server to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, then containerize and deploy to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Come ready with your personal GitHub account. Laptop required.

title: Modernizing Care for the Underserved: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
speakers: Matt Dinger (AWS); Deepesh Chandra (Montefiore Health System)
abstract: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations. To best care for patients, most of whom rely on Medicare or Medicaid, Montefiore needed to modernize its enterprise technology. Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider to build a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation—including an Epic migration—enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the patients and communities Montefiore serves.

title: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
aoi: Global Infrastructure;Generative AI;Amazon Builds on AWS;Machine Learning
speakers: Andrea Rodolico (AWS); Ala Abunijem (AWS)
abstract: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) is helping teams modernize their HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. In this session, hear how organizations have moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions that apply whether you're running simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.

title: Modernizing Legacy Telecommunications OSS/BSS Systems
speakers: Visu Sontam (AWS); Antonello Arpino (amazon web services)
abstract: Legacy modernization is one of the most complex challenges facing Telecommunications companies today. In this Chalk Talk, we will explore strategies to accelerate VMware and mainframe migrations using Agentic AI. Using a real-world scenario, we will walk through how AWS Transform and Amazon Bedrock are used to meet the technical and business requirements of these projects and explore trade-offs in migration design and infrastructure choices. Come ready to discuss your own migration challenges!

title: Molecule to Market: Bayer & Capgemini Accelerate Drug Discovery with NVIDIA BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speakers: Lukas Kuckelkorn (Capgemini); Dr. Janosch Achenbach (Bayer AG - Crop Science)
abstract: Bayer's CropKey strategy relies on target-based and profile-driven discovery to develop the next generation of crop protection solutions. A key challenge is enabling broad access to advanced AI models for protein structure prediction, target exploration, molecular docking, and molecular design, which are often complex and costly to operate. This session highlights how Bayer and Capgemini built a scalable, cloud-native platform on AWS that provides researchers with easy access to state-of-the-art biomolecular AI capabilities by leveraging NVIDIA BioNeMo NIMs. By operationalizing foundation models in a secure and cost-efficient environment, the platform helps close critical knowledge gaps in early discovery and accelerates the application of AI across the crop protection R&D pipeline. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
speakers: Arturo Velasco (AWS); Carlos Salazar (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: More than half of web traffic now comes from AI bots that consume content built for humans while returning little value to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both the content and the monetization side. First, you'll build a pipeline that converts images, video, and audio into concise, agent-friendly markdown summaries including interpreting what's shown, said, and meant, while preserving the originals for human readers. Then you'll monetize bot traffic with AWS WAF AI traffic monetization, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. You'll build a working dual-audience pipeline and WAF pricing configuration you can deploy against your own media.

title: More than a heartbeat: Designing health checks that matter
aoi: Disaster Response & Recovery;Monitoring & Observability;Network & Infrastructure Security
speakers: Andrew Gray (AWS); Satish Katpally (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing, not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 that covers how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures, including diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard, and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

title: Move your app to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and forget the ops
speakers: Aritra Nag (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running a production application should not mean owning the infrastructure under it. This lightning talk shows how AWS Elastic Beanstalk assumes ongoing operational responsibility for your applications — deployment, scaling, patching, monitoring, and upgrades — whether you bring source code, a container image, or an existing workload. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.

title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
speakers: Dimple Dhar (Amazon Web Services); Archana Ambavane (AWS)
abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Multicloud-to-AWS transformation: HealthEdge migrating 8,700 servers
speakers: Ryan Mooney (HealthEdge Software, Inc.); Ben Goulding (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers creates compounding complexity: inconsistent tooling, duplicated licensing costs, and operational overhead that slows everything down. HealthEdge faced exactly this across Azure, GCP, and four data centers while serving 130 health plans daily, where security is paramount. Hear how they're consolidating 8,700 servers via AWS Transform, 1,600 databases, and thousands of cloud services onto AWS on a 2-year roadmap, raising their security bar, and building internal AWS expertise to drive a lasting culture change - all without disrupting the plans that depend on them.

title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
speakers: Enrique Bastante (AWS); Nick Dobson (AWS)
abstract: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
services: Amazon DynamoDB;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Nicholas Tunney (AWS); Dave Roberts (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

title: Multi-tenant SaaS and agentic apps on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Kunal Ghosh (Amazon Web Services); Abraham Arellano (AWS)
abstract: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. The challenge is multi-tenancy: how do you run agent workloads for hundreds of tenants on shared infrastructure without blast radius, cost leakage, or isolation drift? In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Each lab ends with an isolation proof. Leave with a reference architecture you can apply directly to your cluster.

title: Navigating the inter-workings of an agentic SOC & threat hunting analyst
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS CloudTrail
speakers: Moumita Saha (Amazon Web Services); Chris Elmore (Amazon Web Services); Gopinath Jagadesan (Amazon Web Services); Michael Leighty (AWS); Jonathan Nguyen (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.

title: Network Firewall deployment models: pros, cons, best practices
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Network Firewall;AWS Network Security Manager
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Well-Architected Framework;Culture of Security
speakers: Brian Westmoreland (AWS); Luke Notley (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: One firewall, many ways to deploy it, and each mode unlocks a different architectural superpower. This session maps your options: distributed, centralized, multi-endpoint, explicit proxy, and the newest firewall modes. Through real architectures, you'll see where each one shines, how they scale, and the patterns that make your network security clean, flexible, and future-ready. Whether you're protecting a single VPC or a global multi-account estate, you'll leave knowing exactly which mode fits your environment and why. If you route traffic through AWS, this is the map that gets you there faster.

title: Network security architecture: Deployment patterns for firewalls
aoi: Application Security;Network & Infrastructure Security;Culture of Security
speakers: Shakeel Ahmad (AWS); Mahmoud Ismail (AWS)
abstract: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. Join this chalk talk to discuss deployment patterns for AWS Network Firewall and Gateway Load Balancer with third-party firewalls for ingress and egress inspection.

title: Network security innovations for agentic workloads
services: AWS Firewall Manager;AWS Network Firewall;AWS WAF
speakers: Sofía Aluma (AWS); Brandon Carroll (AWS Village - Network Security)
abstract: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.

title: Never Start Over: Chat to Co-Browse, Voice and Video on Amazon Connect Customer
speakers: Amit Gupta (AWS); Ying Qian (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your customer is halfway through an application in your app, and stuck. Today they abandon it, call you, and start explaining from scratch. In this hands-on workshop you build a single unbroken conversation that escalates in richness without losing context. A customer opens chat inside your application. When they stall on a form, the agent co-browses the page and sees the blocking field, then uses agent assist to answer a policy question with cited sources. The conversation carries into an in-app call, context intact, no phone number and no repeated details. Documents are reviewed over screen share, identity is confirmed over video, and because it's a joint application the co-applicant and a product specialist join the same call. Walk away with an escalation pattern combining persistent context, WebRTC channels and AI-assisted agents, for any high-consideration interaction.

title: [NEW LAUNCH] Coming soon!
abstract: Check back soon for more details about this session.

title: [NEW LAUNCH] Coming soon!
abstract: Check back soon for more details about this session.

title: Nine Seconds to Zero: Protecting AWS from AI Agent Disasters
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Jasdeep Singh Bhalla (GoDaddy)
abstract: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. The agent was confidently wrong and had the permissions to act on it. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.

title: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
speakers: Nathan Chong (AWS); Dominic Mulligan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.

title: Not all bots are bad: building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
speakers: Manuel Pata (AWS); Eitav Arditti (AWS)
abstract: Your edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and attackers. Treat them the same and you lose either security or revenue. In this workshop, you turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it. Legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic goes to deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get their own treatment that opens the door to new ways of charging for access. None of it requires changes to your origin logic.

title: No torque sensors, no problem: learning safe physical interaction for humanoids
speakers: Josh Merel (Fauna Robotics)
abstract: How do you make a humanoid robot safe to operate alongside people, without the torque sensors? Fauna Robotics Sprout is a humanoid robot that uses a position-command interface, yet it must regulate the forces it exchanges with the world. We show how Sprout learns compliant behavior that approximates classic impedance control, through mechanisms that control force at the joints and in task space. We describe how these controllers are trained and how they enable safer, whole-body interaction.

title: Observability and operations in the AI era
speakers: Andres Silva (AWS) (Amazon); Pratul Chakre (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

title: Observability patterns for agentic AI in production
