speakers: Joseph Choi (Amazon); chaitanya Gummadi (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic, multi-step, and make autonomous decisions and traditional APM isn't enough. Explore observability patterns for agentic workloads: reasoning chain tracing, token cost attribution, guardrail monitoring, and multi-agent coordination. We'll whiteboard architectures in real time. Bring your toughest production agent monitoring questions and leave with actionable patterns.

title: Observability patterns for Microsoft workloads migrating to AWS
speakers: Jagadeesh Chitikesi (Amazon Web Services); Ashish Bhatia (AWS)
abstract: Migrating Microsoft workloads to AWS requires rethinking your monitoring strategy. Existing observability approaches may not translate seamlessly to the cloud, creating blind spots that lead to costly downtime and degraded end-user experiences. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how to strengthen your observability posture as you migrate .NET applications, SQL Server databases, and Windows services to AWS. We'll cover how to use AWS-native and open-source tooling to monitor workloads across VMs, containers, and serverless, giving you confidence to migrate faster while maintaining operational excellence. Bring your questions.

title: Observable Agents with Lambda Durable Functions and OpenTelemetry
speakers: Raphael Manke (Dash0); Gunnar Grosch (-)
abstract: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.

title: Observe AI agents and workloads end to end
abstract: Get hands-on with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, the next evolution of CloudWatch that monitors your AI stack end to end, from the agent all the way down to the self-hosted inference workload serving it, converging application and agent observability into one AI-powered solution. Instrument an agent, trace its execution, and run evaluations against golden datasets. When something degrades, explore auto-discovered topology and golden metrics to pinpoint where latency or errors creep in. Navigate from alarm to the responsible inference workload, and let Omni's AI-powered investigation trace the root cause.

title: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
speakers: Ainara Manlutac (Amazon Web Services); Gagandeep Singh (Amazon Web Services); Kishore Vinjam (Amazon Web Services); Anil Pathuri (Amazon); Garrett Johnson (AWS)
abstract: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

title: Observe me that: Easy OpenTelemetry monitoring for your systems (sponsored by Dash0)
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Lambda
abstract: OpenTelemetry is the de-facto open-source standard for vendor-neutral traces, metrics, and logs. But, if you are not an OpenTelemetry expert, the learning curve to add it to your systems can be intimidating. This session covers how to bring OpenTelemetry with zero-code/no-touch instrumentation in applications running on AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, ECS and EKS, as well as how to bring into your OpenTelemetry pipelines telemetry from various AWS managed services and how to use agentic skills to level up the quality of your instrumentations and get better value out of your telemetry backends, coding agents, and AI tools. You will leave this session with a concrete map to get your OpenTelemetry journey started with tangible results in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Dash0, an AWS Partner.

title: Observe your applications and agents in one place
abstract: Traditional monitoring tools weren't built for the complexity of modern agentic and distributed applications. Teams juggle siloed dashboards, fragmented logs, and disconnected signals with no unified way to troubleshoot across agents, applications, and infrastructure. Amazon CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience organized around your teams and the applications they run, combining OpenTelemetry interoperability with CloudWatch scale. See how you can troubleshoot applications faster and manage agents with confidence using automatic service discovery, dependency mapping, built-in evaluations, and natural-language investigation — all from the Omni UI, your IDE, or your favorite tools.

title: One agent, any robot: building physical AI with Strands Robots
speakers: Cagatay Cali (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Physical AI puts agents in the real world. This chalk talk builds a robotics agent with the Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands — a MuJoCo simulation by default, real hardware with one code parameter change. We'll whiteboard the loop around the embodied agent: perception, a vision-language-action policy (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), and low-level control. We'll cover the the edge-to-cloud intelligence split, the peer-to-peer mesh and AWS IoT bridge coordinating a fleet, and sim-to-real transfer.

title: One AI Assistant, Every Data Source: Unifying Access with Amazon Quick
speakers: Jess Wang (Amazon Web Services); Jesse Gebhardt (AWS)
abstract: Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask Amazon Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.

title: One query across every signal: centralized security investigations at scale
speakers: Abeetha Bala (Amazon Web Services); Marshall Jones (AWS)
abstract: When an alert fires, your first question is "what else happened?" Answering it means correlating API calls, network flows, DNS queries, and application logs, often across dozens of accounts and regions. In this session, we show how security practitioners centralize every signal into a single queryable layer using Amazon CloudWatch unified data store, then investigate incidents with faceted queries that span all telemetry types at once. We walk through building always-on visibility dashboards, running cross-account investigations without switching tools, and using AI-assisted analytics to surface context before you need to go looking for it. You leave with a reference architecture for turning centralized logs into faster investigations and clearer security posture.

title: One Service, Every Workload: Build, Customize, and Deploy with SageMaker AI
speakers: Sumedha Swamy (Amazon Web Services); Kanwaljit Khurmi (AMAZON WEB SERVICES INC)
abstract: AI/ML teams want to move fast - experiment with models, fine-tune them on their data, and serve them in production, without stitching together separate tools at every step. In this session, see how Amazon SageMaker AI lets you build, customize, deploy, and run inference, all within one service. Learn how to match the right approach to each stage: serverless experimentation for fast iteration, fully managed environments for custom frameworks and training, persistent clusters for large-scale research, and optimized inference for real-time and batch serving in production. Walk away with a practical decision framework and a reference architecture to start simple and scale without switching platforms.

title: One-Way Doors: Launching a Regulated Financial Exchange on AWS in 2026
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Config;AWS Security Hub
speakers: Margaret Valtierra (Optex)
abstract: "AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (Access Analyzer, Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, and WAF) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late."

title: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
speakers: Eric Borland (Amazon Web Services); Chakravarthy Nagarajan (AWS)
abstract: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.

title: On-premises to AWS readiness: foundational decisions before your migration
speakers: Ron Wedel (AWS); Senay Swinney (Amazon)
abstract: Successful migrations are shaped by decisions made well before the first workload moves. This session explores how choices in licensing, operating models, technology architecture, and organizational readiness influence migration outcomes, whether moving off VMware, aging infrastructure, or other on-premises environments. Learn how to assess dependencies and business constraints, align stakeholders, and build a plan that avoids common pitfalls and adapts as your environment evolves.

title: Open for Business: OpenAI on AWS
speakers: Nick McCarthy (AWS)
abstract: There is more than one way to put OpenAI to work on AWS, from coding agents that ship production code to knowledge workflows and custom agents. This session tours OpenAI on AWS, starting with the latest OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock. Put them to work through two agentic surfaces: Codex for coding and ChatGPT Work for knowledge work. Then explore Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents for OpenAI to deploy OpenAI-powered agents in your AWS environment. The session maps OpenAI on AWS and helps you decide which path fits your needs.

title: Open-weights at work: Scaling AI without scaling the bill
speakers: Alex Thewsey (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Agentic and coding workloads are multiplying token consumption, and paying frontier prices on every call adds up fast. This chalk talk shows how open weight models on Amazon Bedrock let you scale that growth affordably without giving up quality or security. We walk through multi-model strategies for agentic and code generation workloads, the unit economics of open weight versus frontier, and how Bedrock's inference engine design keeps security strong regardless of where a model came from. You leave with a practical path to cost-efficient inference at scale.

title: Open weights to production: How Salesforce built and served Koa models
speakers: James Zhu (Salesforce); Amit Gupta (Salesforce); Hrushikesh Gangur (AWS)
abstract: Learn how to turn open-weight models into specialized, production-grade models for enterprise AI. Using Salesforce's Koa models as a real-world example, this session shows how the team built and served classifier, text, and voice agent evaluation models at scale. You'll learn how to choose training techniques for each use case, curate high-quality training environments, and prove accuracy gains against base models. For serving, you'll see how the team selected the serving engine, configuration, and instance type for better price-performance. Salesforce trained on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod and serves on SageMaker AI managed inference, keeping enterprise data within its trust boundary.

title: Operationalize enterprise event routing with Amazon EventBridge
speakers: Stephen Liedig (Amazon Web Services); Jamie Dool (Amazon AWS)
abstract: Scaling event-driven architectures across multiple AWS accounts has long meant managing fragmented buses, cross-account routing complexity, and developer friction. Explore how Amazon EventBridge delivers the scale, reliability, and developer experience that modern event-driven applications demand. It simplifies event routing across accounts and teams. Whether you're consolidating existing event infrastructure or designing a new event-driven platform, you'll leave with a clearer picture of how to reduce operational complexity and ship faster.

title: Optimize AI workloads with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless
speakers: Yaron Sananes (Amazon); Elad Bernstein (AWS)
abstract: Building highly scalable, high-performance AI and data-driven applications requires intelligent caching strategies. In this session, learn how to build with Amazon ElastiCache to scale workloads across caching patterns such as session caching, KV-caching, and more. Dive deep into microsecond latency networking optimizations that enable sub-millisecond response times, and explore common performance pitfalls with practical solutions to keep applications running smoothly.

title: Optimize container observability to reduce cost
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Vikram Venkataraman (Amazon Web Services Inc); Carlo Bergonzini (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: At scale, container environments generate metrics and logs that increase both cost and noise for engineering teams. This session explores architectural strategies for managing observability data across containerized workloads using OpenTelemetry. Learn how to control metric cardinality, design sampling policies that preserve critical signals, and evaluate managed backend tradeoffs. You'll leave with a framework for building cost-aware container observability.

title: Optimize HPC with storage for throughput and IOPS
speakers: Vandana Rungta (Amazon Web Services); Mitch Becker (AWS); Tom McDonald (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: High-performance computing workloads demand storage that keeps pace with thousands of compute nodes processing data in parallel. Amazon FSx for Lustre delivers sub-millisecond latencies and high throughput without the operational burden of managing a parallel file system. Amazon FSx for OpenZFS adds high IOPS with consistent low-latency response for latency-sensitive workloads. Explore how to select the right deployment type based on your workload profile, leverage native S3 integration for data pipelines, and right-size performance independently from capacity. Bring your questions about CFD (computational fluid dynamics), genomics, semiconductor design, weather modeling, and other compute-intensive workloads.

title: Optimize performance and cost of Amazon EBS at massive scale
speakers: Santhosh Arunuri (AWS); Nasan Tsengeg (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Managing production workloads across multiple regions while weighing cost and risk requires optimal strategy. With block storage, operating at scale can mean different things, including delivering high IOPS or I/O bandwidth to applications, managing and monitoring millions of volumes, or protecting petabytes of data with stringent RPO and RTO requirements. In this talk, learn best practices for scaling and managing your Amazon EBS environment, including automation, monitoring at scale, and cost-optimization techniques using cloud-native tools to meet your business needs.

title: Optimizing agentic AI: Vanguard's production deployment journey
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Krishna Gogineni (Amazon); Ritesh Shah (The Vanguard Group); Jay Wolfe (The Vanguard Group)
abstract: Deploying AI agents in production is just the beginning. Optimizing them at scale is the real challenge. In this session, Vanguard shares how they transformed their investor-facing AI agent from functional to fast, safe, and personal. Learn the techniques—from prompt caching to adaptive thinking to guardrail tuning—that delivered 70%+ latency reduction without sacrificing safety, and how long-term memory now powers personalized conversations across sessions. Walk away with battle-tested patterns for balancing response quality, cost, and speed in agentic AI at enterprise scale.

title: Optimizing containerized applications with shared file storage
speakers: Eric Heinrichs (Amazon); Jacob Strauss (AWS)
abstract: Containerized workloads can face unpredictable latency spikes, throughput bottlenecks, and runaway costs as they scale. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through techniques for identifying these issues and solving them in production environments. Bring your use cases, performance questions, and architecture challenges as we tune Amazon EFS, Amazon S3 Files, and Amazon FSx for real-world EKS and ECS deployments. We'll cover IO profiling, throughput vs. latency tradeoffs, cost-optimization strategies, multi-attach EFS configurations, FSx volume sizing, and POSIX-compatible pipeline design on S3 Files. You'll leave with practical insights you can apply to your environment immediately.

title: Optimizing prediction market and trading infrastructure
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Direct Connect
speakers: David-Paul Dornseifer (AWS); Josh Levinson (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges, and prediction markets share a critical challenge: managing the tension between resiliency and latency. AWS customers have solved this at scale on low-latency platforms trading digital assets 24/7. In this session, AWS specialists dive deep into architecture patterns and real-world examples addressing each challenge. Learn best practices for designing resilient, low-latency trading infrastructure using the latest AWS capabilities built for these markets.

title: Orchestrate failover and failback for effective Disaster Recovery
services: Amazon API Gateway;Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Ashish Panwar (Amazon); Jason Brown (AWS)
abstract: Failing over one app is easy — orchestrating failover and fail back across interdependent apps is where DR plans break. Real recovery requires dependency-aware orchestration across your entire stack. In this code talk, we live-code full-stack Region failover using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch: building sequenced workflows so databases switch before app tiers, validating steps with health checks, rehearsing with practice runs, and safely reversing the sequence for fail back. Leave ready to replace your paper DR plan with coded, repeatable recovery and measured RTO to prove it.

title: Orchestrating agentic workflows: Step Functions & durable functions
speakers: Rohan Mehta (Amazon Web Services); Dan Ronald (AWS)
abstract: AI agents need orchestration that handles long-running tasks, human approvals, and recovery from partial failures. In this chalk talk, compare AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for agentic workloads, and learn when to choose code-first, replay-based recovery versus visual state-machine semantics. We’ll whiteboard how durable functions checkpoint progress and resume after failures, how Step Functions handle branching and parallel tool calls, and where Lambda MicroVMs fit for sandboxing agent-generated code execution. Bring your architecture questions—we’ll design hybrid patterns that combine both orchestrators based on your workload shape.

title: Orchestrating AI agents with AWS serverless services
speakers: Dhiraj Mahapatro (Amazon Web Services); Dan Ronald (AWS)
abstract: Production AI agents need orchestration that handles non-deterministic behavior, multi-hour workflows, human approvals, and multi-agent coordination. Learn how AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda durable functions provide the reliability layer that agents demand. We cover patterns for durable execution, human-in-the-loop controls, event-driven agent communication, and the scale-to-zero economics that make serverless the natural home for agentic workloads.

title: Organizing Enterprise Knowledge and Securing Data with Amazon Quick
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);Amazon Quick
speakers: Ryan Leavitt (Amazon); Kent Rademacher (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon Quick transforms how teams access insights and automate decisions. In this SimuLearn session, you design Spaces in Quick to organize enterprise knowledge, configure custom Chat Agents with specialized instructions and curated knowledge bases, and integrate Quick with enterprise systems using Actions and connectors backed by Amazon S3 or Amazon DynamoDB. You then apply row-level and column-level security controls to protect sensitive data and explore Quick Research for comprehensive multi-source analysis and reporting.

title: Origin management for multi-region applications with Amazon CloudFront
speakers: Carlos Salazar (Amazon Web Services); Jonathan Woods (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: In this session, you'll learn comprehensive origin management with Amazon CloudFront to build secure, resilient content delivery systems. We'll cover automatic failover mechanisms with CloudFront and Route 53, configure granular origin routing with CloudFront Functions, and secure origins using S3 with Origin Access Control (OAC) and VPC private origins for enhanced security. We'll explore integrating on-premises infrastructure through AWS Direct Connect for hybrid architectures, and deploy Origin Shield to further optimize cache performance and reduce origin load.

title: Outpace AI attacks: Auto-recover AWS apps at machine speed with Rubrik. (sponsored by Rubrik)
speakers: Kalyan Akella (Rubrik Inc.)
abstract: Abstract: AI-driven attacks move at machine speed, and your AWS application is an interconnected system of code, infrastructure and data. Rebuilding by hand is a nightmare, if it’s even possible. Join us to see how an AI attack unfolds, and how Rubrik brings your business back by recovering the whole application in one automated motion. Rubrik discovers your application's dependencies, flags structural drift before it becomes an incident, and recovers it all together. Hear how Just Eat is moving from manual to validated, isolated recovery on AWS. Outpace AI-speed attacks with machine-speed recovery: less downtime, no manual rebuilds. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

title: Owning atoms to bits: How AWS accelerates network innovation at scale
speakers: Stephen Callaghan (AWS); Giacomo Bernardi (Amazon)
abstract: At AWS, we design everything within our infrastructure networks, from buildings to fiber, routers to protocols. This atoms-to-bits ownership lets us move at breakneck speed: the moment we spot an opportunity to improve customer performance or resilience, we drive it into production. In this talk, Senior Principal Engineers cover how they applied this pattern to develop the random graph fabrics reshaping data center topologies and highly available systems for machine learning at planet scale. Learn what it takes to continually refresh, upgrade, and re-architect live infrastructure without ever interrupting a single customer workload.

title: Physical AI for MedTech: From Intelligent Devices to Business Impact
speakers: Juli Hysenbelli (Amazon Web Services); Shaun Qualheim (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Physical AI — AI that senses, reasons, and acts in the physical world — is reshaping medical devices. From surgical robots to connected infusion pumps, imaging to wearables, every next-gen device needs training, simulation, edge deployment, and fleet management at scale. In this chalk talk, we’ll architect the full Physical AI stack on AWS for medical devices — SageMaker for model training, IoT Greengrass for edge inference, regulated OTA at fleet scale, and NVIDIA solutions integrated into the AWS backbone. We’ll whiteboard the hard tradeoffs — edge vs. cloud, regulatory constraints, and scaling from prototype to 100K devices. Leave with a reference architecture and a clear path to pilot

title: Physical AI in Telecom: A Framework for Workload Placement
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Local Zones;AWS Outposts
speakers: Umer Chaudhary (AWS); Angelo Sampietro (Amazon Web Service); Young Jung (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Some physical AI workloads need sub-millisecond performance at edge cell sites, others are better suited to a full AWS Region, and many fall in between on AWS Local Zones or AWS Outposts. In this chalk talk, we provide a framework for matching each workload to the right option. We trace the physical AI development lifecycle, examining how data sovereignty, latency, data gravity, and token economics interact to shape placement decisions at each phase. Based on real-world use cases, we discuss the options so you leave with a placement framework you can apply immediately.

title: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry
speakers: Kevin Lewin (AWS); Carlos Henriquez Quintana (AWS)
abstract: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.

title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
speakers: Bill Tarr (AWS); Anubhav Sharma (AWS)
abstract: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
speakers: Philipp Page (Amazon Web Services); Andrea Amorosi (AWS); Henrique Graca (AWS); Leandro Cavalcante Damascena (AWS - Amazon Web Services); Stefano Vozza (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

title: Practical PKI for On-Prem Devices with IAM Roles Anywhere
services: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)
speakers: Ben Bridts (Cloudar)
abstract: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. In this session, we'll talk you through multiple ways to set up or use PKI - such as Belgium's eID or a hardware key - to securely access AWS with phishing resistant authentication built using IAM Roles Anywhere. This will include live demos and code samples. By the end of the session we will stop worrying about plain text credential storage because we can use trusted hardware instead.

title: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
speakers: Anthony Liguori (Amazon.com)
abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.

title: Prevent supply chain disruptions with AI-driven insights and action
speakers: Gautam Kamdar (TE Connectivity); Jeet Dattani (AWS); Ozgur Dogan (AWS)
abstract: Only 25% of organizations feel ready to prevent disruptions, and 85% take two or more weeks to resolve the urgent ones. Join a supply chain leader and Amazon to see how agentic AI catches emerging risks early, so teams act before problems turn costly. You will hear the honest before and after, including the hurdles, not just the wins, and leave knowing how to move your team from reacting under pressure to planning ahead with a clear view of risk.

title: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Fargate
speakers: Suguna Devarla (Amazon); Ashok Srirama (Amazon Web Services); Raj Bagwe (AWS); Shamanth Devagari (Amazon Web Services); Sathya Balakrishnan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builder's session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including hardware-level task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Proof of What You Know: Building Trust in an AI Skills Economy (sponsored by Pearson)
speakers: Juan Garcia (Pearson)
abstract: As AI reshapes hiring and learning, proving what you know is becoming just as important as proving who you are. Pearson's digital wallet vision connects verified credentials, skills, and identity into a trusted, portable record that learners can use across certification, education, and employment journeys, helping employers and institutions move beyond self-reported claims to verified evidence of capability. This presentation is brought to you by Pearson, an AWS Partner.

title: Protect EKS and ECS workloads without chasing pod IPs
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Bongkyoon Choi (Amazon Web Services); Amish Shah (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Pod IPs in Kubernetes change constantly as containers scale and restart, making IP-based firewall rules brittle and hard to maintain. In this lightning talk, learn how container attribute-based rules in AWS Network Firewall let you write policy using native attributes like namespaces, cluster names, and labels instead of ephemeral IPs. We'll show how a container association auto-discovers matching pods, refreshes IP mappings in near real-time, and enriches alert logs with container context for faster troubleshooting and audit. Bring the same Layer 7 inspection, FQDN filtering, and managed IDS/IPS protections you already trust to your Amazon EKS and ECS workloads.

title: Protecting hundreds of accounts from one place with AWS Backup
speakers: Stuart Lupton (Amazon Web Services); Mark Choi (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Protecting a single workload is straightforward. But when every team owns their own accounts, organizations need a centralized approach to enforce consistent data protection across all of them. We'll dig into how to build backup architectures that scale across your entire AWS estate, covering Organizations backup policies to enforce protection standards across accounts, cross-account and cross-region copy strategies, and Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring and audit evidence. Whether you're onboarding new accounts or tightening controls on existing ones, we'll walk through patterns for centralized data protection you can prove.

title: Protect workloads with AWS Certificate Manager
speakers: Michael Slaughter (AWS)
abstract: Discover how to automate and manage TLS certificates using AWS Certificate Manager. In this chalk talk, we'll discuss automation opportunities for certificate issuance, export, distribution, and renewal across diverse environments. By attending, you'll gain the skills to eliminate manual certificate management tasks and minimize the risk of certificate-related outages in your organization.

title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
services: Amazon Braket;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Tyler Takeshita (AWS); Mao Lin (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

title: Quantum-proof your IoT fleet: migrate devices to Post-quantum cryptography OTA
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS IoT Core
aoi: Edge Computing;Cryptography and Post-Quantum;Internet of Things
speakers: Samuel Waymouth (AWS); Pravin Nair (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
services: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Bailey (Sohyeon) (Sohyeon) Cho (Amazon Web Services); NS Sabah (AWS); John Lee (AWS); Michael Orman (Amazon Web Services); Justin McGinnity (AWS)
abstract: Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
speakers: Jay Horne (AWS)
abstract: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
speakers: Ikenna Izugbokwe (Amazon); Hema Halagatti (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic, and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session, we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

title: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS Outposts
speakers: Frankie Negro (Amazon Web Services); Marcelo Andrade (SERPRO); Scott Rose (AWS)
abstract: Organizations with data residency and digital sovereignty requirements face a critical question: how do you move workloads from on-premises infrastructure to AWS Outposts without disrupting compliance posture or operations? This Level 300 session distills lessons from migrating customers to Outposts across industries, organization sizes, and migration strategies, featuring SERPRO, Brazil's federal data processing company, and AT&T, migrating telecom workloads at scale. The session walks through the processes that delivered results, the quantifiable outcomes measured, and the critical mistakes to avoid. Learn how to select the right migration approach and navigate common blockers. The session also covers transitioning from first-generation to second-generation Outposts hardware.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Transforming Customer Experience with AI
speakers: Troy Dieter (AWS); Jacob Scheatzle (AWS); Disha Jayswal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: "Your call is important to us." Nobody believes that anymore, and neither do your customers. Contact centers are being rebuilt around AI, and getting the architecture right is what separates the experiences people love from the ones they dread. In this Rodeo session, you'll join a team and design the transformation yourself: voice AI that understands people, routing that knows why they're calling, and handoffs to humans that don't start with "can you repeat your issue?" You'll whiteboard, swap ideas with teammates, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Saddle up! The design that finally makes "your call is important to us" true rides off with the win.

title: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
speakers: Dan Manges (RWX)
abstract: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.

title: Rebuilding a Platform's Foundation on DynamoDB Streams and Lambda
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Lambda;AWS WAF
speakers: Awedis Keofteian (Washmen)
abstract: Our platform had single points of failure baked into its original design. In this session, I walk through how we closed those gaps across all five AWS Well-Architected pillars: moving event-driven workloads onto DynamoDB Streams and Lambda, cutting costs through smarter data tiering, and building the observability needed to trust the new design under real operational pressure.

title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
speakers: Pritam Bhalerao (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

title: Recovering AWS Graviton workloads with orchestrated Disaster Recovery
abstract: You moved to AWS Graviton for better price-performance, but is your disaster recovery keeping pace? A recovery that lands on the wrong architecture, or brings tiers up out of order, turns a routine failover into an outage. In this chalk talk, whiteboard with disaster recovery experts how AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) now protects Graviton-based (arm64) Linux servers and recovers them onto Graviton instances, keeping the architecture intact end to end with nothing extra to configure. Then design a recovery plan that brings your application back tier by tier, in the right order, with wait times and critical-server gates. Bring your toughest arm64 and recovery-order questions, and leave with a DR design you can drill on Monday.

title: Recursive Self-Improvement on the Job
speakers: Yu Su (NeoCognition)
abstract: This talk will discuss RSI (recursive self-improvement) agents that proactively and continuously learn on the job. Agents onboard a new knowledge job just like human employees. Through RSI, we show that agents can outperform human testers on the same job across accuracy, efficiency, and cost. The talk will end with a discussion on the future of human-AI collaboration.

title: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
speakers: Alexander Rubin (Amazon Web Services); Will Sovran (AWS)
abstract: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Learn a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.

title: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Sushanth Mangalore (AWS); Bhupendra Washishtha (AWS)
abstract: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.

title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Transform
speakers: Sunil Ramachandra (AWS); Aswin Vasudevan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.

title: Regulation to Innovation: A Global Enterprise Guide to Digital Sovereignty (sponsored by Accenture)
speakers: Emanuele Baldassarre (Accenture)
abstract: Digital sovereignty is a growing priority for global enterprises operating across Europe as they navigate regulatory requirements, geopolitical uncertainty, and increasing demand for cloud and AI innovation. Organizations must balance data residency, compliance, resilience, and business agility without slowing transformation. Learn how leading enterprises are using AWS European Sovereign Cloud as part of a broader cloud strategy to meet sovereignty requirements while continuing to adopt modern cloud services and AI. Accenture will share practical approaches to assessing sovereignty needs, designing compliant architectures, and integrating sovereign cloud capabilities into enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with actionable guidance for balancing trust, resilience, compliance, and innovation at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: Reimagining how you build AI on SageMaker AI: the idea to AI flywheel
abstract: Building a high-performing generative AI application isn't a one-time model selection. Teams prepare and evolve data, measure quality, decide when customization is needed, compare alternatives, deploy the best candidate, and keep learning from production evaluations. Today those activities live in disconnected tools. In this chalk talk we'll whiteboard and demo new SageMaker experiences, some of it shown publicly for the first time. Bring your questions.

title: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery (sponsored by Deloitte)
speakers: Sara Siegel (Deloitte UK); Nadine Hachach-Haram (Proximie UK)
abstract: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
speakers: Max Clements (Amazon Web Services, Inc.); Nafi Colette Diallo (Amazon)
abstract: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
aoi: Edge Computing;Global Infrastructure;Resilience;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Adam Palmer (Amazon Leo); Nick Matthews (Amazon Leo)
abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

title: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
services: AWS Fault Injection Service;AWS Resilience Hub;Amazon Application Recovery Controller
speakers: Zaiba Jamadar (AWS); John Formento (Amazon Web Services); Jason Niemczyk (Autodesk)
abstract: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

title: Resilient by design: Last Mile and Multicloud Interconnect
speakers: Steve Bruggeman (Amazon Web Services); Donald Quindardo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Connecting a data center, a branch office, or another cloud to AWS has meant weeks of partner coordination, cross-connects, BGP configuration, and redundancy you design. AWS Interconnect - last mile and AWS Interconnect - multicloud move that work into the AWS Console and API, with resilient design built in. We start with the AWS Direct Connect building blocks and whiteboard what changes. You stop ordering cross-connects, configuring BGP, and designing redundancy. You still choose where it connects: a virtual private gateway, AWS Transit Gateway, or AWS Cloud WAN. Bring your hybrid and multicloud challenges.

title: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
services: AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK);AWS Fault Injection Service
speakers: Joel Medois (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.

title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
speakers: Roy Allela (AWS); Aravind Neelakantan (AWS)
abstract: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

title: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Olawale Olaleye (AWS EMEA SARL (Irish Branch)); Premdass Ravidass (AWS); Yaki Ratz (AWS); Bharath Gajendran (Amazon WebServices India); Rajalakshmi Ramasubramanian (Amazon)
abstract: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Resolve Incidents and Validate Releases with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Follow an issue from detection to resolution. In this builder's session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates incidents across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Then use the AWS DevOps Agent release management agent to review the code changes for production readiness before they reach your customers. Every review is informed by production intelligence that AWS DevOps Agent continuously builds from your environment.

title: Resolving and Preventing Production Incidents with AWS DevOps Agent
speakers: Ryan Gallaway (Amazon Web Services); Vicente Aguilar (AWS)
abstract: AWS DevOps Agent investigates production incidents end-to-end: tracing failures to the responsible change, guiding the fix, and verifying recovery. Once the service is stable, the agent converts root cause findings into automated prevention rules that enforce mandatory review gates on the same class of risk in future deployments. In this SimuLearn session, experience the full investigate, resolve, and prevent lifecycle as one continuous workflow in a single session.

title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
abstract: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
speakers: Arun KM (Amazon Web Services); Carl Caum (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
speakers: Sudhi Bhat (Amazon Web Services Inc); Avi Kulkarni (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

title: Right-size your observability: maximize signal, minimize spend
speakers: Kevin Fallis (AWS); Raj Ramasubbu (AWS)
abstract: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. In this chalk talk, we'll tackle your problems head-on with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Bring your toughest scenarios. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. If you're building AI agents, ask how to trace LLM calls, track per-invocation cost, and debug multi-agent workflows. And for any workload, ask how to stack cost levers like right-sizing, tiered storage, and writeable warm to maximize savings.

title: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
speakers: Kinnera Vajjala (Amazon Web Services); Chetan Sharma (AWS)
abstract: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

title: Rivian's journey to Multi-Availability Zone factory resilience on AWS Outposts
services: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS);AWS Outposts
speakers: Adam Shake (Rivian Automotive, LLC); Peter Dachnowicz (Amazon)
abstract: Discover why Rivian chose AWS Outposts to support mission-critical manufacturing applications that produce vehicles at its Normal, Illinois, plant. Explore how Rivian architected highly redundant infrastructure across multiple Outposts racks, using fast Amazon EC2 provisioning and scaling to meet production line demands. This session covers Multi-Availability Zone deployment for high availability, Amazon RDS read replicas across racks for database resilience, and AWS Unified Operations for proactive observability across its hybrid environment. Learn how Rivian plans to scale this model into its 9-million-square-foot mega factory in Georgia.

title: Robinhood: Scaling in-app agentic trading to every investor on AWS
speakers: Sreeram Ramji (Robinhood Markets, Inc.); Viraj Padte (Amazon Web Services); Chirantan Mahipal (Robinhood)
abstract: Hedge funds rely on research, strategy tools, and around-the-clock execution. Retail investors rarely have access to the institutional-grade research and real-time analysis that professionals depend on. In this session, discover how Robinhood built Robinhood Agents, an in-app agentic trading experience built on Amazon Bedrock. Customers can build their own agent to research the market, develop strategies, or trade within the limits they set. Learn how Robinhood's AI engineering leaders built an internal agentic platform focused on trust, security, and safety and how that later evolved and scaled to power Robinhood Agents. Hear about the architecture, guardrails, and lessons learned delivering institutional intelligence at consumer scale.

title: Route, cache, and batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
speakers: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan (Amazon Web Services); Chris Greenwood (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale, and most of that cost is repeat work you already paid for. This chalk talk whiteboards how prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock eliminates redundant computation across system prompts, shared context, and multi-turn conversations, then shows where Intelligent Prompt Routing and batch inference extend the savings further. We walk through cache-hit economics, how to structure prompts for maximum reuse, and when routing or batching is the better lever. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a caching-first cost strategy tuned to your workloads.

title: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
speakers: Patrick Meiler (AWS); David Roberts (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, we show how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure, using the enhanced custom event bus. We will discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events. Along the way, we highlight new multi-account patterns the enhanced custom event bus enables.

title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Carlos Santana (AWS)
abstract: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.

title: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
speakers: Ayush Kulkarni (Amazon); Daniel Abib (AWS); Sathya Shanmugha (Amazon Web Services); Thiago Pádua (AWS); Raphael Lima (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

title: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
speakers: Glenn Phillips (Vercel); Brandon Tuttle (Vercel)
abstract: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Run your largest SAP HANA on AWS: EC2 High Memory deep dive
speakers: Vikas Ratna (Amazon Inc); Linda Wang (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running SAP HANA at scale requires infrastructure that matches the size and criticality of your Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) workloads. EC2 High Memory instances deliver capacity from 256 GB to 32 TB, backed by the AWS Nitro architecture for consistent performance and hardware-level isolation. In this session, we deep dive into the Nitro design powering these instances and hear how customers are scaling production ERP to 32 TB on AWS. Walk away with architectural guidance and real-world deployment patterns for running your largest HANA workloads in a scale-up configuration.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere
speakers: Anthony McClure (AWS); Erik Anderson (AWS)
abstract: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Hasan Tariq (Amazon Web Services); Markus Doepke (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

title: Same code, any compute: Portable architecture on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Fargate;AWS Lambda
speakers: Daniel Abib (AWS); Rafael Barbosa (AWS); Nicolas Tarzia (AWS); Swarna Kunnath (AWS); Michael Costa (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your business logic shouldn't be coupled to a compute service. In this session, apply Hexagonal Architecture and 12-factor patterns to design workloads where compute is a deployment decision, not an architectural one. Through live code, see the same logic packaged as a Lambda function, a Fargate task, and an EKS pod using AWS Lambda Web Adapter and runtime-neutral handler patterns. You'll learn where portability pays off, where it adds unnecessary abstraction, and how to evaluate the trade-offs between pay-per-request, always-on containers, and orchestrated clusters for your workloads.

title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
speakers: Adit Modi (Lauren); Ishan Modi (Avalara)
abstract: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.

title: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
abstract: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.

title: Scalable LLM inference, easy on the ops: CrowdStrike on SageMaker AI
speakers: Felipe Lopez (Amazon Web Services); Vivek Singh (Amazon Web Services); Ruxandra-Maria Caba (CrowdStrike)
abstract: When adversaries move in seconds, security has to move faster. CrowdStrike shares how they built scalable, real time LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker to power threat detection at massive scale, where sub second latency is a hard requirement. Learn how dedicated, configurable endpoints gave them full control over performance, while SageMaker AI's managed infrastructure removed the operational overhead.​

title: Scale financial risk simulations with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Batch
speakers: Boris Litvin (Amazon); Matthieu Bonville (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.

title: Scale reinforcement learning globally with sparse weight updates (sponsored by Modal)
services: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Nan Jiang (Modal Labs)
abstract: Reinforcement learning post training usually keeps trainers and rollout workers in one tightly coupled GPU cluster. This talk shows how to keep backpropagation on fast local fabric while moving independent rollout workers to elastic GPU capacity across regions and clouds. The key is to diff weights in the precision actually served, then publish lossless sparse version transitions instead of full checkpoints. Attendees will learn why Adam/Muon updates often disappear under BF16 rounding, how version aware sidecars commit exact weight versions, and how this architecture turns globally available inference capacity into practical reinforcement learning capacity. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

title: Scale Through Partners: The Partner-Led SMB Growth Engine
speakers: Ethel Garcia Simon Matachana (Amazon)
abstract: SMB is a $1T opportunity—98% of global businesses are small/mid-size, 81% are increasing AI spend, yet fewer than 300 AWS partners hold the SMB Competency. This session unpacks AWS's Indirect Selling engine: new incentives aligned to growth, AI-powered lead generation, SMB solution selling, and a Partnership Maturity Framework turning opportunistic engagement into repeatable business practice. You'll leave with unit economics proving indirect selling reaches SMBs globally, a clear activation timeline from Opportunity through full Business Practice, and specific first moves to build a scalable, profitable SMB practice on AWS—your 20-minute roadmap to outsized growth.

title: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 500+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
speakers: Artem Zheltak (InDrive); Vadym Voitiuk (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 500 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Learn a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.

title: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
speakers: Colin McGrath (Baseten)
abstract: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

title: Scaling interactive generative AI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
speakers: Justin Rosen (Netflix, Inc.); Daniel Heckenberg (Netflix); Mathew George (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows, including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing Amazon EC2 G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AI Toolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.

title: Scaling ISV Revenue: Accelerating Co-Sell with AWS Marketplace
speakers: Erin Smith (AWS)
abstract: AWS Marketplace has become the fastest path for ISVs to scale co-sell, but unlocking its full potential means going beyond procurement and using it as the backbone of how you sell. This session unpacks how high-performing ISVs combine ISV Accelerate with AWS Marketplace to accelerate co-sell. Three points separate top performers: (1) structuring AWS seller alignment to generate Marketplace-routed pipeline, (2) using private offers and channel-partner workflows to compress enterprise deal cycles by 30-40%, and (3) mining Marketplace buyer signals to drive expansion and proactive renewal. Walk away with a focused playbook for turning Marketplace into a scalable revenue motion.

title: Scaling legacy app modernization with autonomous agents
abstract: Legacy application modernization is a coordination and code generation problem. A large application must be understood, verified, and integrated without losing fidelity. AWS Transform for mainframe reads legacy code and extracts its business rules into traceable specifications that describe what the application does. Learn how AWS Transform overcomes this modernization challenge, and discover the latest capabilities for scaling modernization that compress delivery from days to hours.

title: Scaling Multi-Account IAM at Netflix: Access, Visibility and Credentials
speakers: Jay Dhulia (Netflix); Prateek Sharma (AWS)
abstract: Managing IAM across a large, fast-growing AWS footprint quickly outgrows manual review — every permission change creates friction for engineers and queue time for operators.
