We'll cover a control-plane approach that ties together high-level IAM abstractions, automated workflows, and business context to drive the majority of AWS access needs. Developers describe intent against concrete resources instead of hand-writing JSON; Access Analyzer–backed probes auto-approve routine changes; administrators get a single pane of glass over SCPs, identity and resource policies, CloudTrail/S3 errors, and AWS Config history. Credential delivery flows through the same plane, enabling context-aware scoping for human and agentic callers alike.

title: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
speakers: Derek Ziehl (Amazon Web Services); Evan Lecklider (Amazon Web Services); Harith Gaddamanugu (AWS); David MacDonald (Amazon); Kartik Bheemisetty (AMAZON WEB SERVICES)
abstract: Most enterprises don’t run just one website, they run many: a corporate site, regional or sub-brand sites, plus internal portals for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately for every one creates configuration drift, inconsistent security posture, and operational overhead that scales with your site count. In this workshop, you’ll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many websites - whether they represent different brands, business units, or access levels - while still allowing targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ (stricter WAF on internal portals, a custom origin for a sub-brand). You’ll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.

title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS);AWS Secrets Manager
speakers: Enrico Bonaccorsi (Amazon Web Services); Francesc Sala (AWS)
abstract: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
speakers: Ashok Srirama (Amazon Web Services); Nick Peters (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.

title: Secure by design: the AWS foundation for your AI applications
services: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS Organizations
speakers: Maitreya Ranganath (Amazon Web Services Inc); Josh Du Lac (AWS)
abstract: As organizations put AI and agents into production, leaders need confidence that their cloud provider is secure by design. This session explains how AWS foundational security extends into AI services and which AI security capabilities build on that foundation. You see the controls customers use to protect their most critical AI workloads.

title: Secure petabyte-scale data transfers with AWS DataSync
speakers: Sachin Gupta (Amazon Web Services); Manchun Yao (Snapchat); Christie Lee (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Organizations moving data across AWS regions or into AWS need transfers that are fast, secure, and manageable at petabyte scale. In this session, learn how AWS DataSync helps you accelerate large-scale migrations and automate ongoing data movement. We'll show how capabilities like DataSync Enhanced mode help you move data faster with less operational overhead, then hear from Snap about how they moved billions objects and petabytes of data across AWS Regions in weeks. We'll close with best practices for maximizing performance and cost efficiency in your own DataSync deployments.

title: Secure your CI to operate at machine speed (sponsored by Chainguard)
abstract: AI agents are changing how software is built, introducing new security challenges across the software supply chain. CI environments are particularly vulnerable, with access to sensitive credentials and elevated permissions. We’ll explore how Chainguard's trusted artifacts, isolated build environments, and integrations with AWS can reduce risk from development through deployment and what securing software delivery looks like when AI agents are doing more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by Chainguard, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing AI and Autonomous Agents: Protecting the Lifecycle Across Any Platform (sponsored by Fortinet)
speakers: Chad Larter (National Association for Stock Car Auto Racing (NASCAR))
abstract: AI agents are actively running code, accessing databases, and making critical business decisions across every industry. But as these systems gain independence, they also introduce complex security risks throughout their lifecycle. Are you ready to protect a system that learns and acts on its own as your organization embarks on the AI journey? Join our panel of top AI and cybersecurity experts as they break down the end-to-end security of AI systems and agentic applications. We will explore real-world customer challenges and share practical strategies to safeguard autonomous agents across cloud and on-premises environments. This presentation is brought to you by Fortinet, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing and observing Amazon EKS clusters
services: Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Jens Walther (Amazon Web Services); Edgar Costa Filho (Amazon Web Services); Megan Velez Rivera (Amazon Web Services); Hans Nesbitt (AWS); Shamanth Devagari (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this hands-on session, explore how to automate the identification, analysis, and mitigation of risks in Amazon EKS clusters. Learn how to implement robust security controls—including role-based access control (RBAC), EKS Pod Identity, and service accounts—to apply least-privilege access and secure workload isolation. Discover how to use AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch to gain deep visibility into EKS cluster activities, enabling real-time monitoring and automated risk detection. You will learn the skills to automate risk management processes, helping your Kubernetes workloads remain resilient against evolving threats.

title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
services: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);Amazon GuardDuty
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Kubernetes
speakers: Mridul Chopra (Amazon Web Services); Purvi Goyal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Raise the bar on your software supply chain security with AWS. In this chalk talk, we will discuss DevOps security best-practices, threat detection and incident response for containers, and how to leverage AWS security services including Amazon ECR, Amazon GuardDuty, and Amazon Inspector to protect your Amazon EKS workloads. Discover how you can ensure CVE patching while optimizing storage to accelerate image delivery through seamless integration with open-source tools for publishing and deploying containerized workloads at scale. Learn how to efficently streamline your software supply chain while mitigating risks.

title: Securing APIs with AWS
abstract: Teams want visibility into their API landscape and find that traditional controls may miss attacks targeting API-specific vulnerabilities. In this session, learn how AWS is thinking about the modern API security challenge, from discovering unknown and unmanaged endpoints to detecting the kinds of authorization, authentication, and abuse issues that appear normal request by request. We'll explore common patterns behind recent industry incidents, why API visibility and runtime protection matter, and how a native, integrated AWS approach can help you reduce risk and respond faster.

title: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
speakers: Kunle Adeleke (AWS); Daniel Wells (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

title: Securing the agent loop with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
speakers: Felipe Lopez (Amazon Web Services); Shivani Singh (Amazon); Sreedhar Gade (Freshworks)
abstract: You screen the prompt on the way in and the answer on the way out. In between, tool results carry external content straight into the model's context and tool arguments carry the model's decisions out to your systems, without inspection. The middle of the loop is where indirect prompt injection lands. Where you place a guardrail inside the loop is a design decision. In this chalk talk, we place Bedrock Guardrails checks inside the agent loop. We examine ApplyGuardrail and InvokeGuardrailChecks, work through where each one belongs, and look at what risk remains when the checks are in place.

title: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
speakers: Dhawal Sharma (Zscaler, Inc.)
abstract: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing your AI-accelerated software supply chain with AWS Well-Architected
speakers: Anshu Bathla (AWS); Rohit Verma (AMAZON AWS)
abstract: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.

title: Security compliance and hardening with EC2 Image Builder
speakers: Anuj Butail (amazon web services); Manny Sidhu (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Discover how to leverage EC2 Image Builder to create secure, compliant, and hardened AMIs. Learn to automate security baseline implementation, including CIS benchmarks. We'll demonstrate building compliance checks into Image Builder pipelines, integrating vulnerability scanning, and implementing automated testing for regulatory standards.

title: Security Jam - sponsored by Fortinet
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI;Threat Intelligence
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Felipe Baron (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Work through simulated incident response scenarios - including a sponsored challenge from Fortinet to test your skills securing cloud workloads with Fortinet's network and cloud security platform. Can you find the breach and prevent the next one? AWS experts and guided exercises support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Security Jam - sponsored by Semgrep
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI;Threat Intelligence
speakers: Nir Pilo (AWS); Felipe Baron (AWS)
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Work through simulated incident response scenarios - including a sponsored challenge from Semgrep to find and fix code vulnerabilities early using Semgrep's static analysis and code security scanning. Can you find the breach and prevent the next one? AWS experts and guided exercises support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Security leverage at AI velocity: the operating model shift
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Culture of Security
speakers: Ram Ramani (AWS)
abstract: The speed AI gives your developers is also available to attackers, so AI investment is now a security decision as much as an engineering one. This session covers three changes to how security teams work when engineers pair with frontier agents. Agents carry application context across design, code, and pen testing, so security coverage keeps pace with development. When an agent builds a working proof of exploit for a finding, or shows that an existing control already blocks it, the security team no longer has to argue over whether the finding is real, and the false-positive queue shrinks. Agentic development environments also let you put preventive controls on what agents generate. We cover how to adopt these practices and which signals show they're working.

title: Security → Zero-Trust Identity & Data Protection in Amazon Quick
speakers: Munish Gopal (Amazon); Priya Kakarla (AWS)
abstract: Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past "is it secure?" to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes for Amazon Quick. We'll whiteboard the full identity path in Quick: SSO through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to Quick agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection, including Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, and full SIEM auditability.

title: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
speakers: Harold Lotz (Amazon Web Services); Josh Dean (Amazon)
abstract: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface, and many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and on-premises router, watch a Direct Connect maintenance unfold in real-time from both sides of the BGP session. See how AWS signals maintenance ahead of time through AS path prepending, graceful shutdown, and how traffic shifts to the backup path before any route is withdrawn. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, leave with the policy and checklist to get through your next maintenance without a page.

title: See where every AI dollar goes on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Fahad Ahmed (AWS); Yiwen Zhang (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI spend scales fast, and you can't optimize what you can't attribute. In this code talk, build Bedrock cost visibility live: combine CloudWatch metrics and supported invocation logs for timely usage signals with Cost Explorer and CUR 2.0 for billing reporting. Add attribution by IAM principal and cost-allocation tags, then assemble a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models while accounting for each source's freshness and granularity. Turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved Tier, choose models for price-performance, and set budgets and alerts. Use these signals to reconcile engineering usage with finance reports.

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Local Zones;AWS Outposts
speakers: Fernando Galves (Amazon Web Services); Chris McEvilly (AWS)
abstract: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.

title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
speakers: Weitong Ruan (Amazon); Fan Yang (Amazon.com Inc)
abstract: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

title: Serverless application testing in the age of agents
speakers: Brian Krygsman (AWS); Rajdeep Banerjee (Amazon)
abstract: Serverless and agentic tools let you ship fast. A strong testing foundation is what makes that speed sustainable - for you and your agents. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the testing patterns that matter most for serverless and event-driven applications: structuring code for testability, validating service interactions in the cloud, and building harnesses for asynchronous workflows. Join to explore local versus cloud testing tradeoffs and what new test dimensions agents enable for serverless developers. Walk away knowing how to give your agents the feedback loops they need to move quickly, iterate autonomously, and stay on the rails.

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
services: Amazon DynamoDB;Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS);AWS Lambda
speakers: Jay Colodner (Amazon Web Services); Nishtha Yadav (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

title: Serverless compute built for the web
speakers: Julian Wood (AWS); Samrat Karak (AWS)
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, see how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. We cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
speakers: Julian Wood (AWS)
abstract: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session we cover where existing serverless patterns hold up without modification, what actually changes, and how to start with what you have and add only what you need. See how the calls you already run can become tools that describe themselves to the agent that uses them. Learn how coding agents and skills make best practices part of every build, and where doing less with AI pays off.

title: Serverless Java in 2026
speakers: Christian Mueller (Amazon Web Services); Lefteris Karageorgiou (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM native AOT deliver sub-second startup, and Lambda Managed Instances give steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

title: Serverlesspresso: Build an event-driven app from the ground up
speakers: Serda Kasaci Yildirim (Amazon Web Services); Diana Cheng (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Build a fully event-driven, serverless coffee-ordering web application using AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and Lambda durable functions. Design scalable, fault-tolerant architectures as you simulate customers placing orders and baristas managing them in real time. Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Shaping the Future of Guest Support at lululemon with an AI-powered experience
speakers: Shadi El Baba (lululemon athletica canada Inc.); Hannah Bloking (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: What if you could design Guest Support for the future, not just improve the operation you have today? At lululemon, that question shifted the conversation. Rather than patching together fragmented tools and manual planning processes, the team envisioned the experience they wanted to create for guests and their people, then worked backward to build it. The result was a unified, AI-powered experience launched globally, giving employees more time to build meaningful connections with guests. This session explores how lululemon built a fundamentally different future for Guest Support and the principles leaders can use to do the same at their organization.

title: Shared file storage for containers, serverless, and Lambda
speakers: Eric Heinrichs (Amazon); Jacob Strauss (AWS); Samyak Kathane (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Containers spin up and disappear. Your application state needs to outlive them. Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and Amazon S3 Files give your containerized and serverless workloads durable, shared file storage. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era
speakers: Jonathan Jenkyn (AWS Security Assurance Services); Samantha Wylatowska (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

title: Ship Agents You Can Trust: An Agent Evaluation Framework for Partners
speakers: Neha Wadhwani (Amazon Web Services); Vishal Srivastava (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Partners shipping production agents at scale need to answer: is this good enough for customers? Agentic transformation doesn't end at build; quality evaluation is the missing layer. In this chalk talk, we walk through an open-source evaluation framework: define test criteria for your agent, run it in a sandbox on Bedrock, calibrate an automated judge against human labels, and track failure rates in CI. For multi-agent systems, attribute failures to the agent that caused them, not where the harm showed up.

title: Ship permissions faster: IAM policy tools in your CI/CD pipeline
services: AWS CloudTrail;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS IAM Access Analyzer
speakers: Kevin Shanley (AWS); Moumita Saha (Amazon Web Services); Siva Rajamani (Amazon Web Services); Todd Kudlicki (Amazon Web Services); Diana Yin (AWS)
abstract: Build a complete permissions pipeline that identifies IAM policy issues at code review. In this session, we build the pipeline stages: validate policies at pull request time with Access Analyzer, simulate critical access paths before deployment, preview Service Control Policies (SCP) impact against real CloudTrail data, and automatically triage Access Denied errors in production using IAM's new debugging API and autofix recommendations. We'll write commit gates that block overly permissive policies, integration tests that ensure operational permissions, and auto-triage that turns production denials into automated remediation commits.

title: Shipping AI at Full Velocity: Securing the Agentic Pipeline from IDE to Runtime
abstract: Autonomous AI agents are no longer just writing code; they are calling APIs, spinning up cloud resources, and executing commands across build pipelines. But with this level of autonomy, zero-day vulnerabilities can propagate across your stack faster than ever. Staying resilient requires shifting security directly into the agent’s execution loop. Through live demos and an interview with Capita CISO, Luke Beeson, on their rapid AWS adoption, discover how to embed guardrails directly into agentic IDEs. Learn to catch vulnerabilities and overscoped tool permissions as code is written, and walk away with a battle-tested framework to ship agentic AI at full velocity on AWS.

title: Ship software safely with Amazon ECS advanced deployments
speakers: Nikita Dahiya (AWS); Islam Mahgoub (AWS)
abstract: Rolling update, blue/green, canary, or linear? Amazon ECS gives you deployment strategies with built-in safety controls, no extra tooling required. This chalk talk explores how native Amazon ECS deployment options work and when to use each one. Discuss traffic shifting percentages, validation hooks for pre-traffic testing, and alarm integration for automated rollbacks. Learn how to tune bake time and coordinate multi-service deployments so you can ship changes confidently at any scale. Bring your release pipeline challenges for an open discussion.

title: Ship web apps that just work
abstract: Your agent can ship a web application in seconds. What happens after that is the hard part. In this session, learn how you and your agents get everything you need in one place, integrated and ready in seconds. We walk through how to go from code to production without configuring infrastructure, how the Agent Toolkit keeps deployments reliable, and how to scale without starting over.

title: Shrinking the Blast Radius: Breach Containment in AWS (sponsored by Illumio)
topic: Hybrid Cloud & Multicloud;Networking & Content Delivery;Security & Identity
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Firewall Manager
aoi: Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Zero Trust
speakers: Aditya Krishnan (Illumio Inc)
abstract: Staying ahead of threats in the cloud means seeing them before they spread. In this session, we'll demonstrate how Illumio brings together AWS firewall data and live traffic flows to surface risk in real time, how segmentation shuts down exposure across your environment, and how quarantine actions stop compromised workloads in their tracks. See the full journey live, from blind spots to contained blast radius. This presentation is brought to you by Illumio, an AWS Partner.

title: Simplify multicloud: manage and monitor VMs in one place
speakers: Jose Ponce Martinez (Amazon Web Services); Nereida Woo (AWS)
abstract: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

title: Simplify secure file sharing with Transfer Family no-code web apps
speakers: Emma Harrison (AWS); Madhukumar Adavi (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: Traditional file transfer solutions often require complex client software, custom scripts, or technical expertise, creating barriers for business users who need to share data. Learn how AWS Transfer Family web apps enable secure, browser-based file transfers that automatically trigger data processing workflows. We'll show you how to build automated pipelines that process files upon upload while maintaining enterprise-grade security through AWS IAM Identity Center for your workforce or Amazon Cognito for external users. Discover how to streamline file ingestion, kick off validations, and orchestrate downstream processing, starting with a simple drag-and-drop interface for your end users.

title: Single Agent to Global Scale: One Postgres, Any Workload, Run by Agents (sponsored by YugabyteDB)
abstract: An agent needs a Postgres database for perhaps twenty minutes. A payments platform needs one that never goes down across three regions. Most teams cover that range with different products, several vendors, and scores of on-call operators. Yugabyte delivers it as a single stack on AWS. YugabyteDB is distributed PostgreSQL built for global scale and resilience that also scales down to fractional instances. YugabyteDB AMP puts agents in charge of the fleet, handling provisioning, migration, and on-demand tuning. Meko gives agent teams the shared context they run on. See what it takes to run every Postgres workload on one foundation. This presentation is brought to you by YugabyteDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Small Startup. Big Data. Rare Hopes. (sponsored by Cloudera)
speakers: Brian Martin (Cloudera)
abstract: Making a big impact always starts small - a dream, an idea, a hope. Brian Martin - co-founder of Rare Hopes NFP and CTO of Applied AI at Cloudera - will share the story of the non-profit he and industry colleagues founded with the support of AWS, Cloudera, and other companies to deliver a multi-million dollar equivalent platform supporting drug repurposing for rare disease hypothesis generation. Illustrating the concept and components necessary to deliver this advanced graph analytical approach to transforming knowledge into insights, the story demonstrates the power and potential that AI brings allowing companies to work with knowledge - not just data. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

title: Smoking on Airplanes: Rethinking How Enterprises Trust Software (sponsored by Glow)
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Culture of Security;Agentic AI
abstract: Every day, employees install browser extensions, IDE plugins, and open-source packages with powerful access to corporate devices, code, credentials, and data. AI coding agents are accelerating this practice by recommending and installing software to complete tasks. Yet much of it enters the enterprise without comprehensive security review. We've normalized a practice that may someday seem as unthinkable as smoking on airplanes. In this session, we'll expose hidden risks in plugin and package ecosystems, show why traditional application controls miss this rapidly changing software layer, and explore what security teams must rethink as AI makes software adoption faster and increasingly autonomous. This presentation is brought to you by Glow, an AWS Partner.

title: Solving Problems Faster with AI SRE​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
speakers: Aaron Schifman (Cisco)
abstract: The complexity of problems continues to grow, and smart organizations know that leveraging AI is the quickest way to get this complexity under control and keep customers happy.​ In this session, you’ll see a demo of and learn how to use AI SRE in Splunk Observability Cloud to troubleshoot and remediate problems faster no matter how complex or distributed your operating environment is, all powered by OpenTelemetry. ​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Sovereign Transformations: From Legacy to an AI-Ready Estate You Own (sponsored by Concierto by Trianz)
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);AWS Transform
abstract: Enterprises are caught in a catch-22. Legacy estates must modernize to become AI-ready, yet the fastest path to AI runs through shared inference services where your transformation intelligence leaks to competitors. Modernize to build advantage & hand it away. Concierto's Sovereign Transformations breaks the bind. Ravi Kumar R, CTO, Trianz, presents a sovereign, unified platform that migrates, modernizes, manages, & prepares enterprises for agentic AI entirely within customer boundaries. Dual-engine architecture combines deterministic rules with private AI inference under oversight, all in your VPC. Intelligence compounds as a proprietary asset, sharpening transformations. Built on 100+ enterprises in 19 countries, Concierto delivers versatility at scale. Sovereign Transformations is an architectural choice about protecting and growing your intelligence solely for your company's benefit. This presentation is brought to you by Concierto by Trianz, an AWS Partner.

title: Speed Wins: Compress Migration Timelines from Pipeline to Production
services: Amazon Bedrock;AWS Application Migration Service;AWS Transform
speakers: Nic O'Brien (Amazon Web Services); Vanessa Cordero (AWS); Jonathan Kong (AWS)
abstract: Enterprises face a wall of technical debt standing between them and the AI opportunity. In this session, learn how AWS Transform helps compressing the entire partner lifecycle — from intelligent prospecting and AI-powered co-sell through to automated delivery and simplified funding — and why first-movers will own disproportionate share of the opportunity.

title: SQL Server to Amazon RDS: lessons from Xero's 900 database migration
speakers: Lynn Hamilton (Xero); Tobias Ternstrom (AWS)
abstract: What does it take to migrate the databases behind 5 million small businesses without anyone noticing? Xero, the global cloud accounting platform, moved 900 SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for SQL Server with near-zero downtime. In this session, Xero shares how the team orchestrated cutovers, approached schema migration, and used managed patching, automated backups, and capacity planning in Amazon RDS to return engineering time to product development. The session covers the migration planning and decision points most relevant to engineering teams running large SQL Server fleets on aging self-managed infrastructure.

title: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
speakers: Colm MacCarthaigh (AWS)
abstract: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.

title: Stop Building Agents Without Unified Enterprise Context (sponsored by Glean)
abstract: Many AI programs start with a model, a prompt, and a narrow workflow. They stall when agents need to understand permissions, people, policies, past decisions, and data spread across AWS and SaaS systems. This session shows a different path: establish a governed enterprise context layer and scale the enterprise workflows that prove value. Attendees will learn the elements that make up a robust context platform, what to keep open and flexible, and how to measure whether agents improve real work. This presentation is brought to you by Glean, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop Moving AWS Data. Turn It into Action with Splunk​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
speakers: Heath Johnson (Splunk, a Cisco Company); Adrian Acuna (Splunk, a Cisco Company)
abstract: Machine data across AWS environments is growing faster than teams can move, normalize, and analyze it. What if you could stop moving all that data and start putting it to work? In this session, learn how Cisco Data Fabric, powered by Splunk, federates data across AWS and enterprise sources, correlates it at scale, and prepares it for AI and agentic workflows. Through practical architecture patterns and a live demonstration, you’ll see how to reduce data movement and operational cost while turning distributed telemetry into trusted context, faster decisions, and action.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
speakers: Gunnar Grosch (-); Nadia Reyhani (BHP); Kristine Armiyants (Eleveight AI)
abstract: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of organizations that have deployed an AI agent have rolled it back or shut it down, and the rate rises to 81% among those reporting fully mature guardrails. Getting agents into production got easier. Keeping them there without hurting customers did not. We'll walk through the failure patterns behind rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.

title: Stop threats at DNS: what's new in Route 53 DNS Firewall
services: Amazon Route 53;Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC)
speakers: Adhish Bhobe (Amazon Inc.); Jesse Lepich (AWS)
abstract: DNS is where threats are first visible and Amazon Route 53 DNS Firewall is turning that visibility into defense. This session explores how Route 53 DNS Firewall's evolving security capabilities help you resolve, inspect, and protect egress DNS query traffic to the internet across global, multi-account environments. See how deeper integration with other AWS security services, expanded DNS threat detection, wider visibility, and a growing partner ecosystem come together to strengthen your first line of defense. Whether you run a single VPC or a global network across AWS and hybrid networks, you'll leave with a clear picture of how DNS security for egress traffic is advancing and how to put it to work.

title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
speakers: Neil Yajnik (Amazon Web Services); Kartik Ganesh (AWS)
abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.

title: Storage decisions when you're building a multi-tenant business
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon FSx;Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Dave Roberts (Amazon Web Services); David DeLuca (Amazon)
abstract: When your business delivers cloud services to your customers, how you map tenants to storage is one of the earliest architectural choices, and it shapes everything that follows: onboarding automation, billing boundaries, isolation guarantees, and how accounts, users, and data relate to each tenant. Your workload mix adds another dimension, because data types using object, file, or block storage drive the handling of tenancy differently. In this chalk talk, we walk through silo, bridge, and pool deployment models, examining how workload profile, tenant count, and business requirements drive the choice. Bring your architecture and we'll work through it.

title: Storage performance in EC2 instances: What matters to your workload
speakers: Tanmoy Sen (Amazon Web Services); Kshitij Tambe (AWS)
abstract: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. In this chalk talk, we explore why latency-consistent mixed read/write performance drives real application outcomes across database, analytics, and distributed file system workloads. We'll walk through how workload profiles map to different performance dimensions (throughput vs. IOPS vs. latency consistency), how real-world write mixes reveal true storage performance, and how emerging AI workloads are creating demand for an entirely new storage performance profile.

title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
aoi: Culture of Security;Agentic AI;Identity & Access Management
speakers: Omri Shiv (AWS); ENG HWA TAN (Amazon Web Services Singapore Pte Ltd)
abstract: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

title: Strengthen identity verification with Amazon Rekognition
speakers: Sneha Choudhury (Amazon); Divyesha Malhotra (Amazon); Vicky Katara (Amazon)
abstract: Learn how to use Amazon Rekognition Face Liveness to help confirm a real person is present during digital onboarding. This session explores how to integrate liveness checks into your application, detect spoofing attempts, and support identity verification workflows.

title: Switch models without disrupting customers on Amazon Bedrock
speakers: Shash Sapre (AWS); Claudio Mazzoni (AWS)
abstract: Your application is working in production, and then a newer model arrives with better benchmarks or lower cost. You need to decide whether moving is worth the risk. A switch can change outputs, break prompts, raise costs, and create weeks of retesting. This session shows how to reduce that disruption on Amazon Bedrock. Test candidate models against your own use cases, compare quality, latency, and cost, and update prompts without rewriting them by hand. See how Bedrock Evaluations and Advanced Prompt Optimization help you measure the impact before rollout. Leave with a practical plan for switching models without disrupting customers.

title: Tackling a $30M fraud crisis with ML: California Community Colleges
speakers: Julia Arreguy (California Community Colleges Technology Center); Mitul Ganger (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The California Community Colleges, the largest higher education system in the U.S. serving 1 in 4 community college students nationally. Since 2024, it has faced a fraud crisis targeting over $30M, as stolen-identity breaches and generative AI made ghost-student attempts cheaper and harder to catch. Machine learning (ML) on Amazon SageMaker now screens applicants centrally, driving a 64% decrease in attempted fraud year over year. Campus-level detection tools add a second layer, catching 2x more fraudulent applications than human review alone. This session covers the ML architecture, how it integrates across 116 campuses, and how reclaimed seats and aid dollars directly improved access for legitimate students.

title: Take Action on Operational Issues with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: There's a big difference between an agent that gives you a remediation plan and one that can carry it out. In this session, see how AWS DevOps Agent goes beyond investigation to take action on operational issues across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments. Learn how directed actions and defense-in-depth controls govern what the agent can do, with layered opt-in, per-action approval, and built-in guardrails that keep operations safe

title: Talk to your market data: Agentic AI meets exchange feeds
speakers: Santhosh Sampath (AWS); Ravindra Kori (Amazon); Sribalaji Thirunavukkarasu (AWS); Alket Memushaj (AWS); Samrat Lamichhane (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: In this builders’ session, connect an Amazon Bedrock agent layer to a high-performance data pipeline that turns 560M IEX exchange messages into an interactive playground. Analysts describe trading ideas in natural language (no SQL or Python required) while the agent queries Parquet data, generates strategy logic, runs backtests, and returns results. Dig into the C++ parsing, serverless orchestration with AWS Batch and AWS Fargate, Amazon S3, and guardrail patterns that make it production ready. Leave with architecture patterns, a cost model, and a blueprint for adding an agentic layer that takes anyone from market intuition to tested strategy in minutes.

title: Tapestry, Grupo Boticario & Nestle Purina on agentic commerce
speakers: Todd Carter (AWS); Ann Scharenberg (Nestlé S.A.); Mandeep Bhatia (Tapestry, Inc); Isabel Miranda (Grupo Boticário)
abstract: AI agents are changing how consumers discover and buy, splitting into two investments: retailers building conversational shopping on their own properties, and consumer goods companies optimizing how their products surface when agents shop on a consumer's behalf. In this session, hear how Tapestry built the Kate Spade AI Gift Concierge that turns luxury gifting into a guided conversation; Grupo Boticario launched an agentic Virtual Assistant orchestrating product discovery and checkout for millions of users; and Nestle Purina implemented an Answer Engine Optimization strategy, using their native chatbot Allie to pressure-test how external AI engines surface proprietary brand data before releasing it into circulation.

title: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
speakers: Venugopalan Vasudevan (AWS); Avi Nidumbur (Amazon)
abstract: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.

title: Telecom NOC operations: Automating incident response with AI agents
services: Amazon Bedrock;Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Cheng Liu (AWS); Daniel Lupescu (AWS)
abstract: Modern telecom networks span thousands of distributed components, forcing network operations teams to interpret high volumes of alarms, separate root causes from downstream symptoms, and coordinate remediation across systems under time pressure. In this workshop, you will build AI agents that read, reason about, and execute Standard Operating Procedures for network deployment and remediation. First, deploy a 5G standalone core on Amazon EKS using an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock. Next, operate a closed-loop remediation agent, inject real failures, and observe how it detects, correlates, and resolves problems.

title: Tenant isolation at scale: Network patterns for ISVs on AWS
services: Amazon VPC Lattice;AWS Transit Gateway;AWS PrivateLink
speakers: Tom Adamski (AWS); Rizwan Mushtaq (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: As ISVs scale their SaaS platforms, network architecture becomes a critical decision: balancing tenant isolation, compliance, and operational efficiency. In this chalk talk, examine proven connectivity patterns using AWS PrivateLink, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon VPC Lattice for multi-tenant environments. Explore how to enforce strong tenant boundaries at the network layer, handle cross-account connectivity at scale, and reduce operational complexity as your business grows. Whether building a new multi-tenant platform or evolving an existing one, leave with architecture blueprints ready for production.

title: The Agentic MSP: How AI Compounds Customer Outcomes at Every Layer
speakers: Ben Reed (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: The most profitable Managed Services Providers aren't just using AI internally. They're creating a compounding cycle: automate your own operations with Agentic AI, deliver measurably better outcomes to customers, then help those customers adopt AI themselves so the results multiply. This session shows how the AWS Managed Services Provider Program rewards that progression, from foundational automation through outcome-based delivery powered by AI agents. Leave with your own assessment and a concrete plan to reach the next level.

title: The Amplification Effect: How AI Sharpens the Builder
speakers: Umesh Sampat (AWS); ADAM B (AWS)
abstract: Replacement anxiety dominates the AI conversation, but builders who use AI as a daily collaborator are discovering the opposite: AI amplifies human capability. This breakout session presents a practical framework for using AI tooling as a skills accelerator. We'll show how builders who integrate AI into daily workflows develop stronger critical thinking, faster adaptability, and deeper domain reasoning. Drawing from real-world examples, you'll learn how the act of collaborating with AI and refining its direction builds the exact human capabilities organizations need most. Walk away with a progression model from proficiency to mastery and techniques to start sharpening your skills immediately.

title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
speakers: Alex Shovlin (AWS); Liam Greenamyre (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

title: The AWS network I would build today: Identity over topology (sponsored by Tailscale)
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Transit Gateway;Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
speakers: Lee Briggs (Tailscale)
abstract: Modern AWS environments can grow from a handful of VPCs into complex regional and global routing topologies. This session explores a different model: keeping VPC networking local and predictable while using identity-aware connectivity between users, workloads, and networks. See how Tailscale connects AWS environments and resources, including those that cannot run an agent, and explore an experimental integration with AWS Gateway Load Balancer and GENEVE. Attendees will learn the tradeoffs, where native AWS networking remains the right choice, and how identity-aware networking can reduce connectivity complexity without sacrificing control. This presentation is brought to you by Tailscale, an AWS Partner.

title: The Capability Overhang: Ask More of the Frontier (sponsored by Anthropic)
speakers: Matt Bleifer (Anthropic)
abstract: Frontier models can do more than anyone asks of them. At Anthropic, the hardest part of testing a new model is finding work hard enough to make it fail. Outside, most teams hand Claude the tasks they gave last year's model. This session closes that gap: what the newest Claude models do on AWS when you delegate the job, not the task. Multi-day autonomous work, large migrations end to end, agents that verify their results and keep going. Evals, live demos, and how our researchers keep raising the bar. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: The cloud holodeck: Stream NVIDIA Omniverse, scale headless sim on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Batch
speakers: Dan Cotting (AWS); Kurt Scheuringer (AWS)
abstract: Interactive simulation needs RTX-class GPUs engineers lack; rendering millions of frames needs a fleet nobody wants to babysit. Amazon DCV streams a full NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to any browser, while AWS Batch runs the same scenes headless across GPU fleets for scale. The AWS Visual Asset Management System is the control plane: launching jobs, tracking runs, and versioning outputs. Watch an engineer open a cloud viewport and fan out a thousand-frame jobs live.

title: The co-build playbook: Turn AWS partner programs into deployable industrial solutions (sponsored by Belden)
abstract: Manufacturers know their machines generate valuable data — yet most digital initiatives stall before they scale, trapped between legacy OT protocols and cloud analytics that were never designed for the plant floor. This session shows how a connected partner ecosystem closes that gap. Learn how Belden acquires, conditions, and secures data at the physical layer, and how Edge2Web Factory Insights turns that data into high-powered analytics and AI-enriched insights based on AWS IoT SiteWise. Discover the reference architecture behind a joint deployment, from edge protocol connectivity to AI-driven insight. See how co-development with AWS compressed the path from whiteboard to production. And explore how to apply this pattern to your own operations. This presentation is brought to you by Belden, an AWS Partner.

title: The Cogs of a Well-oiled Software Factory
speakers: Graham Neubig (CMU / OpenHands)
abstract: The "Software Factory" is a new buzzword for a fully autonomous agent driven software development process. Many organizations are trying to set up such a factory, but this is easier said than done. In this talk, from my experience setting up such factories for ourselves and other businesses, I will explain some of the elements of a software factory (issue triage, spec generation, implementation, review, and testing), and some of the pain points that we have experienced at each step. I will also cover how to evaluate the effectiveness of each of these steps and how to build a self-improvement pipeline so the factory gets better and better with feedback from its human supervisors.

title: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
speakers: John Dougherty (Amazon); Aishwarya Subramaniam (AWS)
abstract: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.

title: The Economics of an AWS Partner: Revenue, Incentives & AWS Marketplace
speakers: Jahnai Bilovsky (AWS); Snigdha Sahi (AWS)
abstract: A forward-looking session reframing Partner economics for the year ahead. Revenue measurement is no longer just tracking, it's the backbone connecting all AWS Partner Programs. Walk away with a clear action plan to position for next year’s benefits.

title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
speakers: Rohit Malshe (Amazon.com)
abstract: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

title: The future of Kubernetes on AWS
services: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR);Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
speakers: Mike Stefaniak (AWS); Ray Qureshi (OpenAI); Vara Bonthu (Amazon Web Services); Raghav Tripathi (Amazon Web Services Inc)
abstract: Kubernetes has become a standard for organizations looking to modernize their application portfolios. AWS developed Amazon EKS to make Kubernetes more accessible to organizations of all sizes, helping them focus on what matters most for their businesses. In this session, join Amazon EKS product leadership to learn about the latest innovations and strategies for building Kubernetes platforms and applications faster, including building and orchestrating agents. Discover how various organizations use Amazon EKS to run their most demanding applications in the cloud, on premises, and at the edge.

title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
speakers: Tsahi Duek (aws); Dima Breydo (AWS)
abstract: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.

title: The Infrastructure Behind AI: Scaling Access to Web Data (sponsored by Oxylabs)
speakers: Patricija Zemaityte ()
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence directly mirrors the continuous evolution of web intelligence infrastructure. As machine learning models demand exponentially richer datasets, web data extraction has transformed from simple parsing into a sophisticated, mission-critical engineering discipline. In this session, explore how modern web scraping infrastructure actively evolves alongside artificial intelligence to solve live data bottlenecks and complex anti-automation challenges. Discover high-throughput extraction architectures, real-world pipeline designs, and strategic business use cases that turn dynamic web data into production-ready intelligence. Learn how advanced web data infrastructure fuels current artificial intelligence capabilities and shapes the future of automated enterprise decision-making. This presentation is brought to you by Oxylabs, an AWS Partner.

title: The latest innovations in multicloud agent security
abstract: AI agents are showing up everywhere your teams work, and security teams also want to keep pace. In this session, explore the latest innovations in securing AI across multicloud environments. See how AWS is thinking about the challenges security teams face as AI is used by teams, and the direction it is taking to help them stay ahead. Walk away with a clearer picture of where AI security is heading and practical ways to get ahead of it in your own organization.

title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
services: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS);AWS Trainium
speakers: Maen Suleiman (Annapurna Labs)
abstract: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.

title: The Next Phase of AI for SRE: Distributed Reasoning for Enterprise Operations (sponsored by Ciroos)
speakers: Ananda Rajagopal (Ciroos, Inc.)
abstract: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.

title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
services: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3);AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM);AWS PrivateLink
speakers: Matt Meck (AWS); Marshall Jones (AWS)
abstract: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.

title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
speakers: Dhiraj Mahapatro (Amazon Web Services); Heeki Park (AWS)
abstract: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

title: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
abstract: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.

title: Track cross-domain attack vectors with AWS Security Hub extended
speakers: Frank Schwarzenau (AWS)
abstract: In this 20-minute lightning talk, see how AWS Security Hub Extended correlates signals across endpoint, identity, email, data, browser, and AI domains into a single attack narrative. We show how cross-domain correlation surfaces attack vectors invisible to any single tool, and how customers deploy preconfigured detection patterns for immediate value.

title: Transforming business and SAP with Amazon Innovations
speakers: Soulat Khan (AWS)
abstract: The SAP landscape is changing, with customers not just asking “How can you help us migrate and run our SAP applications in the cloud?”, but instead: “How can you help us transform our business, simplify our business processes, and leverage AI to serve our customers and employees?”. Join this session to learn how our marquee customers are combining SAP modernization with Amazon's extensive portfolio to revolutionize customer experiences. You'll hear how customers are redefining customer experience and transforming business processes including finance procurement, manufacturing, operation etc by leveraging Pan-Amazon services, and AWS AI services alongside SAP.

title: Transforming Customer Experiences Through Tapestry’s Order Management (sponsored by Digitate)
speakers: Asif Iqbal (Digitate); Sonal Sharan (Tapestry)
abstract: Customers expect fast, personalized, and seamless experiences across every interaction with a brand. For Tapestry, connecting consumer feedback, sentiment, and operational signals is key to identifying issues that can impact customer experience and brand reputation. In this session, Sonal Sharan will share how Tapestry is leveraging ignio's AI Agents to continuously analyze these signals, surface emerging concerns, and provide real-time visibility into business-impacting issues. Intelligent workflows help prioritize and route issues for faster resolution, while actionable insights support more proactive customer engagement, resulting in a more connected, responsive, and customer-centric organization delivering exceptional experiences across Tapestry’s leading brands. This presentation is brought to you by Digitate, an AWS Partner.

title: Troubleshoot Workloads End to End with AWS DevOps Agent
abstract: Application issues can originate anywhere across the stack, from compute and container environments to networking, data, and AI services. In this session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates issues end to end across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals across layers to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Learn how teams troubleshooting complex workloads can resolve issues faster and spend less time moving between tools and data sources.

title: Trust the Agent, Keep the Keys: The Journey to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by PagerDuty)
speakers: Nick Whiley (Echostar); Alice McElroy (Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd.); Art Rogers (Cox Automotive); Eric Johsnon (Pagerduty, Inc.)
abstract: AI is shipping more code to production than ever before, but incidents are taking longer to resolve. Hear from peers at different stages of operational maturity, all testing out ways to put AI and automation to work so their teams get more time back for innovation. Panelists will share how they decide what's safe to automate outright, where to keep a human in or on the loop, and where full human judgment still matters. You'll hear what convinced them to hand over more control, what happened when it didn't go as planned, and how they cut toil without losing their grip on the systems they're accountable for. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

title: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
speakers: kiran kumar ballari (AWS); Lalit Khatter (AWS India Pvt Ltd); Ansley Verzosa (AWS); Raja N (AWS); Aaron Sempf (AWS)
abstract: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants, but what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their teams with consulting agents? In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

title: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
speakers: Nora Zhang (Amazon Web Services); Salvador Lopez Beneyto (AWS)
abstract: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

title: Turn AWS Security Signals into Action with AI-First SecOps (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company)
aoi: Threat Detection & Incident Response;Agentic AI;Threat Intelligence
speakers: colin gibbens (Cisco); Peter Prizio (Splunk a Cisco Company)
abstract: Security teams operating on AWS need a faster path from signals to action without adding more operational complexity. In this session, Splunk and AWS will explore a new approach to cloud and AI-native security operations designed for faster onboarding, earlier detection, and more efficient investigation and response. You’ll leave with practical insights into AI-first SecOps and how AWS-centered security teams can improve outcomes, regardless of the size or maturity of their security operations. This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Turning Pharma Field Insights into Enterprise Intelligence (sponsored by ZS)
abstract: Learn how ZS and AWS help pharma teams turn field insights into AI-powered intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.

title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
services: Amazon CloudFront;Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Colm MacCarthaigh (AWS)
abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

title: Understand your network: practical network observability on AWS
speakers: Claudia Izquierdo (AWS); Leonardo Solano (AWS)
abstract: You're collecting Amazon VPC Flow Logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics, but still can't answer "why can't this instance reach the internet?" In this chalk talk, explore practical approaches to network observability on AWS, no deep expertise required. Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. Bring your monitoring questions, and we'll discuss real scenarios to help you build observability that works for your team.

title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
services: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS);Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)
speakers: Swapnil Dinkar (Amazon); Kirill Davydychev (AWS)
abstract: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
speakers: Giorgio Bonfiglio (AWS); Donald Quindardo (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.

title: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
speakers: Alex Tarasov (AWS); Aruna Govindaraju (Amazon Web Services); Cedric Pelvet (AWS); Jay Agnihotri (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

title: Unlock Workday data with AWS: Building Trustworthy Agents (sponsored by Workday)
abstract: Generative AI agents and analytics in AWS are only as effective as the enterprise context behind them. While tools like Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Quick deliver powerful reasoning capabilities, grounding those models in authoritative, real-time HR and financial data traditionally requires complex ETL pipelines, custom integrations, and data duplication. In this session, we’ll demonstrate how Workday natively bridges this gap on AWS.
