Through live cross-system AI agent demos, you’ll see how to deliver unified, real-time enterprise insights without writing ETL code or moving data. This presentation is brought to you by Workday, an AWS Partner.

title: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
speakers: Jeremy Schiefer (AWS); Cameron Smith (AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE))
abstract: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Using AI for Impact: Achieving Sustainability and ROI on AWS
speakers: Steffen Grunwald (Amazon Web Services); Francesca Stobbione (Amazon EU SARL); Alexis Bateman (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI is accelerating sustainability at unprecedented speed, but only if the infrastructure behind it keeps pace. In this session, we will explore how AWS makes AI infrastructure more sustainable through hardware design decisions that minimize embodied carbon, custom silicon optimized for energy efficiency, and ML-driven data center optimization. Amazon Operations will show how AI and ML turn facility maintenance into prescriptive, autonomous operations: optimizing HVAC, water, and utilities for greater equipment reliability, and sustainability. Leave with a clear understanding of the AWS services powering these solutions, how AWS is building a more sustainable infrastructure, and how to get started with tracking and reducing your environmental impact.

title: Validate your hands-on AWS skills & earn a Microcredential
speakers: Tom Lawlor (AWS)
abstract: In this session, you will be given time to attempt a microcredential exam of your choice on AWS Skill Builder. These timed, hands-on exams test your skills in a live, provisioned AWS environment and test on popular topics. The product and developer team will be onsite to walk you through the UI and introduce the exam. Please note - this is an individual exam, and you will not be provided any hints or guidance outside of what is provided in the typical test environment. This exam is free to take on AWS Skill Builder. Attendees are required to bring their own device to complete the exam. Those who pass will be issued a microcredential badge on Credly.

title: Vector search, agents, and image matching with Amazon DynamoDB
speakers: Deepthi Mohan (Amazon Web Services); Mo Kamioner (Amazon Web Services); Arjan Schaaf (Amazon Web Services); Greg Krumm (Amazon Web Services); Lee Hannigan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
speakers: Hanno Becker (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

title: Visa: Building autonomous defense for payments security in the agentic AI era
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon GuardDuty
aoi: Application Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response;Zero Trust
speakers: Gaurav Priyolkar (Amazon Web Services); Vaijayanti Korde (Visa Inc)
abstract: Visa secures one of the world's largest payment ecosystems, processing over $14 trillion across 300+ billion transactions annually. As AI-powered threats evolve, Visa is reimagining cybersecurity through hybrid-cloud architecture with 70+ controls framework, AI-driven operations, and an agentic control plane designed for autonomous defense. Built on an Agentic harness with Zero-Trust principles and AWS capabilities, such as Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Nitro Enclaves, and cloud-agnostic security controls, Visa continuously detects and mitigates risk across its cloud environment. Discover how Visa is building a security foundation for the agentic AI era, protecting today's payments ecosystem while enabling AI-powered applications and autonomous workloads.

title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
services: Amazon CloudWatch;AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
speakers: Alex Waddell (Amazon Web Services); Meg Peddada (AWS)
abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.

title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon Cognito;Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
speakers: Sam Sanders (AWS); Amit Lulla (AWS)
abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Visual reasoning will be bigger than language reasoning
speakers: Ranjay Krishna (University of Washington)
abstract: Today’s vision-language models can describe images fluently, yet still struggle with the spatial and perceptual reasoning required for robotics. This talk argues that visual reasoning—reasoning through points, sketches, trajectories, depth maps, and other grounded representations—will become more important than language reasoning for physical agents. It traces progress from benchmarks exposing fundamental perception failures to methods that teach models to reason directly in visual space. These ideas culminate in robotics foundation models that convert visual plans into robot actions. The resulting systems are interpretable, steerable, deployable zero-shot on affordable hardware, and competitive with proprietary models trained on substantially more data. We showcase how these ideas are advancing the goal of accessible, general-purpose robotics to the broader research community.

title: Warehouse Alchemy: How Eni's AI agents cut days of sourcing to minutes
speakers: Andrea Corneo (Eni S.p.A.); Paolo Romagnoli (AWS)
abstract: Eni operates one of the world's most complex upstream supply chains, managing exploration and production materials across warehouses on multiple continents. Tubular items alone represent €1.5 billion out of a €2.5 billion inventory — scattered across dozens of facilities with fragmented visibility. Engineers searching for available spare parts faced a manual, days-long process of cross-referencing spreadsheets, navigating import restrictions, certifications, third-party stock, and delivery schedules — often resulting in unnecessary new purchases while surplus materials sat idle in distant warehouses. With Eni's expansion into fast-track development, biofuel production, and CCUS, the traditional material management approach couldn't keep pace with the speed and complexity of global operations.

title: What AI agents need from an application backend
abstract: AI agents build applications differently than people do. They work from code, call APIs, run in parallel, and keep working after you close your laptop. In this session, learn what a backend has to provide for an agent to carry an application from first prompt to production: schema and configuration as code the agent can read and change, serverless infrastructure with nothing to size or provision, data APIs and authentication that work on the first call, isolated environments for every experiment the agent runs, logs the agent can query when something breaks, and approval steps that keep destructive changes in your hands.

title: What Breaks First: Detection Engineering Lessons at AWS Scale (sponsored by Datadog)
speakers: Andrew Krug (Datadog)
abstract: Tighten the detection rule and you miss the variant. Loosen them and you drown the on-call. Deviate too far either way and you risk missing attackers and getting compromised. FanDuel handled adjustments by hand for years, until attackers started moving faster than the tuning backlog. Join FanDuel and Datadog to see detection rebuilt around automation: SIEM logic as code, orchestrated enrichment and triage, vulnerability workflows in the same pipeline. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for scaling detection engineering, reducing analyst toil, and knowing where AI helps and where it creates new work. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
speakers: Nadia Labai (AWS)
abstract: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

title: What FanDuel learned running containers on hundreds of AWS Outposts
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Outposts
speakers: Josh Coen (AWS); Ramsey McGrath (Fanduel); savallur Vallurupalli (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Running containerized workloads across dozens of AWS Local Zones and hundreds of AWS Outposts demands operational patterns that hold up at fleet scale. In this session, learn how FanDuel operates Amazon EKS across a huge hybrid edge fleet with a focus on high availability, patching, observability, service disruption handling, and autoscaling. The session digs into how workloads respond gracefully to service link and hardware disruptions, and how autoscaling behaves when compute is fixed and on-rack. Discover the operational model that keeps a large edge fleet healthy without growing the platform team at the same rate.

title: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
speakers: Steve Kendrex (Amazon); Chase Kernan (AWS)
abstract: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS operators, can access your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. Use what you learn to make the security case for approving your AI workload.

title: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
speakers: Rayman Aeron (Amazon Web Service); Alexandr Moroz (AWS)
abstract: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale, and this session provides a product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. See how recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications on, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. We'll discuss the range of compute options, from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. You will leave this session knowing how to apply the newest ECS capabilities to your workloads today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds.

title: What's New in Amazon Connect Customer
abstract: Your customers don't experience departments — they experience one journey. But siloed systems, fragmented data, and manual processes between teams create gaps they absolutely feel. This session introduces new Amazon Connect Customer capabilities that close those gaps end to end. Come see how these capabilities work together to deliver the seamless experience your customers expect and the certainty your business demands.

title: What's new in Amazon Route 53: DNS innovations for 2026
services: Amazon Route 53;AWS Cloud WAN;AWS Network Firewall
aoi: Global Infrastructure;Network & Infrastructure Security;Threat Detection & Incident Response
speakers: Bhargav Talluri (Amazon Web Services); Hardik Rathod (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Explore the latest innovations in Amazon Route 53, AWS's fully managed DNS service. This session covers 2026 launches including Route 53 Global Resolver for secure anycast DNS resolution from anywhere without VPNs, DNS Views sharing across accounts, and expanded DNS Firewall threat protection through partnerships. In this session, we also cover Profiles enhancements for simplified multi-VPC DNS management with granular IAM controls, and expanded domain registration support. Learn how these capabilities help you secure DNS resolution, simplify hybrid and multi-account architectures, and strengthen your DNS security posture at scale.

title: What's new in Application Security: Securing applications at machine speed
speakers: Joao Melo (AWS); Daniel Santana (Itau Unibanco SA); Christopher Rae (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: AI is accelerating your release cadence. AWS application security capabilities help engineering teams ship secure applications faster, including AI-powered workloads. In this session, learn how AI-driven services enforce organizational guardrails before code is written, perform threat modeling, review code for vulnerabilities, generate fixes automatically, and enable on-demand penetration testing. See how to codify these into paved pathways that give developers room to build with AI while maintaining consistent security standards. Leave with a clear plan for embedding AWS application security into your platform, from design through continuous validation.

title: What's new in AWS Serverless
speakers: Giedrius Praspaliauskas (AWS)
abstract: The serverless landscape moves fast, and the months leading up to re:Invent bring a wave of new capabilities for building event-driven applications. This hands-on workshop is your chance to explore the latest releases the moment they land. Build with the newest serverless features, work through the technical trade-offs that matter in real systems, and leave with production-ready patterns you can apply the moment you're back at your desk. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: What's new in eero networking
abstract: Join us to learn about the latest innovations in eero networking. This session covers new capabilities in AI-powered network analytics, simplified connectivity, centralized security, and multi-WAN resilience - all built cloud-native and designed to scale.

title: What's new in full-stack AWS app development
speakers: Nikhil Dabhade (Amazon Web Services); Praneeta Prakash (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.

title: What's new with AWS Backup
abstract: Learn about the latest AWS Backup capabilities and how they can help you simplify and strengthen your data protection strategy. We cover new features, use cases, and guidance for getting started.

title: What's new with AWS Transform for migrations
abstract: AWS Transform for migrations is evolving to help enterprises tackle migration challenges head on. With agentic AI capabilities working across the migration lifecycle, AWS Transform automates what previously slowed teams down with manual work. In this session, get a first look at the latest capabilities accelerating your enterprise migration. Whether you're planning a first migration or scaling across hundreds of workloads, walk away knowing how agentic AI is changing how infrastructure migration is done and how you can put it in practice.

title: What's new with NVIDIA GPUs in Amazon EC2
abstract: A large-scale AI workload can run for weeks across thousands of interconnected GPUs, where a single failure or security gap can be costly. Amazon EC2 brings together a portfolio of accelerated computing instances and innovations that keep the most demanding AI workloads secure by default and resilient to failures and maintenance. In this session, discover what's new in the AWS accelerated compute portfolio and dive deep into the architecture behind the latest generation of GPU instances for training and inference across large language and multimodal models. Hear real-world examples of how leading companies build on AWS, and leave understanding how AWS accelerated computing enables AI at scale.

title: What's new with the AWS Sustainability service
speakers: Marta Fraga (Amazon)
abstract: If you've ever wanted to know more about the environmental impact of your cloud usage, this session is for you. In this lightning talk, learn about the latest features of the AWS Sustainability service, including expanded impact areas beyond carbon, increased data granularity, and programmatic access via APIs. We walk through how to use the service to track progress against your sustainability goals and integrate environmental data into your existing workflows and reporting processes. Whether you're just getting started or already reporting on cloud emissions, this session has you covered.

title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
speakers: Simon Moore (AWS); Chetan Suri (AWS)
abstract: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
speakers: Clarke Rodgers (Amazon Web Services); Hart Rossman (AWS)
abstract: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

title: When Software Builds and Improves Itself (sponsored by Factory)
abstract: Software is becoming more than something companies build. It is becoming the system through which they improve. The next generation of software factories will turn business signals into production software, measure the outcomes, and use those outcomes to improve each cycle of development. Engineers set the goals, architecture, policies, and approval gates, while the system handles execution and continuously improves itself. Factory cofounder Eno Reyes will share what this future looks like, what has to be true to build it, and why self-improving software will fundamentally change how every company operates. This presentation is brought to you by Factory, an AWS Partner.

title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
services: Amazon Aurora;Amazon CloudWatch;Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)
speakers: Samir Behara (Amazon Web Services (AWS)); Sasi Kiran Malladi (AWS)
abstract: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

title: Which customization path? A decision framework for fine-tuning on AWS
speakers: Kanwaljit Khurmi (AMAZON WEB SERVICES INC); Jason Berkowitz (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Off the shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice of technique and service. In this chalk talk, we work through that choice live. See when Supervised Fine Tuning is enough, when Direct Preference Optimization or Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback earns its added cost, when Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards or multi turn reinforcement learning is the right call, and what data each needs. Compare Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization, SageMaker AI training jobs, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import by cost and control. Bring a real use case and we'll work through where it fits.

title: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler)
speakers: Mrigank Singh (ZScaler Inc.)
abstract: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Winning the DDoS Game: defend your app under real-time attack
speakers: Julian Garcia (AWS); Jonathan Woods (Amazon Web Services (AWS))
abstract: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!

title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
services: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2);Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS);Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3)
speakers: Sarik Ghazarian (Amazon); Parmida Atighehchian (Amazon (AWS))
abstract: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

title: World Models & Physical AI: The next frontier in intelligent systems
services: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS);AWS Trainium;Amazon SageMaker AI
speakers: Diwakar Bansal (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.

title: Wrong, Not Broken, & Why your Observability should know the difference
speakers: Imaya Kumar Jagannathan (AWS); Nikhil Kapoor (AWS)
abstract: Agentic applications need different access patterns and tooling than traditional apps. Teams often stitch together several tools and act as the human orchestrator just to answer a basic question: is my agent doing what the business needs? That gets harder when the agent runs on one cloud and calls models or APIs on another. In this session, we show how CloudWatch Omni brings AI agents and applications across clouds into one view, accelerating root cause whether its due to performance, availability or response quality.

title: Your Agent Has an Upstream Dependency You Can't See (sponsored by Brave)
abstract: Verify, don't trust: a reproducible needle test that surfaces undeclared upstream calls in any stack. This presentation is brought to you by Brave, an AWS Partner.

title: Your Agent Is in Production. Can You Explain What It Did? (sponsored by Datadog)
speakers: Andrew Krug (Datadog)
abstract: Your team shipped an agent to production last quarter. It works, mostly. When it doesn't, nobody can explain why. This session covers what changes when non-deterministic systems enter your stack: which signals actually matter for agentic workloads, how to trace a multi-step agent across tools and models, and where AI agents can safely take action in your own operations. Live examples from Datadog LLM Observability, the Agent Console, AI Guard, and Bits AI. You'll leave with an instrumentation checklist. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

title: Your data, optimized models, lower costs: Turn business knowledge into AI you control
speakers: Karan Bhandarkar (Amazon Inc.); Pooja Karadgi (Amazon Web Services); Rosa Català (Reddit); Akash Bhatia (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: With dozens of models now available and new ones launching every week, customers face three questions: which models to start from, when does model customization unlock added performance or savings, and when to replace a model, either because their own needs changed or because a better model emerged. In this session, learn how to build custom evaluations for your specific use case with your own data, then reuse it choose the model for your use case based on quality and cost, track how customization improves performance, and confidently decide when a model is ready to deploy to production. When requirements change or new models become available, you can update and rerun the evaluation, enabling ongoing improvement of performance and cost against your specific business needs.

title: Your IPs, your rules: Dynamic edge routing without NAT for AWS BYOIP
speakers: Ammar Latif (Amazon Web Services); Srinivas Kurla (Amazon)
abstract: Some workloads need the public IP the world sees to live directly on the Amazon EC2 instances, with no translation in the path. Email gateways rotating sender IPs, VPN concentrators assigning a dedicated address per client, or security appliances terminating traffic on the exact advertised address need the instance to own those public IPs. In this live-coding talk, we build that model end-to-end on AWS: writing CloudFormation for BYOIP pools and Bring Your Own ASN, coding NAT-free ingress routing so traffic arrives untranslated, and configuring BGP peering with Amazon VPC Route Server for high availability.

title: Your network, your rules: Global routing policies with AWS Cloud WAN
services: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC);AWS Cloud WAN;AWS Site-to-Site VPN
speakers: Shubham Singh (Amazon Web Services); Mandar Sridhar Alankar (Amazon Web Services Inc.)
abstract: As global networks scale, they demand deterministic traffic paths, not best-effort routing. In this workshop, gain granular control over traffic flows between Regions, VPCs, and on-premises locations using AWS Cloud WAN routing policies across a multi-Region network. Through hands-on labs, configure route filtering to control reachability, summarize prefixes to reduce routing table complexity, and influence preferred paths with BGP attributes. Leave with practical skills to design scalable, policy-driven connectivity architectures. Bring your laptop.

title: Your runtime Is being deprecated. Your weekend isn't.
speakers: Alpna Sharma Daniels (Amazon); Renuka Krishnan (AWS)
abstract: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
services: AWS Cloud WAN;AWS Direct Connect;AWS Global Accelerator
speakers: Anandprasanna Gaitonde (AWS); Mehdi Dahane (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone, but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.

title: Zero to multimodal in 60 mins: Building Live Sync on Connect Customer
speakers: Andrei Papancea (AWS); Joe Sullivan (AWS)
abstract: What does it take to synchronize a live voice conversation with a real-time visual interface — and make it feel like magic? In this chalk talk, we'll answer that question by building one from scratch. Starting from first principles, we'll construct a fully functional voice AI agent that leverages the patented Live Sync on Amazon Connect Customer: the signaling that keeps voice and visual in lock-step, the state machine that drives bi-directional interaction, and the rendering layer that turns conversational intent into on-screen UI in real time. No slides, no hand-waving — just building, live, from zero to a working multimodal agent in 60 minutes. At the end, we'll deploy what we built and every phone in the room becomes a live demo.

title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
aoi: Responsible AI;Zero Trust;Agentic AI;Amazon Builds on AWS
speakers: Gopinath Jagadesan (Amazon Web Services)
abstract: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.
